**The problem it solves**

### **The Infrastructure of Trust: How 0xKeep Modernizes Token Management**

0xKeep transforms abstract promises into cryptographic guarantees. It allows founders, DAOs, and investors to secure assets using immutable code rather than human trust.

#### **1. Rug-Proofing Liquidity Pools (Safer & Cheaper)**
*   **The Old Way:** Developers pay predatory lockers a "Tax" (often 1% of their total liquidity) and rely on a platform that holds admin keys. If the platform gets hacked or malicious, the liquidity is gone.
*   **The 0xKeep Way:** Developers pay a **flat fee (0.03 ETH)** to lock LP tokens in an immutable vault.
*   **Why it’s better:** It saves projects thousands of dollars in fees and eliminates "platform risk." There are no admin keys; once locked, the math dictates the release, not a middleman.

#### **2. Automated Team & Investor Vesting (Easier)**
*   **The Old Way:** Founders manually send tokens to team members every month. This is prone to human error, forgotten payments, and lack of transparency for the receiver.
*   **The 0xKeep Way:** Founders configure a **Linear Vesting Schedule** (e.g., "1-year stream with a 6-month cliff") in a single transaction.
*   **Why it’s better:** It’s "Set and Forget." Tokens stream second-by-second. Employees can claim their salary whenever they want, and they can verify on-chain that their allocation is reserved solely for them.

#### **3. Verified "Proof of Lock" Marketing (Viral Utility)**
*   **The Old Way:** Projects post confusing Etherscan links or screenshots to prove they are safe. Investors struggle to verify if the contract is actually secure.
*   **The 0xKeep Way:** Developers generate a **Live Embed Widget** (`<iframe>`) from our dashboard and place it directly on their website.
*   **Why it’s better:** It creates an instant, verifiable trust signal on the project's own landing page. Investors see a "Verified by 0xKeep" badge and real-time countdowns without needing to read Solidity code.

#### **4. Secure Project Handovers (Operational Efficiency)**
*   **The Old Way:** When a developer leaves a project or a DAO takes over, moving locked liquidity is difficult or requires trusting the original deployer to sign transactions indefinitely.
*   **The 0xKeep Way:** Our architecture supports **Full Ownership Transfer**. A dev can launch a token, lock the liquidity, and then cryptographically transfer control of that lock to a DAO Multisig.
*   **Why it’s better:** It professionalizes the lifecycle of a crypto project, allowing for seamless transition of power without unlocking (and risking) the funds.

**Challenges we ran into**

**The Hurdle:**
During our internal audit, we discovered a critical Denial of Service (DoS) vector in our array management logic. Initially, we used a standard "**for**" loop to find and remove a lock ID from a user's list when they transferred ownership. We realized that if a user created thousands of vesting schedules (e.g., for a large airdrop), the loop would exceed the block gas limit, effectively trapping their assets and making the transfer function revert permanently.

**The Solution:**
We refactored the contract to implement an **O(1) "Swap-and-Pop" algorithm** combined with an internal index mapping. Instead of iterating through the array, we track the exact index of every lock ID in a parallel mapping. When a lock is transferred, we swap it with the last element in the array and pop it off. This ensures that gas costs remain constant and low, regardless of whether a user has 5 locks or 50,000, guaranteeing the protocol scales safely on Base.

### LGTM
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/lgtm-f0ad) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Kishan0703/pr_shield) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/5AeXR8BSDug) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/5AeXR8BSDug) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-NMIT%20HACKS%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://nmithacks26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-17-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Shipping fast is great. Shipping secure is better.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

LGTM solves two problems that every software team faces but nobody is fixing together expensive AI code review and unprotected CI/CD pipelines.

Existing tools burn thousands of LLM tokens on every PR by dumping your entire codebase into the model, making costs grow with your codebase size rather than the value you get. At the same time, nobody is watching the pipeline itself the workflow files and deployment configs that have full access to your production servers and secrets. Real attacks happen here, not in the application code.

LGTM fixes both. Our Tree-sitter and PageRank engine selects only the structurally critical code relevant to each change, sending 10x fewer tokens to 6 parallel specialist AI agents security, bugs, performance, style, documentation, and test coverage. You bring your own API key, we charge nothing on top, making a 10-developer team pay around $14 a month instead of $240 with competitors.

For pipeline security, 16 deterministic rule-based detectors scan your CI/CD configuration files on every push zero LLM tokens, sub-second execution. When a critical issue is found, three enforcement gates fire a PR comment with fixes, a blocked merge button, and most importantly a runtime halt that stops the pipeline before checkout, before tests, before anything runs. Direct pushes, cron jobs, tag-triggered deployments all covered. No competitor has this.

We also built a Knowledge Graph an interactive visual dependency map of your entire codebase showing which files are most critical, most coupled, and most risky powered by the same engine that makes our reviews precise.

LGTM is for startups moving fast without a security team, open source maintainers reviewing PRs from strangers, and any engineering team whose pipelines have never been audited.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building LGTM was not straightforward. Every layer of the system introduced its own set of problems that took real debugging time to solve.

The first major challenge was context selection. Getting Tree-sitter to parse a live GitHub repository accurately and then running PageRank on the resulting dependency graph in real time was not trivial. The graph computation had to be fast enough to not block the review pipeline while still being accurate enough to send meaningful context to the agents. Early versions were either too slow or sending irrelevant context, which tanked review quality.

The second challenge was the multi-agent architecture. Running six LLM agents in parallel sounds simple until you realise that parallel API calls fail unpredictably, rate limits hit at random, and the synthesizer has to produce a coherent verdict from six agents that may partially contradict each other. Building a reliable aggregation layer that handles partial failures gracefully without dropping findings or blocking the pipeline took significant iteration.

The third challenge was the BullMQ and Redis reliability issue. Workers were silently dropping jobs whenever Redis disconnected unexpectedly. No errors surfaced, no logs triggered tasks simply vanished. This was invisible until we noticed reviews not completing under load. Solving this required implementing proper Redis reconnection handling and dead letter queues for failed jobs.

The fourth and most frustrating challenge was the GitHub OAuth cold start problem on Fly.io. Our server was spinning down between requests due to Fly.io's idle machine behaviour, which killed active OAuth sessions mid-login. Users would authenticate with GitHub and get dropped back to the login page with no error. The fix was a single configuration line setting min_machines_running to 1 but finding that root cause after hours of debugging session handling code was painful.

The fifth challenge was the runtime halt architecture. Getting the GitHub Action to reliably call our API as step one of any workflow, receive the halt decision, and exit cleanly before any subsequent steps ran across different workflow configurations, different runner environments, and different trigger types required careful design of the Action's failure handling to ensure it never silently passed when it should have blocked.

**AI & ML**

LGTM sits at the intersection of AI and security engineering two fields that are increasingly impossible to separate.

The core of what makes LGTM intelligent is not just that it uses LLMs. It is how it uses them. We built a context selection engine that applies classical ML concepts graph theory and the PageRank algorithm on top of compiler-grade AST parsing to determine which parts of a codebase are structurally critical for any given change. The model does not receive raw text. It receives a mathematically ranked, dependency-aware context. That is applied machine learning directly improving LLM output quality while reducing token consumption by 10x.

The six specialist agents are not generic prompts. Each one is a fine-tuned role with specific instructions, domain focus, and output schema security, bugs, performance, style, documentation, and test coverage running in parallel and feeding into a synthesizer that produces a final weighted verdict. That multi-agent architecture is the same pattern driving the most advanced AI systems being built today.

On the CI/CD security side, the 16 deterministic detectors use pattern recognition on structured AST data not keyword matching, not regex alone to identify dangerous configurations with zero false positives and zero LLM dependency. That is rule-based ML applied to a real security problem.

The Knowledge Graph takes it further visualising the entire codebase as a force-directed graph where node importance is computed using PageRank, edge weights represent dependency strength, and coupling and churn scores surface risk automatically. That is graph ML made visible and actionable for developers.

LGTM does not use AI as a feature. AI is the architecture.

**Google Gemini**

LGTM integrates Google Gemini as one of its selectable LLM providers powering the six parallel AI code review agents. When a developer opens a pull request, our Tree-sitter and PageRank engine selects only the structurally critical context sending 10x fewer tokens than naive approaches and Gemini processes that optimised context to produce specialist reviews across security, bugs, performance, style, documentation, and test coverage. The bring-your-own-key model means teams using Gemini pay Google directly at cost with zero markup from us, making production-grade AI code review accessible to startups and open source maintainers who cannot afford flat per-seat pricing.

**MongoDB Atlas**

MongoDB serves as the primary persistence layer for LGTM, storing everything that matters user accounts, connected repositories, PR reviews, security findings, audit logs, and scan history. The document model was a natural fit for our use case because every review is a richly nested object findings with severity levels, rule IDs, affected file paths, suggested fixes, and resolution status all living inside a single scan document. The audit log is designed write-once at the schema level with only the resolution field remaining mutable, giving teams an immutable security record they can trust for compliance. MongoDB also stores the codebase index per repository, which feeds both the AI review agents and the Knowledge Graph generation pipeline.

**The problem it solves**

**NOTE: The Google Drive link provided in the project section contains the APK file of our application. Please open the link on your mobile device to download and install the app.**


![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/092d9e9df5624d84900a997aae8ee6d3/3e08b17d-5b70-4c02-adc9-010cc87aaff9.jpeg)

Travel planning today is often **time-consuming, unorganized, and lacks personalization**. Tourists **struggle to find reliable itineraries, manage expenses, and explore destinations** effectively. There is also a **lack of immersive experiences before visiting a place**, making it harder to plan confidently.

At the same time, **traveler safety remains a major concern**, especially in unfamiliar locations, with limited real-time monitoring and emergency support. Additionally, there is **no transparent system to support cultural heritage and local communities** during travel.

Our solution addresses these challenges by combining **AI, AR/VR, and blockchain** to provide smart planning, immersive exploration, enhanced safety, and trustworthy transactions in one unified platform.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **API Response Errors (JSON Issues)**
One major issue was handling unexpected or incomplete JSON responses from the itinerary API, which caused errors like “Unexpected end of JSON input.”


2. **AR/VR Integration Complexity**
Integrating AR and VR features with smooth performance across devices was challenging, especially handling camera access and rendering 3D content.

3. **Blockchain Transaction Delays**
While integrating smart contracts, transactions on the testnet sometimes took time or failed unexpectedly.

4. **Real-time Safety Features (SOS & Geofencing)**
Implementing accurate location tracking and triggering alerts in real-time was complex.

**The Render Deployment Bounty ($850 Pool)**

We used **Render for deploying our full-stack application**, ensuring reliable hosting and smooth performance for both frontend and backend services. Render helped us quickly deploy and manage our APIs with minimal configuration.

Additionally, we utilized **Render PostgreSQL** as our **database to support critical features like geofencing. Location data**, user movement tracking, and safety-related information are securely stored and efficiently managed using PostgreSQL.

This setup enables real-time data handling, scalability, and seamless integration of our safety features, making Render a key part of our deployment and backend infrastructure.

### Roots to Routes
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/roots-to-routes-291a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/eshwarsaigoudpanjala-debug/Roots-To-Routes) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://roots-to-routes-lhyb.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Lfgv4Hf109U) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-13-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> " Learn , Play And Discover The Journey of FOOD."

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Many people, especially children and urban consumers, consume food every day without understanding how it is grown, what resources are required for cultivation, when it is harvested, or how it reaches their plates. Information about food production is often scattered across multiple websites, difficult to understand, and not presented in an engaging manner.

Roots to Routes solves this problem by providing a single platform where users can explore the complete journey of food items such as rice, fruits, vegetables, pulses, and dry fruits—from cultivation to consumption.

Users can:
- Learn step-by-step growing processes.
- Understand soil, water, and fertilizer requirements.
- Discover seasonal crops and harvesting methods.
- Explore nutritional benefits of different foods.
- Learn through interactive quizzes, videos, and educational games.

The platform makes agricultural and food education easier to understand, more engaging, and accessible for students, children, teachers, and consumers, helping bridge the gap between people and the origins of their food.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Faced

During development, one of the biggest challenges was collecting and organizing accurate information for different food items such as rice, fruits, vegetables, pulses, and dry fruits. The information was available across multiple sources and needed to be structured into a simple, easy-to-understand format.

Another challenge was presenting agricultural concepts in an engaging way. Initially, the platform displayed large amounts of information, but we realized that younger users, especially children, would find it difficult to read long explanations. To address this, we introduced a more interactive approach through visual content, quizzes, and educational games.

We also faced challenges in designing a user-friendly search experience that could quickly provide relevant information while keeping the interface simple and intuitive.

How We Solved Them

- Organized information into clear step-by-step learning modules.
- Simplified complex agricultural concepts into easy-to-understand content.
- Added quizzes and interactive learning elements to improve engagement.
- Focused on a clean and simple user interface for easier navigation.
- Continuously refined the platform based on feedback from mentors and peers.

**Gemini**

Gemini API acts as the AI engine of Roots to Routes. User queries are sent to Gemini through secure API calls. Gemini analyzes the prompt and generates structured responses related to food cultivation, agricultural practices, nutrition, and farm-to-plate journeys. The generated content is then displayed on the website in an organized format, creating an interactive learning experience.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB serves as the backend database of Roots to Routes. It stores structured data including food categories, cultivation steps, farming requirements, nutritional values, quiz content, and user interactions. When a user searches for a food item, the application retrieves the relevant information from MongoDB and displays it dynamically. Its NoSQL architecture enables flexible data storage for different food types without requiring a rigid schema.

**Sarvam.ai**

Sarvam AI is integrated into our platform to process user queries and generate contextual responses. When users search for a food item or ask questions about its cultivation, Sarvam AI retrieves and organizes information into a simplified step-by-step format. This enables an interactive learning experience where users can explore food origins, farming practices, and nutritional information through natural language interactions.

**Open Innovation**

Roots to Routes fits into the Open Innovation track because it addresses a real-world educational and social challenge that spans multiple domains, including agriculture, education, nutrition, and technology.

The project aims to bridge the gap between consumers and food production by helping users understand where their food comes from and how it is cultivated. Rather than focusing on a single industry-specific problem, it creates a broader learning experience that can benefit students, children, teachers, parents, and general consumers.

By combining food awareness, agricultural knowledge, interactive learning, quizzes, and educational games into a single platform, Roots to Routes encourages informed food choices and promotes appreciation for farming and food production. Its impact extends beyond agriculture, making it a suitable solution for the Open Innovation category.

Avoid high SWIFT fees and long settlement times
Protect value from local currency volatility
Why it’s better:
No correspondent banking delays. No hidden FX markups. Faster, cheaper, and more transparent.
2. Domestic Spending in Dollars
Spend locally using a USD balance
Pay for subscriptions, online services, imports, and digital tools
Avoid forced conversion into weak local currencies
Why it’s safer:
Your purchasing power isn’t eroded by sudden devaluations. You hold value in USD while still spending seamlessly.
3. Dollar Savings That Preserve Value
Store money in USD instead of local currency
Protect savings from inflation and devaluation
Access funds anytime
Why it’s powerful:
Instead of watching savings shrink due to inflation, users preserve wealth in a globally stable unit of account.
4. Yield-Generating Investments
Earn up to 15% through structured DeFi strategies
Capital-efficient strategies designed to prioritize principal protection
Transparent on-chain execution
Why it’s safer:
Strategies are automated, diversified, and transparent, reducing reliance on informal or opaque investment schemes.
5. Freelancers and Remote Workers
Get paid in USD
Avoid costly intermediaries
Instantly move earnings into savings or yield products
Why it’s easier:
Payments, spending, and investing happen within one unified financial system.
6. Importers and Online Buyers
Pay international suppliers directly
Avoid unpredictable FX swings
Manage cash flow in a stable currency

It replaces unstable local banking constraints with stable savings, global payments, and programmable yield, all within one dollar-based account.

**Challenges we ran into**

Our primary challenge is capital constraints.
Operating a modern dollar-denominated neobank requires real infrastructure costs. While much of our system is automated, we still incur ongoing expenses, including:
Server and cloud infrastructure costs to maintain uptime, security, and scalability
AI-powered customer support credits to automate customer service efficiently
SMS and communication provider fees for sending messages and enabling API-based customer calls
Third-party API integrations required for payments, compliance, and operational reliability
Although our customer support is fully automated using AI, it still requires paid credits from AI providers and communication platforms to function reliably at scale.

### Zeus-Cont
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zeuscont-da5d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vorsv/Zeus-Cont) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](http://zeus.xenopent.tech/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/IMjWdcQLZTU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-9-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Less Weighing Collaborative Malware Analysis Env.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Analyzing a virus or "malware" is usually a slow, dangerous, and complicated process. Zeus-Cont makes
  it fast, safe, and easy for everyone.

  1. It creates a "Digital Cage" for Viruses
   * The Problem: You can’t just open a suspicious file on your laptop to see what it does—it could steal
     your data or break your computer.
   * Our Solution: We provide a safe, isolated container (a "sandbox"). You can run the virus inside this
     cage, and it can’t escape to hurt your actual computer or the internet.

  2. It Translates "Matrix Code" into Plain English
   * The Problem: Malware generates thousands of lines of confusing technical logs. It takes a human
     hours to read through them all.
   * Our Solution: We use Gemini AI to read all that "boring" data for you. In seconds, it writes a
     simple report explaining exactly what the virus was trying to do.

  3. It’s a "GPS" for Security Training
   * The Problem: Most hacking tools are very intimidating and hard to learn.
   * Our Solution: We integrated a Voice Assistant (using Sarvam AI). It actually talks to you and guides
     you through the app, making advanced security research as easy as following a GPS.

  4. No More Working Alone
   * The Problem: Usually, security experts work in silos. If they find something, they have to take
     screenshots and send emails.
   * Our Solution: Our platform is collaborative. Multiple people can jump into the same session to hunt
     a threat together in real-time, just like a shared Google Doc.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Container Orchestration: Making the backend "talk" to Docker to create and destroy isolated sandboxes on demand.
2. Network Isolation: Building a "fake internet" so malware stays trapped but still tries to execute its code.
3. Real-Time Streaming: Pushing file, network, and process events to the browser instantly without any lag.
4. Noise Reduction: Automatically hiding normal system processes so the analyst only sees the malicious activity.
5. AI Data Management: Condensing thousands of raw log lines so Gemini can generate a smart, human-readable report.
6. Forensic Tooling: Packaging heavy-duty security tools (like Radare2 and Volatility) into a lightweight, fast-loading image.

**Gemini**

The Gemini API is the project's "Intelligence Layer." While the sandbox and C agent collect raw data, Gemini acts as the Senior Malware Researcher who interprets that data.

  Its involvement is broken down into three key roles:

  1. Automated Forensic Synthesis
  The most significant involvement is in the Report Generation Engine. When an analyst finishes a session, the backend sends a massive volume of telemetry logs (Process trees, File changes, Network packets) to
  Gemini. 
   * The Task: Gemini parses thousands of lines of raw logs into a structured, professional ANY.RUN-style Malware Analysis Report.
   * The Value: It saves analysts hours of manual work by identifying the "needle in the haystack"—such as distinguishing a normal system file edit from a malicious persistence attempt.

  2. Contextual Intelligence & IOC Extraction
  Gemini is used to identify and categorize Indicators of Compromise (IOCs). It scans the telemetry to extract:
   * Malicious Hashes: Identifying suspicious files dropped during execution.
   * C2 Infrastructure: Spotting Command & Control domains or IP addresses hidden in network traffic.
   * Threat Scoring: Based on the activity patterns, Gemini calculates a "Threat Score" (0-100), helping the analyst prioritize the risk level of the sample.

  3. MITRE ATT&CK Reasoning
  While the system can detect what happened, Gemini explains why it matters. It analyzes the sequences of events to confirm MITRE techniques. For example, if it sees a process modifying ~/.bashrc, Gemini maps
  this to T1546.004 (Persistence via Unix Shell Configuration), providing the technical rationale for why that specific action is a security risk.

  Technical Implementation Details:
   * Models Used: Optimized for gemini-2.0-flash for high-speed analysis and long context windows (to handle large log files).
   * Prompt Engineering: Uses a high-precision system prompt with explicit rules to ensure reports are professional, monochromatic, and free of AI "hallucinations."
   * Determinism: Set to a very low temperature (0.1) to ensure that the same malware activity always results in the same technical conclusion.

**Sarvam.ai**

The Sarvam API serves as the "Voice of Zeus," providing the narrative layer for the platform's onboarding and tactical guidance. While the Gemini API handles the "brain" (logic and reporting), Sarvam provides
  the "voice" (audio and communication).

  Its specific involvement includes:

  1. Indic-Specific Tactical Assistance
  The project uses Sarvam’s Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities (specifically the bulbul:v3 model) to provide a localized, natural-sounding audio guide. 
   * The Persona: It powers the "Zeus Tactical Assistant," which speaks to the analyst in high-fidelity Indian dialects/accents.
   * The Goal: This makes the platform more accessible and provides a modern "Mission Control" feel, where the system talks to you while you perform high-stakes analysis.

  2. Interactive Guided Onboarding (Walkthrough)
  The Walkthrough Application is entirely driven by Sarvam. As the user moves through the platform's different zones (Terminal, Telemetry, Intel Column), Sarvam generates real-time audio instructions:
   * It explains complex cybersecurity concepts (like MITRE mapping) through spoken word.
   * It reduces the cognitive load on the analyst, allowing them to keep their eyes on the telemetry feeds while receiving audio cues about the environment.

  3. Real-Time Instruction Proxy
  Technically, the project implements a FastAPI Proxy for Sarvam to ensure security and performance:
   * Security: The API keys are kept on the server side, preventing exposure in the frontend.
   * Speed: It uses Sarvam's low-latency endpoints to ensure that when an analyst clicks "Next" in the walkthrough, the audio response is nearly instantaneous.
   * Hybrid Fallback: The system is designed to check for Sarvam’s availability and fallback to standard Web Speech APIs if the network is disconnected, ensuring the "Assistant" never goes silent.

**CyberSecurity**

Zeus-Cont is a modular Dynamic Malware Analysis Sandbox designed for high-performance threat research. It maps directly to several critical cybersecurity operations:

   1. Isolated Threat Detonation (Sandboxing): The core of the project is the secure execution of suspicious binaries. By using Docker-based isolation and a custom "Fake Internet" gateway, analysts can observe
      malware behavior in a 100% contained environment, preventing any risk to the host system or external networks.
   2. Advanced Behavioral Telemetry: Unlike static analysis, Zeus-Cont captures real-time system behavior. This includes:
       * Process Tree Visualization: Identifying process hollowing, spawning chains, and stealthy execution patterns.
       * Network Forensics: Monitoring DNS queries and C2 (Command & Control) callbacks to identify malicious infrastructure.
       * File System Auditing: Detecting unauthorized modifications to sensitive system configurations.
   3. Framework Alignment (MITRE ATT&CK): The project integrates a real-time mapping system that translates technical telemetry into standardized tactics (e.g., Discovery, Persistence, Exfiltration). This aligns
      analysis with global industry standards used by SOC (Security Operations Center) teams.
   4. Collaborative Incident Response: By supporting multi-user shared sessions and synchronized terminals, the project facilitates collaborative threat hunting. This mirrors modern "War Room" scenarios where
      multiple researchers must coordinate to dissect a high-priority threat.
   5. AI-Augmented Forensics: Through Gemini AI integration, the platform automates the generation of structured forensic reports. This solves the "Documentation Gap" in cybersecurity, allowing analysts to move
      from detection to mitigation significantly faster.

Team **0xXeno** -- [Harish Anand](https://github.com/harukiii98), [Deepika Mahesh](https://github.com/Irisloveschips), [Deepak Arjun](https://github.com/I-am-das), [Vijay Rajan](https://github.com/vorsv)

> there is no bridge, i love you

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![SHA-256 Hashes](https://img.shields.io/badge/SHA--256%20Hashes-333333?style=flat-square) ![Keccak256](https://img.shields.io/badge/Keccak256-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![EIP-4788](https://img.shields.io/badge/EIP--4788-333333?style=flat-square) ![SSZ](https://img.shields.io/badge/SSZ-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most cross-chain applications still rely on relayers, bridges, or oracle networks to tell one chain what happened on another. **Anyware** removes that trust assumption.

Using [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788) beacon roots, it allows EVM networks to verify recent Ethereum state directly onchain through cryptographic proofs instead of externally signed messages.

**The demo use case is exploring trustless lending:**
1. a user locks ETH on Ethereum Sepolia
2. a proof of that vault state is generated
3. Base Sepolia verifies the proof onchain
4. demo USDC is issued without trusting a bridge or relayer

**The same primitive can power:**
cross-chain lending | governance verification | proof-of-reserves | attestations | generalized Ethereum state reads

**Challenges we ran into**

A major hurdle was proving that an execution payload header truly belonged to a beacon block trusted through [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788), while also resolving the correct destination-chain beacon-root timestamp window.

**We solved this by building a prover pipeline that:**
1. scans beacon blocks
2. matches execution payloads
3. constructs SSZ inclusion proofs
4. resolves the correct EIP-4788 anchor timestamp for onchain verification

**Ethereum Core**

Anyware builds directly on top of Ethereum consensus infrastructure using [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788).

We demonstrate via PoC how Ethereum beacon roots can become a native trust anchor for cross-chain verification without relying on bridges, relayers, or oracle committees.

**It combines:** EIP-4788 beacon roots | SSZ verification | execution state proofs | Ethereum Merkle-Patricia Trie verification; into a working trust-minimized interoperability primitive.

**Anyware improves:** security by reducing external trust assumptions, transparency through fully onchain verification, and interoperability across EVM networks.

**Network Economy**

Anyware enables trustless cross-chain economic interactions without relying on bridges, relayers, or oracle networks.
Using [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788), the project allows EVM networks to verify Ethereum state directly through cryptographic proofs anchored to Ethereum consensus.

**The demo shows this through cross-chain lending:**
1. a user locks ETH on Ethereum
2. another chain verifies that state onchain
3. credit is issued without trusting an intermediary


**Our library enabled developers to explore use-cases like:**
- cross-chain lending
- proof-of-reserves
- governance verification
- attestations and reputation
- shared liquidity systems

The project puts user control and protocol-level verification first by replacing externally trusted middleware with direct onchain proof verification.

Team **those two** -- Razvan Mihailescu, [jen sei](https://github.com/jen-sei)

### PoisonGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/poisonguard-c32b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Altaria-hackathon-teams/cybersecurity-three-engineers) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/-wVVMq83cjA?feature=share) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> cybersecurity+AI

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Several Companies are integrating their websites with chatbots, that are built on a RAG pipeline. RAG pipelines often use external documents to produce resources for the chatbot to supply the user answers. When a user asks a chatbot for an image, the chatbot tests the metadata against the user's request to give an output. Attackers can take advantage of this and edit the metadata using misaligned information, hence providing the user with a variation of the request. Our PoisonGuard aims to solve this very problem by comparing the metadata of the image to the description of the image produced by an LLM. If there's an anomaly the answer is withheld from the user thereby preventing the user from getting misinformation.

**Challenges we ran into**

We got inspiration for our idea, from a research paper published in the month of February, 2026. Considering the novelty of the paper we ran into trouble finding trustworthy dataset as well as getting a clear idea of the workflow.

**Cybersecurity + Artificial Intelligence**

Our project focuses on protecting the LLM output, by removing the poisoned documents while retrieving the documents through RAG pipeline. We trained our own ML model that was able to detect whether the document was poisoned (attacker changed the metadata) or not, based on the title and description of the image.

### Base Analytics
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/base-analytics-86fc) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://base-analytics-app.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Batches%20003:%20Student%20Track-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-batches-student-track-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Base Analytics is the ultimate reputation protocol

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Alchemy API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Alchemy%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Viem](https://img.shields.io/badge/Viem-333333?style=flat-square) ![Coinbase Onchainkit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Coinbase%20Onchainkit-333333?style=flat-square) ![Farcaster Frames v2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Farcaster%20Frames%20v2-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Base ecosystem is exploding, but the tools to navigate it are fundamentally fractured. Right now, Web3 power users and builders are forced to juggle multiple disconnected platforms just to get a clear picture of what is actually happening onchain.

Base Analytics solves three critical pain points in the current Web3 landscape:

1. The Fragmentation of Social and Financial Data
Currently, financial data (token prices, volume) lives on heavy trading terminals, while social signal and reputation data live separately on Farcaster. There is no unified command center that links the Base financial ecosystem with decentralized social identity. Users have to switch between tabs and apps to connect the dots.

2. The Noise-to-Signal Ratio
The Base network never sleeps. Humans cannot manually monitor real-time token shifts, protocol updates, and social sentiment 24/7. Users constantly miss critical ecosystem movements and alpha because they simply have to step away from their screens.

3. Opaque Decentralized Reputation
Farcaster is the heartbeat of Web3 social, and reputation metrics dictate visibility, trust, and airdrop eligibility. Yet, the average user has no clean, accessible way to visualize their actual on-chain social quotient, Neynar score, or Ethos credentials without querying raw APIs themselves.

The Solution:
Base Analytics acts as the ultimate autonomous command center. We bridge the gap by providing a unified dashboard where users can instantly track top BASE network assets while simultaneously visualizing their exact Farcaster reputation. To solve the attention problem, we deployed an autonomous AI agent that ingests raw market data, synthesizes the noise, and broadcasts native ecosystem insights every 6 hours—completely removing the need for manual monitoring.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an autonomous, real-time command center for the Base ecosystem sounded straightforward on paper, but wiring together decentralized social protocols, live financial data, and AI agents introduced several major hurdles:

1. The Web2 API Paywall & The Farcaster Pivot
Our original architecture had the AI Agent broadcasting its Base market insights to X (Twitter). However, we immediately ran into X's newly enforced, strict 402 Payment Required API paywall, which blocks automated posting for free-tier developer accounts. Instead of fighting Web2 infrastructure, we executed a hard pivot to Web3. We re-engineered the agent's voice to cast natively directly to Warpcast using a Neynar Signer UUID. This not only bypassed the paywall but actually resulted in a much better product—keeping the agent entirely native to the Base and Farcaster ecosystem.

2. LLM Cost Optimization & Compatibility Routing
Running an autonomous agent that fires every 6 hours can get expensive quickly. We initially built the agent's "brain" using the OpenAI SDK (gpt-4o-mini). When we ran into API billing constraints, we engineered a clever routing workaround. Instead of rewriting the entire AI logic, we utilized Google's Gemini API Compatibility Mode. By simply swapping the base URL and pointing the existing OpenAI SDK to gemini-2.5-flash, we kept the agent lightning-fast and highly capable while dropping our inference costs to zero.

3. Securing the Autonomous Cron Job
Because our AI agent lives on a Next.js serverless API route, we faced the challenge of preventing random users (or malicious bots) from finding the endpoint and spamming the Farcaster timeline. We solved this by implementing a strict verification handshake. The route now checks for a specific, heavily encrypted CRON_SECRET Bearer token that is only known to the secure Vercel Cron server, ensuring the agent only wakes up exactly when it is scheduled to.

4. Taming Live Financial Data with Strict TypeScript
Ingesting live market data from CoinGecko meant dealing with highly dynamic, constantly changing JSON objects. Early on, this caused our Next.js build to fail due to strict ESLint rules rejecting any types. We had to architect custom, strict TypeScript interfaces (CoinMarketData) to define the exact shape of the incoming Base token data, ensuring the app was completely type-safe from the initial data fetch all the way to the final AI prompt.

## About
NFT Battle Arena is a cross-collection NFT battle game on Base where any NFT from any collection becomes a playable fighter with real combat utility.

V2 brings strategic depth: players build full loadouts — pick a Fighter, equip an Item buff, and choose an Arena modifier — creating thousands of tactical combinations. Your entire wallet inventory is scanned for team synergies, rewarding long-term collectors with passive stat boosts.

All PvP matches are cryptographically secured. Players authenticate via SIWE (Sign-In with Ethereum), and combat is resolved entirely server-side using Vercel KV with atomic operations. A custom seeded PRNG engine (mulberry32 + FNV-1a hashing) ensures every battle is 100% deterministic and reproducible for replays and anti-cheat verification.

Key features:
• Universal stat normalization across 12+ Base NFT collections
• Multi-NFT loadouts (Fighter + Item + Arena) with diminishing returns
• 5 passive abilities with cooldown-based trigger systems
• Cinematic battle renderer with particles, screen shake, and damage numbers
• Server-authoritative PvP with SIWE + JWT authentication
• Deterministic seeded PRNG for reproducible battle outcomes
• Anti-drift snapshot hashing (SHA-256) for mutable NFT protection
• Live balance configuration via CDN for real-time meta-tuning
• V2 analytics pipeline tracking loadouts, battles, and results
• Farcaster and Base Mini App native integration


## The Problem it Solves
Most NFT collections become static PFPs with zero utility after minting. NFT Battle Arena solves this by giving every NFT on Base real combat utility through metadata normalization — no matter the collection, no matter the traits.

V2 goes further by solving three critical problems:

1. Single-NFT Boredom: Players now deploy full strategic loadouts (Fighter + Item + Arena), making every battle a tactical decision rather than a coin flip.

2. Client-Side Cheating: All PvP combat is resolved server-side via Vercel Serverless Functions. Players authenticate with SIWE, stats are snapshot-hashed at challenge time, and battles run on a deterministic seeded PRNG — making manipulation impossible.

3. Balance Stagnation: A live balance config system fetches stat cap overrides from a CDN, allowing real-time meta-tuning without redeployment. No more waiting for a code push to fix a broken build.

**Challenges we ran into**

• Metadata normalization across 12+ collections with wildly different trait structures — each collection needed custom mapping logic while keeping the system extensible via a data-driven collection profiles architecture.

• Balancing combat stats so no single collection dominates — implemented stat caps, floors, diminishing returns on buff layers (Items: 100%, Arena: 80%, Team: 60%), and configurable guardrails.

• Making battles feel cinematic in vanilla JavaScript without heavy game engines — built a custom animation system with CSS keyframes for screen shake, crit bursts, dodge ghosts, floating damage numbers, and particle effects.

• Deterministic replay system — implemented a seeded PRNG (mulberry32 + FNV-1a) to ensure the same battle inputs always produce identical outputs for server-side verification and future spectator mode.

• Server-side PvP without WebSockets — built an atomic challenge/fight system using Vercel KV hash operations to prevent race conditions during concurrent challenge acceptance.

• SIWE authentication flow — integrated Sign-In with Ethereum using the `siwe` npm package with `jose` JWT tokens (1h expiry, 5min nonce TTL) for stateless, secure API authentication.

• Browser compatibility — replaced Node.js crypto with Web Crypto API (SHA-256) for stat snapshots, and handled Farcaster miniapp connector nuances across Base and Warpcast hosts.

> Multimodal AI Fraud Verification & Polygon Escrow

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: A 30 Billion Dollar Broken Industry

Traditional insurance claim processing is plagued by three systemic failures:

1. Crippling Processing Delays: Claimants wait anywhere from 14 to 45 days for manual paperwork reviews, adjuster site visits, and back-and-forth email verifications.
2. Astronomical Fraud Overhead: Insurance fraud costs the global industry upwards of 30 Billion dollars annually. To combat this, insurers deploy armies of manual adjusters, driving up administrative overhead by 20 to 30 percent and forcing honest policyholders to pay higher premiums.
3. The Black Box Trust Deficit: Claimants have zero visibility into why their claim was delayed or rejected. Funds remain locked in corporate bank accounts, creating an inherent conflict of interest where insurers profit by delaying or denying payouts.


The Solution: ClaimChain Autonomous Escrow Protocol

ClaimChain completely replaces slow, manual insurance processing with an autonomous multimodal AI agent and trustless blockchain smart contracts on Polygon Amoy.

Instead of waiting weeks for human adjusters, users submit their incident narrative, payout request, and photo evidence. In seconds, ClaimChain executes an automated 3-stage protocol:

1. Multimodal AI Risk Verification
Google Gemini 1.5 Flash simultaneously analyzes the incident description and photo evidence through 5 specialized neural reasoning nodes: Vision Damage Analysis, NLP Semantic Cross-Validation, Risk Scoring Engine, Oracle Signer, and Central Gemini AI Agent. It detects metadata anomalies, lighting inconsistencies, timeline contradictions, and stock image fraud to generate an objective Fraud Risk Score from 0 to 100.

2. Code-Enforced On-Chain Escrow Payouts
Smart contracts deployed on Polygon Amoy hold claim funds in trustless escrow.
For Low Risk below 40, the smart contract instantly auto-executes payout directly to the claimant wallet in under 5 seconds.
For High Risk 40 or above, the smart contract locks escrow funds on-chain and flags the claim for transparent admin verification.

3. Transparent On-Chain Auditability
Every claim verdict, risk score, and transaction hash is recorded immutably on-chain on amoy.polygonscan.com, eliminating insurer-claimant trust deficits and providing 100 percent auditability.


Key Innovations and Real-World Impact

- 99.9 Percent Faster Settlement: Reduces claim processing time from 45 days down to 5 seconds.
- Zero-Trust Escrow: Payouts are enforced by open-source smart contract code ClaimEscrow.sol, not corporate promises.
- 90 Percent Reduction in Administrative Overhead: Eliminates first-level manual adjuster backlogs through automated multimodal AI filtering.
- Dual Demo Infrastructure: Built-in Instant Demo Sandbox Mode for zero-gas presentation testing alongside full Polygon Amoy Testnet live contract verification.


Who Can Use ClaimChain?

1. Micro-Insurance Platforms: Instant automated claims for flight delays, electronics damage, and small asset protection.
2. DeFi and Web3 Escrow Protocols: Automated decentralized oracle payouts for peer-to-peer insurance pools.
3. Traditional Enterprise Insurers: Pluggable AI risk oracle middleware to automate first-notice-of-loss FNOL triage.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into and Technical Solutions


1. Multimodal AI Schema Determinism and Structured Risk Output

Hurdle: Large Multimodal Models like Google Gemini 1.5 Flash often generate natural language conversational responses, which can introduce variance when automated smart contract systems require exact integer risk scores from 0 to 100.

Solution: We engineered strict JSON schema instructions and system prompts within the Express backend SDK. We implemented fallback sanitization parsers that validate output structure, extract explicit numerical scores, and format detected risk signals into deterministic arrays before passing telemetry to the oracle pipeline.


2. Off-Chain AI Oracle Integration with On-Chain Smart Contracts

Hurdle: Connecting off-chain AI risk evaluation with on-chain EVM smart contract execution on Polygon Amoy created security and synchronization challenges, particularly ensuring unauthorized accounts could not submit fake risk scores.

Solution: We implemented a cryptographic Oracle architecture using Ethers.js v6. The Solidity smart contract ClaimEscrow.sol enforces an access-controlled onlyOracle modifier. When Gemini computes a low risk score, the backend oracle signs the payload with its private key to execute automated claim releases securely.


3. Testnet RPC Rate-Limiting and Presentation Resilience

Hurdle: Public blockchain testnet RPC nodes on Polygon Amoy can experience block latency or rate limits during live demonstrations, which could cause presentation bottlenecks for hackathon judges.

Solution: We designed a dual-mode execution architecture. We built an Instant Demo Sandbox Mode that activates when CONTRACT_ADDRESS is set to demo_mode. This simulates smart contract state transitions locally without gas costs, while maintaining full compatibility with live Polygon Amoy contracts when deployed.


4. React SSR Hydration and CSS Variable Theme Synchronization

Hurdle: Developing a text-first developer UI in Next.js 14 with instant Dark and Light mode toggling caused Flash of Unstyled Content FOUC and React server-client hydration mismatches.

Solution: We built a client-side ThemeProvider context wrapper and tokenized all colors into CSS variables on root and html.light. This decouples component styling from hydration states, ensuring instantaneous 60fps theme switching across all inputs, cards, and modal HUDs.

**AI For Society**

ClaimChain uses Artificial Intelligence and blockchain technology to address a real-world societal and financial problem: slow, opaque, and potentially fraudulent insurance claim processing.

The platform allows users to submit an insurance claim along with an incident description and photo evidence. A multimodal AI verification pipeline analyzes both textual and visual information to identify inconsistencies, evaluate supporting evidence, and generate a fraud risk assessment.

Based on the AI-generated risk score, claims follow a hybrid decision workflow. Low-risk claims can proceed toward automated settlement through a smart-contract escrow system, while high-risk claims are flagged for human administrator review. This ensures that AI improves efficiency without completely replacing human judgment in sensitive financial decisions.

Blockchain technology adds transparency and accountability by recording important claim and settlement actions through an auditable on-chain workflow. Smart-contract escrow also helps ensure that funds are handled according to predefined rules rather than opaque manual processes.

ClaimChain demonstrates how AI can be applied to create a more efficient, transparent, and accessible insurance infrastructure. By combining multimodal AI analysis, human-in-the-loop decision-making, smart-contract automation, and blockchain auditability, the project aims to reduce claim-processing delays, improve fraud detection, and increase trust for both claimants and administrators.

> Finding the Right Care, Right When You Need It.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Visual Studio Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Visual%20Studio%20Code-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Embedded Javascript (EJS)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Embedded%20Javascript%20(EJS)-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

Building this project was much more than just connecting an AI model to a map. One of our biggest challenges was making the entire experience feel seamless for users while handling multiple moving parts behind the scenes.

The first hurdle was location accuracy. Different devices sometimes returned slightly different GPS coordinates, which occasionally resulted in inaccurate doctor recommendations. We solved this by improving our location handling logic, adding proper validation, and introducing fallback mechanisms to ensure users still received relevant nearby results.

Another challenge was combining AI with location-based search. The AI could understand a user's symptoms, but converting those symptoms into the correct medical specialty and then finding nearby doctors required careful prompt engineering and structured mapping. We refined our prompts and built a layer that translates natural language into meaningful healthcare categories before searching for nearby medical facilities.

We also faced issues with API response times and data synchronization. Since the application relies on multiple services, loading everything at once sometimes caused delays. We optimized API calls, improved loading states, and reduced unnecessary requests so the interface remained responsive even when external services were slower than expected.

During development, we encountered several frontend issues related to state management. After adding or updating data, the UI sometimes continued showing older information until the page was refreshed. We fixed this by improving our data-fetching strategy, updating application state immediately after successful operations, and ensuring the latest information was always displayed without requiring manual refreshes.

Another important challenge was creating an interface that remained simple during stressful situations. Healthcare applications are often used when people are anxious or in a hurry, so we continuously simplified the user journey, reduced unnecessary steps, improved button placement, and focused on making the most important actions accessible within a single screen.

Finally, integrating all the different components—AI assistance, location services, healthcare information, and a responsive frontend—while working within a hackathon timeline required constant testing, debugging, and collaboration. Every issue we solved helped us make the application more reliable and user-friendly.

These challenges taught us that building a useful healthcare solution isn't just about writing code—it's about creating an experience people can trust when they need it the most.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Imagine it's late at night. A family member suddenly falls sick. You don't know which doctor to visit, which hospital is open, or whether you should see a physician, cardiologist, or orthopedic specialist. In moments like these, people often waste valuable time searching Google, opening multiple apps, reading reviews, calling hospitals, and asking friends for suggestions. During a medical emergency, every minute matters.

This is the problem we wanted to solve.

Our AI Nearest Doctor Assistant is designed to make finding medical help as simple as having a conversation. Instead of searching through dozens of websites, users can simply describe what's happening—for example, "I have severe stomach pain" or "My child has a high fever"—and the AI helps them understand which type of doctor they should consult while instantly suggesting nearby hospitals, clinics, and specialists based on their location.

The goal isn't to replace doctors or provide medical diagnoses. The goal is to help people reach the right healthcare professional faster, especially when they are stressed, confused, or unfamiliar with the healthcare system.

This is useful not only during emergencies but also in everyday situations. Students living away from home, travelers in a new city, senior citizens who are not comfortable using multiple apps, and families looking for nearby specialists can all benefit from one intelligent assistant that brings everything together in one place.

Our platform reduces the time spent searching for healthcare by combining AI-powered symptom guidance with location-based doctor discovery. Instead of switching between Google Search, Maps, hospital websites, and review platforms, users receive relevant recommendations in one simple interface.

We also believe healthcare should be accessible and easy to understand. That's why the assistant communicates in a natural, conversational way rather than expecting users to know medical terminology. It guides them step by step, helping them make informed decisions without feeling overwhelmed.

At its core, this project is about one simple idea:

When someone needs medical help, finding the right doctor should take seconds—not precious minutes.

If our solution can help even one person reach the right healthcare professional faster during a critical moment, then we believe it has achieved its purpose.

> Securing Land Ownership through Smart Contracts.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Etherscan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Etherscan-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today, land records are still managed using paper documents and different government offices. This makes the process slow and sometimes confusing. Fake documents, duplicate registrations, and ownership disputes are common problems. Buying or selling land can take a long time because every document has to be checked manually.

Bhoomi helps solve these problems by creating a secure digital land registry using blockchain technology. Every verified land is given a unique digital ownership record, making it difficult to change or fake the information.

People can use **Bhoomi** to:
- Register land digitally.
- View verified ownership records.
- Check the history of a property before buying it.
- Transfer land ownership more securely.
- Store important land documents safely.
- Fractional deal of NFT land

Bhoomi makes the land registration process faster, more transparent, and easier for landowners, buyers, and government authorities. It reduces paperwork, helps prevent fraud, and builds trust by keeping ownership records secure and easy to verify.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was deploying and managing our smart contracts on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet. We encountered issues related to RPC configuration, account management, gas estimation, contract verification, and maintaining consistent contract addresses across deployments. Since every contract update required redeployment, keeping the frontend synchronized with the latest deployed addresses and ABIs was an ongoing challenge. We streamlined this process using Hardhat deployment scripts, environment-based configuration, and modular contract testing.

Another challenge was designing a secure land minting workflow. We needed to ensure that land NFTs could only be minted after verification by an authorized government authority, rather than allowing unrestricted minting. To solve this, we implemented role-based access control in our smart contracts, ensuring that only authorized authority accounts can approve land records and execute the NFT minting process.

We also had to carefully decide what data belonged on-chain and what should remain off-chain. Storing property documents directly on Ethereum was impractical due to storage costs, so we adopted a hybrid architecture where legal documents are stored on IPFS while only immutable document hashes and metadata references are recorded on-chain. This approach maintains data integrity while keeping the system scalable and cost-efficient.

These challenges gave us valuable experience in smart contract deployment, secure access control, decentralized storage, and building a practical Web3 application that balances transparency, security, scalability and clean system design.

### Rowbo

> Turn your business into a website in 30 seconds.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most small businesses are ran by non-technical people - and their entire online presence is on Airbnb, Instagram, or a Google listing and have no website of their own. They know they need one - it drives direct bookings (no platform fees), helps them rank in search, and makes them look legit - but actually getting one is a slog.

Normally you'd have to write code, push it to GitHub, deploy to Vercel, buy a domain from GoDaddy, and spend hours hunting for photos, writing copy, and laying out the page. Most homestay owners, cafés, and tradesmen are never going to do that - so they just don't, and leave money on the table.

Rowbo collapses that entire stack into a single conversation. We take a link from your existing social media profiles, and the agent scrapes your photos and details, builds you a real site, then lets you tweak it, and puts it live on your own custom domain - hosting subscription and domain both paid for - in the same platform. No code, no accounts, no juggling five providers.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest one was getting a Prava payment to actually complete after approval. We'd set up the mandate, the owner would approve with their passkey… and then nothing - the site never went live and no charge landed.

We were polling the session's payment-result to detect success, which is the right call for a one-off checkout. But for a mandate the session just sits at authorized forever - approval only authorises the mandate, it doesn't move any money. We only worked that out by pulling the Vercel logs (which surfaced a CHARGE_NOT_REPORTABLE error) and then hitting the Prava API directly to watch the session state stay stuck at "authorized" with no credentials issued.

The unlock was realising the money moves when you charge the mandate: POST /v1/mandates/{id}/charge issues the virtual-card credentials, and then you report the outcome to get visaConfirmation: SUCCESS. Prava's webhooks aren't live yet either, so we built the completion as a poll: after the card is sent, the agent watches for the freshly-approved mandate, charges it, reports it, and only then flips the site live - plus a tweak to handle the sandbox auto-settling the charge instantly. Once that clicked, the whole thing ran end to end: approve → charge → site live → confetti.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Rowbo is an AI agent initiating a real transaction on a user-approved, controlled Visa credential that buys domains and subscribes to hosting for websites. 

Prava mints a Visa virtual-card credential (token plus dynamic CVV) that the agent uses to complete the purchase on the owner's behalf. The result is verifiable rather than self-reported - a completed charge returning visaConfirmation: SUCCESS - which means our backend can continue with a domain purchase / deployment of their website.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Rowbo is a real working product that scrapes and generates users websites from their existing social media links. This is perfect for non-technical users like homestay owners, cafe's or even tradesmen - who want a site to portray their work, take direct bookings or even just boost their site rankings.

Now, we are getting ready to cold outreach to these businesses, with the subject line of "I built you a free website" - and they will just need to pay the £30/month hosting and any domain they choose to purchase. 

The underlying engine we built - multi-tenant site generation, real Stripe subscription billing at £30/mo, a self-serve editor, and automated custom-domain provisioning — is running today at rowbo.dev, and the hackathon layer adds the part that makes it a company worth scaling: an AI that can acquire and activate a customer entirely over text, collapsing "find lead → build site → close sale → go live" into a single conversation. 

We proved the whole path tonight end to end: a real owner (Chris) got a generated site, paid through Prava, and is now live on a genuine registered custom domain, chrishomestay.top (DNS provisioned, SSL issued, serving) - all from an iMessage.

**OpenAI**

The rowbo agent is built on OpenAI function-calling (gpt-4o). It runs the whole conversation and decides what to do at each step - when to scrape the listing from airbnb, build the site, send the preview, change the look, take the payment, and buy a domain - all through a set of tools we gave it.

It remembers the conversation, so a quick "yes" or "make it blue" always does the right thing without asking twice. From one inbound text, OpenAI takes the owner the whole way to a paid, live website - no forms, no dashboard, just the agent making the calls.

**iMessage Agent**

The rowbo agent lives entirely inside a iMessage thread over Linq - and allows users to build, deploy and buy domains all from a text. An owner texts us that they'd like a website, the agent asks for their Airbnb link, and from that single message it scrapes their listings, generates a real site, sends it back as a tappable rich-link card, takes edits by text, sells the subscription with a Prava checkout card, and puts the site live - all in Messages. 

We lean into Linq's native surface to make it feel alive: rich-link cards for the preview and the payment, tapback polls to choose a custom domain, confetti when the payment lands and fireworks when the domain goes live, typing indicators while it works, and HMAC-verified inbound webhooks driving the whole loop.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

Usually to create a website, you have to code, upload your code to github, deploy your codebase to vercel, buy a domain from GoDaddy, and spend hours alone finding the right photos, typing the right copy, and laying out your page how you like it. 

Imagine you could do all of that stack with one provider, through one iMessage conversation. That's how easy it is with rowbo.dev

### Voltshield AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/voltshield-b3d4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Akshay-coder17/VoltShield) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zWfLNasRdwE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> voltzz

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

VoltShield AI solves the multimillion-dollar problem of industrial "silent killers"—microsecond power anomalies like voltage sags and harmonic distortions that easily bypass traditional fuses but silently destroy the sensitive logic boards of automated factory machinery (such as CNC units or robotic lines). By replacing slow, reactive manual troubleshooting with a high-frequency, multi-agent digital twin, the system utilizes an autonomous Plan-Act-Reflect loop running at 60Hz to detect electrical anomalies, calculate the mathematical inverse wave, and simulate a corrective power injection to stabilize the grid before equipment damage occurs. Plant managers can visually track this stabilization through a fluid, cyberpunk-inspired, dark-mode HUD optimized to render real-time telemetry at 60FPS without system lag, while an integrated GenAI agent eliminates days of administrative overhead by instantly translating millisecond-level telemetry logs into formal, engineering-grade insurance and utility compliance reports.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was ensuring that the autonomous agent could effectively stabilize the power system after anomalies such as voltage sag, harmonic distortion, and phase imbalance were introduced. Initially, the correction algorithms often overcompensated, causing instability in the balanced waveform. To overcome this, we implemented a feedback-based reflection mechanism that continuously measured residual error and adjusted the agent’s response dynamically. Another challenge was maintaining smooth real-time communication between the simulator and dashboard through WebSockets. We optimized the data streaming process and telemetry structure to achieve reliable real-time performance and consistent visualization across the system.

**Gen AI&ML**

VoltShield aligns with the Generative AI and Machine Learning track by demonstrating an autonomous AI agent capable of perceiving, reasoning, acting, and learning within a simulated power-grid environment. The system continuously monitors three-phase electrical signals, analyzes disturbances such as voltage sag, harmonic distortion, and phase imbalance, and decides the most appropriate corrective action without human intervention.

The project follows an Agentic AI architecture consisting of Plan, Act, and Reflect stages. The agent analyzes incoming telemetry data, evaluates system health, applies corrective strategies, and learns from previous disturbances to improve future responses. This mimics the decision-making workflow of modern AI agents.

From a Machine Learning perspective, VoltShield provides a foundation for training anomaly detection and predictive maintenance models using data generated by its digital twin environment. The simulator can create labeled datasets representing different grid conditions, enabling the development of classifiers and forecasting models for real-world applications.

By combining digital twins, adaptive learning, autonomous reasoning, and future ML-driven anomaly detection, VoltShield demonstrates how AI can move beyond simple prediction to intelligent decision-making and self-correcting system management.
