![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Fast bowlers in India train without any biomechanical feedback — technique faults go undetected for months, silently limiting pace and building towards serious injuries, while professional analysis tools remain locked behind crore-level setups only IPL franchises can afford. BowlSmart solves this by turning a regular phone video into a full AI-powered biomechanics coaching report in under 60 seconds, giving every bowler their Form Score, current pace, maximum potential pace, Pace Efficiency, and a calculated Injury Risk score based on their actual movement patterns — so they can see rising risk before the body breaks down, not after. Coaches get objective data on each bowler's technique instead of relying on guesswork, and bowlers can use our Before vs After comparison to select any two sessions and watch both deliveries as animated skeletons side by side, with every angle and metric showing exactly what changed — turning invisible progress into something you can actually see and measure.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into

The biggest challenge was getting MediaPipe's pose estimation to work accurately on fast bowling videos — the extreme body positions in a delivery stride, like hyperextended trunk rotation and rapid arm acceleration, fall outside the typical poses the model was trained on, which caused keypoint confidence to drop and produced incorrect angle measurements. Getting the AI-generated report to give specific, biomechanically meaningful feedback instead of generic summaries was another major hurdle — early outputs were vague and unhelpful without the right structured input. Building the Before vs After comparison also proved tricky, since synchronising two skeleton animations frame by frame while keeping the UI smooth required careful state management. On top of that, connecting the Python pose estimation pipeline to the Next.js frontend without introducing long processing delays took significant iteration.

How I solved them

For pose accuracy, I switched to MediaPipe BlazePose Heavy at maximum model complexity and added a visibility confidence filter — only landmarks above 60% confidence are used in angle calculations, which eliminated most of the bad data. For the AI reports, instead of sending raw video or vague descriptions to the model, I built a structured JSON pipeline that feeds pre-computed biomechanical metrics — specific angles, phase timestamps, and scores — directly to Claude with an expert coaching system prompt, which forced specific, grounded outputs. The Before vs After synchronisation was solved by normalising both deliveries to the same frame count and using a shared playback state across both canvas renderers. For the pipeline latency, I moved video processing to an asynchronous queue so the frontend stays responsive while analysis runs in the background, and the user gets notified when the report is ready.

**Gemini**

BowlSmart is a natural fit for the MLH Gemini AI track because Gemini 1.5 Pro sits at the core of the product's most valuable layer — the intelligent analysis and coaching report generation. After our computer vision pipeline extracts structured biomechanical data from the bowler's video, we use the Gemini API to interpret those measurements, identify the highest-priority technique fault, explain the biomechanical mechanism behind it, and generate a specific, actionable coaching report that reads like it came from an expert fast bowling coach — output that no rule-based system could produce. Gemini's advanced reasoning capability is what transforms raw numbers like joint angles and phase timings into genuine coaching intelligence, and its ability to handle structured domain-specific context makes it uniquely suited to a technical field like cricket biomechanics where precision of language matters as much as precision of data.

**Open Innovation**

BowlSmart fits squarely in Open Innovation and AI because it takes two powerful AI technologies — computer vision pose estimation and large language model reasoning — and applies them to a real-world domain that has never had access to either, creating something genuinely new rather than incrementally improving an existing product. The core of the platform is an AI pipeline that uses MediaPipe's neural network to extract 33 biomechanical landmarks per frame from a phone video, computes joint angles and phase-specific metrics automatically, and then passes that structured data to Claude to generate coaching insights that would otherwise require a trained biomechanics expert to produce — making the AI not a feature layered on top, but the entire engine of the product. The innovation is not just technical but contextual: we are taking tools built for general human pose detection and adapting them to the highly specific, biomechanically extreme domain of fast bowling, solving for a gap in a 40-million-player ecosystem where professional-grade analysis has never been accessible below the elite level.

**The problem it solves**

> Every body deserves a comeback.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Rehabilitation is one of the most expensive, gatekept corners of healthcare, and almost none of it is built for non-standard bodies. A single supervised physiotherapy session costs money and travel that injured veterans, paralympic athletes, and people with disabilities cannot sustain week after week, for months. So they stop. Recovery stalls, compensating movements set in, and re-injury follows. AdaptAble turns a phone camera into a personal physiotherapist that never closes and never charges by the hour.

Professional-grade rehab, at home, for free. AdaptAble delivers a structured recovery plan and live form correction from one camera. The routine continues in a living room instead of a clinic, which is the only way long-term recovery actually happens.
Form correction in real time, with no therapist in the room. The system tracks body landmarks through every movement and fires instant cues like "lean left," "extend further," "hold." This is the exact safeguard people lose when they train alone, and losing it is what causes re-injury.
Exercises shaped to the body that is actually there. Plans target specific muscle groups and adjust for wheelchair users, amputees, and limited range of motion, rather than forcing a template designed for typical bodies onto people it was never built for.
Movement, nutrition, and wellbeing in one loop. Image-based food logging estimates calories and macros, diet plans respect allergies and goals, and wearable heart-rate data sets how hard each session should push. Recovery depends on all three at once, so the app treats them as one system.
Progress people can see. Slow gains are invisible day to day, and invisible progress is why people quit. Clear charts make a 12 percent range-of-motion improvement something a user can watch climb, alongside a peer forum and accessibility coaching that keep them showing up.
Wellbeing signals that route to real help. Mood trends flag sustained negative patterns over time and connect the user to crisis resources and trusted contacts, framed as support rather than diagnosis.

**Challenges we ran into**

Every pose model assumes an able body. MediaPipe's 33-landmark model expects two arms, two legs, and a standing torso. Point it at a wheelchair user or an amputee and it invents missing joints and miscounts reps, which is fatal for an accessibility app. We built a one-time calibration that maps each user's available landmarks at setup, then compute joint angles only from joints that exist, with confidence thresholds that discard phantom predictions. The app adapts to the user instead of the other way around.
Live feedback was too slow to be useful. Running pose estimation, angle math, and rendering on every frame dropped us below a usable framerate, and laggy correction is worse than no correction. We moved inference off the main thread, downscaled frames before the model, and changed feedback to fire on state changes ("rep complete," "form broke") rather than every frame. It went from a slideshow to real time.
Rep counting kept lying. Landmark jitter made the joint-angle signal flicker across our counting threshold and double-count reps. We smoothed the angle stream with a moving average and drove counting with a two-state machine plus hysteresis, so a rep only registers after a clean up-to-down transition. Counts became trustworthy.
Emotion detection cried wolf. A single-frame expression read is unreliable, and firing a wellbeing alert off one bad frame is actively harmful. We rebuilt it around trends across a window of sessions, required sustained signals before surfacing anything, and route to resources instead of making clinical claims. Safer, and far more credible.
Food calorie estimates drifted on real plates. Lighting and portion size vary wildly, so raw model output was unreliable. We let the user confirm or correct the detected item and portion, then pull nutrition from a structured database. A quick human check kept daily totals honest.
No one gives outside apps a real ordering API. Swiggy and Blinkit do not expose public ordering endpoints, so rather than fake a direct integration we ship deep links that open the app with a prefilled search or cart. We say so plainly in the demo, because an honest integration beats a fragile fake one.

**Gen AI&ML**

AdaptAble is an end-to-end ML system, and it uses generative AI exactly where generation earns its place: turning raw sensor signals into personalized, human guidance for bodies that no fixed template can serve.
The generative layer does the personalization. An LLM takes each user's profile (injury, available limbs and range of motion, target muscles, wearable baseline) and generates a structured, progressive rehab plan, then rewrites it week to week as pose and heart-rate data show what is working. The same model converts joint-angle and rep data into plain-language coaching and end-of-session summaries, proposes meals that respect allergies and the day's logged calories, and powers a coach that answers questions grounded in the user's own session history through retrieval (RAG), not generic advice.
The perception layer feeds it. Pose estimation extracts body landmarks per frame, a facial-expression classifier reads mood trends, a food-image classifier identifies meals, and signal processing handles rep counting.
Why it belongs here. The novel, hard problem is generative: producing safe, individualized rehab for bodies standard plans ignore, and grounding every word the model says in real sensor data so it personalizes without hallucinating. We constrain generation to a vetted exercise library and validate it against each user's calibrated range of motion, so the model never invents an unsafe movement. The CV gives it eyes. The GenAI gives it judgment.

> An Execution Intelligence for AI Agents

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Golang](https://img.shields.io/badge/Golang-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![BeautifulSoup](https://img.shields.io/badge/BeautifulSoup-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents today are powerful but inefficient. They repeat the same workflows, use expensive models even for simple tasks, and lack memory of past executions. This leads to higher costs, slower performance, and unpredictable results.

Athena solves this by giving agents visibility and memory. It tracks how agents behave, learns from past runs, and helps optimize future ones. This means agents can avoid repeating mistakes, choose better models for each task, and complete workflows faster and cheaper.

In short, Athena makes AI agents more efficient, predictable, and scalable by turning execution data into actionable intelligence.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was finding an AI agent setup that actually supports proper observability and then getting it to work cleanly with Athena. Capturing useful execution data across runs and making it consistent was harder than expected and took a lot of trial and error.

Another issue was working with multiple models. We had to figure out how to connect different LLMs and decide when to use each one.

We solved this by using Ollama and model SDKs to standardize integrations and adding simple routing logic to switch between models based on task complexity.

**Gemini**

Athena uses Gemini as a fast and reliable model for agent tasks like reasoning, search, and summarization. It tracks how Gemini performs across runs and learns from this data to improve future executions. This allows Athena to choose when Gemini is the best option and optimize for better performance and lower cost over time.

**Gen AI&ML**

Athena sits on top of Generative AI agents and turns their execution data into a continuous learning system.
We use embeddings and similarity search to learn from past runs, predict future outcomes and optimize cost, latency, and success rates.
Instead of just running LLMs, Athena makes them smarter over time.

**The problem it solves**

Metalytics AI addresses one of the biggest challenges in the metal industry: the generation of large amounts of industrial waste and the inefficient utilization of valuable resources. Across industries such as aluminium, iron, steel, titanium, and other metal processing sectors, waste streams often contain recoverable materials that remain unused, leading to environmental degradation, increased waste management costs, regulatory pressure, and significant economic losses.

Currently, sustainability assessment, circularity analysis, environmental impact evaluation, and financial impact calculations are performed using fragmented tools and manual processes. This makes it difficult for industries to understand the true environmental and economic impact of their operations.

Metalytics AI solves this problem by providing a unified platform that measures sustainability metrics, identifies recovery opportunities, calculates monetary losses and gains, compares metal recovery pathways, generates AI-powered recommendations, and visualizes environmental impact geographically. By helping industries recover more resources, reduce waste, improve operational efficiency, and support circular economy practices, Metalytics AI transforms industrial waste from a liability into a valuable asset.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was integrating multiple sustainability and circularity analysis modules into a single platform while ensuring that all metrics remained synchronized across different pages. Since the dashboard, circularity gap analysis, metal comparison, monetary impact analysis, and PDF reporting modules all depend on shared data, maintaining consistency across the application was challenging.

Another hurdle was designing meaningful sustainability metrics and visualizations that could present complex environmental and economic data in a simple and actionable way for users. We also faced challenges while integrating AI-generated insights and ensuring that recommendations were relevant to the calculated metrics.

To overcome these issues, we implemented a centralized data flow architecture, optimized backend calculations, and extensively tested data synchronization between modules. We refined our visualizations through multiple iterations and carefully engineered prompts and validation mechanisms to improve the quality and reliability of AI-generated insights. The result is a unified platform that provides accurate, real-time sustainability analysis and decision support.

**Gemini**

Gemini is a core component of Metalytics AI and is used across multiple parts of the platform. It powers AI-generated sustainability insights by analyzing environmental and circularity metrics and providing actionable recommendations. Gemini is also utilized for intelligent interpretation of sustainability data, report generation, and summarizing key findings for decision-makers. Additionally, it assists in processing and analyzing data collected from various sources, enabling users to better understand environmental impact, recovery opportunities, and economic potential. By integrating Gemini throughout the workflow, Metalytics AI transforms complex sustainability data into clear, actionable business intelligence.

**Sustainable Development**

Metalytics AI strongly aligns with the Sustainable Development domain by promoting resource efficiency, waste reduction, circular economy practices, and responsible industrial production. The platform addresses the challenge of industrial waste, particularly red mud generated during aluminium production, by helping industries identify valuable materials that can be recovered instead of discarded.

By measuring environmental indicators such as carbon footprint, energy consumption, water usage, and waste generation, Metalytics AI enables organizations to make data-driven sustainability decisions. Its circularity analysis encourages the reuse and recovery of resources, reducing the need for raw material extraction and minimizing environmental impact.

The platform also supports economic sustainability by identifying the monetary value hidden within industrial waste streams, helping industries transform waste from a liability into an opportunity. Through AI-powered insights and impact assessment tools, Metalytics AI contributes towards cleaner production systems, reduced environmental degradation, and a more sustainable and circular industrial ecosystem.

The project directly supports the goals of sustainable development by balancing environmental responsibility, economic growth, and efficient resource utilization for future generations.

> Discover, Track, and Never Miss an Opportunity.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## Problem Statement

Students and young professionals often miss valuable opportunities such as internships, hackathons, scholarships, jobs, and competitions because information is scattered across multiple platforms, websites, social media channels, and communities.

Finding relevant opportunities requires significant time and effort, while understanding eligibility criteria, tracking deadlines, and managing applications becomes overwhelming. Many users also face language barriers and struggle to stay updated on opportunities that match their interests and goals.

As a result, countless opportunities are missed not due to a lack of talent, but due to a lack of awareness, organization, and timely action.

OppTrax addresses this problem by providing a single AI-powered WhatsApp assistant that discovers relevant opportunities, summarizes important details, answers user questions, tracks progress, and sends timely reminders—ensuring users never miss opportunities that matter to them.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges Faced

* Integrating the WhatsApp business cloud API and designing a seamless conversational experience for users.
* Aggregating opportunities from multiple sources through web scraping and handling inconsistent data formats(time limit error returned by google and google bot blocking our request)
* Extracting structured information from posters, screenshots, and unstructured content using Sarvam OCR .
* Personalizing opportunity recommendations while maintaining relevance for user and reducing information overload.
* Implementing reliable tracking and reminder systems for deadlines, applications, and events.

**Gemini**

### Gemini Integration in OppTrax

OppTrax uses Gemini as its core AI engine to understand user needs, discover relevant opportunities, and provide intelligent assistance throughout the opportunity journey.

* **AI-Powered User Onboarding:** Analyzes user goals, skills, interests, preferences, and career aspirations to build a personalized opportunity profile.
* **Personalized Opportunity Discovery:** Generates intelligent search queries and matches users with relevant internships, jobs, hackathons, scholarships, and competitions.
* **Opportunity Summarization:** Converts lengthy opportunity descriptions into concise summaries containing eligibility, deadlines, rewards, location, and key requirements.
* **Opportunity Q&A Assistant:** Answers user questions such as eligibility, deadlines, application requirements, remote availability, and other opportunity-specific queries.
* **Context-Aware Conversations:** Maintains conversational context to provide personalized recommendations and guidance based on the user's profile and previous interactions.
* **Intelligent Information Extraction:** Processes content from links, documents, posters, and screenshots to identify and structure important opportunity details.

By leveraging Gemini, OppTrax transforms raw opportunity data into actionable insights, helping users discover, understand, and act on the most relevant opportunities through a simple WhatsApp-based experience.

**MongoDB**

### MongoDB Integration in OppTrax

OppTrax uses MongoDB as its primary database to store and manage user profiles, opportunities, tracking data, and interaction history.

* **User Profile Management:** Stores onboarding information such as goals, skills, interests, preferred location, language, and user preferences.
* **Opportunity Storage:** Maintains a centralized repository of internships, jobs, hackathons, scholarships, and other opportunities discovered by the platform.
* **Opportunity Tracking:** Stores user-specific tracking statuses such as Interested, Applied, Rejected, and Completed.
* **Reminder Management:** Maintains application deadlines, interview schedules, and event dates to enable timely WhatsApp reminders.
* **Conversation & Activity History:** Preserves user interactions and feedback to provide personalized recommendations and improve future opportunity matching.

**Sarvam.ai**

OppTrax is a multilingual, AI-powered WhatsApp assistant that helps users discover, understand, track, and manage opportunities such as internships, jobs, hackathons, scholarships, fellowships, and competitions.

After a simple AI onboarding process, OppTrax learns a user's goals, skills, interests, and preferences to deliver highly personalized opportunities. Unlike traditional opportunity portals that only list opportunities, OppTrax acts as an AI Opportunity Copilot, supporting users from discovery to application and completion.

> Digital Estate Manager That Activate After You Die

**The problem it solves**

What happens to your digital life when you're no longer here? LastLogin helps families securely access important digital assets, financial information, and final messages without the confusion of lost passwords or lengthy legal processes. By combining AI and blockchain, it makes digital inheritance simple, transparent, and secure.

**Challenges we ran into**

Making a live death-trigger land on-chain, on cue, was our biggest demo hurdle. Solana Devnet faucets are heavily rate-limited, so just keeping our deployer wallet funded with test-SOL for repeated runs was a chore. Even worse, the critical state switch from Confirmed to Active needed to happen instantly during the live demo, where a lagging RPC node could stall the whole presentation.

We solved this by making the frontend update instantly the exact moment the wallet returns a successful transaction signature hash. If the node lags, the UI doesn't freeze it falls back gracefully, ensuring the live Solana Explorer link serves as our proof, never our bottleneck.

**Gemini**

we have used it as a core AI engine , which is uses for scanning death certificates-AI Vision and gemini flash lite for fast and accurate responses.

**ElevenLabs**

ElevenLabs — the person's actual voice, kept alive. This is the emotional core of LastLogin: from a single 60-second recording, ElevenLabs clones a user's voice so their final words can be heard, not just read.

Why: a goodbye in your mother's real voice hits differently than text on a screen. That's the whole product.

Where we use it:

Final messages — the user writes a note, Sarvam translates it to the family's language, and ElevenLabs speaks it back in the user's own cloned voice (legacyMessage.js). ← the centerpiece.
The AI clone companion — guardians can talk with a safety-railed persona of the departed, who replies aloud in that same voice (clone.js).
Voice capture — the cloning happens right on the Messages page from one short reading (elevenlabs.js).

**MongoDB**

we have used it solely to store out user database which are encrypted using DEK  algorithm.

**Sarvam.ai**

When a person passes away, we don't just want to pass down their files; we want to preserve their voice, their language, and their essence. To do this, our platform embraces Open Innovation by integrating external, state-of-the-art AI models from Sarvam AI directly into our ecosystem. Instead of wasting time building expensive language tools from scratch, we plug into Sarvam’s public infrastructure to provide seamless Speech-to-Text (STT) and real-time translation. This allows a grieving loved one to speak naturally in their native language and have a real-time, translated voice chat with an AI persona modeled after the deceased person's memories. By merging public blockchain security with open AI innovation, we are transforming a cold digital vault into a living, breathing legacy.

**Open Innovation**

"When a person passes away, their entire life story—from financial accounts to priceless digital memories and photos is often permanently locked behind corporate silos. Our platform changes this through Open Innovation by breaking down these closed walls. Instead of forcing grieving families to fight tech monopolies for access passwords, we built an open, decentralized bridge directly into the public infrastructure of the Solana Blockchain. When a user passes, our backend securely anchors their verified proof-of-death on-chain. This allows their designated Guardian to simply connect a Phantom Wallet and securely unlock their inheritance completely for free. By combining public blockchain technology with human estate planning, we ensure a person's digital accounts and memories are seamlessly passed down to the next generation without a single point of failure

**BlockChain & Web3**

Our platform completely eliminates hackable passwords by using Solana and the Phantom Wallet to protect sensitive recovery keys. When a verified guardian needs to access the vault, they simply connect their wallet and approve a secure sign-in prompt. Because this identity check uses off-chain cryptography, it is 100% free and costs zero gas fees. The exact second the signature is approved, the system confirms their identity and instantly unblurs the secret seed phrases on the screen. This ensures that the keys can never be exposed unless the real guardian approves it with their own wallet

### Planet Prompt
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/dum-biriyani-f1b8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/PratyushPanda2005/planet-prompt) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://planet-prompt-tau.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/gcY536p71Fg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Where every prompt meets the biosphere.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prism.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prism.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI usage has a real environmental cost — every query consumes electricity (carbon), cooling water, and grid-related land — but that cost is **completely invisible** to the people generating it. Developers see token counts and dollar costs in their API dashboards, but nothing about carbon, water, or land footprint. So there's no feedback loop, no accountability, and no incentive to write leaner prompts.

This is becoming a real business problem too: regulations like CSRD (EU) and emerging SEC climate disclosure rules are pushing companies to report Scope 3 emissions — and AI/cloud usage increasingly falls under that umbrella. Most companies have **no idea what their AI usage actually costs the planet**, let alone a way to break it down per team or per query.

## What People Can Use It For

**Individual developers** get visibility into the hidden cost of their experimentation — every prompt they test, every model they call, translated into concrete units (grams of CO₂, ml of water, cm² of land) instead of abstract token counts.

**The Prompt Advisor** turns "I should probably write a tighter prompt" into an automated, one-click action — paste a prompt, get a leaner rewrite, and see exactly how many tokens (and how much carbon/water/land) you saved, side by side.

**Teams and organizations** (with the org features) get an aggregated view across all members — a leaderboard of who's using the most resources, org-wide totals, and trends over time — without anyone having to manually collect numbers from individual dashboards.

**Sustainability/ESG teams** get auto-generated monthly narrative reports that summarize the org's AI footprint in plain language with an actionable tip — exactly the kind of content that otherwise has to be written by hand for sustainability reports.

## How It Makes Things Easier / Safer

- **Makes the invisible visible** — the same way cost dashboards made cloud spend visible and changed engineering behavior, PlanetPrompt does that for environmental impact.
- **Turns abstract numbers into intuition** — "0.3g of CO₂" means nothing to most people; "equivalent to driving an EV 25 meters" or "X smartphone charges" does.
- **Removes manual reporting work** — instead of someone compiling usage stats for an ESG report once a quarter, the data and narrative are generated automatically.
- **Builds in optimization, not just monitoring** — most footprint trackers just show you a number; the Advisor actively helps you reduce it.
- **De-risks future compliance** — orgs that start tracking this now won't be caught scrambling when AI-related emissions reporting becomes a regulatory requirement.

If it's useful, I can tighten this further or adjust the framing depending on whether this is going into a hackathon submission, a README, or a pitch deck — they each tend to want slightly different emphasis (technical vs. business vs. narrative).

**Challenges we ran into**

## Building on Next.js 16 with stale assumptions

The project runs on Next.js 16, which has enough breaking changes from earlier versions that a lot of standard conventions don't apply anymore — including the AI tooling we used to scaffold parts of the app, whose training data predates these changes. The most visible example: middleware now lives in `proxy.ts` instead of `middleware.ts`, with a different matcher convention for distinguishing static assets from API routes. We hit a few dead ends where generated code assumed the old conventions and silently didn't run (auth wasn't being enforced on protected routes). The fix was to explicitly point any AI-assisted changes at the actual docs shipped in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` rather than relying on memorized APIs, and to add a project note (`AGENTS.md`) flagging this so it gets re-checked on every change.

## The "optimizer" sometimes made things worse

Early on, the Prompt Advisor's optimization step (heuristic rewriting + Gemini fallback) would occasionally return a prompt that was the *same length or longer* than the original — either because the heuristic regex passes didn't actually trim much, or because the LLM rewrite added explanatory framing instead of compressing. This broke the UI in an ugly way: the "Resource Savings" badge would show a **negative percentage**, which looks like the tool is actively making things worse — exactly the opposite of the product's pitch.

We added a safety net in `/api/optimize`: after generating the optimized version, we compare token counts. If the optimized count isn't strictly lower than the original (or the text is identical), we short-circuit and return an "already optimized" response instead — same code path used when the input was already lean. This turned a confusing negative number into a positive, encouraging message ("Great prompt, already optimized!"), which is both more honest and a better UX.

## Avoiding the irony of an inefficient "efficiency tool"

A sustainability tool that calls a full LLM to rewrite *every* prompt — even ones that are already concise — would be burning extra tokens (and therefore extra carbon/water) just to tell someone their prompt is fine. That felt like it undermined the whole premise.

To solve this, we added a lightweight gatekeeper (`gatekeeper/gatekeeper.ts`) that runs a zero-shot classifier (Hugging Face's `facebook/bart-large-mnli`) against the prompt first, with three labels: "needs no optimization," "needs some optimization," and "needs significant optimization." Only prompts classified as needing real optimization get sent to the heavier Gemini rewrite step — anything already lean returns early without the extra API call. It's a small architectural detail, but it kept the tool's own footprint consistent with what it's trying to encourage.

**Sarvam.ai**

****Sarvam AI plays two distinct roles in PlanetPrompt, and both of them sit at the heart of the product's most interactive features.
The first role is prompt optimization, handled in app/api/optimize/route.ts. When a user pastes a prompt into the Prompt Advisor and clicks "Analyze & Optimize," the backend sends that prompt to Sarvam's sarvam-30b model with a very specific system instruction: rewrite the prompt to be leaner and more token-efficient while preserving all the original meaning, and output only the rewritten text with no explanations or conversational fluff. The model's response is then compared against the original — token counts are estimated for both, footprint metrics are calculated using the selected model's carbon, water, and land coefficients, and the savings percentage is computed. This means Sarvam is doing the actual semantic compression work, understanding what a prompt is trying to say and finding a shorter way to say it, which is fundamentally harder than a find-and-replace approach and why the heuristic fallback exists for when the API isn't available.
The second role is running the optimized prompt to show the user a real AI response, handled in app/api/run-prompt/route.ts. After the advisor shows the before-and-after comparison, users can click "Run Optimised" or "Run Unoptimised" to actually execute either version and see the output side by side. Both of these calls go to Sarvam's chat completions endpoint with the sarvam-30b model, and the response gets rendered directly in the advisor panel. This makes the comparison concrete — you're not just told that the optimized prompt is shorter, you can verify that it produces an equivalent answer, which is the real proof that compression didn't sacrifice quality.
What makes this architecture interesting is that Sarvam is being used as both the tool that reduces AI usage and the engine that demonstrates the result of that reduction, which fits neatly into PlanetPrompt's broader message that being environmentally efficient and being technically capable aren't in conflict.

**Sustainable Development**

## Sustainable Development, Concretely

"Sustainable development" usually means meeting present needs (here, using AI tools productively) without compromising future resources (energy, water, land used by data centers) — and PlanetPrompt operationalizes that at the layer where the decision actually happens: the moment someone is about to send a prompt.

### Aligns with established sustainability frameworks

- **SDG 13 (Climate Action)** — direct carbon accounting for AI workloads, the fastest-growing source of compute-driven emissions.
- **SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)** — encourages "consuming" AI compute more efficiently rather than wastefully, the same logic as reducing food waste or energy waste.
- **SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure)** — pushes toward sustainable infrastructure choices by surfacing *which models/regions* are more resource-intensive, so teams can factor that into architecture decisions.

### Measurement enables behavior change

A core principle of sustainable development is that **what gets measured gets managed**. Right now, AI usage is one of the only major categories of corporate resource consumption with *zero* visibility — teams know their cloud spend down to the cent, but have no equivalent for carbon/water/land from AI. PlanetPrompt closes that gap at the individual-decision level, the same way a smart electricity meter changes household behavior simply by making consumption visible in real time.

### Built to scale from individual to systemic impact

Sustainable development isn't just personal virtue — it's about **systems**. A single developer trimming a prompt saves a negligible amount. But:

- The **org/leaderboard features** turn individual habits into measurable organizational metrics, which is what actually drives policy (e.g., "our team must reduce average tokens-per-query by 10% this quarter").
- The **monthly AI-generated reports** feed directly into ESG/CSRD-style sustainability reporting, which is increasingly *required*, not optional — so the tool helps organizations meet emerging regulatory sustainability obligations rather than just "feel good" about it.

### The tool practices what it preaches

This is the part we're proudest of: most sustainability tools have a footprint problem of their own (dashboards that poll constantly, AI features that call expensive models for trivial tasks). The **gatekeeper classifier** ensures the optimizer itself doesn't burn extra carbon/water optimizing prompts that don't need it — so the tool's own resource consumption stays proportional to the value it delivers. That's a small-scale example of a bigger sustainable-development idea: efficiency has to be designed into the system itself, not bolted on as an afterthought.

### The bigger picture

AI adoption is accelerating faster than the infrastructure to power it sustainably. Tools like PlanetPrompt don't solve the energy problem on their own — but they shift the *incentive structure* so that "use AI efficiently" becomes a visible, trackable, and rewarded behavior, for individuals and for the organizations that will increasingly be held accountable for it.

### Sanket
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sanket-7c52) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/cyberkunju/sanket) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.sanket.versifine.com) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/WtPGfqiudTg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Check before you trust.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Nginx](https://img.shields.io/badge/Nginx-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Microsoft Azure](https://img.shields.io/badge/Microsoft%20Azure-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The problem it solves

Digital fraud often starts with something small: a message, a link, a UPI ID, a call, or a screenshot that looks real enough to trust. Most people do not have a quick way to check it before they reply, pay, or share personal information.

**Sanket gives people a simple safety step before taking action.**

Users can send suspicious messages, links, phone numbers, UPI IDs, screenshots, or voice notes on WhatsApp and get a clear risk check with practical next steps. It helps them understand whether something looks like a scam, what warning signs were found, and what they should do next.

It can be used to:

* Check suspicious payment requests, job offers, delivery/KYC messages, refund claims, and investment promises.
* Verify links, UPI IDs, phone numbers, and screenshots before trusting them.
* Get help in Indian languages through text or voice.
* Understand what to do after a scam, including reporting and recovery steps.
* Build community memory so repeated scam identifiers can be flagged faster for others.

Sanket makes scam checking easier by bringing fraud detection, explanation, and recovery guidance into the place where many scams already happen: WhatsApp.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I ran into

One of the biggest challenges was making Sanket reliable in messy real-world situations, not just clean demo inputs. Scam reports can come as screenshots, forwarded WhatsApp messages, voice notes, broken links, UPI IDs, phone numbers, or code-mixed Indian languages. The same scam can also look different depending on who reports it.

A major hurdle was **extracting scam identifiers accurately**. Early versions depended too much on the model output, which sometimes missed UPI IDs, mixed up phone numbers, or treated official helplines as suspicious. I fixed this by adding deterministic cleanup after the AI step: regex-based extraction, identifier normalization, masking, whitelisting for official contacts, and separate handling for UPI IDs, URLs, phone numbers, Telegram handles, and bank details.

Another challenge was **multilingual voice and text support**. Users do not always write in one language, and many messages are romanized, like Hindi or Malayalam typed in English letters. Voice notes added another layer because audio formats from WhatsApp are not always consistent. I handled this by using Sarvam for speech-to-text, translation, language detection, and text-to-speech, with fallbacks so the bot can still respond even if one service fails.

The **agentic call flow** was one of the hardest parts. Sanket is not only a text bot; it also supports voice interaction through an agentic calling setup. The challenge was making sure the voice agent did not confidently act on a misheard UPI ID, phone number, or link. To solve this, I added a read-back confirmation step: the agent repeats the detected identifier and asks the user to confirm before giving a verdict. I also connected the call flow back into the main fraud-checking system so a voice conversation can still use the same scam memory, risk checks, and recovery guidance as WhatsApp chat.

Webhook reliability was another important issue. WhatsApp requires fast responses, but scam analysis can take time because it may involve media download, OCR/STT, database lookup, web search, VirusTotal, Reddit signals, and final reasoning. I solved this by acknowledging the webhook quickly, then processing the message asynchronously and sending the final result back to the user once the analysis is complete.

I also had to deal with **external service failures and cost control**. The system depends on multiple APIs, and any one of them can be unavailable or rate-limited. I added graceful degradation: if one provider is missing or fails, Sanket falls back to another method, a simpler heuristic, or a safer partial response instead of breaking completely. I also added rate limits around the public demo endpoint to reduce abuse.

Another hurdle was building a useful **community memory** without exposing sensitive data. Sanket needs to remember repeated scam identifiers, but users may send personal information inside screenshots or messages. I handled this by normalizing and masking identifiers for public display, hashing reporters, and separating fraud signals from raw user details. This made the system safer while still allowing repeated scammers to be flagged faster.

The final challenge was keeping the architecture maintainable. The live bot, migration orchestrator, Python workers, fraud memory, and voice system all had overlapping responsibilities. I treated the live WhatsApp bot as the production path and kept the newer orchestrator/worker setup as a migration layer until it can fully match the live features. This helped avoid breaking the working product while still moving toward a cleaner long-term architecture.

**ElevenLabs**

Sanket uses ElevenLabs to make fraud checking available through natural voice conversations, not only text.

The ElevenLabs agent lets users call and speak to Sanket when typing is difficult, slow, or unsafe in the moment. A user can explain a suspicious call, message, UPI ID, link, or payment request in their own words, and the voice agent guides them through the check.

The key part is safety. The agent does not blindly trust what it hears. When it detects a sensitive identifier like a phone number, UPI ID, or link, it reads it back and asks the user to confirm before running the final scam check. This reduces errors from misheard audio and makes the flow more reliable for real fraud situations.

The voice agent connects back to the same Sanket fraud-intelligence pipeline used on WhatsApp, including scam-memory lookup, risk analysis, and recovery guidance. This makes ElevenLabs a practical access layer for the project: users can verify scams, understand risk, and get next steps through a phone-like conversation.

**MongoDB**

Sanket uses MongoDB as the main memory and intelligence layer behind the fraud-checking system.

Every report submitted through WhatsApp is stored with normalized scam identifiers such as UPI IDs, phone numbers, links, bank details, Telegram handles, and fraud patterns. MongoDB helps Sanket quickly check whether the same identifier has been reported before, how many people reported it, what type of scam it was linked to, and how confident the system should be.

MongoDB also supports the community memory of the project. Instead of treating every scam report as a new case, Sanket can connect repeated reports and detect recurring fraud campaigns. This makes the system more useful over time as more people use it.

The project also uses MongoDB Atlas Vector Search for similarity matching. Scam messages are converted into embeddings, allowing Sanket to find related scams even when the wording, language, or format is different. This is important because fraudsters often change small details while keeping the same underlying pattern.

Overall, MongoDB is used for storing reports, managing scammer intelligence, tracking conversations, supporting fast lookups, and powering the fraud-memory system that makes Sanket improve with real-world usage.

**Sarvam.ai**

Sanket fits the **Sarvam.ai** track because Sarvam is used to make the fraud-checking experience truly accessible for Indian users across language, speech, and text.

Many scam victims do not describe fraud in clean English. They may send a WhatsApp voice note, a screenshot, a forwarded message, or a code-mixed sentence like Hindi, Malayalam, Tamil, or Kannada written in English letters. Sarvam helps Sanket handle this naturally.

The project uses Sarvam for **speech-to-text**, **speech translation**, **text translation**, **language identification**, and **text-to-speech**. When a user sends a voice note, Sanket can transcribe it, detect the language, translate it for scam analysis, and then reply back in the user’s language. This makes the system useful for people who are more comfortable speaking than typing.

Sarvam also helps Sanket support Indian-language scam reports instead of forcing users into English. This is important because many real scams happen through regional-language calls, WhatsApp messages, delivery alerts, KYC warnings, job offers, loan traps, and UPI payment requests.

By combining Sarvam’s language and voice capabilities with Sanket’s fraud-intelligence pipeline, the project makes scam checking easier, faster, and more inclusive for real users in India. It allows people to report and understand suspicious messages, links, UPI IDs, phone numbers, screenshots, and voice notes in the language they actually use.

**Gen AI&ML**

Sanket fits the **Gen AI & ML** track because it uses AI as the core decision layer, not just as a chat interface.

The system analyzes suspicious WhatsApp messages, screenshots, links, UPI IDs, phone numbers, and voice notes to identify scam risk and explain why something may be unsafe. It combines LLM-based reasoning with deterministic entity extraction, multilingual speech-to-text, translation, text-to-speech, web intelligence, VirusTotal checks, and fraud-memory search.

A key part of the project is its AI-powered scam memory. Reports are converted into embeddings so Sanket can find similar scam patterns even when the wording, language, or format is different. This helps detect repeated fraud campaigns instead of treating every report as isolated.

The project also includes an agentic call flow, where users can speak to the assistant. The voice agent can understand the user, extract suspicious identifiers, confirm them through read-back, and then run the same fraud-checking pipeline used by the WhatsApp bot. This makes scam checking accessible to people who may not be comfortable typing or reading long responses.

Overall, Sanket uses Gen AI and ML to make fraud detection faster, multilingual, explainable, and practical for real-world users.

### Orion

> Autonomous QA & GitHub Self-Healing Platform

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Here's the submission answer:

The Problem Orion Solves
Every engineering team reviews pull requests for logic, architecture, and bugs. Nobody reviews them for quality.
Not because they don't care — because it's slow, manual, and always someone else's problem. So broken experiences ship to production every day:

🐌 Pages with 4-second load times that kill conversions
♿ Images without alt text that screen readers can't parse
🔗 Broken links that 404 silently
🔍 Missing meta descriptions that tank SEO rankings
🔒 Missing security headers that leave users exposed

You find out three days later. Sometimes three weeks.

What Orion Does
Orion is an autonomous QA platform that integrates directly into your GitHub workflow. The moment a PR is opened, Orion:

Crawls your staging URL using four specialized AI agents — Discovery, Performance, Hygiene, and Scoring
Posts a score (0–100) as a GitHub status check on the PR — blocking merges below your threshold
Drops a full report in the PR comments — every finding, its severity, and a suggested fix
Leaves inline review comments on the exact files that caused the issues

No CI yaml. No configuration files. No new tools to learn. Just install the GitHub App and every PR gets automatically audited.

Who It's For
UserHow They Use OrionFrontend developersCatch performance regressions before mergeSolo foundersGet QA coverage without hiring a QA engineerOpen source maintainersEnforce quality standards on every contributionStartup engineering teamsShip fast without sacrificing quality

What Makes It Different
Most tools are passive — they sit in a separate dashboard, generate reports nobody reads, and tell you about problems that already shipped.
Orion is active — it lives inside the PR, speaks the language developers already use, and catches issues at the only moment that matters: before the merge.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
1. The Signature Verification Bug That Broke Everything
The single most painful bug was GitHub webhook signature verification silently failing on every request.
The webhook handler was verifying signatures like this:
typescripthmac.update(JSON.stringify(req.body)).digest("hex")
This looks correct but is completely wrong. GitHub signs the raw request bytes — the exact bytes it sent over the wire. But Express was parsing the body into a JavaScript object first, and JSON.stringify() of that object doesn't match the original bytes — key ordering, whitespace, and encoding all differ.
The result: every single webhook returned 401. Silently. No error in GitHub's delivery logs except a failed response.
The fix was to mount the webhook route with express.raw() before the global express.json() middleware, and sign the raw Buffer directly:
typescript// BEFORE (broken)
app.use(express.json()) // parses body globally
app.use("/api/v1/github/webhook", webhookRoutes)

// AFTER (fixed)
app.use("/api/v1/github/webhook", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), webhookRoutes)
app.use(express.json()) // everything else
The order of middleware in Express matters more than almost anything else — and this one cost hours.

2. ngrok Forwarding to the Wrong App
The monorepo runs multiple apps simultaneously via Turborepo — the Next.js frontend on port 3000 and the Express API on port 4000. ngrok was tunneling to port 4000, but GitHub's webhook responses were returning Next.js HTML pages.
The cause: ngrok on Windows sometimes can't reach 0.0.0.0:4000 via localhost. The fix was explicitly binding to 127.0.0.1:
bash# Broken
ngrok http --domain=xxx.ngrok-free.dev 4000

# Fixed
ngrok http 127.0.0.1:4000 --domain=xxx.ngrok-free.dev
One flag. Two hours lost.

3. Route Path Mismatch — The Silent 404
The GitHub App webhook URL was set to /api/v1/github/webhook. The Express router was mounted at /api/v1/webhooks. Inside that router, the route was router.post("/github", handler).
The actual path the handler was listening on: /api/v1/webhooks/github.

The path GitHub was posting to: /api/v1/github/webhook.
GitHub was getting 404s but still returning 200 to GitHub (Express's default HTML 404 has a 200 status in some proxy configurations), so the delivery logs showed green checkmarks while nothing actually worked.
The fix was aligning the mount path in app.ts with the webhook URL, and changing the router's internal route from /github to /:
typescriptrouter.post("/", handleGithubWebhook) // not "/github"

4. Repo Not Registered — The Silent Skip
Even after the webhook was working perfectly, the Orion QA Agent check never appeared on PRs. The server logs showed:
[webhook] no staging URL for Mohfazam/FOODZY — skipping run
The installation webhook that should have auto-registered the repo fired before the server was correctly set up, so the repo was never saved to the database. With no staging URL in the DB, the handler silently returned 200 and did nothing.
The fix was manually registering the repo via the API with the correct installationId, owner, repo, and stagingUrl — and then redelivering the pull_request webhook from GitHub's delivery logs.

The Pattern
Every single one of these bugs had the same underlying theme: silent failures. No crash, no error, just a 200 response that masked the real problem. The lesson — always log the event name and action at the very top of a webhook handler, before any logic runs, so you can see exactly what's being received.

**Gemini**

How We Used Gemini
Orion uses the Gemini API as the intelligence layer powering its AI agents.
After crawling the target URL, each page's content, structure, and metadata is passed to Gemini for deep analysis. Gemini is responsible for:

Identifying issues — detecting missing alt text, broken links, SEO gaps, security header violations, and performance anti-patterns from the raw page data
Severity classification — determining whether each finding is critical, high, medium, or low based on its real-world impact
Generating fix suggestions — producing human-readable, actionable fix recommendations for each finding that get posted directly into the GitHub PR as inline review comments
Root cause analysis — synthesizing all findings into a single root cause summary that explains the underlying pattern behind the issues

Rather than using hardcoded rules, Gemini lets Orion understand context — it can tell the difference between an image that's decorative and one that genuinely needs alt text, or identify when a performance issue is structural vs incidental.
Every finding you see in the PR comment and on the dashboard — the title, the detail, the suggested fix — is Gemini's output, formatted and delivered automatically into your GitHub workflow.

**The problem it solves**

Millions of deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals face communication challenges every day because most people do not understand sign language. Existing solutions are often limited, support only one-way communication, or lack regional sign language support.

SignBridge bridges this gap by enabling seamless, real-time communication between sign language users and hearing individuals through instant translation of signs into text and speech, and speech/text into animated sign language.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges:
	•	Finding high-quality, open-source datasets for multiple sign languages (ASL, ISL, and WSL).
	•	Achieving accurate real-time hand gesture recognition across varying lighting conditions and camera angles.
	•	Creating a smooth two-way communication flow with minimal latency.
	•	Designing an animated avatar capable of representing sign language naturally.

How We Overcame Them:
	•	Combined and curated multiple open-source sign language datasets.
	•	Leveraged MediaPipe hand tracking and optimized machine learning models for robust gesture detection.
	•	Implemented efficient processing pipelines to reduce translation delays.
	•	Developed an avatar-based signing system that converts text and speech into understandable sign animations.

### PyBitrum
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/pybitrum-b9f8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Srizdebnath/PyBitrum) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/pybitrum/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeStorm%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codestorm-week1-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Smart Contracts For Agents

![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vyper](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vyper-333333?style=flat-square) ![Monaco Editor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Monaco%20Editor-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Werkzeug](https://img.shields.io/badge/Werkzeug-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zustand](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zustand-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zod](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zod-333333?style=flat-square) ![Arbitrum Sepolia](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arbitrum%20Sepolia-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

PyBitrum solves the critical challenge of **making smart contract development accessible to Python developers** while ensuring production-grade security and autonomy. Here's what it enables:

### **1. Democratizing Smart Contract Development**
- **Write Once, Deploy Everywhere**: Developers can write smart contracts in Python (a language 10M+ developers know) and simultaneously compile to both **Solidity and Vyper**, eliminating the steep learning curve of specialized smart contract languages.
- **Lower Barrier to Entry**: Python's readability and familiar syntax reduce cognitive overhead compared to learning Solidity from scratch.

### **2. Autonomous Agent Deployment**
- **24/7 Agent Execution**: PyBitrum enables developers to deploy `AgentWallet` entities - autonomous agents with their own EOAs (Externally Owned Accounts), private keys, and on-chain identities that execute missions without human intervention.
- **Mission Board Economy**: Post bounties in ETH, let agents claim, execute, and settle transactions autonomously - creating a decentralized task execution marketplace.
- **Swarm Orchestration**: Coordinate fleets of agents using concurrent Python threads with shared state broadcasting, enabling complex multi-agent scenarios like market making, arbitrage, and liquidation bots.

### **3. Industrial-Grade Safety & Security**
- **Compile-Time Security Guardrails**: 14 dangerous patterns (exec, eval, os, subprocess, sockets, etc.) are blocked at the security check stage - before any code transformation.
- **Dual-Language Validation**: Code is validated for both Vyper and Solidity compatibility, ensuring maximum deployment flexibility and catching language-specific bugs early.
- **Automatic Reentrancy Protection**: The `@agent_action` decorator auto-injects `@nonreentrant` and `msg.sender` verification, preventing common attack vectors without manual intervention.

### **4. Cloud-Native Development Experience**
- **Browser-Based IDE**: The Playground provides a Monaco Editor with syntax highlighting, real-time compilation feedback, GitHub OAuth, and one-click MetaMask deployment.
- **Instant Feedback Loop**: Developers see compilation errors/warnings and generated Solidity/Vyper code in real-time, accelerating iteration.
- **Full-Stack Tooling**: Includes a Mission Board UI for agent interaction, comprehensive documentation hub, and a pip-installable SDK for local development.

### **5. Reduces Smart Contract Bugs & Costs**
- **AST-Based Transformation**: Uses Abstract Syntax Trees to intelligently map Python constructs to EVM semantics, handling edge cases like memory layout and type conversions automatically.
- **Consistent Code Generation**: The dual-compiler pipeline ensures generated contracts are idiomatic in both Solidity and Vyper, reducing the risk of subtle compiler-specific bugs.
- **Lower Deployment Costs**: Vyper code often generates smaller bytecode than Solidity, reducing gas costs for on-chain deployments.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenge 1: Dual-Compiler AST Parity**
**Problem**: Python's AST has fundamentally different semantics than Solidity/Vyper. For example, Python's dynamic typing, runtime method resolution, and duck typing don't map cleanly to EVM's static types and fixed memory layout.

**Specific Issues**:
- Python `dict` → Vyper `HashMap` requires knowing the key/value types upfront (which Python doesn't enforce).
- Python `list` → Vyper `DynArray` with a compile-time size limit (Vyper limits arrays to 256 elements by default).
- Python's `self` context needed to be inferred as either `@internal` or `@external` visibility in Vyper/Solidity.

**How I Solved It**:
- **Type Inference Engine**: Built a multi-pass type analyzer that infers types from variable assignments, function return statements, and decorator hints.
- **Decorator Annotations**: Introduced `@contract`, `@action`, `@read` decorators that let developers explicitly annotate visibility and mutability where inference fails.
- **AST Transformation Layers**: Created separate `PythonToVyperTransformer` (36KB) and `PythonToSolidityTransformer` (24KB) classes, each handling language-specific quirks (e.g., Vyper's strict `String` sizing vs Solidity's dynamic `string`).

---

### **Challenge 2: Security Without False Positives**
**Problem**: Blocking dangerous patterns like `exec()` and `eval()` is straightforward, but legitimate Python patterns get caught. For example:
- A function named `execute()` shouldn't be blocked.
- A variable containing `"os"` as a string shouldn't trigger an "os import" warning.
- Developers were frustrated with overly strict validation.

**Specific Issues**:
- Regex patterns for `os.*` and `sys.*` produced false positives on identifiers like `custom_os_path` or `system_config`.
- The first version blocked all `import` statements, making it impossible to use `from pybitrum import Contract`.

**How I Solved It**:
- **AST-Based Pattern Matching**: Replaced string regex with proper Python AST analysis. Now only `import os` and `import sys` are blocked, not arbitrary string matches.
- **Whitelisted Imports**: Allowed safe imports like `from pybitrum import Contract`, `from typing import Dict`, etc.
- **Multi-Pass Validation**: Split validation into a `SecurityChecker` (14 hard-coded patterns) and `CodeValidator` (AST walks), allowing different severity levels.
- **Detailed Error Messages**: When validation fails, the compiler now returns specific line numbers and context (e.g., "exec() at line 42 is not allowed"), not just "bad code."

---

### **Challenge 3: TypeScript ↔ Python Serialization**
**Problem**: The frontend (TypeScript/Next.js) sends Python code to the Flask compiler service and receives back Vyper/Solidity code + AST JSON. Serializing complex Python objects across HTTP required careful schema design.

**Specific Issues**:
- Python's `ast.AST` nodes aren't JSON-serializable by default.
- Type mismatches between TypeScript interfaces and Python dictionaries caused runtime errors on the frontend.
- Large ASTs (100+ KB for complex contracts) bloated JSON payloads, causing slow compilation responses.

**How I Solved It**:
- **Custom JSON Encoder**: Built a `PyBitrumJSONEncoder` that converts `ast.AST` nodes, code objects, and other non-serializable types to dictionaries.
- **Zod Schemas**: On the backend (Express), used Zod to validate all compiler responses against strict TypeScript interfaces before returning to the frontend.
- **AST Pruning**: Limited the AST response to only essential fields (function names, arguments, return types) rather than the full parse tree, reducing payload size by ~70%.
- **HTTP Compression**: Enabled gzip compression on the Flask compiler service to further reduce response times.

---

### **Challenge 4: Vyper vs Solidity Bytecode Divergence**
**Problem**: The same Python contract compiled to both Vyper and Solidity could produce different EVM bytecode and gas costs. For example:
- Vyper's `HashMap` generates different storage layout than Solidity's `mapping`.
- Vyper's built-in overflow checks add runtime gas overhead that Solidity 0.8.x includes at the language level.
- Compiler optimizations differ-solcx defaults to different optimization runs than vyper.

**Specific Issues**:
- Agents couldn't trust both compiled versions; they'd pick one and ignore the other.
- The Hive Registry contract expected a specific ABI, but Vyper and Solidity generated slightly different ABIs for the same logic.
- Gas estimates were inconsistent, making it hard to price agent missions on the Mission Board.

**How I Solved It**:
- **Dual-ABI Registration**: Modified the Hive Registry to accept both Vyper and Solidity ABIs, storing them alongside the contract address.
- **Deterministic Compilation**: Locked compiler versions (solcx 0.8.20, vyper 0.4.3) and fixed optimization settings to ensure reproducible bytecode.

### The Sealed Sky
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/the-sealed-sky-01e1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/id144/sealed-sky-web) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://ethprague2026.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHPrague%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethprague2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Messages for the future

![Cryptography](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cryptography-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contract](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contract-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Sealed Sky is a consumer grade timelock encryption tool with easy to use user interface. 

It allows to encrypt - seal the content  now, decrypt only when a future moment arrives.

Use cases:
- Time capsules at any scale - 30 seconds, a year, a decade.
- Sealed-bid auctions where everyone reveals at the same instant, nobody before.
- Dead-man's switches and posthumous notes, with no trusted custodian holding the key.
- MEV-resistant order submission and time-locked DAO votes.
- Predictions of future that can be undisclosed after the fact.
- Intergenerational messaging - send a message to yourself or your closed ones that becomes legible only in 2030. 

The demo website uses TypeScript implementation of the TimeLock library based on Boneh–Franklin's IBE paper. 

Complementary part of the project is a Trusted Edge Oracle - small stack that lets you treat a USB Armory (Secure World / TrustZone) as a signing oracle for short, structured payloads. A Node backend re-checks proofs with the same HMAC rule as the Armory, records accepted and rejected runs, and optionally pushes on-chain attestations to Sepolia and surfaces validation through ENS.

It can be used to 
- As a proof “This result came from our edge device, not from a browser tab.”
-Cheaper, clearer audits than “trust our server.”
-Safer automation with a relayer.
-Public transparency without dumping your whole database.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges are surprisingly the opposite of what we were used at the hackathons years ago. 

We admit utilized AI agent tools (Claude Code, Cursor), they helped us reach to develop proof-of-concepts at paces not possible before, but for us  developers, it became complicated to keep track of all the important technical  nuances of the proposed solution.

Issues that would need further attention - handling of the K key (there are ways how to tie the message to a specified public address without the need to store the K key safely until the unlock time).  If the messages are meant to be unlocked by public, the K key storage is not an issue.

**Network Economy**

Timelock is the missing primitive behind sealed-bid auctions, vesting cliffs, time-locked DAO votes, dead-man's switches, and MEV-resistant transaction submission. 

Anywhere "everyone reveals at the same instant, nobody before" is a useful property. Sealed Sky makes it usable today. 

The envelope format works in the browser and in the Python CLI. No trusted keeper, no custody risk between commit and reveal.

**Future Society**

Both backends work at year-scale and decade-scale unlocks. 

Sealing is non-interactive, and reveal only needs the latest beacon block at unlock time, so there's no chain walking or archive crawl. 

It makes intergenerational messaging real: a posthumous note, a 10-year time capsule addressed to *.eth, a long-horizon promise that becomes legible on a fixed date without any custodian holding the key.

**SpaceComputer Bounty**

The cTRNG IPFS beacon is wired in as a real encryption backend. 

Each cTRNG capsule has a SHA-256 commitment that binds it to a future unlock time, and reveal is gated on a live beacon block we fetch from ipfs.io. 

When the message decrypts, the Detail panel shows the witness block's sequence, timestamp, randomness, and gateway URL, so the cosmic origin is visible at the moment of unlock.

**Most Creative Use of ENS**

Every sealed message gets its own ENS subdomain. On seal we publish cap-*.id144.eth via NameStone, with records for the envelope. 

The capsule then resolves in any standard ENS client, including the ENS app. 

Share links collapse to ?ens=cap-3f2a9c1b.id144.eth, which uses ENS as a registry of time-bound content. 

The connect flow also falls back to NameStone's API when no on-chain reverse record is set, so NameStone-issued names work as primary names without a separate transaction.

### Blober - Blob Verification Library in Solidity
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/blober-blob-verification-library-in-solidity-5856) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/markolazic01/blober) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1TosN0BSJFnfTL6wRi8U3asQXC7zm99zR/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=108657623827748726808&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHPrague%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethprague2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Verify your blobs with Blober : )

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![BLS](https://img.shields.io/badge/BLS-333333?style=flat-square) ![foundry](https://img.shields.io/badge/foundry-333333?style=flat-square) ![EIP-4844](https://img.shields.io/badge/EIP--4844-333333?style=flat-square) ![EIP-2537](https://img.shields.io/badge/EIP--2537-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Blober is a Solidity library for Ethereum blob verification (and more), by introducing a well designed set of blob point verification flows it eases helps the L2 settlements. 
So far L2s usually build their own blob verification flows, in a non-standardized and sometimes messy way, Blober serves as a library that abstracts away the precompile interactions and makes the verification clean and efficient.
Blober's special feature is in multi-point verifications, across multiple blobs, where by utilizing the BLS precompiles from EIP-2537 it merges the blob points into a single point, making a verification process of multiple points less costly (by much).
Blober also contains other utils that can help you checksum the specific blob hash, get a versioned hash from the blob data hash, check if blob is present in the tx and more! 
With introduction of 21 blob per block limit, Blober multi-point verification becomes increasingly effective, for L2s using Blober instead of iterative point validation, gas consumption can be reduced by up to 80%!
Danksharding and Block-in-Blob EIPs can further leverage usage of Blober, potentially requiring the development of new features.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challange was designing the flow for multi-point verification using EIP-2537 precompiles as it requires in-depth cryptography knowledge. Also it required a lot of work to properly benchmark scenarios, and decide on the threshold point which determines an exact place where iterative single point verification becomes more expensive than batched verification. Even though this library is small, it is quite challenging.

**Ethereum Core**

Blober introduces a standard for blob on-chain verification, as a gas optimized solution for L2s to use in their verification flow along with the state updates.

**Network Economy**

Blober provides up to 70% gas savings to the L2s that would use it using batch point verification. Batching provides a steadier gas growth when working with multiple points, and it gets steadier as the number of points grows resulting in astonishing gas savings with tens or hundreds of points. This flow can directly impact the gas prices on L2s that use this library - making it a strong candidate to become a standard in blob point verification.
