> smart hospital service

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

##

People often struggle to understand medical information because symptoms, medical reports, medicines, and health terminology can be complex and difficult to interpret. Searching online can also lead to confusing, unreliable, or misleading information.

**MediMatrix AI** helps make healthcare information easier to understand and access by providing AI-powered explanations in simple language. Users can use it to:

* Understand symptoms and possible health concerns
*  Get easy-to-understand explanations of medical reports
* Learn about medicines, their common uses, and precautions
* Ask health-related questions through an AI assistant
*  Find relevant and understandable medical information
*  Identify situations where professional medical attention may be important
*  Organize and review personal health information

By simplifying complex medical information and providing structured guidance, MediMatrix AI can help people make more informed decisions, reduce confusion, and prepare better questions for healthcare professionals.

MediMatrix AI is designed for health information and guidance, not for replacing doctors or providing definitive medical diagnoses.

**Challenges we ran into**

##

While developing **MediMatrix AI**, we faced several challenges:

* Ensuring medical information is accurate, reliable, and easy to understand.
* Designing AI responses that are helpful without giving unsafe or misleading medical advice.
* Handling different ways users describe the same symptoms or health concerns.
* Making complex medical reports and terminology understandable to non-medical users.
* Maintaining user privacy and protecting sensitive health-related information.
* Balancing AI functionality with a simple, fast, and user-friendly interface.
* Clearly communicating that the platform provides guidance and does not replace professional medical diagnosis.

**AI For Society**

MediMatrix AI is an AI-powered healthcare assistant that simplifies medical information, helping users understand symptoms, reports, medicines, and health questions through clear and accessible guidance.

### RELIEFCHAIN
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/reliefchain-2722) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Riju79/relief-chain) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://relief-chain-cyan.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zmKse7QxKLk?si=Nv8RRjgtxEU4_33P) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> REBUILDING HUMINITY THROUGH RELIEFCHAIN

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![move](https://img.shields.io/badge/move-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🛠️ Challenges We Ran Into

Building ReliefChain as a genuinely Web3-native disaster-relief protocol came with several challenges — especially around making **on-chain funds, verification logic, and decentralized evidence work together reliably.**

### 1. Designing Non-Custodial Fund Management

One of our biggest challenges was ensuring that donated funds were **not simply transferred to a campaign creator's wallet**.

We redesigned the flow around a Move smart-contract treasury where donations remain controlled by the protocol. Instead of relying on the frontend to enforce rules, the Move contract becomes the source of truth for:

**Donation → Campaign Treasury → Milestone Verification → Fund Release**

This forced us to think carefully about authorization, object ownership, treasury accounting, and preventing unauthorized withdrawals.

### 2. Connecting On-Chain State With the Frontend

Another hurdle was keeping the frontend synchronized with blockchain state.

Initially, some UI state could become stale after transactions or page refreshes. We moved toward treating **Sui as the source of truth**, fetching campaign and transaction state from the blockchain rather than relying on temporary frontend state.

This was especially important for ensuring that campaigns and donation history remain verifiable after a refresh.

### 3. Wallet & Transaction Handling

Wallet integration introduced another layer of complexity.

Transaction signing, gas management, network configuration, wallet connection state, and transaction confirmation all had to work together. A transaction could be successfully submitted while the frontend was still waiting for confirmation or displaying stale information.

We addressed this by improving transaction lifecycle handling:

`Connect → Build Transaction → Sign → Execute → Confirm → Refresh On-Chain State`

This made the application much more resilient to delayed confirmations and RPC responses.

### 4. Making Relief Evidence Verifiable

Disaster-relief evidence can include large files such as photographs, invoices, delivery manifests, and reports. Storing everything directly on-chain would be inefficient and expensive.

We therefore separated the architecture into two layers:

**Sui = Financial & Verification Layer**
**Decentralized Storage = Evidence Layer**

Instead of putting large files on-chain, the system stores the evidence off-chain in decentralized storage and anchors its identifier/hash to the corresponding on-chain milestone.

This gives us the scalability of decentralized storage while preserving a verifiable connection between **evidence and fund releases.**

### 5. Designing for Real-World Failure

A disaster-relief application cannot assume that every transaction, upload, RPC request, or verification step will succeed.

We added explicit handling for failed transactions, rejected wallet signatures, missing evidence, invalid campaign states, and incomplete milestone flows.

The result is a system where failures are treated as expected protocol states rather than silent frontend errors.

### 💡 Biggest Lesson

The hardest part wasn't simply putting a donation button on a blockchain.

It was designing the system so that **money, evidence, permissions, and verification all share the same source of truth.**

That led us to our core design principle:

> **The frontend can display the truth — but the smart contract must enforce it.**

**The problem it solves**

**## 🌍 The Problem It Solves

When disaster strikes, **people donate fast — but accountability moves slowly.**

Traditional disaster-relief funding relies on banks, crowdfunding platforms, organizations, spreadsheets, and centralized databases. Donors often have no way to independently verify:

* **Where their money went**
* **Who received it**
* **What it was spent on**
* **Whether the reported relief actually happened**

This creates a fundamental problem:

> **You can trust the intention of a donation without being able to verify its journey.**

ReliefChain changes that by turning disaster relief into a **transparent, programmable, and auditable on-chain process.**

### 🚨 What ReliefChain Enables

**For Donors**

Donate directly through Sui and follow the movement of funds on-chain — from the campaign treasury to verified relief milestones.

**For Relief Organizations**

Create structured campaigns with defined funding milestones such as:

`Emergency Supplies → Medical Aid → Food Distribution → Reconstruction`

Funds are managed by Move smart contracts rather than being immediately handed to a campaign creator.

**For Verifiers**

Authorized verifiers can review submitted relief evidence and approve milestone-based fund releases, creating an additional accountability layer between donations and spending.

**For Auditors & the Public**

Every important financial action can be independently inspected on-chain, creating a permanent and transparent audit trail.

### 🔐 Making Disaster Relief Safer

| Traditional Relief                        | ReliefChain                                           |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Trust the organization to report spending | **Verify transactions on-chain**                      |
| Funds controlled by intermediaries        | **Funds governed by Move smart contracts**            |
| Manual milestone tracking                 | **Programmable milestone-based releases**             |
| Centralized records                       | **Public blockchain audit trail**                     |
| Difficult to trace donations              | **Trackable fund flow from donation to disbursement** |
| Evidence disconnected from payments       | **Relief evidence linked to on-chain milestones**     |

### ⚡ The Core Idea

**ReliefChain separates *trust* from *transparency*.**

Instead of asking donors to simply believe that their donation reached the right place, the protocol makes the financial journey **cryptographically verifiable**.

**Donate → Verify → Release → Audit**

The result is a disaster-relief system designed to make humanitarian funding **more transparent, accountable, and programmable.**

> **Don't just donate. Know where your relief goes.****

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

## 💸 How ReliefChain Fits the Payments & Stablecoin Track

ReliefChain applies blockchain payments to one of the most important real-world payment problems: **getting humanitarian money to the right people quickly, transparently, and with less dependence on intermediaries.**

Today, international disaster relief can involve multiple payment processors, banks, organizations, and manual reconciliation steps. ReliefChain turns this process into a **programmable payment flow secured by smart contracts.**

### 🌍 Stablecoins as the Humanitarian Payment Rail

While SUI can be used for native on-chain payments, the protocol is designed to support **stablecoin-based humanitarian funding** as the ecosystem evolves.

A stablecoin such as a USD-pegged asset can provide a predictable unit of account for:

* International donations
* NGO and relief-organization funding
* Contractor payments
* Medical and emergency-supply procurement
* Cross-border humanitarian disbursements

This is particularly useful when donors and relief providers operate across different currencies and financial systems.

### 🔄 From Donation to Real-World Payment

ReliefChain transforms a donation into a programmable payment lifecycle:

**Donor → Campaign Treasury → Verified Milestone → Relief Provider → On-Chain Settlement**

Instead of releasing an entire campaign balance upfront, funds can be tied to predefined milestones.

For example:

> **$10,000 stablecoin campaign**
>
> → $3,000 for emergency food & water
> → $2,500 for medical supplies
> → $2,000 for temporary shelter
> → $2,500 for reconstruction

Each payment can be governed by the campaign's smart-contract rules and released when the corresponding milestone is approved.

### 🔐 Why Blockchain Payments Matter Here

ReliefChain combines **payments + programmable money + verification**.

Traditional payment systems answer:

> **“Did the payment happen?”**

ReliefChain aims to additionally answer:

> **“Why was the payment released, who authorized it, where did it go, and which relief milestone did it fund?”**

Because the financial activity is recorded on-chain, donors, verifiers, and auditors can independently inspect the payment trail.

### 🚀 Why This Belongs in the Stablecoin Track

Stablecoins make the model particularly powerful for **cross-border disaster response**.

A donor in one country can fund a relief campaign while a verified organization or contractor in another country receives a blockchain-native payment — without requiring the entire payment flow to depend on traditional correspondent banking infrastructure.

The long-term vision is:

**Global donations → Stablecoin settlement → Programmable escrow → Verified milestone → Direct humanitarian payment**

ReliefChain therefore isn't simply using crypto as a donation method.

**It is exploring how stablecoins can become programmable infrastructure for faster, more transparent humanitarian payments.**

> Milestone escrow powered by AI

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prisma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prisma-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fastify](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fastify-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

AI Hallucinations in Contract Terms: The language model initially assumed missing details, such as fabricating wallet addresses or guessing review deadlines. We resolved this by constraining the AI strictly to data structuring, adding a deterministic Zod validation layer, and introducing an explicit "Help us fill in the gaps" step for mandatory human input.  Upstream AI Outages & Timeouts: Live API calls to the LLM backend occasionally timed out or returned unexpected formats. We fixed this by saving raw terms as local drafts first and adding a fallback manual entry path that enforces the same strict validation rules.  Balancing Privacy with On-Chain Integrity: Writing plain-text contracts and evidence to the blockchain would expose private business data and increase costs. We implemented a hybrid architecture where sensitive records remain off-chain in PostgreSQL, while only an immutable SHA-256 agreement hash and coordination anchors interact with Sui.  Escrow Math & State Safety in Move: Ensuring locked funds could never be double-spent across multi-milestone lifecycles or disputes required rigid accounting. We built and verified 18 Move unit tests to strictly enforce single-release invariant checks and freeze disputed milestones until resolved.  Mobile Key Management: Exposing private keys or burdening users with seed phrases undermines mobile security and UX. We decoupled custody by leveraging native Google sign-in with Enoki nonces, generating unsigned transaction builders locally, and never storing keys on the backend.

**The problem it solves**

In freelance and service-based work, trust frequently breaks down before any payment actually occurs because informal communication over chat, email, or calls leaves payment conditions, deliverables, and revision rules open to conflicting interpretations. This creates a stalemate where clients risk losing their money by paying upfront for incomplete or substandard work, while contractors risk working without compensation if payment is withheld. Without a shared, objective source of truth, vague agreements inevitably result in payment friction, stalled projects, and contentious disputes. TrustFlow resolves this dilemma by bridging casual conversational terms into deterministic, milestone-structured agreements backed by non-custodial smart contracts, protecting both parties with clear review windows, objective evidence requirements, and controlled fund releases.

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

TrustFlow integrates Sui’s payment infrastructure through a dedicated PaymentFlow Move smart contract that operates as an autonomous, non-custodial escrow using native SUI tokens scaled to nine decimal places. When an agreement is finalized, the client locks the full project deposit into the contract via create_flow, ensuring funds cannot be withdrawn arbitrarily once the contractor accepts. The contract coordinates sequential milestone progression: funds are released either through explicit client approval or automatically claimed by the contractor via claim_after_review if the client fails to review the work before the deadline expires. If a dispute arises, the milestone freezes until an authorized resolver determines a precise fund split, backed by strict invariant math ensuring no locked balance can ever be released twice. On the client side, the Android application binds user identities using Enoki and constructs unsigned Sui transaction builders locally, keeping private key custody and execution authority entirely in the user's hands rather than on the backend.

Built for a hackathon project using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Flask, Python, MySQL, and Gemini AI.

📄 Resume Analysis – Upload a PDF or DOCX resume and extract skills using AI.
🧠 AI Skill Evaluation – Identify strengths and weaknesses from the resume.

🛣️ Personalized Roadmap – Generate a step-by-step roadmap for the selected career path.
📊 Progress Tracker – Track completed roadmap steps and learning progress.
🎯 Career Ready Dashboard – View overall resume score, skills, and next learning tasks.

**Challenges we ran into**

Resume Data Extraction: PDF aur DOCX resumes ka content different formats mein hota hai, isliye resume se accurate text aur relevant skills extract karna challenging tha.
Accurate Skill Identification: Resume mein explicitly mention na ki gayi skills ko identify karna aur technical skills ko properly categorize karna difficult tha.
AI-Based Evaluation: Gemini AI se meaningful strengths, weaknesses aur career recommendations generate karwana challenging tha, especially because AI output ko relevant aur consistent rakhna zaroori tha.
Career Matching: User ke skills ko suitable job roles ke saath accurately match karna aur meaningful match percentages provide karna ek major challenge tha.
Personalized Roadmap Generation: Har user ke skill gaps ke according customized learning roadmap generate karna challenging tha, instead of providing the same roadmap to everyone.
Frontend–Backend Integration: HTML/CSS/JavaScript frontend ko Flask backend, AI services aur database ke saath properly integrate karna debugging aur API handling ke perspective se challenging tha.
Database Management: Users, resumes, analysis reports, jobs, required skills, roadmaps aur progress ko relational database mein properly connect aur manage karna challenging tha.
Progress Tracking: User ke completed roadmap steps ko accurately store karna aur dashboard par real-time progress reflect karna additional implementation challenge tha.
AI Response Reliability: AI-generated responses kabhi-kabhi inconsistent ya unexpected format mein aa sakte hain, isliye responses ko handle aur validate karna important tha.
Security & File Handling: Resume uploads ko securely handle karna, supported file types validate karna aur sensitive user/resume data ko safely manage karna bhi challenging tha.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![POSTGIS](https://img.shields.io/badge/POSTGIS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![SHA-256 Hashes](https://img.shields.io/badge/SHA--256%20Hashes-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prism.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prism.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges we Ran Into

One of the main challenges we faced was making sure a land record could not be added or updated without proper verification. We had to connect the user’s land details, map location, admin approval, OTP authentication, and blockchain transaction into one flow.
We also faced issues while checking whether a newly submitted land record already existed. A survey number alone was not always enough, so we added checks against previous records and land boundaries shown on the map.
To solve these problems, we divided the process into separate steps: **user submission → admin validation → OTP confirmation → blockchain update**. We also kept detailed land information in the database while storing its hash and transaction details on the blockchain. This made the system easier to manage while still maintaining a tamper-evident record.

**The problem it solves**

Land records are still difficult to verify in many situations. A person may have the correct documents, but it can be hard to know whether the land has already been registered under someone else, whether the records have been changed, or whether the actual land boundary matches the submitted details.
This can lead to duplicate registrations, ownership disputes, fraudulent transactions, and lengthy manual verification processes.
Our project aims to make land verification faster, more transparent, and easier to trust by combining digital land records, map-based verification, OTP authentication, and blockchain-based history.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an autonomous multi-agent career transformation platform with real-time 3D graphics, psychological gamification, and instant dynamic roadmaps came with significant full-stack engineering hurdles:

1. Server-Client Boundary Leaks & Vercel Hydration Crashes
The Hurdle: Our execution protocol engine worked seamlessly on localhost but threw client-side runtime error boundaries on Vercel production.
The Investigation: A "use client" component imported curriculum helpers from our agent pipeline (deployer.ts), which pulled server-only Node.js dependencies (OpenRouter, OpenAI SDK, crypto, and private environment variables) into the client bundle.
The Solution: We cleanly decoupled the architecture by building a pure TypeScript, zero-dependency engine (curriculumGenerator.ts) using strict import type definitions. We also added an autonomous client-side synthesis guard that dynamically reconstructs missing curricula on direct tab refreshes without network bottlenecks.
2. Three.js Matrix Projections & 3D Orbit Physics Tuning
The Hurdle: In the 3D Holographic Growth Timeline, DOM cards warped into awkward aspect ratios on viewport resizing, and the 3D cylinder orbit suffered from aggressive damping and jittery physics.
The Investigation: Three.js <Html transform> non-linearly scaled DOM projection matrices across dynamic screen dimensions, while vertical bobbing frequency (1.5x) was too fast for readable typography.
The Solution: We normalized camera optics (fov: 46, cameraZ: 9.6, distance factor 5.0) to lock fixed card dimensions (320px × 460px). We re-engineered the damping physics to a silky-smooth inertia factor (3.2) with a calm floating frequency (0.35), and added on-canvas step navigation for 1-click milestone centering.
3. Eliminating AI Latency in Visual Roadmap Generation
The Hurdle: Relying on real-time remote image diffusion models caused 3–7 second latency spikes, leaving empty placeholder boxes and blocking fast PDF exports.
The Solution: We engineered a dual-layer rendering pipeline. We built an instant (<1ms) high-resolution Vector SVG Blueprint Engine that renders structured 3-step milestones with glowing obsidian-neon themes directly from client memory. Remote AI visuals preload in the background and smoothly cross-fade into view without ever blocking user interaction or PDF generation.
4. Deep State Null-Safety Across Multi-Year Timelines
The Hurdle: Uninitialized local storage states or varied user inputs (6_weeks to 10_years) caused runtime NaN calculations and unhandled null property exceptions.
The Solution: We implemented an effectiveState proxy pattern that guarantees complete fallback to validated demo schemas, paired with a comprehensive mapping table covering all duration horizons. We also wrapped all 3D canvas subsystems in React <Suspense> boundaries to ensure WebGL context loss never crashes the application.

**The problem it solves**

1. The Core Problem: The Execution Void
Most people have ambitious dream careers (e.g., Trader, AI Engineer, Creator, Founder), but fail because of two fatal bottlenecks:

Analysis Paralysis: They don't know the exact, day-by-day sequence of tasks and tools needed to transition from their current baseline.
Procrastination & Zero Accountability: Motivation fades after a few days without an active pressure system to keep them consistent.
2. How VibeForge Solves It (The 3 Pillars):
🎯 100% Tailored Execution Protocol Takes your exact starting point (e.g., Student in Kolkata) and goal (Full-time Trader), delivering a week-by-week curriculum with practical deliverables and verified top-rated video guides.

⚔️ Psychological Rival & Ego-Hurt Engine Pits you against a relentless AI adversary who is outpacing you. It triggers competitive urgency through live taunts, 25-minute focus sprints, and pace-lead counters that eliminate laziness.

📊 Visual Multi-Dimensional Blueprints Transforms abstract career growth into tangible 2D/3D visual roadmap holograms and instant printable protocols so you always know your exact progress and upcoming milestones.

> An API that charges per call, not per month.

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/x402-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part wasn't the payment logic: it was that x402 is new enough that two incompatible versions were in circulation at the same time, and the docs hadn't caught up.

My endpoint was correctly returning 402 with payment requirements, but the client couldn't generate a signature. The only error I got was Cannot convert undefined to a BigInt:  which doesn't tell you which field is missing or why.

**The problem it solves**

Every API is sold by the month, and that's not a product choice it's a payments. Card networks charge ~$0.30 in fixed fees per transaction. A single LLM call costs $0.000037. You cannot sell that on card rails, so it gets bundled into a subscription instead.

**The result:** a developer who needs five API calls has to create an account, hand over a card, and commit to a month. An AI agent, which can do none of those things, is locked out entirely.

**METER** makes the API pay for itself, mid-request. The client sends a request with no credentials. The server responds **402 Payment Required** with a price. The wallet signs a USDC authorization, the request retries, and settlement happens onchain about one second, end to end.

What this enables:
**Pay for what you use :** five calls costs five calls, not a month
**No signup, no API key :** nothing to issue, rotate, or leak
**No card required :** works for developers who can't easily get international cards, which is a real barrier in India
**Agents can buy things : **an autonomous client can't fill in a signup form, but it can sign a payment inside an HTTP request

Why it's safer: there's no stored credential to steal. Each payment is a single-use signature, scoped to one amount, one recipient, with an expiry.

Built on the x402 protocol, running on Base Sepolia.

[Deven Sawant](https://github.com/d-even)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was designing a Trust Score that was more than just an AI generated number. An LLM can produce convincing explanations, but relying entirely on it to determine a risk score can make results inconsistent.

I addressed this by separating risk-signal detection from score calculation. The AI identifies relevant signals such as suspicious payment requests, urgency, phishing patterns, impersonation, and unusual claims, while a structured scoring layer uses those signals to calculate the Trust Score. The AI then explains the result in simple language.

Another challenge was handling different input types websites, job offers, messages, screenshots, and Web3 data through one consistent experience. I solved this by designing TrustLayer around a common analysis pipeline that converts different inputs into a standardized trust report.

**The problem it solves**

TrustLayer AI helps people decide whether something online is trustworthy before they click, pay, share, or act.

Scams are becoming increasingly convincing from fake job offers and phishing websites to suspicious emails, social profiles, screenshots, and crypto addresses. Existing tools are often fragmented, requiring users to check different services for different types of threats.

TrustLayer AI provides a single AI powered trust layer where users can submit suspicious digital content and receive a simple Trust Score, risk level, evidence-based red flags, positive signals, and a clear recommendation. This makes digital risk easier to understand, even for users without cybersecurity expertise.

For Web3, TrustLayer AI also explores verifiable trust reports, allowing the fingerprint of a report to be recorded on-chain for a transparent and tamper-resistant trust history.

### Apples & Oranges
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/apples-and-oranges-10b0) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Sharann-del/Apples-and-Oranges) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://applesandoranges.vercel.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Origins-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://origins.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Rescued before the crash even finishes

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. The gross-up factor can be below 1 — and that broke our first solver

Our closed-form repayment solver `R* = (HFₜ·D − L) / (HFₜ − G·λₖ)` depends on `G`, the
collateral value consumed per unit of debt repaid. We first modelled it as `G = 1 + fees`
— always greater than 1.

Then a crash test produced an intervention where collateral consumed came in *below* debt
repaid. It wasn't a bug. Oracles update on heartbeats, so mid-crash the DEX often prices
collateral **richer** than Aave's oracle still believes — `G < 1`. A "friction-only" model
can't express that and systematically oversizes every rescue, spending more of the user's
capital than needed.

**Fix:** `G` is now read from a live DEX quote every time, so it captures the real
oracle-to-market basis. The solver handles `G < 1` explicitly, and we now demo it as a
feature — the exact edge case, observed live.

## 2. Bit-exact Solidity ↔ TypeScript parity on the solver

The agent computes `R*` off-chain; the vault re-derives it on-chain in its post-condition
block. If the two disagree by even one wei of rounding, a plan the agent believes is
optimal gets rejected by the vault — or worse, accepted while mis-sized.

Getting fixed-point division to round *identically* in both languages took several passes
— `Math.floor` vs integer division, order of operations, where truncation lands. We
generate a grid of fixture cases from a Foundry script and a test replays them through
both implementations demanding exact equality. It's now part of `make test`.

## 3. The agent crash-looped the moment we deployed it

Locally the agent scanned `ShieldRegistry` logs from genesis in one call. On a hosted
free-tier RPC that's fatal: Alchemy caps `eth_getLogs` at a 10-block range and throttles
by compute-units-per-second. On first boot the agent fired hundreds of requests, hit HTTP
429, and `process.exit(1)` — then the host restarted it, and it did the whole thing again.

**Fix, in four parts:**
- The API and the first position start *immediately*, so the health check passes in ~2s;
  the full scan runs in the background.
- Discovery uses a dedicated `LOG_RPC_URL` (a public node that serves unbounded ranges) —
  one request instead of hundreds of throttled windows.
- A checkpoint (last block + known users) is persisted so restarts resume incrementally.
- Discovery is serialized, non-fatal, and has exponential backoff on 429.

## 4. Two different time horizons, one bug

The safety buffer asks *"how far can the market move while my rescue transaction is in
flight"* — a handful of blocks. We reused that same horizon in the economic viability gate,
which asks a completely different question: *"what happens if I stand down"* — minutes to
hours of exposure.

The result: over a 3-block horizon, almost nothing looks dangerous, so the gate declined
nearly every intervention. Separating the two horizons — a short one for the buffer, a long
one for the stand-down decision — fixed it.

## 5. Nonce races against a lagging RPC

The crash simulator fires dozens of sequential transactions to keep the mock AMM in sync
with the oracle. Against Alchemy, `eth_sendRawTransaction` started rejecting with
"replacement transaction underpriced" — its `pending` transaction count lags the mempool,
so the client re-derived a nonce that was just used. Switched the simulator to a local
nonce manager (deterministic increments) and a public node with consistent nonce
reporting.

**The problem it solves**

## The problem

If you borrow against crypto on Aave, a price drop can push your position past its
liquidation threshold. When that happens, anyone can repay your debt and seize your
collateral **plus a 5–15% bonus** — value taken straight out of your pocket, in seconds,
often over a dip that recovers an hour later. Billions in collateral are lost this way in
every market crash.

Your options today are all bad:

- **Watch it yourself** — doesn't scale, and you can't monitor a position while you sleep.
- **Run your own keeper bot** — crude: it deleverages by round numbers, overshoots, and
  sells the wrong collateral.
- **Use a custodial service** — you hand over control, and it still uses fixed thresholds.

## What Apples & Oranges does

A non-custodial vault that **deleverages your position the block before it can be
liquidated** — one atomic transaction that repays part of your debt with flash-loaned
liquidity, restores your health factor above a target *you* signed, and reverts leaving
nothing changed if any step fails. You keep your keys; `approve(0)` revokes it entirely.

An off-chain agent watches every armed position and:

1. Sizes the **mathematically minimum** repayment from a closed-form solver, priced off a
   live DEX quote — no overshoot.
2. Runs an **economic gate** — it only acts if the liquidation penalty avoided exceeds the
   flash + swap + gas cost. Otherwise it stands down and tells you why.
3. Executes through the cheapest venue and fee tier, with an on-chain post-condition block
   that guarantees the outcome.

## Who it's for

- **Leveraged borrowers** who want liquidation protection without giving up custody.
- **Anyone** — a public `/inspect` page reads any Aave address's risk and shows what the
  shield would do, no wallet, no gas.

## Why it's safer than the alternatives

- **Non-custodial** — the vault never holds your position; no admin key can touch it.
- **No single point of failure** — `protect()` is permissionless. If the agent goes down,
  any address can trigger the same rescue, because the contract enforces the outcome, not
  the caller. A small capped tip funds a keeper market.
- **Provably minimal** — bit-exact Solidity/TypeScript parity on the solver, and the vault
  reverts any intervention that would leave you worse off or exceed the cost you set.

Team **Curos** -- Dhriti Vaz, Sharann Manojkumar

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/hookdca-0312) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/iamRaz-01/VIT-CSI-ORIGIN) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Origins-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://origins.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Decides smart. Trusts nothing. Verifies twice

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![AAVE](https://img.shields.io/badge/AAVE-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![forge](https://img.shields.io/badge/forge-333333?style=flat-square) ![Anvil](https://img.shields.io/badge/Anvil-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

On-chain DCA has two major problems: capital reserved for future purchases often sits idle, while fixed schedules execute regardless of market conditions. Our DCA Vault addresses both by keeping deposits in yield-bearing ERC-4626 vaults backed by Aave v3, while a deterministic engine can execute a full tranche, reduce it, or delay based on price deviation and urgency. User-defined limits control frequency, delay, tranche size, and slippage. Execution is atomic, and a Uniswap v4 hook independently verifies constraints at settlement. The result is yield-bearing, market-aware, non-custodial DCA without relying on a privileged operator.

**Challenges we ran into**

During development, we found a critical security flaw: user limits were passed through caller-controlled `hookData`, making them forgeable. We fixed this by making the hook ignore numeric values and independently fetch constraints from trusted Coordinator storage. We also separated the core flow from Uniswap v4 using a standalone fallback, making demos reliable while testing the full pool path separately. Testing exposed v4 deployment fragility, a demo limitation for `DELAY`, tiny ERC-4626 variance from timestamp drift, and mock-yield accounting issues. These findings shaped the final architecture: untrusted inputs, independent enforcement, graceful degradation, and layer-specific determinism.

> Secure Temporary print jobs

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Swift](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

So we all know that whenever we have to go to get a print of our confidential document(like passport, aadhar card etc.), there's a large amount of uncertainty associated with it. We never know when such documents can be used against us and without our knowledge.
Then it clicked me that Ethereum and BlockChain are all about privacy and decentralization. So i decided to build upon that idea and make this build my app, PrintShield. 

In this app, after selecting document u can review the sensitive fields and then set a copy limit and an expiry limit, after this u get and QR which u can scan and then the files are sent to the printer without being locally saved on the Printer Shop's computer .

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Designing privacy without overclaiming security

The biggest challenge was figuring out what the MVP could actually guarantee. We didn't want to claim that a QR code alone makes a document secure, so we separated the current UX/prototype layer from the future encryption and backend enforcement layer.

2. Making temporary access meaningful

We had to think about how a print authorization should work: the user chooses a copy limit and an expiry time, then the QR becomes invalid after the selected window. Designing that flow while keeping it simple for a normal user was a challenge.

3. Designing the QR system without putting sensitive data inside it

A major design decision was keeping the actual document out of the QR code. The QR only carries things like the job reference and expiry information, while the document remains on the user's phone in the MVP.

4. Balancing security and UX

We wanted users to understand that shorter expiry times and fewer copies provide more control, without pretending that our “privacy score” is an actual security measurement. That led us to make the score explicitly a UX heuristic.

5. Building a convincing prototype without the complete infrastructure

A real system needs a backend, authenticated print-shop client, encryption, printer integration and secure deletion. Implementing all of that during an MVP would have significantly increased the scope, so we focused on proving the core user experience and QR authorization flow first.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ai-based-sentiment-analysis-tool-4e73) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/suryamouli09/Sentiment-Analysis-Tool) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://sentiment-analysis-tool-1-59h0.onrender.com/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20to%20Devcon%20--%20NITK%20Surathkal-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-nitk-surathkal.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> "Turn Raw Feedback into Real-Time Emotion

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional sentiment analysis tools often suffer from binary over-simplification. When a customer leaves a detailed 10-point review praising 8 aspects of a product while pointing out 2 minor flaws, standard AI models frequently get swayed by negative keywords at the end of the text and classify the entire review as 100% Negative. Furthermore, conventional tools lack emotional nuance (failing to distinguish between anger, sadness, or fear), lack multi-language support, and force teams to manually copy-paste data without providing actionable business recommendations or executive-ready reports.

Sentix AI solves this by providing a multi-dimensional Sentiment & Emotion Intelligence Suite. It combines sentence-level clause aggregation, phrase highlighting, multi-language detection, live web scraping, and automated AI executive insights into a unified SaaS tool.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Mixed Review" Misclassification Bug
The Hurdle: Initially, single-pass binary transformer models evaluated long reviews as a single block of text. When testing a review with 8 positive sentences and 2 negative sentences, the model exhibited a recency bias toward the ending negative clause, incorrectly flagging the overall review as NEGATIVE.
How We Overcame It: We re-architected the sentiment engine to use sentence-level clause aggregation and weighted consensus calibration. The engine now splits text into individual sentences, evaluates each sentence independently, and calculates a net weighted positive ratio combined with keyword density scoring. This ensures mixed reviews with 8 positive points and 2 negative points are accurately classified as POSITIVE (or MOSTLY POSITIVE), while still flagging the 2 negative points in the pain points section.

2. Cloud Memory (OOM) Crash on Free Hosting Tiers (512 MB RAM Limit)
The Hurdle: When deploying our initial build to free cloud hosting platforms (Render.com), the deployment failed with a Ran out of memory (used over 512MB) error. Heavy PyTorch libraries and transformer weights allocated over 1.2 GB of RAM on startup, exceeding free tier hardware bounds.
How We Overcame It: We optimized the core runtime engine by integrating a high-precision, multi-clause VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner) engine combined with sentence-level clause breakdown. This optimization slashed RAM usage from ~1,200 MB down to under 35 MB, accelerated cold server startup times from 45 seconds down to 0.4 seconds, and allowed the entire application to deploy flawlessly on Render's 512 MB free tier.

### Payshade
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/payshade-b387) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/fictiondharm/Devcon) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://payshade.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/6JTmx16JKhI?si=juCVhyIK7SHLrTnU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20to%20Devcon%20--%20NITK%20Surathkal-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-nitk-surathkal.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> One transaction. Zero identity leaks.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

On Ethereum, payroll is public surveillance. When a company pays salaries on chain, every transfer is permanently visible: who got paid, how much, how often. Anyone (competitors, analytics firms, stalkers) can link an employee's wallet to their identity and see exactly what they earn. Traditional crypto payroll forces a brutal choice: leak everyone's salary, or pay people off chain and lose the auditability and composability that made you use crypto in the first place.

What Payshade does about it

It uses ERC-5564 stealth addresses plus the ERC-6538 meta-address registry so payments are real on-chain transfers, but unlinkable to recipients:

Employee registers once. They sign locally; a spending key and viewing key derive in-browser, and only a public key goes into the shared ERC-6538 registry.
Company pays in bulk. The payrun derives a fresh one-time stealth address per employee client-side (from their meta-address) and pays everyone in a single PayshadeCore contract call (about 46 lines by design).
Nobody can connect the dots. Observers see N transfers to N random addresses. No pattern links them to each other or to any identity. Amounts per person are hidden too.
Only the employee can find their money. They scan announcements locally with their viewing key, then sweep funds from each stealth address into their real wallet privately.

So employees get salary privacy without trusting a custodian or mixer, and companies get one-transaction payroll with no server, no KYC, no accounts. Fully non-custodial.

**Challenges we ran into**

The one that cost me the most time was a React crash I caused myself. On the company page, every recipient row checks the ERC-6538 registry live and shows a little registered / not registered yet badge. My first version did if (!address) return null before calling useReadContract — React does not like that at all, so the whole payrun page crashed whenever rows were added or removed mid-edit. Took an embarrassing number of console errors to realize it was the Rules of Hooks biting me. Rewrote it so hooks always run unconditionally and the query is just gated with enabled.
Another sneaky one: refreshing the Employee page made it look like you'd never set up private payments, even though you registered on-chain earlier. Turns out wagmi restores the wallet connection asynchronously, and I was reading keys/payment history from storage during the very first render — while the address was still undefined. Moved all rehydration into an effect keyed on (address, chainId) and it went away. Cool side effect though: my stealth keys are derived deterministically from a signature, so even if the browser wipes session storage, signing the same message regenerates the exact same keys. A bug turned into self-healing.
And the classic deploy one: everything worked locally, pushed to Vercel, homepage fine — then refreshing /company 404'd, because the SPA lives inside an npm-workspaces monorepo and nothing told Vercel about client-side routes. ### Private Wallet and Privacy
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/private-wallet-and-privacy-a90a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Anup-Mamadapur/Private-wallet-and-privacy) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://frontend-eight-kappa-gy6dh8gsgc.vercel.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20to%20Devcon%20--%20NITK%20Surathkal-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-nitk-surathkal.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Send crypto. Not your privacy.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![ERC5564](https://img.shields.io/badge/ERC5564-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Ethereum is a fully public ledger — every transaction, balance, and wallet address is permanently visible to anyone. Once a wallet is linked to a person's identity even once, their entire financial history (salary, donations, business payments) is exposed forever. This is a major barrier to using Ethereum for everyday, business, or sensitive payments.

BEARS solves this by letting users send and receive ETH through one-time stealth addresses (ERC-5564) instead of their real wallet address. The sender generates a fresh, one-time address tied to the recipient's public stealth meta-address; on-chain, it looks like a payment to a random new address with no visible link to the recipient. The transaction remains fully valid and verifiable by the network — blockchain's core trust guarantees are untouched — but no outside observer, chain analyst, or advertiser can trace the payment back to the recipient's identity or spending history.

People can use BEARS to receive salaries, donations, or business payments privately, without exposing their full financial history to anyone who looks up their wallet address.

**Challenges we ran into**

We started this hackathon as complete beginners to blockchain development, with no prior Solidity experience. Our biggest early challenge was deciding how to implement stealth addresses without deep cryptography knowledge — we initially considered writing our own privacy contract from scratch, which would have been unrealistic in the timeframe.

We solved this by discovering and integrating the canonical, already-deployed ERC-5564 Announcer and ERC-6538 Registry contracts on Sepolia, along with the official @scopelift/stealth-address-sdk. This let us focus our limited time on correctly integrating a proven, audited standard rather than reinventing cryptographic primitives.

On the frontend, we hit a bug where our "Disconnect Wallet" button only appeared on the home page and disappeared when navigating to other screens, due to the header being duplicated across pages without the button included everywhere. We traced this to the page-routing logic and fixed it by adding the disconnect handler consistently across all page views.

We also ran into a payment-scanning issue where the app initially failed to detect real stealth payments due to block-range and RPC timing issues, which we resolved by adjusting the announcement scanner's block range logic.

As a 3-person team of blockchain beginners, coordinating git workflows, environment setup, and debugging Windows-specific PowerShell issues alongside the actual privacy tech was itself a real challenge — but it taught all three of us practical, end-to-end Web3 development in under a week.

**Private Wallets and Payments**

BEARS is a wallet application built specifically for the Private Wallets and Payments track. It lets users send and receive ETH such that sending and receiving money does not leak the sender, recipient, or amount — using stealth addresses (ERC-5564), where every payment goes to a fresh, one-time address that only the intended recipient can detect and claim. The transaction remains fully valid and verifiable on-chain, but no outside observer can link it to the recipient's real identity or wallet history, directly addressing the track's goal of private wallets and payments.

Team **BEARS** -- SATHVIK G, [Bharat Naik](https://github.com/bharat251cs220-stack), [Anup Mamadapur](https://github.com/Anup-Mamadapur)

### Silent Council
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/silent-council-9509) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/lakshay196/silent-council) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://silent-council-six.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/SPlt0yBAj8g) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20to%20Devcon%20--%20NITK%20Surathkal-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-nitk-surathkal.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Private NITK voting on Ethereum

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![EAS](https://img.shields.io/badge/EAS-333333?style=flat-square) ![zk.email](https://img.shields.io/badge/zk.email-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## Issuer key vs address
We first stored a **wallet address** as `ISSUER_PRIVATE_KEY`. Signing failed until we used the real 64-character hex key on Vercel.

## Unique vs alias URLs
CLI deploys created one-off Vercel URLs that never updated. We always demo **https://silent-council-six.vercel.app**.

## One mock email for every wallet
Early mock verify used the same demo email, so the second wallet hit `already_verified` without being registered. We switched to a unique mock email per wallet.

## Onchain vs database
The UI could show verified from the contract while `/api/vote` only checked Supabase. Vote now recovers the nullifier from chain if the row is missing.

## Honest ZK vs OTP
Live demo uses a fast verify path plus OTP fallback. OTP is **not** zero-knowledge. We say that in the README and in the pitch.

**The problem it solves**

## Problem

Campus votes today run on **Google Forms and WhatsApp**. Identity leaks. Counts can be changed.

## What Silent Council does

NITK students prove they own an allowed email **without putting the email onchain**, then vote once per proposal. The tally is public on **Base Sepolia**.

1. **Verify** with zk.email (or email OTP fallback if the prover is slow).
2. **Hide** identity: the chain stores a **nullifier** (hash), not the email.
3. **Vote** Yes / No / Abstain. Double votes are rejected onchain.

Production would accept only `@nitk.edu.in`. This judging demo also allows `@gmail.com`.

## Try it

- Live app: https://silent-council-six.vercel.app
- Code: https://github.com/lakshay196/silent-council
- Contract (Base Sepolia): [`0x4838024E8611d4E67fe6B9f6f43559A7e0971130`](https://sepolia.basescan.org/address/0x4838024E8611d4E67fe6B9f6f43559A7e0971130)

**What we built:** voting contract, issuer signatures, APIs, UI.
**What we use:** zk.email, EAS, RainbowKit.

**Overall**

Silent Council is a privacy-preserving campus voting app on Ethereum. Students prove email ownership without publishing the email. Ballots use onchain nullifiers so one identity gets one vote. Tallies are public on Base Sepolia. Built for the Make Private Apps using Ethereum theme: identity stays private, results stay auditable.

### ProofChain
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/proofchain-8386) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/VedantModhave/ProofChain) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://proofchain-one.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/_abs5ESO3c0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20to%20Devcon%20--%20NITK%20Surathkal-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-nitk-surathkal.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Prove it existed. Keep it private.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WalletConnect](https://img.shields.io/badge/WalletConnect-333333?style=flat-square) ![pinata](https://img.shields.io/badge/pinata-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wagmi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wagmi-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### Keeping Proof IDs Correct After Filtering

The smart contract stores proofs in a single array, while the dashboard only displays proofs belonging to the connected wallet. Initially, filtering the list could cause the displayed array index to differ from the actual on-chain proof ID. This created a risk of generating verification links for the wrong proof.

We solved this by preserving the original contract index before filtering:

```ts
allProofs
  .map((proof, index) => ({ ...proof, contractId: index }))
  .filter((proof) => proof.owner.toLowerCase() === address.toLowerCase());
```

Every dashboard item now links to its original on-chain ID, ensuring that verification always opens the correct proof.

### Handling Incorrect Wallet Networks

Users may connect their wallet while being on Ethereum Mainnet or another network instead of Sepolia. Transactions would fail or be sent to the wrong network.

We added network detection before submission. When the connected wallet is on the wrong network, ProofChain requests a switch to Ethereum Sepolia and prevents the transaction from continuing until the correct network is selected.

### Uploading Files Without Exposing API Credentials

Pinata requires API credentials, but exposing those credentials in frontend code would create a security risk. We solved this by routing uploads through a server-side Next.js API endpoint. The browser sends the file to `/api/pinata`, and the server forwards it to Pinata using credentials stored in environment variables.

This keeps the credentials off the client while still providing upload progress and clear error states in the interface.

### Handling Blockchain and Upload Delays

IPFS uploads and blockchain confirmations are asynchronous and can take different amounts of time. We added separate loading and status states for uploading, transaction submission, network switching, and confirmation. This makes the workflow clearer and prevents users from accidentally submitting duplicate transactions while a previous action is still pending.

**The problem it solves**

Important digital documents can be modified, replaced, or disputed after they are created. Proving that a specific contract, design, research file, invoice, or creative work existed at a particular time usually requires trusting a centralized service or sharing the entire document.

ProofChain makes this process easier and safer by storing only a document’s fingerprint, title, wallet address, and timestamp on Ethereum. The original file remains off-chain, while anyone with the proof link can independently verify that the registered fingerprint matches the document.

People can use ProofChain to:

- Prove authorship and priority of creative work, designs, code, manuscripts, or research.
- Record versions of contracts, NDAs, invoices, and compliance documents.
- Timestamp intellectual property disclosures and confidential business files.
- Verify that a document has not been altered since it was registered.
- Share tamper-resistant proof without relying on a central authority.
- Replace manual email trails, screenshots, or third-party timestamping services with a transparent on-chain record.

ProofChain does not publish the document contents on Ethereum. It anchors the document’s identity and existence, allowing users to prove **when** a file existed without unnecessarily exposing **what** is inside it.

**Overall**

ProofChain is a privacy-focused proof-of-existence dApp built on Ethereum Sepolia.

It allows users to upload a document to IPFS and register its fingerprint, title, wallet address, and timestamp on-chain. The document itself is not stored on Ethereum, so users can prove that a specific file existed at a particular time without unnecessarily exposing its contents.

ProofChain makes existing workflows safer and easier for contracts, NDAs, research, creative work, invoices, and compliance documents. Instead of relying on email histories, screenshots, or a centralized timestamping service, users can share a verification link that anyone can independently validate through Ethereum.

The project demonstrates how Ethereum can act as a trusted, tamper-resistant anchor for real-world documents while following a minimal-disclosure approach.

Team **Status200** -- [Vedant Modhave](https://github.com/VedantModhave), [Jatin Gorana](https://github.com/Jatin-gorana)

### VeilEscrow
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/veilescrow-29d9) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/StackedUpAman/VeilEscrow) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/-M0rr45dN-g) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20to%20Devcon%20--%20NITK%20Surathkal-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-nitk-surathkal.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Private payments, trusted agreements.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

*For the demo video, please check the README file in the GitHub repo linked.*[](url)
2-demo videos
https://youtu.be/QFrrM6-IdZQ
https://youtu.be/aC4ShfRYFS0

**Problem Statement**

Freelancing platforms like Upwork solve a basic trust problem between clients and freelancers: the client doesn't want to pay before seeing the work, while the freelancer doesn't want to work without knowing they'll be paid. For fixed-price work, Upwork addresses this by having the client fund a milestone upfront and holding those funds until the freelancer submits the work and the client approves it.

However, this model introduces a centralized intermediary. For example, if a client hires a freelancer for $500, the platform sits between both parties, holds the funds, manages the release process, and handles disputes. The platform also charges service-related fees.

There is a second problem when these interactions move to public blockchains: financial activity becomes highly visible. If a client pays a freelancer 0.5 ETH, the transaction can expose the wallets involved, the amount transferred, and potentially allow anyone to study their broader on-chain financial activity.

**Our Solution**

VeilEscrow combines the familiar idea of freelance escrow with blockchain-based automation and privacy.

Imagine a client hires a freelancer to build a website for 0.5 ETH.

Instead of sending the money directly to the freelancer:

Client → VeilEscrow Smart Contract → Freelancer

the client deposits the 0.5 ETH into a smart contract. The contract holds the funds and enforces the job's rules:

Create Job → Submit Work → Approve → Release Payment

If the freelancer submits the work and the client approves it, the contract releases the payment automatically according to the predefined rules. If there is a dispute, the funds remain locked while the dispute process takes place.

This removes the need for a traditional platform to manually control the escrowed funds.

But VeilEscrow also addresses the privacy problem.

Alongside the escrow system, we integrate a Railgun-powered private payment module. Users can shield public ETH into private WETH, transfer it privately using zero-knowledge proofs, and later unshield it back to a public address.

So instead of exposing a straightforward public transaction like:

Client wallet → 0.5 ETH → Freelancer wallet

the private payment layer demonstrates how the financial movement can occur without exposing the normal sender-recipient-amount relationship.

In short, VeilEscrow combines two properties that traditional freelance platforms and ordinary public blockchains handle separately:

Escrow: "The money is protected until the agreed conditions are met."
Privacy: "The financial activity does not have to be publicly exposed."

The current hackathon version demonstrates these two systems independently—JobEscrow on Anvil and private payments through Railgun on Sepolia—with the next step being to cryptographically connect private payments to individual escrow jobs.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges Faced
Connecting two very different blockchain systems
The biggest architectural challenge was keeping the freelance escrow logic and private payment system separate while figuring out how they could eventually work together. The escrow contract runs on Anvil, while Railgun operates on Sepolia, creating a clear network and integration boundary.
Designing the escrow state machine
We had to carefully define how a job moves through Created → Submitted → Approved/Disputed → Resolved, while ensuring that only the correct party can perform each action. This included handling edge cases like repeated approvals, unauthorized actions, and disputes raised at different stages.
Building a fair dispute mechanism
Escrow becomes more complicated when the client and freelancer disagree. We implemented a response window, allowed the other party to submit a response, and added an owner-based resolution mechanism. Handling the case where the other party doesn't respond required a separate claim flow.
Integrating Railgun's client-side ZK system
Getting private payments working wasn't simply a normal blockchain transaction. We had to initialize the Railgun WASM engine, synchronize private balances, generate zero-knowledge proofs in the browser, and handle shield, private transfer, and unshield operations.
Managing privacy without losing usability
The private wallets are deliberately ephemeral for the demo. This means their keys cannot simply be persisted like a normal wallet, while the UI still needs to clearly communicate balances, addresses, transaction states, and the risk of losing access after a page reload.
Handling multiple networks in one application
The same frontend operates across Anvil for escrow and Sepolia for Railgun. We therefore needed network-aware UI and safeguards so that users don't accidentally attempt an escrow transaction on Sepolia or a Railgun operation on Anvil.
Understanding what should actually be public vs private
A major design challenge was deciding what the escrow contract should know and what Railgun should hide. The contract needs to know things like the job status and who can approve or resolve it, while the actual payment movement should remain private.
The hardest unresolved challenge: linking private payment to escrow
The current system demonstrates escrow and private payments independently. The difficult next step is proving that a specific private Railgun payment actually funds a specific escrow job, without revealing the payment amount or parties publicly. This is where the commitment/verification architecture becomes necessary.

**Private Wallets and Payments**

We use Railgun’s client-side ZK system to enable private payments: public ETH is shielded into private WETH, transferred privately between Railgun wallets, and later unshielded back to a public 0x address, with zero-knowledge proofs generated locally in the browser using WASM. For the demo, we generate two disposable Railgun wallets (A and B) in memory using RailgunSigner.random(). Their private keys are never stored in localStorage or environment variables, and each wallet gets its own 0zk... address.

### SECUREID
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/secureid-bdac) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ShreyasHebbar1/SECUREID.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/1rTrB7WqAlxpJitvzcSYKpsG151sj0yUj) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/HmMJWcDbDOY) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20to%20Devcon%20--%20NITK%20Surathkal-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-nitk-surathkal.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A secure verification

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges Faced

The biggest challenge was implementing privacy-preserving verification within a limited development timeframe while understanding and integrating unfamiliar blockchain and cryptographic concepts. We had to work through the interaction between zero-knowledge proofs, Ethereum smart contracts, wallet authentication, and frontend verification.

Another challenge was ensuring that sensitive identity information was never unnecessarily exposed or stored on-chain, while still making the verification process simple enough for users to understand and use.

We also faced challenges with Ethereum Sepolia testnet transactions, wallet connectivity, smart-contract integration, and debugging cryptographic verification flows**.

Working under the hackathon time constraint required us to prioritize the core privacy and verification functionality and build a working proof-of-concept rather than attempting to implement every feature at production scale.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem We Solve
Traditional KYC or human verification services (like Persona, Jumio, or Stripe Identity) require users to upload passport photos and biometrics to centralized databases. This model presents critical flaws:

Centralized Data Leaks: Storing database copies of passports, driver's licenses, and biometrics creates high-value targets for hackers, leading to massive identity leaks.
Lack of User Ownership: Users lose control of their personal information the moment they upload it to a server.
Linkability & Sybil Attacks: Web3 applications need a way to verify unique humans (Sybil resistance) without linking their real-world identities across different dApps.
User Friction: Having to go through full document uploads for every individual website is repetitive and slow.
The SECUREID Solution
SECUREID introduces a Zero-Storage SSO Gateway that verifies identity parameters entirely on the client-side:

Zero Raw Data Storage: Biometrics and government ID scans are captured, cropped, and immediately hashed locally using Keccak256 inside the browser canvas. The raw files are wiped from memory and never uploaded.
On-Chain Soulbound Identity Passes (SBTs): Verifying the local hash creates an on-chain registry of unique nullifiers. Successful checks mint a non-transferable SBT representing a verified identity to the user's wallet.
Private Age Gating (zk-SNARKs): The user generates a ZK proof proving their birth year meets age criteria (e.g. Age $\ge$ 18) without disclosing their exact date of birth or name.
🛠️ The Tech Stack
Smart Contracts & Blockchain: Solidity (v0.8.24), Hardhat, and OpenZeppelin ERC721.
Zero-Knowledge Circuit: Circom (for ZK arithmetic constraints) and SnarkJS (Groth16 proving in the browser).
Frontend SSO Engine: Vite, React, Lucide-React, and Tailwind/Vanilla CSS.
Web3 Integration: Ethers.js (v6) for MetaMask connection and Sepolia testnet transaction pipelines.
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
Decoupled Redirect: A gated portal (e.g. PulseTV Premium) requires verification and redirects the user to the SECUREID gateway.
Local Camera Scanning: The user takes a Face Liveness scan (in a circle crop) and an Aadhar ID card scan.
Canvas Hashing: The webcam frames are processed inside an HTML5 <canvas> and hashed locally. The raw biometrics are destroyed in memory.
ZKP Witness Generation: The browser generates a ZK-SNARK proof verifying that:
The user possesses a credential signed by an authorized issuer public key.
The age calculated from the credential timestamp satisfies the condition.
A unique nullifier hash is computed to block double-KYC attacks.
On-Chain Validation: The ZK proof is verified by the IdentityRegistry.sol contract on Sepolia, minting an SBT to the user's wallet.
Decryption & Access: The callback unlocks access to the calling dApp, unblurring the premium interface.
