### CargoSync – Smart Cargo Monitoring System
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cargosync-blockchainbased-multisensor-cargo-integrity-monitoring-system-c515) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Surajvhankalas90/cargosync) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Port%20Mortem%202026%20--%20Code%20Resurrection%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://portmortem.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Smart IoT-powered cargo monitoring with blockchain

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![GPS](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPS-333333?style=flat-square) ![SHA-256 Hashes](https://img.shields.io/badge/SHA--256%20Hashes-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building CargoSync involved integrating multiple hardware and software components into one reliable system. Some of the major challenges we faced were:

### 1. Sensor Integration
Interfacing multiple sensors (DHT11, SW-420, Reed Switch, and Neo-6M GPS) with the ESP32 while ensuring stable and accurate readings was challenging. We carefully calibrated the sensors and optimized the firmware to minimize noise and false readings.

### 2. Real-Time Data Communication
Maintaining a stable MQTT connection between the ESP32 and the backend was difficult due to network interruptions. We implemented reconnection logic and efficient data transmission to improve reliability.

### 3. GPS Accuracy
Obtaining consistent GPS coordinates, especially indoors or in areas with weak satellite signals, affected tracking accuracy. We improved reliability by validating GPS data before displaying it on the dashboard.

### 4. Blockchain Integration
Recording critical events on the Ethereum Sepolia Testnet introduced challenges such as transaction delays and gas management. We addressed this by storing only SHA-256 hashes of important events, ensuring tamper-proof verification while keeping the system efficient.

### 5. Real-Time Dashboard Synchronization
Keeping the dashboard synchronized with continuously changing sensor values required efficient backend APIs and database updates. We optimized data flow to provide smooth live telemetry and historical analytics.

Overcoming these challenges helped us gain practical experience in IoT, embedded systems, blockchain integration, real-time communication, and full-stack development while building a robust cargo monitoring platform.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem

Modern logistics and supply chain operations often lack continuous, trustworthy, and real-time cargo monitoring. During transportation, cargo may experience temperature fluctuations, excessive humidity, strong vibrations, unauthorized door openings, or even theft. Most existing systems either provide limited monitoring or store data in centralized databases, making records vulnerable to tampering.

This creates major challenges for logistics companies, manufacturers, pharmaceutical suppliers, and food distributors who require secure proof that cargo conditions remained within safe limits throughout the journey.

## Our Solution

CargoSync addresses these challenges by combining IoT, Blockchain, AI, GPS Tracking, and Full Stack Development into one intelligent monitoring platform.

The system continuously monitors cargo conditions using multiple sensors connected to an ESP32. Live sensor data is transmitted through MQTT, stored in MongoDB, and displayed on a real-time dashboard. Whenever abnormal conditions are detected, CargoSync immediately generates alerts and securely records critical events using SHA-256 hashing anchored on the Ethereum Sepolia Testnet.

Along with live GPS tracking, historical analytics, configurable alert thresholds, and AI-generated journey reports, CargoSync provides a transparent, tamper-proof, and intelligent cargo monitoring solution for modern supply chains.

SURAJ VHANKALAS

> Auto-Buy for the open web, powered by Prava.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

**Merchant Payment Sandboxes**: Neither Zepto nor Swiggy publishes a payment test environment. We solved this by creating a transparent /capabilities badge system that explicitly tags every step as real, sandbox, or disclosed_mock so judges have 100% transparency.
**Cold-Start Prediction**: Single households don't have historical reorder data on day one. We solved this by seeding initial cadences from Instacart market dataset category priors and providing an explainable EWMA recalibration loop as users complete purchases.
**Credential Custody Safety**: Ensuring zero credit card or passkey data touched persistent storage required designing a strict consume-once memory boundary for Prava one-time tokens.
**Reviewer Password**:  reviewer123

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem:** Households and small teams sit on a bad binary every week: over-order recurring essentials to avoid running out, or under-order and pay panic prices. It's an attention problem, not a decision problem — you already know you’ll need coffee in 10 days or that a team software subscription renews on Friday. Most shopping agents wait for you to type a prompt. A chat window doesn't replace proactive replenishment.

**The Solution:** Restock is Auto-Buy for the open web. It tracks trigger dates — predicted depletion for physical consumables or known renewal dates for SaaS subscriptions — and proactively proposes and executes purchases through Prava’s passkey-approved, merchant-scoped mandate flow before you run out.

Restock operates on two distinct tracks:

1. **Restock Home** (Consumer Consumables): Predicts when household items (coffee, printer paper, milk, detergent) will deplete using an Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) recalibration model and price drop triggers, executing reorders via merchant MCP tools (Zepto & Swiggy).
2. **Restock Teams** (B2B SaaS Renewals): Tracks software subscription renewal dates, proposing automatic renewals or right-sizing switches (e.g. annual plan savings) to avoid unexpected auto-renewals.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Restock interfaces with Prava’s payment virtualization rails, which utilize Visa credentials to issue scoped, one-time virtual card tokens and dynamic CVVs upon user passkey approval. 

Restock's payment completion pipeline (`payments/prava_client.py`) receives opaque credential references, executes merchant checkouts through a consume-once server boundary, and reports terminal transaction status back to Prava (`report_status`), validating Visa confirmation responses (`visa_confirmation: SUCCESS`).

**OpenAI**

Restock’s core orchestrator agent is built on the official OpenAI Agents SDK (`openai-agents` package) running `gpt-5.4-mini`. 

The agent runs autonomous scheduled evaluation ticks to analyze predicted depletion dates and live price drops, synthesizing natural-language purchase proposals and sequencing tool calls. Code-level Guardrails enforce per-item, per-transaction, and monthly budget caps before requesting Prava payment sessions, ensuring the LLM cannot exceed user spend limits.

**Best Prava Adapter for the NANDA Town**

We built the standalone `nanda_prava_adapter` package (submitted via upstream Pull Request #208 to `projnanda/nandatown`), which implements NANDA Town's payment plugin specification over Prava's REST API.

The adapter exposes NANDA's standard `quote`, `pay`, `verify_payment`, and `refund` interfaces, mapping NANDA payment intents into Prava Sessions and mandate status checks. It includes a complete test suite, interactive sandbox runner, and an installable `nest.plugins.payments` entry point.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

Restock reimagines agentic commerce by replacing generic AI chat prompts with a physical, tactile product experience designed for zero-friction proactive buying:

1. **Physical Pantry Shelf Metaphor**:
   Instead of flat SaaS tables or text-only lists, Restock Home presents a physical pantry layout where products sit on two-tier wooden shelves with real manufacturer photography, natural sunlight/shadows, and physically attached cardboard labels. Restock Teams visualizes subscriptions as 3D extruded provider plaques.

2. **Photorealistic 3D WebGL Parcel Reveal**:
   Opening product details triggers an unboxing interaction—a shoebox-style WebGL 3D cardboard parcel opens smoothly, allowing the selected product to rise from the box into a floating focus view before purchase approval.

3. **Proactive Single-Tap Decision Controls**:
   Restock eliminates prompt typing. Proactive depletion and price-drop notifications present three clear, high-contrast actions: **Approve** (initiates Prava passkey mandate), **Adjust** (modifies quantity/amount), and **Skip** (defers reorder).

4. **Honest Point-of-Action Trust Badges**:
   Every approval surface features human-readable spend caps and clear `Real`, `Sandbox`, or `Disclosed Simulation` badges directly above action buttons, giving users 100% transparency over payment boundaries.

5. **Multi-Channel & Responsive Excellence**:
   Fully responsive across Mobile, Tablet, and Desktop with specialized typography (Inter, Radio Canada Big, Geist Pixel), plus a live Slack Bolt Socket Mode integration that updates button states in real-time once resolved.

### NagarDrishit-AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nagardrishit-1d82) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/TuhinMandal27/NagarDrishit-AI) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://nagar-drishit-ai.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HexaFalls%202-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hexafalls2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> See it. Snap it. Solve it.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![fast.ai](https://img.shields.io/badge/fast.ai-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

**Inconsistent GeoJSON ward data.** Ward-boundary files name the ward-number field differently across publishers (ward_no, WARDNO, etc.), silently breaking auto-detection. Fixed with inspectWardGeojson.js to inspect the real property names, plus a fallback candidate list.

**Ward polygons only cover Kolkata.** Citizens elsewhere in West Bengal got ward: null. Added a Nominatim reverse-geocoding fallback for locality/district/state — respecting its 1 req/sec limit and required User-Agent, and made it best-effort so a slow API never blocks a complaint.

**Merging two independently-built AI services.** The vision classifier (Flask) and chatbot (FastAPI) were built separately. Kept aiService.js's existing mock response shape as the contract, so swapping in the real HTTP call needed zero changes downstream.

**Model detects more than the UI supports.** The vision model's issue vocabulary is far larger than the app's five categories. Solved with a many-to-one category_mapper.py, while still preserving the model's raw label for later use.

**The problem it solves**

Reporting a civic issue in Indian cities today means either a clunky government portal nobody finishes, or a WhatsApp photo to a local councillor that goes nowhere — untracked, unrouted, and unaccountable. NagarDrishti AI fixes the two biggest failure points: citizens not knowing who to report to, and authorities not knowing an issue exists.

**For citizens:** 

- Snap a photo — AI auto-detects the issue type (pothole, garbage, streetlight, waterlogging, dumping, fire/smoke, exposed wiring), severity, and priority, and drafts a description.

- Location auto-matches to the correct KMC ward (or locality/district for outside Kolkata) — no guessing who's responsible.

- Track any complaint by ID, or ask the AI assistant (Nagrik Mitra) civic questions.

**For admins:** 

- Issues auto-route to the right ward admin (falling back to state/super admin) — no manual triage.

- Instant in-app + SMS notification the moment a matching complaint lands.

- Live dashboard: totals, status breakdown, category breakdown, and ward-by-ward hotspots — automatically scoped to each admin's jurisdiction.

**Net effect:**  turns unstructured complaint photos into structured, prioritized, department-tagged, routed, and notified data — so urgent hazards get seen faster, citizens get a real paper trail, and administrators get city-wide visibility instead of a pile of unread tickets.

**Best Use of MongoDB Atlas**

**Flexible schema for uneven data.** An Issue document mixes optional AI fields (severity, priority score, raw issue type), an optional voice note, an optional AI-drafted email, and either a ward number or locality/district/state — depending on how and where it was filed. Document storage handles this naturally, without sparse relational columns.

**Aggregation pipelines drive the dashboard.** $match + $group + $sort (with $cond for resolved counts) compute live totals, category breakdowns, and ward hotspots directly in the database — no pulling all records into app code.
Indexes match real query patterns. Issue is compound-indexed on { category, status, ward } plus { createdAt: -1 }; Notification on { recipientAdmin, read, createdAt } — built to match the actual filtered queries in the controllers, not added generically.

**Access control enforced at the query level.** Every issue/analytics/notification query is scoped server-side to the logged-in admin's ward or state, so a ward admin and a state admin query the same collection but only ever retrieve their own jurisdiction's data.

**One Atlas cluster, three independent services.** The Node backend, Flask ML service, and FastAPI chatbot all connect through the same MONGO_URI — a single managed, always-on data layer shared across services that are built and can scale independently.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

**One model, two distinct capabilities.** Gemini's multimodal input handles vision (photo → structured issue analysis) and its text generation handles multilingual drafting (complaint emails) and conversation (Nagrik Mitra chatbot) — three real product features from a single API, not a one-off gimmick.

**Structured output, not free-text parsing.** The vision call uses response_schema with a Pydantic model (CivicIssueSchema) and response_mime_type: application/json, so Gemini returns guaranteed-valid, typed fields (issue_type, severity, confidence, department) directly usable by the backend — no regex-scraping a text response.

**Powers the conversational layer too.** The Nagrik Mitra assistant (meow/backend) uses Gemini via langchain-google-genai for open-ended civic Q&A and complaint guidance — extending the same API from a perception task to a reasoning/dialogue task within one product.
 
**Structured output, not free-text parsing.** The vision call uses response_schema with a Pydantic model (CivicIssueSchema) and response_mime_type: application/json, so Gemini returns guaranteed-valid, typed fields (issue_type, severity, confidence, department) directly usable by the backend — no regex-scraping a text response.

**Open Innovation**

**We combined multiple independent systems ourselves** — a vision-classification service (ml-service/), a conversational assistant (meow/), ward-boundary geospatial matching (wardLookupService.js), and a Node/React civic platform were built as separate pieces and integrated into one working product — not a single off-the-shelf API wrapped in a UI.

**We designed the logic from scratch, not from a dataset or template** — there was no existing pipeline for "map a photo + GPS pin to the correct ward admin and notify them." We built the point-in-polygon ward matching, the Nominatim fallback for non-Kolkata areas, the five-category mapping from the model's larger vocabulary, and the admin escalation hierarchy ourselves.

**The solution is genuinely open-ended, not a fixed deliverable** — we built it to extend (new cities, more categories, more languages) rather than to satisfy one narrow spec, e.g. aiService.js keeps a fixed contract specifically so the ML backend can be swapped or scaled independently.

**It targets a public-good problem with no obvious commercial category**  — better citizen-government responsiveness isn't a funded or "expected" hackathon vertical, which is exactly what makes it fit Open Innovation rather than a domain-specific track.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Sending money abroad or across banks is slow (1-5 days), costly ($15-50 per transfer), and non-transparent — Zpay settles in ~3 seconds on Stellar with near-zero fees

No easy way for freelancers to trust unknown clients for payment — Zpay's Soroban escrow locks funds until work is delivered, with an arbiter to resolve disputes

Wallet addresses are long and error-prone (56 characters) — Zpay gives every user a simple Universal ID like div@Zp

Splitting group bills is manual and awkward — Zpay tracks who paid what automatically, on-chain

Idle crypto earns nothing — Zpay's Vault lets users stake ZPAY or deposit XLM to earn yield (up to ~24% APR)

Indian merchants can't easily accept crypto — Zpay's UPI bridge lets users pay any UPI QR using crypto, merchant gets INR

Network fees discourage small/frequent payments — Zpay sponsors gas so users pay 0 XLM fees

**Challenges we ran into**

Storing private keys safely was a real challenge — initially kept as plain text, later fixed with AES-256 encryption so a database leak can't expose user wallets

PIN security was weak at first — moved from plain storage to bcrypt hashing, with a silent upgrade so old users aren't broken

Handling escrow disputes fairly needed an extra "arbiter" role instead of just buyer/seller logic, since Soroban's resolve function wasn't fully usable yet — worked around it using refund + manual token transfer

Making UPI and crypto talk to each other was hard — crypto settles instantly on-chain, but UPI/INR settlement needs a licensed partner, so real bank payout isn't live yet, only simulated on testnet

Deciding between custodial (easy signup) vs non-custodial (user owns keys) wallets was a tough tradeoff — chose custodial first for smooth onboarding, knowing it adds security responsibility on our side

Preventing abuse (spam logins, repeated payment attempts) needed rate-limiting logic added across multiple routes, not just one

![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Noir](https://img.shields.io/badge/Noir-333333?style=flat-square) ![Groq](https://img.shields.io/badge/Groq-333333?style=flat-square) ![Soroban](https://img.shields.io/badge/Soroban-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ultrahonk](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ultrahonk-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

The Soroban WASM Memory Bottleneck: Deploying an UltraHonk ZK verifier onto Stellar's Soroban smart contract platform originally hit strict execution and memory limits. The standard verifier logic was too heavy for a no_std Rust environment.

The Fix: I had to strip down the dependencies in the ultrahonk-soroban-verifier crate, optimize the field element decoding to exactly 456 elements (14,592 bytes), and pre-allocate memory buffers during the Sumcheck and Shplemini protocol evaluations to keep the contract footprint within Soroban's native constraints.

Designing ZK-Friendly Hashing on a Hackathon Timeline: Traditional ZK-optimized hashes like Poseidon or Pedersen require large lookup tables and complex implementations that were too cumbersome to spin up rapidly in Noir v0.36.0.

The Fix: To maintain momentum, I developed lightweight custom polynomial field arithmetic functions (custom_hash_1 and custom_hash_2) over the BN254 scalar field. While less cryptographically secure than standard implementations (and marked as a limitation for production), they successfully compressed the constraint count to ~41,000, allowing fluid browser-side proof generation.

Browser-Side WASM Memory Exhaustion: Bundling both the Noir ACVM compiler stack and the Barretenberg proving backend inside a Vite/React application routinely caused dependency caching issues and memory spikes during the 5-second proof generation process.

The Fix: I configured Vite with specific --force routines to continuously clear out the WASM dependency cache and meticulously optimized the ProofGenerator.ts script to stream the decompressed witness stack as a single-map gzip rather than a heavy multi-stack object.

**The problem it solves**

The current $800 billion/year cross-border remittance market forces users into a brutal compromise: choose traditional banks (like SWIFT) for privacy at the expense of high fees (5–10%) and long wait times (3–5 days), or choose public blockchains for near-instant, low-cost transfers at the cost of exposing sensitive financial data.

Public ledgers permanently broadcast a sender’s identity, the recipient's address, and the exact transactional volume to the entire world. A worker sending a portion of their hard-earned paycheck home shouldn't have to sacrifice their basic financial privacy to avoid predatory banking fees.

What People Can Use It For (How It Makes Tasks Easier & Safer)
zkRemit merges the speed and negligible costs of the Stellar network with the cutting-edge financial privacy of zero-knowledge cryptography.

Private Global Remittances: Migrant workers can send stablecoins (USDC) across international corridors without exposing their identity, how much money they earn, or where it is going.

On-Chain Regulatory Compliance: Users don't have to choose between privacy and legality. The system proves on-chain that the sender is fully KYC-verified and that the transfer adheres to strict AML corridor limits—all without revealing the underlying private data.

Replay & Fraud Prevention: Transactions remain robustly secure. Every transfer utilizes a unique cryptographic nullifier generated by the user's secret, ensuring no transaction can be double-spent or hijacked on the public ledger.

Invisible AI Risk Auditing: Compliance officers can rely on an LLM "copilot" that risk-assesses transaction metadata (such as routing and timing frequencies) without ever compromising or seeing the hidden financial amounts.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
KrishiRakshak bridges the language-tech divide for India's 140+ million farmers by providing AI-powered crop disease diagnosis in 23 Indian languages.

Key Features & Use Cases:-
1)Photo Diagnosis: Farmers upload a picture of a diseased leaf to get instant    identification, symptoms, and treatment options.

2)Voice-First Accessibility: Includes voice input (ASR) for illiterate/semi-literate farmers and reads full diagnoses aloud (TTS) in their native dialect.

3)Eco-Friendly Safety: Prioritizes organic remedies, provides chemical instructions with safe pre-harvest intervals, and categorizes risks (Low/Warning/Critical).

Before vs. After:-
Access: Shamed from traveling to distant offices to snapping a photo at home.
Language: Replaces unreadable English/Hindi pesticide labels with localized audio and text.
Application: Prevents over-application of chemicals via precision organic and chemical guidance.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge 1: Sarvam TTS 1000-Char Limit
Hurdle: Comprehensive diagnoses exceeded the API limit, cutting off critical treatment info.

Solution: Developed a text-chunking engine to split text at sentence boundaries, made sequential API calls, and used Python’s struct module to binary-merge the raw PCM streams into a single valid WAV file.

Challenge 2: Unsupported TTS Languages
Hurdle: 10 of the 23 target languages lacked native voice models in the Sarvam API.

Solution: Created a backend linguistic fallback matrix. Unsupported scripts maintain their native text on-screen but route to the closest phonetic equivalent for audio (e.g., Maithili to Hindi, Konkani to Marathi).

Challenge 3: Multi-Language UI Label Alignment
Hurdle: The text-to-speech engine was reading section headers (like "Symptoms:") in English instead of the farmer's native tongue.

Solution: Unified the backend config so localized UI labels are dynamically injected into the text payload before generating the audio.

Challenge 4: Fragmented Device & Camera Support
Hurdle: Budget Android phones ran mismatched browsers, causing getUserMedia() crashes or low-res streams.

Solution: Implemented defensive camera constraints with automatic fallback routes, forced canvas-based frame captures for a uniform image format, and aggressively cleared streams to prevent memory leaks.

### Cyphra
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cyphra-1736) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/choksi2212/theoriginals-cyphra) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://business-website-lake-chi.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/TTDrZziL2_w) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Built for the Field Trusted Under Fire

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSOC](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSOC-333333?style=flat-square) ![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/Database-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern military and defence organisations face three critical challenges simultaneously:

1. **Network attacks go undetected for hours** — traditional rule-based IDS miss novel attacks, and security teams can't monitor dashboards 24/7. By the time a human notices, data is already exfiltrated.

2. **Communication content is encrypted, but metadata isn't** — adversaries use traffic analysis (timing, volume, frequency) to extract intelligence without breaking encryption. They know WHO is talking to WHOM, WHEN, and HOW OFTEN.

3. **Separate tools for detection, response, and communication** — teams juggle 5-10 different products (SIEM, IDS, firewall, messenger, VPN) that don't talk to each other. Alerts in one system don't trigger actions in another.

---

## What People Can Use It For

**Security Operations Teams:**
- Deploy on any Windows machine → instantly monitors ALL network traffic on that NIC
- Automatically blocks attackers via firewall within 5 seconds of detection (no human needed)
- Demo mode lets you simulate attacks for training exercises without real risk

**Military/Defence Units:**
- Detect electronic warfare (jamming, spoofing, rogue nodes) from signal telemetry
- Communicate with self-destructing messages that leave zero forensic trace
- Switch mission presets based on threat level — one click changes encryption cadence, traffic padding, and routing

**Any Organisation Handling Sensitive Data:**
- End-to-end encrypted team chat where the server NEVER sees plaintext
- Post-quantum cryptography (Kyber-1024) protects against future quantum attacks TODAY
- Ghost Codes let people share identity without exposing email/phone numbers

---

## How It Makes Things Easier/Safer

| Without CYPHRA | With CYPHRA |
|---|---|
| Manually review security logs hours later | AI classifies every flow in 5ms, auto-blocks threats |
| Use separate apps for chat + security + monitoring | One unified platform for all three |
| Encrypted messages but metadata exposed | Traffic padding + mixnet hides communication patterns |
| Key compromise = all past messages readable | Double Ratchet = unique key per message, old keys deleted |
| Need expensive enterprise SIEM ($100K+/year) | Self-hosted, runs on a single laptop, free |
| Detection only (alert fatigue) | Detection + autonomous response (blocks before human even sees the alert) |

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Rust crypto libraries couldn't compile to WebAssembly**
Our in-house Rust crates use `libsodium` and `liboqs` (C FFI dependencies) which are incompatible with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target. Solution: We built a separate pure-Rust WASM crate using `aes-gcm`, `x25519-dalek`, and `ed25519-dalek` (zero C dependencies) — giving us real crypto in the browser at 153KB.

**2. XGBoost GPU training crashed with Out-of-Memory (8GB VRAM)**
Training on 19.5M samples required 15GB VRAM — our initial GPU only had 8GB. Solution: Retrained XGBoost on CPU first, then when we got access to an RTX 5070 Ti (12GB), we successfully trained all models on GPU in 65 minutes.

**3. VedDB uses a proprietary binary protocol — no Node.js client existed**
Our custom Rust database doesn't speak JSON, Redis, or HTTP. We tried raw TCP probing (JSON, text, RESP) — nothing worked. Solution: We call `veddb-client.exe` as a subprocess from Node.js and parse the output. Later upgraded to a proper Rust REST API server that uses the native async client internally with TLS 1.3.

**4. Live traffic scored 95%+ threat (false positives) on real Wi-Fi**
The ML model was trained on 2017 lab traffic. Modern Windows telemetry (Teams, OneDrive, Discord) didn't match the "benign" distribution it learned. Solution: Set `dataset_onehot` flags to 0.0 for live traffic — model correctly identifies real benign patterns. Demo attacks use `onehot_0=1.0` to classify against the trained CICIDS2017 domain.

**5. LightGBM model files corrupted by Git line-ending conversion**
Git's `autocrlf` converted LF to CRLF in the `.txt` model files, breaking LightGBM's parser (`"Model format error, expect a tree here"`). Solution: Stripped all `\r` bytes from the files and added `*.txt binary` to `.gitattributes` to prevent future corruption.

**CyberSecurity**

CYPHRA is a **full-stack cybersecurity platform** that addresses all three pillars of the cybersecurity triad — detection, response, and secure communications:

**Threat Detection & Classification:**
We capture live network packets using Scapy + Npcap, extract 100 CICFlowMeter features per flow, and classify them using a 6-model gradient boosted ensemble (LightGBM + XGBoost + CatBoost) trained on 19.5 million real-world attack flows from 4 published cybersecurity datasets. The system identifies DDoS, brute force, port scans, web attacks, botnets, and infiltration in real-time with 98.85% accuracy.

**Autonomous Incident Response:**
Unlike traditional IDS that only generate alerts, CYPHRA autonomously neutralizes threats — blocking attacker IPs via Windows Firewall (Tier 1), injecting TCP RST packets to kill active malicious connections (Tier 2), and rate-tracking repeat offenders for automatic escalation (Tier 3). All within 5 seconds of detection.

**Secure Communications & Cryptography:**
End-to-end encrypted messaging using AES-256-GCM (Rust WebAssembly) with PQC-Hybrid key exchange (Kyber-1024 + X25519) — quantum-resistant before most enterprises have even started planning for it. Self-destructing messages, traffic padding to defeat timing analysis, and multi-hop onion routing for metadata protection.

**Signal & Electronic Warfare Defence:**
Real-time monitoring of Wi-Fi signal integrity (SNR, latency, jitter, timing drift) with automated detection of jamming, spoofing, beaconing, and man-in-the-middle attacks using feature-weight scoring matched to trained model importance values.

The entire system runs on real hardware telemetry and real packet capture — not simulations — making it directly applicable to SOC operations, defence communications, and critical infrastructure protection.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Data Mining](https://img.shields.io/badge/Data%20Mining-333333?style=flat-square) ![Scraping Tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/Scraping%20Tools-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

A junior developer opens a file that's been running in production for years. No documentation. The original author left. The commit history is long but unreadable in any reasonable amount of time. They're told to "add a field" or "fix this bug," and every tool they have — Copilot, Cursor, Codex — will happily generate code anywhere in that file, with equal confidence everywhere. None of them know the file is too big to hold in your head, and none of them know which parts of it are load-bearing.

**Challenges we ran into**

The single-author integration sprawl. Lore's architecture spans PyDriller, Tree-sitter,  FastAPI, VS Code extension API, D3, GitHub Actions, and Gemini — seven distinct technologies, each with its own setup, failure modes, and quirks, built and wired together by one person. The hardest part wasn't any single integration; it was keeping the seams between them clean enough that a failure in one (Atlas timeout, IPFS unreachable, Ethereum RPC down) didn't cascade into the others. Designing the failure-mode table — what degrades and what still works for each component — took longer than building several of the components themselves.
Creating a visual studio extension seemed to be a new experience for our team which provided new challenges in both backend and frontend sides.

**Gemini**

Gemini has three jobs, and in all three it routes or rewrites — never invents facts.
Question routing (/query): when a developer asks something like "why was this rewritten?", Gemini picks which capsule fields (decision, risk, expert, etc.) are relevant to the question. Output is checked against a whitelist — it can only point at fields that actually exist.
Readability rewrite: raw decision text from PR/commit messages is often terse ("sync dispatcher acceptable until 10k req/s"). Gemini rewrites it in plain English for display, while the original stays available on hover with its source link. Worst case here is low — the source is always one click away.
Task-to-region matching (/scope) — the big one: a dev types "add a field for currency conversion" on a 10,000-line file, and Gemini reasons over a pre-computed function/call-graph index (never the raw code) to return which line ranges are relevant, plus any "looks tempting but isn't safe" caution ranges. Every returned range is validated against the real Tree-sitter index — anything outside known function boundaries gets rejected.
Across all three: Gemini decides which verified thing to show or how to phrase it, never what's true. It's also never on the /analyse hot path, so the 100ms ambient guarantee is untouched — it only fires when a developer types a question or task, where slower responses are expected.

**Open Innovation**

Lore fits Open Innovation because it occupies a moment in the development workflow that no existing tool addresses: the thirty seconds after a developer is assigned a task and before they write any code, when they're staring at a file too large to understand and have no way to know where their change actually belongs or what they'd break by guessing wrong. AI assistants, linters, and documentation tools all operate either before this moment (writing docs nobody reads) or after it (suggesting code once you've already picked a spot) — none of them help with the spot-picking itself, and worse, tools like Copilot or Cursor will generate confidently at your cursor regardless of how dangerous that location is, because they have no concept of "this file is too big and tangled to reason about safely." Lore's combination of pre-computed repository history, structural analysis, and task-aware focus creates an entirely new interaction — dimming a massive file down to the handful of lines that matter for your specific task, while flagging the regions that look tempting but aren't safe — which isn't a feature added to an existing category of tool, it's a category that doesn't currently exist.

**Gen AI&ML**

Lore's relationship to GenAI isn't "we use an LLM," it's "we're the missing piece that makes every other GenAI coding tool trustworthy." Think about where the entire industry is headed: Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Claude Code — every one of them is racing toward more autonomous agents that read your codebase and make changes with less human oversight. That's the trend, and it's accelerating. But every one of those tools, no matter how good the underlying model gets, faces the same fundamental limitation: when they "understand" your codebase, they're doing it fresh, in a sandbox, from scratch, every single session. They have no persistent, shared, verified memory of why your code is the way it is — they're reasoning from the code itself, which means a brilliant model can still confidently walk into a landmine because nothing tells it "three downstream services depend on this exact behavior, here's the PR where someone explained why."

> From "What if to What's next"

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

SafeSphere is a proactive AI-powered digital safety platform and browser extension designed to protect users from cyberbullying, grooming, sextortion, blackmail, harassment, doxxing, and other forms of digital abuse. Unlike traditional solutions that react only after incidents are reported, SafeSphere identifies threats early by analyzing text, screenshots, emails, audio, and social media communications in real time. Powered by Google Gemini AI and Sarvam AI, it understands context, intent, power dynamics, and cultural nuances across multiple languages. The platform categorizes threats, assigns severity scores, explains risks in simple language, securely preserves digital evidence, and provides personalized safety guidance and reporting resources. Built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Chrome Extension APIs, Python Flask, SQLite, and PostgreSQL, SafeSphere transforms online safety from a reactive process into a proactive protection ecosystem, helping users recognize, understand, and respond to threats before they escalate into real-world harm.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. API connections

2. Real-time testing, especially cross-language

3. Integrating it into web extension

**Gemini**

SafeSphere is a strong fit for the Gemini Track because Google Gemini serves as the core intelligence engine powering both the platform and its browser extension. Through the SafeSphere web extension, users can instantly analyze suspicious content from websites, social media platforms, emails, and online chats with a single click. Gemini's advanced reasoning and natural language understanding capabilities enable SafeSphere to go beyond keyword-based detection by analyzing context, intent, power dynamics, emotional manipulation, and conversational patterns. It accurately identifies threats such as cyberbullying, grooming, sextortion, blackmail, harassment, and coercion, while generating severity scores and personalized safety recommendations in real time. Gemini also helps explain threats in a clear, user-friendly manner, allowing users to understand not just what is harmful, but why it is harmful. By embedding Gemini-powered intelligence directly into a browser extension and digital safety platform, SafeSphere demonstrates a practical, scalable, and impactful application of Gemini technology to proactively protect users from online harm.

**Sarvam.ai**

SafeSphere is an excellent fit for the Sarvam AI Track because Sarvam AI enables the platform to break language barriers in digital safety. Online abuse, harassment, blackmail, grooming, and manipulation often occur in regional languages and dialects that traditional moderation systems struggle to understand. By integrating Sarvam AI's multilingual capabilities, SafeSphere can process and translate content across multiple Indian languages, perform speech-to-text conversion for audio messages, and identify culturally specific abuse patterns, honor-based threats, coercion tactics, and regional linguistic nuances. This allows SafeSphere to detect threats regardless of the language in which they are communicated and explain them in a clear, understandable manner to users. Through its browser extension and digital safety platform, SafeSphere leverages Sarvam AI to make digital protection more inclusive, accessible, and effective for India's diverse linguistic population, demonstrating a high-impact real-world application of multilingual AI technology.

**Open Innovation**

SafeSphere aligns strongly with the Open Innovation theme by combining advanced external technologies, collaborative ecosystems, and real-world safety infrastructures to address the growing challenge of digital abuse and online harassment. The platform integrates cutting-edge AI models such as Google Gemini for contextual threat analysis and Sarvam AI for multilingual understanding, speech processing, and cultural-context awareness. Beyond technology integration, SafeSphere is designed to work alongside social media platforms, educational institutions, cybercrime portals, NGOs, mental health organizations, and law-enforcement agencies, creating a connected digital safety ecosystem. By enabling multilingual threat detection, evidence preservation, actionable guidance, and future interoperability with existing reporting and support systems, SafeSphere demonstrates how open collaboration and shared innovation can be leveraged to create a scalable, inclusive, and impactful solution for protecting individuals in the digital world.

### AGENTGRID

> An Autonomous Multi-Agent Energy Operating System

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Renewable energy adoption is growing rapidly, but residential communities still operate in a highly inefficient manner.

Solar panels generate energy unpredictably, batteries are often underutilized, electric vehicles are charged during expensive peak hours, and households consume electricity independently without any coordination. Existing energy dashboards only display information — they do not actively make decisions.

As a result:

* Communities pay higher electricity bills.
* Renewable energy is wasted when generation exceeds demand.
* Peak-hour grid dependence increases costs and carbon emissions.
* EV charging occurs at suboptimal times.
* Residents receive little to no actionable sustainability guidance.
* Non-technical and multilingual communities struggle to access energy insights.

AGENTGRID addresses this challenge by introducing an Autonomous Multi-Agent Energy Operating System that continuously coordinates households, renewable generation, batteries, EV charging, and grid interactions in real time.

Instead of simply monitoring energy consumption, AGENTGRID actively analyzes forecasts, negotiates resource allocation, predicts future demand, and recommends optimal actions that reduce costs, maximize renewable utilization, and improve sustainability across the entire community.

The platform combines Multi-Agent AI, Energy Forecasting, Digital Twin Simulation, Multilingual AI Assistance, and Community Gamification into a single intelligent operating system for sustainable neighborhoods.

Our vision is to transform residential communities from passive energy consumers into self-optimizing energy ecosystems.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/89acf4fe26594b6abc46ebec356e364f/fc914110-938f-4cdc-943d-c396cb54fdcf.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/89acf4fe26594b6abc46ebec356e364f/fbb9f4a3-ca14-4edd-865e-48f083a4f49f.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building AGENTGRID required solving challenges across AI, simulation, forecasting, and real-time system design.

One of the biggest challenges was designing a Multi-Agent System capable of coordinating multiple energy assets simultaneously. We needed autonomous agents representing households, solar generation, battery storage, EV charging, and grid infrastructure, while ensuring that decisions remained explainable, deterministic, and suitable for real-time execution.

Another major challenge was integrating forecasting with optimization. Renewable generation and energy demand are highly dynamic, so our forecasting models needed to provide reliable predictions that could directly influence agent decisions without introducing instability into the system.

Creating a real-time Digital Twin posed additional challenges. The platform visualizes an entire community through an interactive 3D environment where changes in generation, demand, battery usage, and optimization decisions are reflected dynamically. Maintaining responsiveness while displaying multiple interconnected assets required careful system design.

Multilingual accessibility was another challenge. Energy management systems are often inaccessible to non-technical users. By integrating multilingual conversational AI, we ensured that sustainability recommendations and savings plans could be understood by a much broader audience.

These challenges ultimately shaped AGENTGRID into a scalable and modular platform capable of supporting future smart-city and community-energy applications.

**Sarvam.ai**

AGENTGRID closely aligns with Sarvam's vision of making advanced AI accessible to India's diverse linguistic population.

Energy management systems are typically designed for technical users and are often available only in English. However, real residential communities consist of families that communicate in different regional languages. For large-scale adoption of sustainable technologies, language must not become a barrier.

AGENTGRID uses Sarvam's ecosystem to ensure that every resident can interact with the platform naturally in their preferred language, making energy intelligence truly inclusive.

### Sarvam Technologies Used

**1. Sarvam 105B – Multilingual Large Language Model**

Sarvam 105B serves as the primary intelligence layer of AGENTGRID.

It powers:

* Energy recommendations
* Sustainability guidance
* Savings planning
* Community energy insights
* What-if scenario analysis
* Personalized action plans

Residents can ask questions such as:

* "How can I save ₹1500 this month?"
* "When should I charge my EV?"
* "How can I reduce my electricity bill?"
* "What happens if I install rooftop solar?"

and receive actionable recommendations in their preferred language.

---

**2. Sarvam Bulbul V3 – Text-to-Speech**

AGENTGRID uses Bulbul V3 to provide natural and expressive voice responses across Indian languages.

This enables:

* Voice-based sustainability guidance
* Accessibility for non-technical users
* Support for elderly residents
* Hands-free interaction with the system

Residents can listen to energy recommendations and savings plans instead of reading complex dashboards.

---

**3. Sarvam Saras V3 – Speech Recognition**

AGENTGRID uses Saras V3 for low-latency multilingual speech recognition.

This allows residents to communicate naturally with the platform through voice.

Capabilities include:

* Voice queries in regional languages
* Multilingual speech recognition
* Code-mixed language support
* Real-time conversational interaction

Users can simply speak questions in Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Marathi, Bengali, Malayalam, or other supported languages and instantly receive intelligent responses.

---

By integrating Sarvam 105B, Bulbul V3, and Saras V3, AGENTGRID transforms a technically complex energy optimization system into a multilingual, voice-enabled, and highly accessible community platform.

The result is an AI-powered sustainability solution that can be adopted not only by urban English-speaking users, but also by diverse communities across India, ensuring that the benefits of clean energy and intelligent resource management are available to everyone, regardless of language.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/89acf4fe26594b6abc46ebec356e364f/2968fc37-ec06-40cf-9946-7267f6f77495.png)

**Sustainable Development**

AGENTGRID directly addresses one of the biggest challenges in sustainable development: the perceived trade-off between environmental responsibility and economic benefit.

Traditionally, sustainability initiatives are often viewed as activities that require additional investment, lifestyle changes, or financial sacrifice. AGENTGRID challenges this assumption by demonstrating that sustainable behavior can also be economically beneficial. Through intelligent coordination of renewable energy generation, battery storage, EV charging, and household demand, the platform helps communities reduce electricity costs while simultaneously lowering carbon emissions.

By maximizing renewable energy utilization, minimizing peak-hour grid dependence, and optimizing community-wide energy allocation, AGENTGRID enables households to save money while contributing to environmental sustainability. In other words, sustainability is no longer a cost—it becomes a source of measurable financial savings.

The project aligns strongly with multiple United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):

**SDG 7 – Affordable and Clean Energy**

* Increases renewable energy utilization.
* Optimizes solar generation and battery storage.
* Reduces dependence on expensive grid electricity.

**SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities**

* Promotes community-wide coordination instead of isolated household decision-making.

**SDG 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production**

* Encourages efficient energy consumption.
* Reduces energy wastage through AI-driven scheduling and optimization.

**SDG 13 – Climate Action**

* Lowers carbon emissions by prioritizing renewable energy sources.
* Reduces reliance on carbon-intensive grid electricity.

**SDG 9 – Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure**

* Introduces a next-generation AI-powered energy operating system.
* Combines Multi-Agent AI, forecasting, digital twins, and intelligent optimization for modern energy infrastructure.

Through AGENTGRID, sustainability becomes accessible, measurable, economically rewarding, and scalable, creating a model for future smart communities and energy-resilient cities.

### Kavach-AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/kavachai-3bed) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://kavach-ai-kappa.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/b2XOUGvKKG8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI Powered Multilingual Fraud Intelligence Engine

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Framer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Framer-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Kavach-AI (कवच-AI) acts as an intelligent, localized digital armor designed to protect vulnerable demographics—such as elderly citizens and non-tech-savvy individuals—from the rapidly growing epidemic of voice phishing (vishing), SMS spam scams, and social engineering frauds.

How it makes tasks safer and easier:
Deciphers Local Language Scams: Most financial fraudsters in India target victims in regional Indic dialects (Hindi, Telugu, etc.) to induce panic. Kavach-AI utilizes advanced AI translation and transcription to ingest regional voice recordings or texts and translate them into normalized English.
Cognitive Fraud Assessment: Instead of just blocking numbers based on a static list, Kavach-AI uses Google Gemini Flash to run a cognitive assessment on the message context—flagging scam patterns like fake bank blocks (SBI Yono), Kaun Banega Crorepati (KBC) lottery winnings, and urgent electricity bill disconnection threats.
De-escalates Panic in Real-Time: If a high threat is detected, the system immediately plays a localized voice alarm (synthesized via Sarvam TTS) to warning the user in their preferred regional language (e.g. Hindi), keeping them calm and alert.
Guardian Alert Safety Net: Simultaneously, Kavach-AI routes an emergency SMS notification to a registered trusted family member (guardian) using the Twilio SMS API. This allows guardians to intervene immediately and prevent the protected user from completing a fraudulent transfer.
Seamless Authentication: Integrates Twilio Verify OTP authentication to bind user configurations securely to verified physical devices.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an end-to-end multi-language AI pipeline comes with real integration hurdles. Here are the key challenges we faced and how we overcame them:

1. Next.js CSS Transform Build Crashes
The Hurdle: During initial development, the Next.js dev server and production builds kept throwing fatal errors (Uncaught Error: globals.css: Parsing CSS source code failed). The parser was failing because the @import statements for Google Fonts were placed below normal CSS rules, violating standard PostCSS rules.
The Solution: We removed the @import font rule from globals.css and loaded the Google Fonts (Inter and JetBrains Mono) natively using the Next.js App Router next/font/google configuration in layout.js. This fixed build performance and ensured 100% compilation success.
2. Infinite Loop and Recursion Errors
The Hurdle: During API stress testing, state updates on the dashboard were triggering endless render loops, leading to recursion depth exceeded exceptions. Setting profile configs or triggering a threat analysis caused state modifications that recursively re-ran the logic.
The Solution: We audited and cleaned up the useEffect dependencies across the main components, decoupling state hooks from triggering mechanisms, ensuring data workflows proceed in a linear, single-direction path.
3. Profile Onboarding State Synchronization Bug
The Hurdle: After completing the Twilio OTP verification, the onboarding setup data (Protected Name, Guardian Number, preferred language) was occasionally getting dropped, causing the Settings page to appear empty when the dashboard launched.
The Solution: We consolidated all profile information into a single unified profile state object in the parent component as the single source of truth. We also created a hard dashboard route guard useEffect that checks local storage and the backend API, forcing the setup page if the profile setup isn't complete (profile_completed !== true).
4. Render Python Version Maturin Build Failures
The Hurdle: When deploying the FastAPI backend to Render, the build server failed during package installation with metadata-generation-failed: pydantic-core maturin failed because Render's default environment was utilizing Python 3.14, which was incompatible with the pydantic compiler.
The Solution: We created a runtime.txt file in the backend directory locking the execution container environment to python-3.11.9, forcing Render to build on a stable Python environment and resolving compilation issues.
3:35 PM

**Gemini**

How Gemini AI fits into Kavach-AI

Google Gemini API serves as the core cognitive threat intelligence engine of Kavach-AI and is responsible for analyzing whether an incoming message or call represents a cybersecurity threat. After suspicious audio or SMS content is processed and normalized into English through Sarvam AI, Gemini performs deep contextual analysis instead of simple keyword matching. It evaluates the intent behind the communication by identifying patterns commonly used in cyber fraud such as phishing attempts, impersonation of trusted authorities, fake urgency tactics, unauthorized payment requests, social engineering manipulation, and scam language designed to trigger panic in victims. Based on this behavioral and contextual analysis, Gemini classifies the interaction into categories such as Safe, Suspicious, or High Threat while assigning a confidence score and identifying the probable fraud type. This allows Kavach-AI to move beyond traditional spam detection systems and build an intelligent real-time cybersecurity defense layer capable of understanding human manipulation tactics used in modern AI-driven fraud attacks before financial damage occurs. 🚀

**Sarvam.ai**

How Sarvam AI fits into Kavach-AI
Kavach-AI is designed to protect users from AI-powered scam calls and fraudulent SMS attacks that are increasingly being executed in Indian regional languages, mixed dialects, and colloquial speech patterns that traditional security systems fail to understand. sarvam.ai⁠� serves as the core linguistic intelligence layer of our system by enabling multilingual processing at multiple stages of the pipeline. When a suspicious SMS or audio input is received, Sarvam AI first performs speech-to-text conversion for audio and translation or normalization for text written in languages such as Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Hinglish, or other regional variants, converting them into clean standardized English text. This normalized output is then sent to Gemini API, which performs contextual threat analysis to identify scam intent, urgency manipulation, impersonation attempts, or fraudulent financial requests and assigns a threat level such as Safe, Suspicious, or High Risk. Once a threat is detected, Sarvam AI is again used through text-to-speech generation to convert the warning message back into the user’s preferred local language and play an immediate voice alert, ensuring accessibility even for elderly, rural, or digitally vulnerable users. By acting as the bridge between India’s diverse linguistic ecosystem and our AI threat detection engine, Sarvam AI enables Kavach-AI to deliver an India-first, multilingual, real-time fraud prevention system that directly addresses one of the biggest gaps in existing cybersecurity solutions.

**CyberSecurity**

Why Kavach-AI belongs in the Cybersecurity Track

Kavach-AI is fundamentally a cybersecurity solution because it focuses on protecting users against one of the fastest-growing modern cyber threats: AI-powered social engineering and financial fraud attacks. Today, cybercriminals are no longer relying only on malware or traditional phishing links; they are increasingly using advanced AI tools to generate highly convincing scam calls and fraudulent SMS messages that impersonate banks, government authorities, electricity boards, or even family members to manipulate victims into transferring money or revealing sensitive information. Kavach-AI acts as a real-time cyber defense layer by intercepting suspicious communication, processing multilingual or regional language content through, analyzing intent and scam patterns using Gemini AI, and instantly warning the user before any harmful action is taken. Unlike conventional spam filters that rely on static keyword detection, our system performs intelligent behavioral threat analysis to detect phishing attempts, impersonation fraud, social engineering attacks, and digital payment scams in real time. Since the project directly addresses fraud prevention, digital identity protection, secure communication analysis, and proactive defense against evolving AI-driven cyber threats, Kavach-AI strongly aligns with the Cybersecurity track. 🚀

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem It Solves

Many students can solve coding questions but struggle to apply those concepts in real-world projects. Traditional learning platforms often focus on theory and isolated problems, leaving learners unsure about how data structures and algorithms are used in practical software development.

This challenge becomes even bigger for students who are more comfortable learning in their native language. Most technical resources, coding explanations, and interview preparation content are available only in English, creating a learning barrier for millions of students.

PrayogShala bridges this gap by transforming DSA learning into a practical, project-based journey. Students first understand concepts through guided questions, then apply those concepts in hands-on projects, write and execute code in an integrated workspace, and finally defend their implementation through an AI-powered viva.

The platform also supports multilingual learning and voice-based interaction, making technical education more accessible and inclusive. Instead of simply memorizing solutions, learners gain practical experience, improve problem-solving skills, and develop the confidence to explain their coding decisions like they would in a real technical interview.

PrayogShala makes learning more engaging, application-oriented, and accessible, helping students move from "I know the concept" to "I can build and explain it."

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

Building PrayogShala in a hackathon environment came with several technical and product challenges.

### 1. AI-Powered Viva Generation

One of our biggest goals was to create a viva system that generates personalized questions based on a student's actual code. Making the AI understand different coding styles, identify data structures and algorithms used, and generate meaningful follow-up questions proved to be more complex than expected.

To overcome this, we designed a fallback architecture that ensures the viva workflow remains functional even if AI analysis is unavailable, allowing users to continue the learning journey without interruptions.

### 2. End-to-End Workflow Integration

PrayogShala combines multiple components including learning modules, project unlocking, code editing, code execution, progress tracking, and viva evaluation. Ensuring smooth communication between these components while maintaining a clean user experience required careful planning of the frontend and backend architecture.

We solved this by creating a modular service-based architecture and defining clear workflows between each stage of the learning process.

### 3. Project Generation vs Reliability

Initially, we explored dynamically generating projects using AI. However, during development we realized that reliability and consistency were more important for the MVP than dynamic generation.

We introduced a curated project bank mapped to specific DSA topics, ensuring every user receives meaningful, relevant projects while preserving a smooth and predictable learning experience.

### 4. Voice-Based Multilingual Experience

Supporting multilingual learning and voice interactions introduced additional complexity. Managing language preferences, speech recognition, and text-to-speech while keeping the experience intuitive required several iterations of the UI and workflow design.

### 5. Hackathon Time Constraints

Like many hackathon teams, balancing ambitious ideas with limited development time was a challenge. We continuously prioritized features that delivered the highest impact to learners, focusing on building a complete working journey from learning concepts to defending code through an AI-powered viva.

These challenges ultimately helped us refine the product vision and focus on creating a practical, reliable, and engaging learning platform rather than simply adding more features.

**Gemini**

# How We Used Gemini API

Gemini powers the project intelligence layer of PrayogShala.

After a learner completes the prerequisite DSA questions for a topic, Gemini helps bridge the gap between theory and practical application by generating project-specific learning guidance.

### Project Understanding

When a project is unlocked, Gemini analyzes the selected DSA topic and project context to provide:

* Project overview
* Learning objectives
* Skills covered
* Real-world relevance of the project

This helps students understand why they are building a particular project and how it connects to the underlying DSA concepts.

### Milestone Generation

Gemini breaks larger projects into structured milestones and subtasks.

For example:

**Library Management System**

* Create Book Model
* Add Book Functionality
* Search Books
* Issue Books
* Return Books

This transforms a potentially overwhelming project into a guided learning experience.

### Learning Assistance

During project development, Gemini can provide:

* Implementation guidance
* Problem-solving approaches
* Development checkpoints
* Best practices

without directly giving away the complete solution.

### Project Reflection

Once a project is completed, Gemini helps summarize:

* Concepts applied
* Skills practiced
* Areas for improvement
* Suggested next topics

This creates a more personalized learning journey and helps learners understand their progress.

By using Gemini to structure and guide project-based learning, PrayogShala helps students move beyond solving isolated coding problems and start building real-world software solutions.

**MongoDB**

# How We Used MongoDB Atlas

MongoDB Atlas serves as the central data layer of PrayogShala, enabling us to track a learner's complete journey from concept learning to project completion and AI-powered viva evaluation.

### Learning Progress Tracking

MongoDB Atlas stores:

* User profiles
* Current streaks
* Maximum streaks
* Completed modules
* Completed topics
* Project completion status

This allows learners to resume their progress seamlessly across sessions.

### Curriculum Management

Our DSA learning path is organized into modules and topics stored in MongoDB Atlas.

Examples include:

* Arrays & Hashing
* Two Pointers
* Sliding Window
* Stack
* Binary Search
* Linked List
* Trees
* Heap
* Tries

This structure enables dynamic content delivery without hardcoding learning paths into the frontend.

### Project Unlock System

PrayogShala uses MongoDB Atlas to manage project progression.

When a learner successfully completes prerequisite questions:

* Question completion status is stored
* Project unlock state is updated
* Milestone progress is tracked

This creates a structured learning experience where projects are unlocked based on demonstrated understanding.

### Code Submission Storage

Every coding attempt made inside the Monaco Editor is stored in MongoDB Atlas.

Stored data includes:

* Source code
* Programming language
* Submission timestamps
* Associated topic and project

This allows learners to revisit, improve, and compare previous solutions.

### Judge0 Execution Results

After code execution, MongoDB Atlas stores:

* Execution status
* Runtime
* Memory usage
* Compilation errors
* Output logs

This creates a historical record of learner performance and project progress.

### AI Viva Sessions

MongoDB Atlas stores the complete viva lifecycle:

* Generated questions
* Student answers
* Evaluation results
* Scores
* Feedback

This enables personalized assessment and progress analysis over time.

### Skill Reports & Analytics

Using the collected learning data, MongoDB Atlas powers:

* Topic mastery tracking
* Progress analytics
* Skill reports
* Learning history
* Performance insights

This helps learners understand their strengths and identify areas that need improvement.

### Why MongoDB Atlas?

PrayogShala deals with highly dynamic and evolving data, including code submissions, project milestones, viva sessions, and learning progress. MongoDB Atlas allows us to model these relationships efficiently while maintaining flexibility as the platform grows.

MongoDB Atlas acts as the backbone of PrayogShala, enabling a complete end-to-end learning journey from learning concepts, building projects, writing code, and defending solutions through AI-powered vivas.

**The problem it solves**

Currently, city data and citizen complaints (like broken roads, garbage, and faulty streetlights) are scattered across different departments. Because authorities lack a unified view, complaints are handled individually rather than analyzed collectively. This leads to inefficient resource allocation, leaving critical issues regarding water, sanitation, and infrastructure unresolved for long periods.
SDGround is a centralized, AI-powered platform that unifies scattered government data and citizen reports onto an interactive city map.  
For Citizens: It simplifies reporting by allowing users to upload a photo/video with their location. By integrating Sarvam.ai, citizens can report issues using their voice in local regional languages (like Telugu), making civic participation highly inclusive.  

For Authorities: The AI automatically categorizes and clusters similar complaints to reveal major problem hotspots. Municipal officers receive real-time, prioritized alerts and actionable insights on a dashboard, helping them deploy resources efficiently and resolve urban issues much faster.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Data Ingestion and Standardization**: Combining unstructured citizen inputs (photos/videos/text) with highly structured government API datasets  was a major hurdle. Incoming data streams were completely disorganized, which initially broke our analytical models. We overcame this by building a dedicated *Data Pipeline* to strictly ingest, clean, and standardize the data before it hits the storage layer.

**Integrating SDGround with Drishti**: Merging the city intelligence logic of SDGround with the data visualization framework of Drishti posed significant architectural challenges. Syncing the live, multi-source data feeds from SDGround with Drishti's geospatial maps in real time caused performance bottlenecks and state-management conflicts. We had to heavily optimize our backend engineering and implement strict client-side state logic to ensure that incoming citizen alerts would trigger map updates without lagging the entire authority dashboard.

**Multilingual Localization and Audio Processing**: Integrating *Sarvam.ai* for voice-based reporting and translation brought up audio latency issues, especially when handling regional accents like Telugu. We had to refine our backend engineering to ensure the translation and Text-to-Speech processes occurred seamlessly in real-time without delaying critical dashboard alerts for municipal authorities.

**Gemini**

SDGround aligns with the Gemini track by integrating Gemini throughout our development workflow to enhance productivity and accelerate innovation. We leveraged Gemini to generate and refine code for several key components of the platform, enabling faster implementation and iteration. Gemini was also instrumental in summarizing technical documentation, guiding API integration, and helping establish the complete process for acquiring and configuring the required API keys. By utilizing Gemini as an AI-powered development assistant, we streamlined research, reduced development time, and improved the overall quality and efficiency of our project.

**Sarvam.ai**

SDGround uses Sarvam.ai to remove the language barrier that keeps a huge number of citizens from engaging with civic platforms in the first place — most government and civic apps default to English or Hindi, which excludes a large share of users who are most affected by issues like water contamination and sanitation failures.
We integrate Sarvam.ai's speech and translation models in two places:

Voice-based reporting: Citizens can describe a civic issue by speaking in their regional language (e.g. Telugu). Sarvam.ai converts and translates this into structured text, which then flows into our AI-prioritization pipeline alongside photo/location data — so someone who isn't comfortable typing in English can still file a report with full context.
Drishti groundwater alerts: When Drishti flags a high-risk groundwater zone, the alert is converted into a Telugu audio message via Sarvam.ai's text-to-speech and pushed to residents in that area — turning a dashboard warning that only an official would see into something an everyday citizen can actually hear and act on.

**Sustainable Development**

SDGround is built around the idea that the UN Sustainable Development Goals shouldn't just live in policy documents — they should be something a city actively tracks and improves, issue by issue, in real time. The platform maps every citizen complaint directly to the SDGs it affects, turning abstract national targets into a live, ward-level scoreboard.
The project directly addresses:

SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation): Citizen reports of leaks, sewage overflow, and contamination are AI-classified and prioritized, while Drishti continuously monitors groundwater quality across 4,300+ stations in 36 states — catching contamination risks before they become a public health issue.
SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities): By giving municipal authorities a prioritized, evidence-backed dashboard instead of an unsorted complaint queue, civic issues — potholes, waste management, infrastructure failures — get resolved faster and with clear accountability.
SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being): Early groundwater contamination alerts and faster resolution of sanitation issues directly reduce the waterborne illnesses that disproportionately affect low-income communities.
SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities): Multilingual voice reporting and alerts (via Sarvam.ai) ensure that citizens who can't engage in English — often the same citizens most affected by these issues — aren't left out of the system.

**The problem it solves**

Production issues are often discovered only after customers report them or after they start affecting business operations. Engineers then have to manually check dashboards, analyze logs, identify the root cause, and apply fixes, which can be stressful and time-consuming, especially during critical incidents.

Siren AI acts as an intelligent 24/7 monitoring and incident-response assistant. It continuously watches application logs, infrastructure metrics, and system behavior to detect problems as soon as they occur.

When an issue is detected, Siren AI automatically analyzes the problem, identifies the most likely root cause, generates an incident report, and suggests possible solutions. It then calls on the phone to the responsible engineer with a clear summary of the issue. The engineer can either approve one of the suggested fixes or provide a custom solution. Once approved, Siren AI executes the fix and verifies whether the issue has been resolved.

By automating the first-response process, Siren AI helps teams detect and resolve incidents much faster, reduces downtime, minimizes manual troubleshooting, and allows engineers to focus on more important tasks. Instead of learning about failures from customers or managers, teams are informed immediately and can take action before the problem impacts users.
