![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) in India often lose significant revenue due to missed calls, language barriers, and the inability to afford 24/7 human receptionists. When a customer calls to book a table, ask about opening hours, or check stock availability, an unanswered phone call usually means a lost customer.

Furthermore, existing AI phone agents are incredibly difficult to set up. Business owners are forced to navigate complex dashboards, write system prompts, configure webhooks, and map APIs—a process that requires technical expertise they simply don't have time for.

How VoiceClaw Makes it Easier
VoiceClaw completely eliminates the technical friction of building AI voice agents. It introduces a revolutionary "Talk and Build" interface where non-technical users can literally just talk to the platform to configure their AI.

Frictionless Setup: Instead of typing out prompts and mapping API keys, the user speaks their business requirements (e.g., "Hi, I run a vegan restaurant called Green Leaf. We are open from 9 AM to 10 PM. I want the AI to book tables for customers on my Google Calendar."). VoiceClaw automatically parses this natural speech, configures the backend, and injects the necessary tools.
Multilingual & Code-Mixing Support: The agent natively understands and mirrors Indian "code-mixed" speech (like Hinglish or Tenglish), automatically adapting its accent and language to match the caller's comfort zone, ensuring every customer feels understood.
Automated Operations: It connects seamlessly with everyday tools (like Google Calendar for bookings and Telegram for instant owner notifications), effectively serving as a 24/7 receptionist that never sleeps, never misses a call, and never drops a lead.
Ultimately, VoiceClaw democratizes enterprise-grade AI phone automation, allowing local businesses to scale their customer service effortlessly while they focus on running their actual business.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a seamless, continuous 2-way voice agent required overcoming several deep technical hurdles, particularly around latency, voice activity detection, and regional language processing.

1. Achieving Seamless "Talk and Build" Turn-Taking

The Hurdle: We wanted the user to build their agent purely through voice without constantly clicking a "record" button. However, basic microphone streaming either cut the user off while they were pausing to think, or resulted in awkward overlaps where the AI and human talked over each other.
The Solution: We built a custom Voice Activity Detection (VAD) system directly in the React frontend using AudioContext and AnalyserNode. We tuned the decibel threshold to ignore background noise and implemented a strict 1.5-second continuous silence timer. This allowed the user to pause naturally mid-sentence. We also tied the AI's Text-to-Speech (TTS) onended event to instantly toggle the VAD back on, creating a perfect, hands-free ping-pong conversational loop.
2. Handling "Code-Mixed" Indian Speech (Hinglish/Tenglish)

The Hurdle: Standard Speech-to-Text models struggled heavily when Indian users mixed English words into regional languages (e.g., Telugu + English = Tenglish). The generated text was often inaccurate, and the AI's spoken responses sounded robotic or used the wrong regional accent.
The Solution: We deeply integrated Sarvam AI's STT and Language ID endpoints. When an audio blob is processed, if the base STT fails to confidently identify the source language, we route the transcript through Sarvam's Language ID model. We then mapped these detected language codes to specific Sarvam Voice Personalities (te-IN -> amartya, hi-IN -> aravind). This ensured the AI dynamically replied in the exact localized accent the user was speaking.
3. Dynamic Tool Calling & Rejection Handling

The Hurdle: The agent needed to trigger real-world actions (booking Google Calendars or sending Telegram messages) based on voice intent, but basic LLMs would either call tools prematurely or rudely insist on calling a tool even if the user rejected the suggestion.
The Solution: We implemented a custom XML tag steering system in the RAG backend. The AI was strictly prompted to output invisible XML tags (e.g., <tools>calendar</tools>) only after gathering all required parameters. To fix the pushiness, we injected strict rejection-handling rules into the dynamic system prompt—instructing the LLM to instantly drop the goal and revert to a polite greeting if the user explicitly canceled or denied a booking.
4. Audio Payload Validation Errors

The Hurdle: While building the continuous STT pipeline, the FastAPI backend silently failed with 422 Unprocessable Content errors, causing transcription failures on the frontend.
The Solution: By diving into the backend logs, we discovered a strict schema mismatch: the frontend was appending the audio blob to the FormData under the generic key "file", while FastAPI strictly validated against the parameter name "audio". Aligning the payload keys and injecting a placeholder agent_id for the onboarding flow instantly resolved the bottleneck.

**Sarvam AI Integration Details:**

We deeply integrated Sarvam AI’s cutting-edge models as the core foundation of our voice agent infrastructure to solve the unique challenges of the Indian SMB market.

1. **Speech-to-Text (STT) & Language ID:** We utilized Sarvam’s STT to power our hands-free "Talk and Build" interface and real-time caller interactions. 3. **Document Intelligence:** We leveraged Sarvam Document Intelligence to power our Knowledge Base ingestion. When business owners upload custom menus, FAQs, or policies, the model intelligently parses and extracts the unstructured data, which is then vectorized for our RAG pipeline, allowing the agent to answer highly specific business questions instantly.

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem It Solves

## The bottleneck moved — but the tooling didn't

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9e3cc29dae324c2a85c33323e8b4efb1/490d5393-195b-424c-b9c1-3e72da976f09.png)
AI now writes most new code. **~46% of code shipped today is AI-generated, heading toward 60% within the year** — and that number keeps climbing. Writing code became nearly free. Everything *after* writing it didn't.

Software now has two processes running at machine speed: **generation and decay**. The industry spent years building the accelerator. Nobody built the metabolism.

## Five symptoms, one disease

Every team shipping AI-generated software is quietly fighting the same five fires — and treating them as five unrelated problems:

| Symptom | What's actually happening | The data |
|---|---|---|
| **Security rot** | AI picks the insecure pattern by default | AI chooses an insecure option **~45% of the time**; of agent-written code that *passes its tests*, only **~10.5% is actually secure** |
| **The fix-it loop makes it worse** | Each "fix" iteration degrades the code further | Critical vulnerabilities **rise ~37% after five revision rounds** |
| **Intent drift** | A fix silently drops a rule nobody asked to remove | "Almost right, but not quite" is the **#1 developer frustration** — specs are read once, then ignored forever |
| **Production failures** | Deploys break behaviour, not just uptime | **~69% of heavy-AI teams hit regular deploy problems**, and recovery is getting *slower* |
| **Entropy / rewrite cliff** | Duplication and inconsistency compound daily | **50–70% of AI-generated code is technical debt on arrival**; **~70% of vibe-coded MVPs need a full rewrite** to scale |

None of these are five problems. They're **one phenomenon: divergence** — the gap between what software is *supposed to be* and what it's *becoming*, growing every time an AI agent touches the codebase.

## Why existing tools can't close this gap

Every category of tool addresses a slice and stops:

- **Scanners (Snyk, etc.)** flag vulnerabilities — they don't heal, re-verify, or remember.
- **Spec/plan tools** generate intent once — then the code drifts and nothing notices.
- **Observability (Datadog, Sentry)** shows symptoms — not the cause, and certainly not a cure.
- **Refactoring tools** run at human speed, against code generated at machine speed.
- **The AI generator itself** cannot police its own drift — the thing causing the decay can't be the thing that detects it.

## What HELIX does about it — and has actually built

HELIX is an autonomous layer that sits beside an AI-built app and gives it the things every living system has and every codebase lacks: **a genome, an immune system, a memory, a metabolism, a nervous system, and homeostasis.**

Concretely, in this build:

1. **Attacks itself, continuously.** A scoped, allow-listed scanner attacks a live app for SQL injection, XSS, missing row-level security, secret leaks, and auth bypass — the exact classes AI coding agents reproduce most.
2. **Heals itself, with proof.** A confirmed vulnerability gets a generated patch, applied to an isolated **Shadow twin**, re-attacked with the *same exploit* — only promoted to the real app once the verdict is `promote`. **No write ever reaches production without a stored equivalence proof.** This is enforced in code, not policy.
3. **Never forgets a cure.** Every healed vulnerability mints a permanent **antibody** — a regression test, a runtime assertion, and a vector embedding stored in MongoDB Atlas. Re-running the same attack — or a semantically similar one — is blocked automatically, forever.
4. **Catches "up but wrong" failures, not just crashes.** Learned behavioural baselines detect divergence within seconds of a bad deploy, auto-rollback restores users *first*, then HELIX reconstructs the exact causal chain from captured evidence — every step grounded in real data, nothing guessed.
5. **Flags silent intent drift.** Continuous intent–code "base-pairing" catches the fix that quietly dropped a compliance rule (e.g. "refunds over a threshold require approval") and names the *exact* unpaired invariant and diff.
6. **Tells the truth about build speed.** A single homeostasis number answers the question every CTO is afraid to ask out loud: *"Are we shipping faster than this system can stay alive?"*

## Who this is for

- **Solo founders / vibe-coders** shipping fast with no security depth — "is my app a breach waiting to happen?"
- **Small dev pods** running daily AI-generated code — no more 3am pages with no first responder.
- **SREs / platform leads** — cut MTTR with a causal chain that's *evidence-backed*, not guessed.
- **CTOs** — see rewrite risk and safe build rate on one screen, before it becomes an emergency.

## The bottom line

In 2026, code writes itself. **HELIX is the layer that keeps it honest, safe, and alive** — not by slowing AI down, but by giving the software it produces the one thing it's never had: a metabolism.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

## 1. The Shadow invariant had to be *un-bypassable*, not just a convention

Early on, every organ (Immune, Resurrection, Metabolism) had its own idea of
"apply the patch." That's exactly how an autonomous system writes to
production by accident. The fix was to make `verifyEquivalence()` produce a
`shadow_proof` doc, and export a single `assertPromotable(changeRef)` that
**throws `VerificationError`** unless `verdict === 'promote'`. Every promotion
path — vuln heals, incident heals, repair enzymes — now calls this one
function. The invariant lives in code, not in a comment.

## 2. Promoting a patch without a "real" deploy pipeline

For the demo, "promote" means writing a Shadow-proven diff back onto the
target app's source tree. Doing this safely meant: write each file's diff to
`shadow/staging/<ref>/N.patch`, then apply with `patch -p1
--no-backup-if-mismatch` from the **monorepo root** — never from the cwd a
Next.js dev server happens to be in. That root path turned out to be a
problem of its own (see #3).

## 3. `__dirname` lies inside a bundled Next.js app

Engine code resolves paths relative to the repo root to apply patches and
read source for entropy measurement. In dev that's fine — but once webpack
bundles the route handlers, `__dirname` points at the *build output*, not the
source tree, so patches landed in the wrong place. The fix: walk up from
`process.cwd()` looking for `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, with `__dirname` only as a
last-resort fallback for non-bundled contexts (tests, CLIs).

## 4. Keeping two LLM providers from blurring together

With Sarvam as the reasoning brain and Gemini as the wide-context reader, it
was tempting to just "use whichever client is loaded" for a given call. We
hard-locked this in `CLAUDE.md` as a ground-truth rule — Gemini is *never*
allowed to write a patch or make a judgement call, only to read and parse —
so the architecture doesn't quietly drift into "one model does everything"
over the course of 36 hours of iteration.

## 5. Strict-JSON from an LLM is never actually strict

Sarvam's chat responses sometimes wrapped JSON in code fences, added a
preamble sentence, or returned a field name that was *close but not exact* to
the Zod schema. `sarvam.chat({ json })` now strips fences, parses, validates
against the schema, and **retries once** before throwing a typed
`ValidationError` — so a single flaky generation doesn't cascade into a bad
patch being treated as valid.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9e3cc29dae324c2a85c33323e8b4efb1/ba3c6420-0e8e-46b5-a1f2-cd315625be23.png)
## 6. Atlas Vector Search isn't always there

`matchAntibody()` depends on an Atlas `$vectorSearch` index on
`antibody.embedding` — but that index can take time to build, or Atlas Search
might not be enabled on a given cluster tier. Rather than fail the whole
immune-memory loop, we added an in-memory cosine-similarity fallback so
recurrence blocking still works (just less efficiently) if the vector index
isn't ready yet.

## 7. Building a *realistically* vulnerable app without a real vulnerability

ShopLite needed exactly four planted vulns (SQLi, XSS, missingRLS,
secretLeak) — no more, no less — so the scanner's precision/recall could be
scored against `vulns.manifest.json`. The hard part was making each one
*genuinely exploitable* (not theoretical) while keeping the reproduction
steps strictly read-only and non-destructive, and clearly bannered
`// HELIX-DEMO-VULN` so nothing escapes the authorized scope.

**Best Hack Built using n8n**

HELIX uses n8n as its **autonomic nervous system** — the layer that turns AI cognition into autonomous action with zero human intervention.

Every critical HELIX reflex runs as an n8n workflow:

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9e3cc29dae324c2a85c33323e8b4efb1/0976ba2d-8ffc-4f3d-8e0a-7875233de4df.png)

- **Immune reflex** — on every deploy, n8n triggers the Immune System to red-team the live app for SQLi, XSS, authBypass, secretLeak, and missingRLS. On a confirmed finding, it chains directly into patch synthesis → Shadow verification → re-attack confirmation → production promotion. No human in the loop.
- **Resurrection Reflex** — n8n detects the production anomaly, fires causal reconstruction via Sarvam AI, routes the fix through the Shadow twin for equivalence verification, and promotes — all within 71 seconds of the crash.
- **Metabolic loop** — nightly n8n workflows trigger entropy measurement across the codebase, identify the hottest zones, and dispatch consolidation patches through the same Shadow-verified pipeline.
- **Governor loop** — periodic n8n runs compute the generation rate vs. repair rate balance and gate or reprioritise organ effort when the system is overloaded.

Without n8n, HELIX is a set of smart functions. With n8n, it becomes a living organism that breathes on its own — scanning, healing, digesting, and self-correcting on a continuous clock, triggered by webhooks and schedules, with every action chained and auditable.

**Gemini**

# Partner Track Fit — Gemini

**HELIX gives Gemini the one job no other model in the stack can do well: seeing the whole codebase at once.** While Sarvam AI handles narrow reasoning and patch generation, Gemini is deliberately scoped as the system's **perception layer** — the wide-context "senses" of the organism.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9e3cc29dae324c2a85c33323e8b4efb1/7fae0208-f75d-4515-b5fa-94c134c0aaad.png)
## How HELIX uses Gemini

**1. Whole-repo intent–code base-pairing (Genome)**
HELIX is built on the idea of two paired strands — an *intent* strand (what the code is supposed to do) and an *implementation* strand (what it actually does) — that must stay matched, like DNA base pairs. Computing a **pairing score** for this requires reading a module's intent record *and* its current implementation *and* related files simultaneously. Gemini's long context window is used to ingest these multi-file bundles in one pass and flag drift in both directions: code that silently dropped an invariant (e.g. a fix that removes a refund-approval check), or intent that changed while the code was left behind.

**2. Entropy field computation (Metabolism)**
The "temperature gauge" — how much disorder (duplication, pattern variance, coupling, vuln density, comprehension difficulty) a codebase has accumulated — is computed by feeding large swaths of the repository to Gemini in `gemini.analyze()` calls with strict-JSON output, validated against Zod schemas. This produces the five-dimension `EntropyPoint` that drives HELIX's "rewrite cliff" projection.

**3. Log and DOM parsing for incident diagnosis (Resurrection Reflex)**
When a production incident occurs, Gemini parses raw logs, traces, and DOM/response snapshots into structured evidence — which Sarvam then uses to reconstruct a grounded causal chain (`deploy → triggering request → fault → failing line`), with every step required to cite an `evidenceRef` back to something Gemini actually extracted. No step in the chain is allowed to be a guess.

**4. Subtle vulnerability signature recognition (Immune System)**
HELIX's scanner detects SQLi, XSS, missing RLS, secret leaks, and auth bypass via standard detection vectors, then uses Gemini to recognize subtle signatures in the resulting responses, DOM, and error output — the kind of nuanced pattern recognition across a large response surface that benefits from a strong general-purpose multimodal model.

**5. A real architectural decision, not a checkbox**
Gemini's role is intentionally bounded and documented as a hard constraint in the project's operating contract: it is the wide-context reader, never the reasoning or patch-writing engine. This separation of concerns — perception vs. cognition — is itself part of the engineering story: each model is used where its real strengths are, rather than routing everything through one provider for convenience.

## One-line pitch
HELIX uses Gemini as the **eyes of an autonomous software organism** — the only component capable of reading an entire codebase, its history, and its runtime evidence at once, turning that wide view into structured signals the rest of the system can act on.

**MongoDB**

# Partner Track Fit — MongoDB

**MongoDB isn't a bolt-on database for HELIX — it's the organism's biology.** Every organ writes its memory, history, and proofs into MongoDB, and the live dashboard reads exclusively from it. Seven purpose-built collections form the entire persistent state of the system.

## How HELIX uses MongoDB

**1. Document model for evolving, semi-structured "genome" data**
The `intent_strand` collection stores each module's intent record — purpose, invariants (with rationale and compliance flags), edge-case decisions, and a live `pairing` score against the actual code. This kind of nested, evolving, schema-flexible record is exactly what a document database is built for — a relational schema would require constant migrations as invariants and edge cases are added.

**2. Atlas Vector Search for the immune memory**
Every healed vulnerability or production incident is minted into an **antibody** — a document containing a 1536-dimensional embedding alongside its regression test and runtime assertion. New threats are matched against this embedding space using **MongoDB Atlas `$vectorSearch`** (cosine similarity over `antibody.embedding`), letting HELIX instantly recognize "we've seen something like this before" and block recurrence — with an in-memory cosine fallback if the Atlas index is temporarily unavailable.

**3. Time-series collection for entropy trajectories**
`entropy_timeseries` is a true **MongoDB time-series collection** (timeField `ts`), storing per-run entropy dimensions (duplication, pattern variance, coupling, vuln density, comprehension) and a derived temperature scalar. This powers the "Lifeline" projection — bending toward green or counting down to a rewrite — using MongoDB's native time-series storage and query efficiency rather than a bolted-on metrics store.

**4. Single source of truth across organs**
`vulnerability`, `incident`, `shadow_proof`, and `homeostasis` collections give every organ (Immune System, Resurrection Reflex, Shadow, Governor) a shared, auditable record. The **Shadow invariant** — no patch is promoted to production without a stored `shadow_proof` document carrying `verdict: 'promote'` — is enforced by querying MongoDB directly, making the database itself the gatekeeper for autonomous code changes.

**5. Live dashboard powered entirely by MongoDB reads**
The Vital Signs dashboard (`/api/vitals`, SSE activity stream) computes nothing client-side — it streams real-time state straight from these collections via Mongoose repositories, so the "living organism" view is a direct reflection of MongoDB's current data, not a cached or simulated layer.

**6. Mongoose + Zod for safety at the data boundary**
Every write is validated against Zod schemas mirrored 1:1 to the TypeScript domain types before hitting Mongoose models, keeping all seven collections byte-aligned with the system's data contracts as the codebase evolves.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9e3cc29dae324c2a85c33323e8b4efb1/dcdaaf05-ec3b-48c3-a9dc-c25b8140ff01.png)

## One-line pitch
HELIX treats MongoDB as the literal **memory and nervous system of an autonomous AI organism** — combining documents, vector search, and time-series collections in one database to store everything the system knows about its own health, history, and immunity.

**Sarvam.ai**

Sarvam AI is the **primary cognition layer** of HELIX — every reasoning task, every autonomous decision, every spoken briefing routes through Sarvam. It is not a feature; it is the brain of the organism.

**What Sarvam powers in HELIX:**

- **Patch synthesis** — when the Immune System confirms a vulnerability (SQLi, XSS, missingRLS, secretLeak, authBypass), Sarvam writes the candidate fix targeting the exact vulnerability class, not a generic template. The patch is precise enough to close the hole while leaving surrounding behaviour untouched — verified by re-attack in the Shadow twin before it ever touches production.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9e3cc29dae324c2a85c33323e8b4efb1/28794401-0a3c-45ea-abde-f4791345642e.png)
- **Drift judgement** — when the Genome detects a mismatch between an intent strand and its implementation, Sarvam identifies the specific invariant that broke, explains the divergence in plain language, and proposes the minimal correction. It distinguishes "code drifted from intent" from "intent changed and left code unpaired" — two different failure modes requiring different responses.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9e3cc29dae324c2a85c33323e8b4efb1/a14e0c3d-e86d-469a-abd4-013438bcde01.png)
- **Causal reconstruction** — when the Nervous System detects a production crash, Sarvam reconstructs the causal chain from captured evidence (logs, failing requests, baseline delta) and generates a targeted fix routed through the Shadow twin. The Resurrection Reflex reduced user-facing impact to 71 seconds in our demo scenario.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9e3cc29dae324c2a85c33323e8b4efb1/97b25e5b-9b76-4410-9249-c8c27863f7e0.png)
- **Behaviour-equivalence judgement** — after every Shadow replay, Sarvam judges whether the patched version is behaviourally equivalent to the original beyond the intended fix. This is the gate that prevents "the AI fixed one bug and introduced three others."
- **Test and assertion generation** — every healed vulnerability becomes a generated regression test and runtime assertion injected into the genome, making the system permanently more resistant to that class of bug.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9e3cc29dae324c2a85c33323e8b4efb1/0d99a2e9-511c-41e7-86f6-3662a30ec720.png)
- **Sovereign on-prem mode** — `HELIX_SOVEREIGN=1` routes all Sarvam reasoning to a local open-weight model via an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The same pipeline runs in air-gapped or regulated environments with zero code changes. Activates automatically on Sarvam 402/429.
- **Voice layer (Bulbul TTS + Saaras STT)** — the Governor delivers a spoken morning briefing in the engineer's language summarising overnight immune activity, entropy trajectory, and safe build rate. Engineers query HELIX's status by voice; Sarvam responds. `ttsSafe()` degrades gracefully to text if TTS is unavailable.

HELIX is built on the thesis that intent drift, vulnerabilities, entropy, and production failures are one phenomenon — divergence over time. Sarvam is the reasoning engine that diagnoses every form of that divergence, synthesises the correction, and explains it in human language. Every other organ in HELIX depends on Sarvam to think.

**Gen AI&ML**

# Partner Track Fit — Gen AI & ML

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9e3cc29dae324c2a85c33323e8b4efb1/734a0725-ff35-4ec3-8293-68e70b355f70.png)
**HELIX is a Generative AI system end-to-end** — every organ in the architecture is an LLM-driven agent that perceives, reasons, generates, and verifies code changes autonomously, with zero human steps in the core loop.

## How HELIX fits Gen AI & ML

**1. Multi-model generative reasoning core**
HELIX runs on a dual-LLM cognition stack: **Sarvam AI (sarvam-105b)** is the primary reasoning engine — it performs root-cause analysis, synthesizes security patches, generates regression tests and runtime assertions, judges behavioural equivalence between code versions, and reconstructs causal incident chains, all via strict-JSON structured generation validated against Zod schemas. **Gemini** handles wide-context perception — reading entire codebases at once to compute intent–code "base-pairing" scores and entropy fields across hundreds of files, a task that needs long-context multimodal reading rather than narrow reasoning.

**2. Generative code repair, not just detection**
Unlike static analysis tools that only flag problems, HELIX's Immune System and Resurrection Reflex **generate real, file-level diffs** to fix SQL injection, XSS, missing RLS policies, and secret leaks — then open PRs autonomously. This is applied generative AI for software engineering: the model doesn't just describe a fix, it writes one.

**3. Self-verifying AI loop (LLM-as-judge)**
Every AI-generated patch is replayed against a **Shadow twin**, where Sarvam acts as an automated judge — comparing before/after behaviour to confirm the intended fix worked and nothing else regressed (`verdict: 'promote' | 'reject'`). No generated code reaches production without this AI-adjudicated proof, directly addressing the trust gap in autonomous codegen.

**4. ML-based memory via vector embeddings**
Every healed vulnerability or incident is converted into an **"antibody"** — a 1536-dimensional embedding stored in MongoDB Atlas Vector Search. New threats are matched against this embedding space (`$vectorSearch` cosine similarity) to instantly recognize recurring or similar attack patterns and block them — a practical, production-grade ML retrieval system layered on top of the generative core.

**5. Multimodal generative voice interface**
The Vital Signs dashboard uses **Sarvam Bulbul (TTS)** to generate a spoken "state of the organism" briefing and **Saaras (STT)** for spoken follow-up Q&A answered directly from live incident/health data — generative AI as the primary human interface, not a chatbot bolted on afterward.

**6. Autonomous agentic orchestration**
n8n reflex workflows chain these generative steps (scan → reason → patch → verify → mint → report) into closed-loop autonomous agents that run on schedules and triggers — a real demonstration of agentic AI operating on live infrastructure, with guardrails (allowlists, Shadow isolation, sovereign on-prem fallback for regulated environments).

## One-line pitch
HELIX uses generative AI not to write more code faster, but to **keep AI-written code alive** — autonomously diagnosing, generating fixes for, and verifying its own software in a continuous, self-correcting loop.

> safety for the queens

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![POSTGIS](https://img.shields.io/badge/POSTGIS-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most "safety apps" today are basically a panic button with extra steps. They assume the worst-case scenario gives you time to unlock your phone, open an app, and tap a button but real danger doesn't work like that. During an actual assault, a snatching, or an abduction, your hands are the first thing taken away from you. The one moment you need help is the exact moment you physically can't ask for it.

Our project solves that gap by removing the human from the loop. Instead of waiting for a button press, it watches, listens, routes, and acts on its own.

Here's what people can actually use it for:

Walking home at night without thinking about it. Before you even start moving, WSF routes you through safer streets, it actively bypasses areas with a history of incidents instead of just dropping you on the fastest (and often emptiest) path. You get to your destination on a route that was chosen to keep you safe, not just to save 4 minutes.

Being protected even when you can't reach your phone. The app listens to your surroundings on-device. If it hears screaming, shouting, glass breaking, or sounds of a struggle, it triggers an SOS on its own, no tapping required. None of that audio ever leaves your phone, so it doesn't cost you your privacy to stay safe.

Getting help if your phone is snatched or you're forced off your path. If you drift far off your safe route and don't respond, it silently assumes something is wrong and escalates automatically.

Letting institutions actually respond, not just record. Universities, corporate campuses, and police get a live command dashboard. They can see who's in distress, where they are in real time, and dispatch help, even projecting a user's likely path if their connection drops mid-incident.

The core difference: existing apps document what happened after it's already too late. Our Project is built to intervene while it's happening, and to do it autonomously, on the edge, even when the person it's protecting can't lift a finger. It turns personal safety from a reactive button into a proactive system that's always paying attention, so the user doesn't have to.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest bugs were all in the Sarvam AI integration, because Sarvam's newer models are reasoning models, they don't behave like a normal chat API, and that caught us off guard a few times.

The AI kept replying with nothing. Our chat and deterrent would randomly come back completely empty. After a lot of digging we realized sarvam-30b thinks before it answers, it writes an internal chain-of-thought first, then the actual reply. If the token budget was too small, the thinking ate the entire budget (finish_reason: "length") and the real answer came back null. We fixed it by requesting the full token ceiling for the tier, not passing reasoning effort (setting it made the model think even longer and starve the answer), and retrying once if the reply still came back empty.

The whole chat would freeze for a full minute. Tapping send sometimes hung the app for ~60 seconds. Turned out we hadn't set timeouts on our HTTP calls, so requests would block forever on a stalled connection until the Flutter client's own 60s timeout finally fired. Adding explicit connect/read timeouts (5s connect, 45s read) fixed the hang instantly.

Every single request was 400-ing for no reason. This one was sneaky, a blank line in our .env (SARVAM_CHAT_MODEL=) was setting the model name to an empty string. We were using os.environ.get(key, default), which only falls back when the key is missing, not when it's empty, so we were sending a blank model name to the API. Switching to os.environ.get(key) or default solved it.

The deterrent voice flat-out refused to work. Bulbul v3 rejects all the old v1/v2 voice names (meera, anushka, etc.) with a 400. We had to switch to valid v3 speakers and picked vijay, an authoritative voice that's perfect for the fake police-dispatch deterrent.

The bigger lesson across all of these: because Sarvam sits in the critical path of an emergency, we couldn't let it ever fail silently. So we made the panic button fall back to a deterministic spoken dispatch line if the model ever returns empty, the deterrent can never produce silence, no matter what goes wrong upstream.

**Sarvam.ai**

We use two Sarvam models:

1. The Safety Companion (Sarvam LLM — sarvam-30b)
A built-in AI a woman can talk to. It's fused with the app's live context, her GPS location, the risk level of her surroundings, the time, and the nearest safer spots. So it gives concrete guidance ("head 200m north to the lit main road").

2. The Audible Deterrent (Sarvam TTS — bulbul:v3)
On trigger, it generates a live police dispatch line naming her exact street, then speaks it aloud in an authoritative voice. To an attacker, it sounds like police are already en route to that location, a powerful deterrent that's location specific and in the local language.

**Open Innovation**

The Open Innovation track is about taking a real, unsolved problem and attacking it with a genuinely original approach instead of building yet another version of something that already exists. That's exactly what our framework does.

The problem is real and underserved. Women's safety isn't a niche or a hypothetical,  it's a daily reality for millions. Yet almost every existing "safety app" is the same thing: a panic button you have to consciously tap. That's the gap our project was built to break out of.

The innovation is in the approach, not just the idea. our project rethinks safety as a proactive, autonomous system rather than a reactive button:

It routes users around danger before anything happens (DBSCAN-clustered risk zones + safe routing).
It listens on-device and triggers help on its own when it hears a struggle, no tap needed.
It acts even when the phone can't be touched (drift detection, 3× volume-down hardware SOS).
It speaks using Sarvam AI to guide a woman and to scare off attackers with a live, location-specific fake police dispatch.
It combines fields that usually live in separate silos. Our framework pulls together edge AI (on-device audio), geospatial ML (PostGIS + clustering), native OS-level engineering (battery-first geofencing, hardware key bridge), generative AI (Sarvam), and real-time systems (a live authority dashboard) into one cohesive product. That cross-disciplinary mix is what Open Innovation is meant to reward.

It's open and scalable by design. It isn't locked to one campus or city, plug in any region's incident data and the risk zones generate themselves. That makes it a framework, not a one-off app, ready to be adopted by universities, companies, or police anywhere.

**The problem it solves**

# Bhumi — Problem, Solution & Future Scope

## The core problem
Cities like Hyderabad are getting hotter, flooding more, losing green cover and lakes — fast. The data to act on this **exists** (satellites, surveys, reports), but it's scattered, technical, and locked away from the people who actually make decisions. So a city official is left asking three questions they can't easily answer:

> **Where is it worst? Why is it happening? And with the limited money I have — where do I act first?**

Today that means weeks of consultants, spreadsheets, and guesswork. The result: climate action is **slow, reactive, and poorly prioritized** — money often goes where there's political noise, not where it does the most good.

## What Bhumi solves
Bhumi is a **living digital twin of the city's climate** — it mirrors every neighborhood's real conditions on **one map you can simply talk to**, by voice or text, in your own language.

- **See** — the digital twin instantly shows which neighborhoods are worst-hit and how things have changed over the years.
- **Ask** — ask a plain question ("why is this area flooding?") and get a clear answer **backed by real evidence and sources**, not opinion.
- **Plan** — tell it your budget, and the twin tells you **exactly which areas to act on for the biggest impact per rupee** — *"this ₹10 crore protects ~700,000 people."*
- **Justify** — one click produces a ready, costed action plan to take to the council.

In short: **Bhumi turns climate data into a decision.** It's a digital twin that doesn't just *show* the city — it compresses what takes a planning department weeks into a few minutes, and makes climate action **proactive and money-smart**, usable by any officer, not just data scientists.

## Future scope
- **Any city, any country** — the same digital-twin engine works for any region with satellite coverage; onboard a new city by pointing it at the map.
- **Live & predictive** — a real-time twin with monsoon/heatwave **early-warning alerts** and "what-if" scenario planning before disasters hit.
- **Citizen edition** — a public version of the twin so residents can see their own neighborhood's risk and push for action.
- **Plug into city systems** — connect the twin to municipal budgets, work orders, and IoT/ground sensors so a plan becomes actual on-ground execution and tracking.
- **Broader decisions** — extend the twin beyond climate to water, air quality, and urban-planning approvals — a true decision twin for the whole city.

**One line for the form:**
*"Climate data exists but cities can't act on it. Bhumi is a living digital twin of the city's climate you can ask — and it tells a city exactly where to spend its limited budget for the most impact, in any language."*

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges

* **Data reliability:** Satellite data can have cloud cover, missing values, and noisy signals.
* **Real-time forecasting:** GEE gives observations; forecasting needs ML + weather inputs.
* **Model accuracy:** Flood/heat prediction needs validation with real ground data.
* **Complex UI:** Too many features can make the dashboard cluttered.
* **GEE setup:** Authentication, quotas, and service-account setup can be tricky.
* **Explainability:** AI outputs must clearly show measured vs modeled vs predicted data.
* **Scalability:** Moving from Hyderabad MVP to many cities needs better data pipelines.
* **Sarvam integration:** Voice, TTS, and multilingual responses need stable API handling.

**Sarvam.ai**

## How Bhumi Uses **Sarvam AI + LangGraph Orchestration**

* **Sarvam AI is the core reasoning brain** that understands user voice/text queries and decides what the user wants: risk analysis, planning, forecasting, what-if simulation, or report generation.

* **LangGraph orchestrates the multi-agent workflow**, routing Sarvam’s decision through the right tools and maintaining state across the full journey: **See → Ask → Plan → Justify**.

* **Voice-enabled interaction:** Sarvam STT converts Indian-language speech into text, Sarvam Chat reasons over it, and Sarvam TTS speaks the final answer back to the user.

* **Tool-grounded decisions:** Instead of giving generic answers, Sarvam triggers **12 specialized tools** through LangGraph/MCP to produce map actions, risk scores, plans, forecasts, and reports.

## 12 Tools in Bhumi

1. **GEE Satellite Tool** — gets NDVI, NDWI, LST, and satellite indicators.
2. **Ward Risk Tool** — fetches flood, heat, water, and vegetation risk scores.
3. **Top Risk Wards Tool** — ranks highest-risk Hyderabad wards.
4. **Map Control Tool** — highlights wards, changes layers, and flies camera.
5. **XGBoost Forecast Tool** — predicts next-year climate-risk trend.
6. **Diffusion Scenario Tool** — generates multiple plausible future-risk scenarios.
7. **What-if Simulation Tool** — tests trees, drains, cool roofs, and lake restoration.
8. **Budget Planner Tool** — ranks interventions by impact per rupee.
9. **Population Impact Tool** — estimates people helped by each action.
10. **Evidence Tool** — explains measured vs modeled vs projected data.
11. **Voice Tool** — handles Sarvam STT and TTS.
12. **Report Generator Tool** — creates a council-ready action PDF.

**One-line fit:**

> Sarvam AI acts as Bhumi’s voice-enabled reasoning brain, while LangGraph orchestrates 12 MCP-powered tools to convert climate-risk questions into map actions, forecasts, simulations, budget plans, and reports.

**Gen AI&ML**

## How BhumiAI Fits the **GenAI & ML Track**

* **GenAI Layer:** Bhumi uses **Sarvam.AI** as a multilingual assistant where users can ask questions in voice/text and get climate-risk explanations in local languages.

* **Agentic AI:** **LangGraph** coordinates multiple agents for intent routing, map control, planning, what-if simulation, and report generation.

* **ML Forecasting:** **XGBoost** predicts next-year climate-risk trends using satellite and rainfall features like NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, LST, and rainfall.

* **Generative Modeling:** A **diffusion model** generates multiple plausible future climate-risk scenarios, helping users understand uncertainty instead of relying on one fixed prediction.

* **Tool-Augmented AI:** **MCP tools** connect the AI system with Google Earth Engine, risk scoring, budget planning, scenario generation, and PDF reporting.

* **Decision Intelligence:** The system converts GenAI + ML outputs into practical actions: **which ward to fix first, what intervention to choose, and how much impact per rupee.**

**One-line fit:**

> Bhumi combines GenAI agents, ML forecasting, diffusion-based scenario generation, and tool-calling workflows to turn climate data into actionable urban resilience decisions.

### HMS - Hospital Management System
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/hms-hospital-management-system-e584) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI-Powered Emergency Healthcare Intelligence

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![Spring](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spring-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Emergency departments often struggle with overcrowding, fragmented patient information, delayed triage decisions, and communication barriers during high-pressure situations. Existing hospital systems are mostly static and centralized, making it difficult to respond dynamically during sudden patient surges or emergencies.

Our project, the Vitality Triage System, addresses these challenges through an AI-powered hospital intelligence platform that combines multilingual voice triage, computer vision distress detection, AI-assisted clinical summaries, and real-time hospital coordination.

The system helps solve several critical healthcare problems:

1. Patients frequently fail to communicate complete medical history, allergies, or prescriptions during emergencies.
2. Nurses experience alarm fatigue due to excessive generic alerts from monitoring systems.
3. Traditional hospital redirection systems are rigid and unable to adapt to real-time conditions like staffing shortages or equipment failures.
4. Many patients communicate using regional or code-mixed languages such as Hinglish, which standard systems fail to interpret accurately.

To address this, our platform integrates:

1. AI-powered prescription OCR and RAG-based patient history retrieval
2. Real-time computer vision distress detection
3. Autonomous hospital negotiation workflows for patient redistribution
4. Indic multilingual voice triage using Sarvam AI
5. AI telemetry and audit logging for observability and governance

The result is a scalable, intelligent, and human-in-the-loop triage ecosystem that improves emergency response efficiency, patient safety, and healthcare accessibility.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was integrating multiple AI systems into a single unified architecture within a limited hackathon timeline. Our project combines Java Spring Boot, FastAPI microservices, MongoDB telemetry logging, Supabase, OpenCV pipelines, RAG workflows, and multilingual voice AI, which created significant orchestration and synchronization challenges.

Some of the key difficulties included:

1. Designing a clean hybrid architecture between the Java transactional core and Python AI sidecar services
2. Integrating multiple AI workflows such as OCR, RAG retrieval, computer vision, and multilingual voice processing into one unified backend
3. Managing frontend synchronization across multiple live dashboard pages during simulation events
4. Handling real-time state updates consistently between simulations, patient queues, alerts, and monitoring systems
5. Creating a polished frontend dashboard with scalable component architecture while avoiding performance bottlenecks
6. Balancing cinematic UI ambitions with stability and responsiveness during development
7. Managing API compatibility and maintaining clean contracts between backend services and frontend components
8. Ensuring AI outputs remained explainable, observable, and governed through telemetry and audit logs
9. Working with diverse technologies and frameworks under hackathon time constraints while keeping the system modular and maintainable

Another major challenge was ensuring the platform remained reliable even when AI confidence scores dropped or services failed. We implemented fail-safe mechanisms and maintained a strict human-in-the-loop approach to ensure medical staff always retained final control over critical decisions.

**Gemini**

Our project heavily relies on Gemini APIs as the core reasoning and multimodal intelligence engine powering several major workflows across the platform.

Gemini Flash is used for:

1. handwritten prescription understanding
2. multimodal OCR processing
3. contextual clinical summarization
4. emergency distress interpretation
5. AI-assisted reasoning workflows
6. structured healthcare data extraction

One of the system’s key features is converting messy handwritten prescriptions and clinical sheets into structured medical data. Gemini processes visual prescription inputs and generates structured JSON outputs that are later embedded into a RAG pipeline for historical patient retrieval.

Gemini is also used in the distress monitoring workflow, where computer vision events from waiting room surveillance are combined with patient context to generate intelligent explanations for medical staff. This helps reduce alarm fatigue and improves prioritization during emergencies.

Additionally, Gemini powers several agentic reasoning workflows that assist with:

1. patient prioritization
2. contextual medical summaries
3. AI-assisted triage recommendations
4. healthcare workflow orchestration

The project demonstrates practical multimodal Generative AI usage in a real-world healthcare operations system rather than a standalone chatbot application.

**ElevenLabs**

Our project fits into the Eleven Labs track through the integration of expressive AI-generated voice communication within emergency healthcare workflows.

After multilingual voice triage is processed, Eleven Labs is used to generate natural and human-like audio responses for patients and healthcare environments.

The platform uses Eleven Labs for:

1. multilingual patient confirmations
2. emergency guidance announcements
3. AI-generated clinical floor alerts
4. accessible voice-assisted navigation
5. emotionally expressive audio communication

In high-stress emergency situations, clear and natural communication is critical. Instead of robotic system prompts, Eleven Labs enables the platform to provide more human-centered and understandable voice interactions.

For example:

1. patients receive spoken guidance in their preferred language
2. emergency alerts can be broadcast clearly to staff
3. triage instructions become more accessible for elderly or stressed patients

This improves accessibility, patient experience, and communication efficiency within hospital environments.

**MongoDB**

Our project fits strongly into the MongoDB track because MongoDB serves as the core AI telemetry and audit logging engine of the platform.

Instead of using MongoDB as a traditional relational database replacement, we designed it specifically for high-volume unstructured AI observability data. Every AI pipeline execution generates telemetry documents containing:

1. AI execution metadata
2. latency metrics
3. confidence scores
4. token usage
5. OCR extraction details
6. distress analysis outputs
7. workflow audit logs
8. payload snapshots

These telemetry events are written asynchronously into MongoDB to create a scalable audit and monitoring system for all AI-driven workflows inside the hospital platform.

MongoDB was chosen because:

1. telemetry payloads are highly dynamic and schema-flexible
2. AI outputs vary across workflows
3. observability pipelines require scalable document storage
4. audit logging demands efficient querying of nested execution data

This architecture allows us to:

1. track AI system reliability
2. monitor model confidence
3. debug workflows
4. ensure governance and traceability
5. support real-time operational observability

MongoDB therefore acts as the backbone for AI monitoring, telemetry, and compliance within the system.

**Sarvam.ai**

Our project strongly fits into the Sarvam AI track because multilingual and code-mixed voice intelligence is one of the core pillars of the system.

The platform includes an AI-powered voice triage kiosk designed specifically for diverse Indian healthcare environments where patients often communicate using regional languages and mixed dialects such as Hinglish or Marathi-English blends.

We use Sarvam AI’s speech and language models to:

1. Transcribe multilingual patient speech during triage check-in
2. Understand code-mixed medical conversations
3. Convert natural speech into structured clinical intake data
4. Improve accessibility for patients who may struggle with traditional text-based interfaces

This directly addresses a major real-world healthcare challenge in India: communication barriers during emergency intake and triage.

The system allows patients to speak naturally in their preferred language while the AI structures the information for hospital staff in real time. This improves inclusivity, reduces misunderstandings, and accelerates emergency workflows in multilingual environments.

**Gen AI&ML**

Our project fits strongly into the Generative AI and Machine Learning track because it combines multiple AI-driven systems to solve real-world healthcare triage and emergency management problems.

The platform uses Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Computer Vision, multilingual speech intelligence, and agentic workflows to create an intelligent hospital operations ecosystem.

Key AI/ML integrations include:

1. Generative AI Clinical Reasoning: We use Gemini Flash to process handwritten prescriptions, generate structured medical summaries, explain emergency alerts, and assist clinicians with contextual patient insights.
2. RAG-Based Patient History Retrieval: Historical prescriptions and clinical records are converted into vector embeddings using sentence-transformer models and stored in ChromaDB. When a patient arrives, the system retrieves the most relevant historical context to generate AI-assisted summaries for clinicians.
3. Computer Vision Distress Detection: OpenCV and AI-assisted analysis are used to detect abnormal patient behavior such as collapses, seizures, or distress events from waiting room video feeds. The AI then generates contextual explanations to reduce alarm fatigue for medical staff.
4. Multilingual AI Voice Triage: The system supports Indic and code-mixed languages such as Hinglish using Sarvam AI’s speech models. Patients can speak naturally during check-in, and the AI converts speech into structured clinical intake information.
5. Agentic AI Workflows: Autonomous negotiation agents coordinate hospital redirection workflows during capacity surges by exchanging structured healthcare payloads and evaluating real-time operational constraints.
6. AI Telemetry & Observability: Every AI execution is logged into MongoDB telemetry pipelines for auditability, confidence monitoring, latency tracking, and governance.

The project demonstrates practical real-world AI usage beyond chatbots by integrating machine learning and generative AI directly into healthcare operations, emergency triage workflows, and hospital decision support systems.

> Forecasting the Future of Research

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

PaperMind helps researchers quickly understand how a research field is evolving. Instead of manually reading hundreds of papers, users can discover emerging topics, identify accelerating research trends, forecast future directions, and uncover potential research gaps. This makes literature exploration faster and helps researchers find promising areas for new work.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was generating meaningful topic clusters from research paper abstracts. Initial BERTopic configurations either produced too few broad topics or too many fragmented ones. I resolved this by tuning UMAP, HDBSCAN, and BERTopic parameters and validating the results on sample research domains until the discovered topics were coherent and interpretable.

**Gemini**

PaperMind uses the Google Gemini API to transform raw research data into actionable insights. Gemini is used to analyze rapidly growing research topics and generate research-gap recommendations, helping users identify under explored opportunities and future research directions. By combining topic modeling, trend analysis, and Gemini-powered reasoning, PaperPulse goes beyond paper discovery to provide intelligent research intelligence and innovation guidance.

**Gen AI&ML**

PaperMind is fundamentally an AI/ML powered research intelligence platform. It uses machine learning techniques such as BERTopic, Sentence Transformers, UMAP, and HDBSCAN to automatically discover research topics from thousands of paper abstracts. It then applies trend analysis and forecasting models to identify emerging and accelerating areas of research. On top of this, Google Gemini is used for generative AI-powered research gap analysis, helping users uncover under explored opportunities, potential future directions, and novel intersections between topics. Together, ML handles large-scale topic discovery and trend detection, while Gen AI provides high-level reasoning and insight generation, making research exploration faster and more actionable.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Youtube Playlists API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Youtube%20Playlists%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### Problem Statement

Millions of people have valuable thoughts, opinions, experiences, and ideas every day, but most of those ideas never get shared.

Creating meaningful content requires more than having an idea. Users must organize their thoughts, understand relevant discussions, research context, structure their message, and adapt it for different platforms. This process creates significant friction, causing many people to consume content passively rather than contribute their own perspectives.

Existing AI tools can generate content, but they typically require users to know exactly what they want to say and how to prompt the AI. As a result, generated content often feels generic, disconnected from the user's authentic voice, and detached from the thoughts that inspired it.

Detea addresses this problem by helping users move from unstructured thinking to structured expression. It captures thoughts, surfaces relevant discussions and community perspectives, generates insights, and transforms ideas into platform-ready content while preserving the user's voice and intent.

In short, Detea solves the gap between thinking and expressing by reducing the friction required to turn ideas into meaningful content.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Detea involved several technical and product challenges:

Preserving authenticity: One of the biggest challenges was ensuring AI-generated content reflected the user's actual thoughts and opinions rather than producing generic content that could be generated for anyone.
Reducing friction: We wanted users to express ideas naturally instead of learning prompt engineering. Designing an experience that felt conversational while still producing high-quality content required multiple iterations.
Content discovery and summarization: Aggregating information from news sources, community discussions, and trending topics while presenting concise and useful insights was a significant challenge.
Generating platform-specific content: Different platforms require different writing styles and formats. We had to build workflows that could transform the same idea into content suitable for LinkedIn, X, and other platforms.

**Gemini**

We used gemini api for image generation, post generation, day reflect as an thereapist and assistant.

**Gen AI&ML**

Detea is an AI-powered thinking and expression platform that helps users transform unstructured thoughts, conversations, and information into structured insights and platform-ready content.

The core innovation of Detea is that it combines AI-assisted reflection, content discovery, and content creation into a single workflow. Instead of requiring users to manually prompt an AI model, Detea continuously helps users capture thoughts, explore trending discussions, understand community perspectives, and convert those ideas into authentic posts for platforms such as LinkedIn and X.

The platform uses generative AI to:

* Analyze and summarize trending discussions, news, and community conversations.
* Generate AI-powered insights and reflections from user thoughts.
* Create platform-optimized content while preserving the user's voice and perspective.
* Generate custom AI visuals for discussion topics.
* Help users discover patterns in their thinking and build a consistent personal brand.

Unlike traditional AI chat tools that focus primarily on answering questions, Detea focuses on the entire journey from thought to expression. The system acts as both a thinking partner and an expression engine, helping users move from ideas to meaningful content with minimal friction.

By combining generative AI, content understanding, summarization, personalization, and AI-generated media, Detea demonstrates how modern AI can be used not only to generate content but also to enhance self-expression, creativity, and knowledge discovery.

**The problem it solves**

RoadSense AI is an AI-powered civic issue reporting platform that enables citizens to quickly report public infrastructure problems such as damaged roads, drainage issues, overflowing dustbins, streetlight failures, and other municipal concerns. Users can submit complaints through text, voice commands, or images, making the reporting process simple and accessible for everyone.

The platform uses AI to automatically understand, categorize, and prioritize complaints, reducing manual effort and ensuring faster issue resolution. With integrated voice support and an AI chatbot powered by Sarvam AI, users can interact naturally in their preferred language, making the system inclusive and user-friendly.

How it makes existing tasks easier
Eliminates the need to visit government offices or navigate complex complaint portals.
Allows citizens to report issues instantly using voice, text, or images.
Automatically categorizes complaints, reducing administrative workload.
Provides real-time complaint tracking and status updates.
Enables faster communication between citizens and authorities.
How it makes communities safer
Promotes quick reporting of hazardous road conditions, open drains, and damaged infrastructure.
Helps authorities identify and resolve issues before they become major safety risks.
Encourages active citizen participation in maintaining public infrastructure.
Creates cleaner, safer, and more sustainable urban environments.
Key Benefits

* Faster complaint registration and resolution
* AI-powered issue categorization and prioritization
* Voice-enabled accessibility for all users
* Improved transparency and accountability
* Better citizen-government collaboration

**Challenges we ran into**

Major Hurdle We Faced

One of the biggest challenges while developing RoadSense AI was integrating voice-based complaint registration with the AI complaint processing system.

Initially, voice inputs were not being converted accurately into structured complaints. Different accents, background noise, and variations in how users described issues caused the AI to misclassify complaints. For example, a user reporting a "blocked drainage" could be categorized incorrectly as a general sanitation issue.

How We Solved It

To overcome this, we integrated Sarvam AI for speech-to-text processing and added an AI-based complaint categorization layer. We created predefined civic issue categories such as:

Road Damage
Drainage Problems
Waste Management
Streetlight Issues
Water Supply Issues

After converting the user's voice into text, the AI analyzes the complaint and automatically maps it to the most relevant category. We also tested the system with multiple voice samples and refined the prompts to improve classification accuracy.

Result

This solution significantly improved the reliability of voice-based complaint submission, making the platform more accessible and user-friendly. Citizens can now report issues naturally through voice commands, while authorities receive properly categorized complaints for faster resolution.

Key Learning: We learned that integrating AI models is not just about connecting APIs—it requires careful handling of real-world user inputs, testing, and prompt engineering to achieve accurate and reliable results.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB serves as the primary database for RoadSense AI. It stores and manages all complaint-related information submitted by citizens and enables real-time access to data for both users and authorities.

Why We Chose MongoDB

RoadSense AI handles different types of data, including:

Text complaints
Voice-generated complaint transcripts
Image URLs and metadata
User information
Complaint status updates
Location details

Since this data can vary in structure, MongoDB's flexible document-based model is ideal for storing and managing it efficiently.

How MongoDB Is Used in the Project
1. Complaint Storage

When a citizen submits a complaint, MongoDB stores:

{
  "complaintId": "12345",
  "category": "Road Damage",
  "description": "Large pothole near bus stop",
  "location": "Vijayawada",
  "status": "Pending",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-14",
  "imageUrl": "...",
  "voiceTranscript": "There is a huge pothole near the bus stop"
}
2. Complaint Tracking
Every complaint is assigned a unique ID.
MongoDB stores status changes such as:
Pending
In Progress
Resolved
Users can track complaint progress in real time.
3. User Management
Stores citizen profiles and complaint history.
Enables users to view previously submitted complaints.
4. Dashboard Analytics

Authorities can retrieve complaint data from MongoDB to:

View active complaints.
Filter by category.
Analyze issue trends in different locations.
Prioritize urgent problems.
5. Integration with AI Components
Sarvam AI converts voice to text.
Gemini processes and categorizes the complaint.
MongoDB stores the final structured complaint for future retrieval and analysis.
Technical Flow

Citizen Complaint (Text / Voice / Image)
↓
Sarvam AI → Speech-to-Text
↓
Google Gemini → Classification & Summary
↓
MongoDB → Stores Complaint Data
↓
Authority Dashboard
↓
Status Updates & Resolution

**The problem it solves**

Problem:
Farmers and livestock owners often attend training programs on farming, dairy, poultry, irrigation, pest control, animal health, and government schemes. However, after the training, there is no proper system to check whether they understood the concepts, improved their knowledge, or still need support.

Because of this:

Farmers do not get personalized guidance.
Officers cannot identify knowledge gaps.
Training effectiveness cannot be measured.
Resources and training programs are not targeted to the right villages or farmers.

Our Solution:
We propose a Digital Learning and Analytics Platform for Farmers and Livestock Owners.

The platform provides:

Personalized learning modules based on crops and livestock.
Pre-tests and post-tests to measure learning improvement.
Skill scores for topics like pest control, irrigation, vaccination, nutrition, and disease prevention.
AI-based recommendations for weak areas.
Certificates for completed courses.
Analytics dashboards for officers, NGOs, and government departments.

Example:
If a dairy farmer scores 35% in cattle vaccination before training and 80% after training, the system records a 45% improvement and recommends further learning if needed.

Impact:

Farmers receive continuous and personalized learning support.
Officers can identify village-wise and district-wise skill gaps.
Training programs become data-driven and more effective.
Government and NGOs can measure the real impact of their training initiatives.

One-Line Conclusion:
"Our platform bridges the gap between training delivery and real learning outcomes by helping farmers learn better and helping authorities make smarter training decisions."

**The problem it solves**

JADU – The VayuSync

Joint AI-Driven Utility for Touchless Human-Computer Interaction

Tagline: Control Beyond Touch

The Problem It Solves
Modern desktop workflows still rely heavily on manual point-and-click navigation and memorized keyboard shortcuts, which can be slow, repetitive, and mentally taxing. JADU – The VayuSync bridges the gap between natural human intent and digital execution by acting as a universal, hands-free operating system agent that combines gesture-based input with voice-driven automation.
AirMouse AI lets you control your computer — or your phone — entirely through hand gestures, no physical contact required. All gesture detection runs locally in the browser via MediaPipe WASM — no cloud, no remote inference latency, and no privacy concerns.
Who it's for and what it replaces:

Accessibility: Users with motor impairments who can't easily use a mouse or touchpad can navigate their entire desktop through mid-air gestures detected by a standard webcam.
Hygiene-sensitive environments: Doctors, lab workers, or anyone in a clean room can interact with a screen without touching peripherals.
Presenters & teachers: Control slides or a whiteboard app from across the room without needing a clicker or assistant.
Mobile users without a stylus: Use your phone's front camera as a gesture input device — no extra hardware needed.

AirMouse AI runs in three modes:

Laptop mode — your laptop's webcam drives your mouse cursor via hand gestures, system-wide.
Mobile-as-camera mode — point your phone at yourself; the video streams to your laptop over WebRTC and controls your desktop cursor remotely.
Mobile-native mode — gestures detected on your phone control the phone itself through an Android Accessibility Service, replacing touch entirely.

JADU complements gesture control by handling natural language commands. By routing voice input through Whisper and Gemini 2.5 Flash and executing intent directly at the OS level via PyAutoGUI, JADU makes interacting with your computer faster, intuitive, and deeply integrated.
What people use it for:

Hands-free multitasking: Execute complex system or browser sequences (e.g., "Open Chrome and go to Instagram") while keeping your hands on the keyboard for actual work.
Enhanced accessibility: A seamless, voice-first alternative for users with mobility or dexterity challenges, making standard OS navigation completely accessible without a mouse.
Frictionless workflow automation: Inject keystrokes, manage active windows, mute audio, and navigate the web without digging through nested menus.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Keeping tracking alive when the browser tab is hidden

requestAnimationFrame and setInterval on the main thread are throttled by browsers when you switch away from the tab — which breaks the entire point of a system-wide mouse controller. The fix was moving the tick loop into a Web Worker. Worker timers (setInterval inside a worker) are not throttled, so gesture frames keep firing at 20 fps even when the user switches to VS Code or a game.
2. Mouse control without native bindings that break on install

robotjs and nut-js both failed to build reliably on Windows due to native N-API and node-gyp issues. Rather than fight the build toolchain, we embedded the mouse controller as a Python subprocess (pyautogui + ctypes) spawned from Node.js. Python is widely available and the script is reliable across Windows versions. The subprocess stays alive for the session and receives JSON commands over stdin.
3. Cursor jitter from raw landmark coordinates

MediaPipe's raw index-fingertip coordinates jitter several pixels frame-to-frame even on a still hand. Applying a simple moving average added lag. We implemented a One Euro Filter — a well-known adaptive low-pass filter that minimizes lag at high velocity and smooths aggressively at low velocity — which made the cursor feel close to a real mouse.
4. WebRTC from a mobile browser to a desktop over LAN

Mobile browsers require HTTPS to access the camera. Setting up a self-signed cert on the Express server and serving the mobile page on a separate HTTPS port (3443) solved camera access, but then Socket.IO signaling had to handle the mixed HTTP/HTTPS context. The /api/server-info endpoint dynamically resolves the LAN IP so the dashboard can generate the correct https://<LAN-IP>:3443/mobile URL for the user to scan.
5. Ghost WebSocket connections

The frontend UI would show a permanent loading spinner even though the Python backend successfully executed the command. React 18's Strict Mode was mounting the component twice, creating a "ghost" WebSocket connection. This was solved by adding aggressive connection-state checks (ws.current?.readyState) and strictly cleaning up socket instances on unmount.
6. AI pipeline bottlenecks

During live testing, the Gemini API would occasionally throw 503 Service Unavailable errors due to high server demand, completely breaking the intent-parsing pipeline. We built a resilient task queue UI that gracefully catches the JSON errors and marks the task as "Failed" rather than crashing the application.
7. UI/hardware syncing

Keeping the React UI perfectly synced with physical hardware execution (like human-mimicking typing delays) was tricky. We solved this by moving the WebSocket listener into a global Zustand store, ensuring the loading animations turned off the exact millisecond the backend broadcast a success message.
