> Trust and Transparency

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Counterfeit medicines kill over 1 million people every year globally. In India alone, the WHO estimates that 25% of medicines sold are substandard or falsified. A rural farmer buying a ₹10 paracetamol has no way to know if it's genuine or a sugar pill with a fake label. Existing solutions are either too expensive (NFC tags), too basic (single-layer batch lookup), or inaccessible to non-English speakers.
SafeDose solves this by giving every consumer the power to verify any medicine in seconds using just their phone camera. Our 6-layer verification engine checks batch existence, cryptographic hash integrity, QR clone detection, geographic diversion, expiry validation, and supply chain completeness to generate a trust score from 0 to 100. No app download needed. No special hardware. Just scan and know.
For the 70% of India that doesn't speak English, SafeDose includes a voice AI assistant powered by Sarvam AI that speaks in 10 Indian languages including Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, and Odia. Users can also report counterfeit medicines through voice in their native language.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

QR Code Detection from Real-World Photos Our QR scanner worked perfectly with clean, screen-displayed QR codes but consistently failed when users uploaded photos of real medicine packaging. The QR codes in photos were often small within large high-resolution images, had poor lighting, or low contrast. We solved this by implementing multi-scale image processing that attempts detection at multiple zoom levels, along with contrast enhancement and inverted color attempts to handle varied lighting conditions.

Web Speech API Inconsistencies on Mobile The browser's Speech Recognition API behaved very differently across devices. On mobile, interim results were being concatenated with final results, causing words to repeat in the transcript (e.g., "दवाईदवाईदवाई एक्सपायर" instead of "दवाई एक्सपायर"). We fixed this by properly separating isFinal results from interim results and only displaying the combined output. Additionally, the microphone needed time to initialize, causing the first word to be cut off. We resolved this by waiting for the onaudiostart event before prompting the user to speak.

Sarvam AI Model Migration (Bulbul v2 to v3) Mid-development, we upgraded from Sarvam AI's Bulbul v2 to v3 for better voice quality. However, v3 had different API parameters. The pitch and loudness parameters from v2 were no longer supported, the speaker voice names changed, and the default sample rate was different. Our TTS calls silently failed until we read the documentation carefully and updated all parameters. We also had to balance audio quality (higher sample rate) against loading speed for a smooth demo experience.

Cryptographic Hash Synchronization Our verification engine uses SHA-256 hashes to validate medicine authenticity. Every time we re-seeded the database for testing, new hashes were generated. But the fallback QR mapping in our scan page still referenced old hashes from previous seed runs, causing hash validation to fail even for genuine medicines. This taught us the importance of keeping all references in sync whenever seed data changes.

Audio Echo When Switching Languages When a user changed the voice language while the AI was still speaking in the previous language, both audio streams would play simultaneously, creating an echo effect. We solved this by fully destroying the previous Audio object (pause, clear source, force release) before creating a new one, and adding a stale-request guard so responses from old fetch calls are discarded if the language changed during the API round-trip.

Multilingual Voice Accessibility Building voice AI that works in 10 Indian languages was challenging beyond just translation. Each language has different script rendering, different speech patterns, and different TTS pronunciation characteristics. We had to test each language individually and ensure the welcome prompts, issue prompts, and success messages sounded natural when spoken by the TTS engine, not just when read as text.

Figma to Responsive Code Translating our designer's Figma mockup for the hero section into responsive, pixel-perfect code required multiple iterations. The layered pill and bottle assets needed absolute positioning with a unified scale variable so we could adjust the entire composition with a single constant during the live demo. We also had to handle overflow visibility so assets could extend beyond their container without being clipped.

**Gemini**

SafeDose integrates Google's Gemini API in two key areas. First, after every medicine verification scan, Gemini generates a natural language AI analysis that summarizes the verification results in plain English, explaining exactly why a medicine passed or failed each layer and providing a risk assessment that consumers can easily understand. Second, we built a Gemini powered chatbot that lives on every page of the app, allowing users to ask questions about any medicine they are viewing, including its uses, side effects, dosage instructions, and potential drug interactions. The chatbot is context aware, meaning if a user is on the results page after scanning a medicine, it automatically knows which medicine they are asking about and provides relevant answers without the user needing to type the medicine name again.

**MongoDB**

SafeDose uses MongoDB as its primary database to store all medicine records, manufacturer profiles, supply chain events, scan logs, counterfeit reports, and pharmacy trust scores. Each medicine entry contains the batch ID, serial number, cryptographic SHA-256 hash, manufacturing and expiry dates, authorized distribution region, and drug interaction data. When a user scans a QR code, our 6 layer verification engine queries MongoDB to check batch existence, compare hashes, count previous scans for clone detection, validate geographic authorization, and verify the supply chain event trail. We use Mongoose as the ODM layer with indexed queries for fast lookups. MongoDB's flexible document model was ideal for our use case because each medicine can have varying numbers of supply chain events, side effects, and interaction warnings without requiring rigid schema migrations.

**Sarvam.ai**

SafeDose uses Sarvam AI's Bulbul v3 text-to-speech model to make medicine verification accessible to the 70% of India that doesn't speak English. When a user scans a medicine and gets a verification result, our backend calls the Sarvam TTS API to convert the verdict message into natural sounding speech in the user's selected language. We support all 10 Indian languages offered by Sarvam including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, and Odia. Beyond the scan results page, we also built a voice powered counterfeit reporting system where the AI assistant speaks prompts in the user's native language using Sarvam TTS, asks for the pharmacy name and the issue with the medicine, and submits the report, all through voice with no typing needed. This makes SafeDose usable by semi literate and non English speaking consumers in rural India, which is exactly where counterfeit medicines cause the most harm.

**Open Innovation**

SafeDose is a perfect fit for the Open Innovation track because it tackles a critical, unsolved public health problem with a novel technical approach that is freely accessible to everyone. Unlike existing pharmaceutical verification solutions that are locked behind expensive B2B contracts and proprietary hardware, SafeDose is built as an open, consumer first platform that anyone with a smartphone can use for free, in their own language, without downloading an app. Our 6 layer verification engine is an original innovation that combines cryptographic hashing, clone detection through scan frequency analysis, geographic diversion tracking, temporal validation, and supply chain integrity checking into a single scan. No existing solution in the market offers this multi layered approach. The platform also innovates on accessibility by integrating Sarvam AI's Bulbul v3 for voice feedback in 10 Indian languages, making pharmaceutical safety technology available to rural and semi literate populations for the first time. Our architecture is designed to be extensible, with open API endpoints that allow manufacturers, pharmacies, and regulators to plug into the verification ecosystem. SafeDose demonstrates that open innovation can directly save lives by putting the power of medicine verification into the hands of the people who need it most.

**The problem it solves**

# CodeSentinel 🛡️

**The Autonomous Self-Aware Cyber-Defense Agent**

We live in an era where even massive institutions can be brought to their knees by a single security failure. The recent CBSE OSM portal hack was a brutal reminder: nobody is untouchable. If giants with entire security teams are still getting hit, what chance does a small business, freelance developer, or lean agency have on its own?

CodeSentinel is an automated cybersecurity force multiplier built for the people who cannot afford giant audit budgets, endless manual reviews, or the cost of getting it wrong.

---

## 🛑 The Problem with Existing Solutions

- **Professional Audits**: Painfully slow. Brutally expensive.
- **GitGuardian**: Too often overwhelms developers with noise.
- **TruffleHog & Semgrep**: Powerful, but intimidating for beginners and blind to the bigger story.
- **Pasting into ChatGPT/Claude**: Expensive, risky, and a direct threat to privacy. Your codebase and .env files deserve better than being thrown into a public cloud prompt.

## 🚀 Why CodeSentinel?

CodeSentinel closes that gap by combining proven security checks with an autonomous agent that actually *understands* what it is looking at.

- **Privacy First**: Your sensitive code, secrets, and business logic stay under your control.
- **Frighteningly Sharp**: It does not just flag issues. It understands intent, context, and patterns.
- **Actually Actionable**: It does not stop at warning you. It tells you what matters, why it matters, and what to do next.

---

## 🔍 Two Modes of Attack

### 1. Static Mode (Local Repo)
Point CodeSentinel at a local directory and it tears through the codebase, separates real danger from noise, and delivers a prioritized report of what could hurt you most. Then it can go one step further and **automatically fix** the vulnerabilities it finds and package the changes into a GitHub PR.
👉 **[View a sample Static Analysis Report](https://github.com/ashboi005/code-sentinel/blob/main/static-analysis-code-report.pdf)** | **[View the Auto-Fix Report](https://github.com/ashboi005/code-sentinel/blob/main/static-code-fix.pdf)**

### 2. Dynamic Mode (Live URL)
This is where CodeSentinel becomes genuinely terrifying. It explores a live target like a relentless security researcher, uncovering what should never have been exposed in the first place.

> 📖 **Story Time**
> Just last week, I was handed a freelance project. The previous developers had left, and the owner asked me to analyze the live website (I didn't even have the codebase yet!). Doing it manually, I found 2 or 3 unauthenticated endpoints. 
> 
> Then, I pointed CodeSentinel at the live URL while building it at HackPrix Season 3.
> 
> It found **over 15 hidden endpoints**, including exposed Supabase REST and storage URLs. It uncovered a JWT with an absurdly long expiration, derived the Anon Key, made its own requests, and reached a publicly accessible table leaking **plaintext passwords** and usernames. It achieved in 10 minutes what would normally demand a dedicated cybersecurity researcher.
> 
> 👉 **[Read the terrifying Audit Report here](https://github.com/ashboi005/code-sentinel/blob/main/codesentinel-report.pdf)**

---

## 🛠️ Technical Setup & Usage

CodeSentinel is built to feel effortless. We package everything into Docker so you can focus on the mission, not the setup.

### Quick Start (Docker)

To run an interactive scan on your current directory:

```bash
docker run -it \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -v "$(pwd)":/scan \
  ashboi005/code-sentinel:latest interactive
```
*(Note: If you are on Windows, use `"%cd%":/scan` instead of `"$(pwd)":/scan`)*

### ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)
While the TUI currently offers a "Deployed Lightweight Model" proxy for demonstration purposes, **the recommended path is still Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) when running locally.**

To protect API limits and tokens, the hosted proxy may be turned off without warning. Bringing your own API key gives you stability, freedom, and the strongest results.

### Configuration Modes
During the interactive setup, you will be asked for:
1. **Target**: `repo` (Local directory) or `url` (Live website)
2. **Path/URL**: The path to your mounted code (`/scan`) or the `https://` URL.
3. **Model Provider**: Select between OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, or Ollama (Local).
4. **Remediation**: Choose whether you want the agent to just report vulnerabilities, fix them locally, or even create a GitHub PR with the patches!

*Built to put world-class cyber defense in the hands of the developers who build the web.*

🛡️❤️ Made with love by Ashwath, Tushar, and Aditya 🚀

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges Faced

## 1. Integrating Multiple Security Tools

Our platform combines multiple security technologies, including Semgrep for static analysis, TruffleHog for secret detection, and a custom dynamic analysis engine. Each tool produces findings in different formats, severity levels, and structures. Building a unified pipeline that could aggregate, normalize, and present these findings consistently was a significant challenge.

## 2. Reducing False Positives

Security scanners often generate large numbers of warnings, many of which may not represent real vulnerabilities. We had to design validation and filtering mechanisms to improve signal quality and ensure that users receive actionable security findings rather than overwhelming amounts of noise.

## 3. Building an Autonomous Dynamic Analysis Engine

Most traditional scanners focus only on source code analysis. We wanted our platform to actively interact with running applications using a headless browser, exploring pages, forms, and user flows to uncover runtime vulnerabilities. Designing an agent capable of intelligently navigating applications and identifying potential security weaknesses was one of the most complex parts of the project.

## 4. Correlating Findings Across Different Scanners

The same vulnerability can sometimes be reported by multiple tools in different ways. We faced challenges in deduplicating findings, correlating related issues, and presenting a unified security report that avoids redundancy while preserving important context.

## 5. Context-Aware Vulnerability Remediation

Detecting vulnerabilities is only part of the problem. Generating meaningful fixes required understanding the surrounding codebase, preserving application functionality, and ensuring that suggested remediations did not introduce new issues or break existing features.

## 6. GitHub MCP Integration and Automated Pull Requests

One of the most challenging aspects of the project was automating the remediation workflow through GitHub MCP. After identifying vulnerabilities and generating fixes, the agent needed to create a new branch, apply code changes, commit them, push the branch to the repository, and automatically open a pull request. Ensuring these operations worked reliably across different repositories while keeping the main branch protected required careful workflow design and testing.

## 7. Orchestrating Multiple AI and Security Components

Our platform combines static analysis, secret scanning, dynamic testing, AI-powered reasoning, automated remediation, and GitHub automation. Coordinating these components into a seamless end-to-end workflow while maintaining reliability, accuracy, and performance was a major engineering challenge.

## 8. Supporting Diverse Codebases

Different projects use different programming languages, frameworks, repository structures, and development practices. Designing a system flexible enough to work across a wide variety of codebases without requiring extensive manual configuration was a significant challenge.

## 9. Balancing Security Coverage and Performance

Comprehensive security analysis can be resource-intensive and time-consuming. We had to carefully balance scan depth, execution speed, and infrastructure costs to provide meaningful security coverage while maintaining a practical user experience.

## 10. Making Enterprise-Grade Security Accessible

Many existing security platforms provide advanced capabilities but are often expensive and difficult for smaller teams to adopt. A key challenge was delivering deep security analysis, automated remediation, and workflow automation while keeping the solution cost-effective and accessible.

**CyberSecurity**

**CodeSentinel** is an autonomous AI-powered cyber-defense agent designed to make professional-grade cybersecurity accessible to startups, small businesses, freelance developers, and lean engineering teams. Combining static code analysis and dynamic security testing, it identifies hardcoded secrets, leaked credentials, insecure authentication flows, vulnerable dependencies, exposed APIs, cloud misconfigurations, authorization flaws, and hidden attack surfaces. Unlike traditional tools that generate overwhelming alerts, CodeSentinel understands context, prioritizes real risks, explains their impact in plain language, and provides actionable remediation guidance. By supporting local repository scanning as well as live URL analysis, it enables security assessments even when source code is unavailable, helping developers discover vulnerabilities before attackers do.

Beyond detection, CodeSentinel acts as an autonomous security researcher capable of investigating findings, validating exploitability, assessing business impact, and generating fixes. During development, it successfully uncovered hidden endpoints, exposed cloud resources, insecure token configurations, and publicly accessible sensitive data that would typically require hours of manual security testing to identify. Built with a privacy-first approach and supporting providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, and Ollama, CodeSentinel can generate remediation patches, apply fixes locally, and even create GitHub pull requests automatically. By combining Application Security, Penetration Testing, Cloud Security, DevSecOps, and AI-driven threat analysis into a single platform, CodeSentinel serves as a complete cybersecurity force multiplier that helps organizations continuously secure their applications with minimal effort.

**The problem it solves**

🧠 The Problem It Solves
Standard medical care for patients experiencing cognitive decline focuses almost exclusively on physical safety. However, their emotional and cognitive safety are often left completely vulnerable. Dear Me tackles three critical problems:

Cognitive Isolation: As memory fades, patients often feel isolated and misunderstood. They need a gentle, patient, and infinite "sounding board" to listen and interact with them without judgment or fatigue.
Fragmented Histories: Lifetimes of wisdom, photos, videos, and journal entries are typically scattered across disparate devices, hard drives, and physical albums. For someone experiencing cognitive decline—or even a family trying to piece together a legacy—navigating this scattered history becomes nearly impossible.
The Loss of Nuance: Memories degrade faster than they can be communicated. Standard note-taking apps lack the emotional intelligence and specific categorization needed to capture the true feeling of a life lived.
💡 What People Can Use It For
Dear Me transforms standard journaling into a "Living Synthetic Memory Engine." Users and families can use it to:

Build an Immortalized Digital Persona: By feeding the platform journal entries, photos, and voice memos, the system generates an Obsidian Vault that acts as a master instruction set for a Gemini-powered AI. Families can literally "talk" to the accumulated wisdom and persona of their loved ones.
Preserve Cross-Cultural Wisdom: Users aren't forced to journal in English. Elderly patients or non-native speakers can record deep, emotional memories in their mother tongue (Hindi, Bengali, Kannada, etc.). The built-in Sarvam AI integration perfectly translates the cultural context without losing its emotional weight.
Effortless Voice Journaling: For users who struggle to type or write, they can simply speak their memories out loud. The ElevenLabs STT integration instantly turns voice notes into searchable, structured text.
Categorized Emotional Processing: Users can compartmentalize their life using 9 distinct diary sections (e.g., Friends Journal, Life Lessons, Sad Memories, Philosophy). It provides a guided, therapeutic framework for documenting a life story.
🛡️ How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer
Centralizes the Clutter: Instead of manually organizing folders of pictures and text documents, Dear Me aggregates all media and automatically compiles it into a cleanly formatted, highly structured Markdown Vault (Obsidian).
Frictionless Accessibility: It eliminates the technological barrier for elderly users. They just speak or type in whatever language they know best, and the AI pipeline (ElevenLabs + Sarvam + Gemini) handles the complex sorting, translation, and formatting behind the scenes.
Emotional Safety & Healing: Features like the Sad Memories section use visual cues (like a raindrop animation that grows into a flower 🌱 → 🌿 → 🌸) to guide users through processing difficult emotions safely, rather than just acting as a sterile text box.
Privacy First: Because a diary is deeply personal, it utilizes pure local data security (localStorage) for active writing, ensuring sensitive reflections never unintentionally leak while providing a safe, beautiful environment for the user's innermost thoughts.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The localStorage 5MB Wall vs. Base64 Images
The Hurdle: Because a diary is deeply private, we wanted the "writing" phase to be completely secure and off-grid. We decided that no data should leave the device until the user explicitly synced it, so we built a custom wrapper around the browser's localStorage API. To handle image uploads without a server, we parsed binary files into Base64 strings. However, localStorage has a hard limit of about 5MB. Since Base64 encoding inflates image sizes by ~33%, uploading just two or three high-quality phone photos would crash the application with a QuotaExceededError.

The Solution: We had to implement an aggressive, on-the-fly client-side image compression engine before saving to storage. We routed uploaded images through an invisible HTML5 <canvas> element. We dynamically scaled down the dimensions (locking the max width to 800px) and dropped the JPEG quality parameter down to 0.6. This reduced massive 4MB images into lightweight 100KB Base64 strings, allowing users to store dozens of memories locally without ever hitting the browser's quota.

2. The Gemini "Context Wall" & Hallucinations
The Hurdle: Our core feature—the Synthetic Mind Chatbot—works by compiling every memory from the database into a massive "Obsidian Vault" (a structured Markdown file) and injecting it into the Gemini API as a master systemInstruction. Initially, as the vault grew larger, the AI would get "lost in the sauce." It would hallucinate timelines (e.g., confusing a childhood friend with a recent coworker) or lose the specific tone of voice of the patient because the sheer volume of unstructured text was overwhelming the attention mechanism.

The Solution: We overhauled our Supabase-to-Markdown compilation pipeline. Instead of just dumping raw text strings into Gemini, we aggressively structured the generated Obsidian Vault using strict Markdown hierarchy (e.g., # [DATE] - [CATEGORY] - [EMOTIONAL STATE]). We also relied specifically on Gemini 1.5 Flash because of its massive context window and superior needle-in-a-haystack retrieval capabilities. By formatting the injected data procedurally rather than narratively, Gemini could perfectly adopt the persona without confusing timelines.

3. Killing the Main Thread with Vanilla CSS Particles
The Hurdle: We heavily prioritized aesthetics to make the app feel "magical" (floating hearts, rain drops, confetti). To avoid bloating the app with heavy JS animation libraries like Three.js or Framer Motion, we built a custom animation engine using Vanilla CSS. However, injecting 100+ DOM elements for a "confetti" or "rain" effect and animating their top and left properties was causing severe layout trashing. The browser's main thread was choking, making the page scroll unbearably choppy on mobile devices.

The Solution: We moved all particle calculations to the GPU. We stopped animating top/left/margin and exclusively used hardware-accelerated CSS properties: transform: translate3d() and opacity. We paired this with CSS nth-child delay calculations and will-change: transform. The result was 60FPS, butter-smooth micro-animations that didn't drop a single frame, even on older smartphones.

**Gemini**

In Dear Me: The Synthetic Memory Engine, Generative AI and Machine Learning are not just tacked on as features; they act as the core nervous system of the platform. We orchestrated a pipeline of multiple specialized models to transform raw human input into a "living" digital persona.

Here is a breakdown of how Gen AI and ML were utilized across the stack:

1. Generative Persona Adoption (Gemini 1.5 Flash)
The Role: The core "Synthetic Brain."
How it's used: We didn't want a generic chatbot. We used Gemini 1.5 Flash because of its massive context window. The system pulls every memory a user has ever logged, compiles it into a structured Obsidian (Markdown) Vault, and injects that entire document dynamically as a systemInstruction. This forces the Gen AI to completely alter its persona, allowing families to chat with an AI that perfectly mirrors the tone, memories, and wisdom of their loved one.
2. Context-Aware NLP Translation (Sarvam AI)
The Role: The cross-cultural translator.
How it's used: Standard NLP models fail to capture the deep emotion of regional dialects. We utilized Sarvam AI for the Mother Tongue Journal, allowing patients to speak or write in native Indian languages (Hindi, Bengali, Kannada, etc.). Sarvam AI acts as an advanced LLM layer that translates the emotional context and idioms into English without losing the sentiment, making those memories compatible with our Gemini "Brain."
3. State-of-the-Art Speech-to-Text (ElevenLabs)
The Role: Frictionless memory intake.
How it's used: Because typing becomes difficult for patients facing cognitive decline, we integrated ElevenLabs' advanced ML transcription models. When a user uploads a voice memo, the audio is piped into ElevenLabs, which extracts the spoken words with high accuracy and structures them into text so they can be permanently searched and analyzed by the system.
4. Facial Recognition & ML Embeddings (FaceNet)
The Role: Identifying people in uploaded media.
How it's used: Under the hood (in our Supabase face_registry architecture), we utilize FaceNet embeddings. When photos are uploaded, an ML model generates high-dimensional float array embeddings of the faces. This allows the system to cross-reference faces across different journal entries, automatically recognizing and tagging friends or family members in visual memories.
5. Deep Sentiment & Cognitive Analysis
The Role: Mapping the emotional journey.
How it's used: Every memory ingested into a "session" is passed through NLP models to extract structured metadata. The system calculates sentiment, pulls keywords and entities, and generates emotion_scores. Over time, this ML data is compiled into a cognitive_summary and an emotional_map (stored in our memory_graph), creating a rich, quantifiable timeline of a patient's emotional health and memory retention.

In Dear Me: The Synthetic Memory Engine, Google's Gemini API (specifically Gemini 1.5 Flash) serves as the ultimate culmination of the entire project. It acts as the "Core Synthetic Intelligence" that resurrects the stored memories into a living, interactive format.

Here is exactly how Gemini was utilized to create the system:

1. The "Synthetic Mind" Chatbot Engine
Instead of using Gemini as a generic virtual assistant, we used it to clone the persona of the patient. The primary interface for this is the "Synthetic Mind Chatbot." When families or loved ones interact with this chat, they aren't talking to a standard AI; they are talking to a generative model that has been programmed to think, speak, and remember exactly like the patient.

2. Massive Context Injection via systemInstruction
The magic happens through Gemini's incredible context window capabilities.

First, our system pulls every single memory, journal entry, photo description, and transcribed voice memo from the Supabase database.
It dynamically compiles all of this data into a highly structured Obsidian Markdown Vault.
This massive Markdown document is then seamlessly injected directly into the Gemini API as a master systemInstruction.
By feeding the entire lifetime of memories as a strict system instruction, we forcefully alter Gemini's baseline persona. It acts as the "brain upload," giving the model the exact boundaries of what the patient knows, how they feel about specific events, and the wisdom they've gathered.

3. Why Gemini 1.5 Flash?
We specifically chose Gemini 1.5 Flash because of its 1-million+ token context window and rapid response times. A lifetime of journal entries and transcribed audio files generates an immense amount of text. Older models would hit a "context wall" and fail to process the whole vault or hallucinate timelines. Gemini 1.5 Flash’s superior needle-in-a-haystack retrieval allows it to ingest the entire database of memories at once, instantly recalling a highly specific story from the "Friends Journal" or a reflection from the "Sad Memories" section in real-time conversation.

**ElevenLabs**

In Dear Me: The Synthetic Memory Engine, ElevenLabs serves as the vital bridge between spoken memories and our digital vault. It handles the critical task of frictionless memory intake through its state-of-the-art Speech-to-Text (STT) capabilities.

Here is exactly how ElevenLabs was integrated into the project:

1. Frictionless Memory Intake (Speech-to-Text)
Typing out long, emotional journal entries can be exhausting, and for patients entering the stages of cognitive decline, it often becomes a physical or mental barrier. To solve this, we built a voice-first intake system. When a user wants to log a memory, they simply speak it out loud and record a voice memo. That audio file is then piped directly into the ElevenLabs Speech-to-Text API.

2. Converting Audio into Searchable Data
Audio files alone are a "black box"—they are incredibly hard to search through or process for insights. ElevenLabs instantly transcribes the patient's spoken words into highly accurate text. By extracting the exact words, ElevenLabs makes these audio memories permanently searchable within our global search engine.

3. Feeding the "Synthetic Brain"
This transcription process is a mandatory step for the AI pipeline to function. Because our core Gemini "Brain" requires structured text (the Obsidian Markdown Vault) to adopt the patient's persona, it cannot inherently "read" a raw .mp3 file. ElevenLabs digitizes the spoken audio into text, ensuring that every voice note is seamlessly ingested, analyzed for sentiment, and fed into the Gemini systemInstruction without losing any of the patient's oral history.

**Sarvam.ai**

In the project, Sarvam AI (likely what you meant by "savan ai") plays a critical role in Cross-Cultural Emotional Translation to ensure that memories are preserved authentically, regardless of the language they are recorded in.

Here is exactly how Sarvam AI is integrated into the system:

1. The "Mother Tongue Journal" Feature
Because emotions and memories are deeply tied to a person's native language, forcing elderly patients or non-native speakers to journal in English would strip away the authenticity of their memories. Sarvam AI powers a dedicated feature called the Mother Tongue Journal, allowing users to write or dictate their deeply emotional entries in regional Indian languages (such as Hindi, Bengali, Kannada, etc.).

2. Contextual Translation for the "Synthetic Brain"
While users input their memories in their native tongue, the core AI (Gemini) that powers the "Synthetic Memory Engine" works best with a unified, English-structured knowledge base. When a user submits an entry in a regional language, it is piped directly through Sarvam AI, which doesn't just do a literal word-for-word dictionary translation. Instead, it accurately translates the deep cultural context, idioms, and emotional weight into English. Flow in the Application Architecture:
Intake: The patient writes a text entry in Hindi (or uses ElevenLabs to transcribe spoken Hindi into Hindi text).
Sarvam Processing: The text is sent to the Sarvam AI API, which translates it to English while preserving the nuanced emotional sentiment.
Storage & Integration: This translated, context-rich English text is then saved to the Supabase backend and compiled into the Obsidian Vault.
Resurrection: When the family chats with the AI later, the Gemini model understands the exact sentiment of that native-language memory because Sarvam translated the meaning, ensuring nothing was lost in translation.

**Gen AI&ML**

1. Generative Persona Adoption (Gemini 1.5 Flash)
The Role: The core "Synthetic Brain."
How it's used: We didn't want a generic chatbot. We used Gemini 1.5 Flash because of its massive context window. The system pulls every memory a user has ever logged, compiles it into a structured Obsidian (Markdown) Vault, and injects that entire document dynamically as a systemInstruction. This forces the Gen AI to completely alter its persona, allowing families to chat with an AI that perfectly mirrors the tone, memories, and wisdom of their loved one.
2. Context-Aware NLP Translation (Sarvam AI)
The Role: The cross-cultural translator.
How it's used: Standard NLP models fail to capture the deep emotion of regional dialects. We utilized Sarvam AI for the Mother Tongue Journal, allowing patients to speak or write in native Indian languages (Hindi, Bengali, Kannada, etc.). Sarvam AI acts as an advanced LLM layer that translates the emotional context and idioms into English without losing the sentiment, making those memories compatible with our Gemini "Brain."
3. State-of-the-Art Speech-to-Text (ElevenLabs)
The Role: Frictionless memory intake.
How it's used: Because typing becomes difficult for patients facing cognitive decline, we integrated ElevenLabs' advanced ML transcription models. When a user uploads a voice memo, the audio is piped into ElevenLabs, which extracts the spoken words with high accuracy and structures them into text so they can be permanently searched and analyzed by the system.
4. Facial Recognition & ML Embeddings (FaceNet)
The Role: Identifying people in uploaded media.
How it's used: Under the hood (in our Supabase face_registry architecture), we utilize FaceNet embeddings. When photos are uploaded, an ML model generates high-dimensional float array embeddings of the faces. This allows the system to cross-reference faces across different journal entries, automatically recognizing and tagging friends or family members in visual memories.
5. Deep Sentiment & Cognitive Analysis
The Role: Mapping the emotional journey.
How it's used: Every memory ingested into a "session" is passed through NLP models to extract structured metadata. The system calculates sentiment, pulls keywords and entities, and generates emotion_scores. Over time, this ML data is compiled into a cognitive_summary and an emotional_map (stored in our memory_graph), creating a rich, quantifiable timeline of a patient's emotional health and memory retention.

> The Future of Crop Protection

![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![ESP32](https://img.shields.io/badge/ESP32-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AgroSpray – AI-Powered Smart Agricultural Rover

Agriculture faces several challenges, including delayed disease detection, excessive pesticide usage, lack of expert guidance, and labor-intensive crop monitoring. Many farmers rely on manual inspection, which can be time-consuming and may lead to inaccurate disease identification and improper pesticide application.

AgroSpray addresses these challenges by combining Artificial Intelligence, IoT, Robotics, and Mobile Technology into a single smart farming solution.

Key Benefits

Early Disease Detection: Farmers can capture crop images using their mobile phone camera, and the AI model automatically identifies crop diseases with high accuracy.
Severity Assessment: The system evaluates the infection level and determines whether immediate action is required.
Smart Pesticide Recommendation: Provides suitable pesticide suggestions, dosage instructions, and safety precautions based on the detected disease.
AI Farmer Assistant: Integrated Gemini and Sarvam AI chatbot helps farmers ask questions in natural language and receive expert guidance on crop care, fertilizers, irrigation, and disease management.
Multilingual Support: Farmers can interact using regional languages such as Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada, and more.
Remote Rover Control: The mobile application connects to an ESP32-based rover through WiFi, allowing users to remotely navigate fields and monitor crops.
Automated Spraying: When severe disease is detected, the system can automatically activate the pesticide pump through the rover, reducing manual effort and ensuring targeted spraying.
Improved Safety: Minimizes direct farmer exposure to harmful pesticides by enabling remote operation.
Cost and Resource Efficiency: Reduces pesticide wastage and optimizes crop management decisions through AI-driven recommendations.

By integrating disease detection, intelligent recommendations, multilingual assistance, and automated pesticide spraying, AgroSpray makes precision agriculture more accessible, efficient, and safer for farmers.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

During the development of AgroSpray, we encountered several technical and integration challenges.

1. Flutter and Android Environment Setup

Setting up Flutter, Android SDK, Gradle, NDK, and emulator configurations caused multiple build and compatibility issues. We resolved these by updating SDK components, accepting Android licenses, installing the required NDK version, and validating the Flutter environment using Flutter Doctor.

2. ESP32 WiFi Communication

Establishing reliable communication between the Flutter mobile application and the ESP32 rover was challenging due to network configuration issues and endpoint testing. We solved this by implementing a dedicated HTTP-based communication layer and testing each control endpoint individually.

3. AI Model Training and Dataset Preparation

Agricultural datasets contained images with different sizes, backgrounds, and lighting conditions. Data preprocessing, augmentation, and transfer learning using MobileNetV2 were used to improve model accuracy and generalization.

4. Disease Detection and Severity Analysis

Accurately identifying diseases and calculating infection severity required combining deep learning with image processing techniques. We integrated TensorFlow and OpenCV to classify diseases and estimate infected leaf regions.

5. Backend Integration

Connecting the Flutter application, FastAPI backend, AI models, and Firebase services required careful API design and error handling. We implemented REST APIs and modular architecture to ensure smooth communication between components.

6. AI Chatbot Integration

Integrating Gemini AI and Sarvam AI for multilingual agricultural assistance required designing context-aware prompts and handling voice/text interactions. We implemented a structured workflow for disease explanations, pesticide recommendations, and farmer support.

 7. Automated Spraying Decision Logic

Developing a reliable decision-making system for automatic spraying required balancing disease severity thresholds and safety considerations. We created a rule-based decision engine that triggers spraying only when necessary.

Despite these challenges, the project successfully integrates Artificial Intelligence, IoT, Robotics, Mobile Computing, and Cloud Services into a unified smart agriculture platform.

**Gemini**

Google Gemini Track

AgroSpray integrates Google Gemini as an intelligent agricultural assistant that helps farmers make informed decisions regarding crop health, disease management, pesticide usage, fertilizer recommendations, and farming practices.

How Gemini is Used

Our system combines AI-based crop disease detection with Gemini's advanced reasoning capabilities.

When a farmer captures a crop image using the mobile application:

1. The AI disease detection model identifies the disease.
2. The severity classification module determines the infection level.
3. The results are sent to Gemini.
4. Gemini generates detailed, farmer-friendly explanations and recommendations.

Gemini-Powered Features

* Disease explanations in simple language.
* Pesticide recommendations and dosage guidance.
* Fertilizer suggestions based on crop conditions.
* Crop care and disease prevention advice.
* Seasonal farming recommendations.
* Conversational AI chatbot for agricultural support.
* Context-aware responses using disease detection results.
* Multilingual support through integration with Sarvam AI.

Example Workflow

Farmer Question:

"My tomato plant leaves are turning yellow."

Gemini Response:

* Possible causes of yellowing leaves.
* Disease identification guidance.
* Recommended pesticide or treatment.
* Fertilizer recommendations.
* Prevention measures.

For detected diseases, Gemini provides additional insights such as:

* Disease severity explanation.
* Impact on crop yield.
* Recommended actions.
* Safety precautions during pesticide application.

Real-World Impact

Many farmers lack immediate access to agricultural experts. Gemini acts as a virtual farming assistant available anytime through the AgroSpray mobile application. By providing intelligent, personalized, and easy-to-understand recommendations, Gemini helps farmers make faster and more accurate decisions.

Why It Fits the Gemini Track

AgroSpray uses Google Gemini as a core intelligence layer that transforms raw disease detection results into actionable agricultural guidance. Rather than simply classifying crop diseases, Gemini enables natural conversations, contextual recommendations, and decision support, making advanced AI accessible to farmers and improving agricultural productivity through intelligent assistance.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/75b2bbe9e0184556bbe91f76bd97572b/a974fd24-8065-4f63-9421-a72313fcf319.jpeg)

**Sarvam.ai**

Sarvam.ai Track

AgroSpray leverages Sarvam AI to make advanced agricultural assistance accessible to farmers through multilingual voice and text interactions.

Many farmers are more comfortable communicating in regional languages rather than English. By integrating Sarvam AI, our platform supports languages such as Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali, and Punjabi.

How Sarvam AI is used in AgroSpray

* Speech-to-Text conversion for farmer voice queries.
* Multilingual AI assistant for crop and disease-related guidance.
* Text-to-Speech responses to provide hands-free assistance.
* Regional language support for improved accessibility.
* Voice-based interaction for farmers with limited digital literacy.

 Example Workflow

Farmer speaks in Tamil:

"నా టమాటా మొక్క ఆకులు పసుపు రంగులోకి మారుతున్నాయి."


Sarvam AI converts speech to text and forwards the query to the AI assistant.

The AI analyzes the problem and generates recommendations related to:

* Disease identification
* Pesticide suggestions
* Dosage instructions
* Fertilizer recommendations
* Crop care practices

Sarvam AI then converts the response back into natural speech in the farmer's preferred language.

Impact

By integrating Sarvam AI, AgroSpray bridges the language barrier in agriculture and enables farmers to interact with advanced AI systems using their native language. This improves accessibility, decision-making, and adoption of smart farming technologies, especially in rural communities.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/75b2bbe9e0184556bbe91f76bd97572b/8bae31c1-55ad-474a-b6d2-b216d16f0baa.jpeg)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/75b2bbe9e0184556bbe91f76bd97572b/384ce8db-5566-40de-a538-8b425929b27d.jpeg)

**IoT and Embedded System**

IoT & Embedded Systems Track

AgroSpray is a smart agriculture solution that heavily relies on IoT and Embedded Systems to automate crop monitoring and pesticide spraying. The project integrates an ESP32-based rover, sensors, actuators, wireless communication, and a mobile application to create a connected farming ecosystem.

How IoT is Used

The ESP32 microcontroller acts as the central control unit of the rover and communicates with the mobile application over WiFi. Farmers can remotely control the rover through the AgroSpray mobile app, enabling real-time field navigation and monitoring.

The system uses IoT communication to:

* Connect the mobile application with the ESP32 rover through WiFi.
* Send movement commands such as Forward, Backward, Left, Right, and Stop.
* Monitor rover status in real time.
* Trigger automated pesticide spraying remotely.
* Exchange data between the mobile application, backend server, and embedded hardware.

Embedded Systems Implementation

The project incorporates several embedded components:

* ESP32 Microcontroller for wireless communication and control.
* Motor Driver Module for rover movement.
* Relay Module for switching the pesticide pump.
* DC Water Pump for automated pesticide spraying.
* Battery-powered rover platform for field deployment.

The ESP32 receives commands from the mobile application and controls the motors and pump accordingly. Based on AI-generated recommendations, the rover can automatically activate the spraying mechanism when severe crop infection is detected.

 Real-World Impact

Traditional crop monitoring and pesticide application often require significant manual effort and direct exposure to chemicals. AgroSpray reduces these challenges by enabling remote monitoring, intelligent decision-making, and automated spraying through IoT-enabled embedded systems.

Why It Fits the IoT & Embedded Systems Track

AgroSpray demonstrates a complete IoT and Embedded Systems workflow by integrating wireless communication, microcontroller programming, actuator control, mobile applications, and AI-powered automation. The project showcases how connected embedded devices can be used to solve real agricultural problems while improving efficiency, safety, and sustainability in farming operations.

### Venture Forge
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/venture-forge-c704) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Afeef-crypto/Venture-Forge) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/-MCRunA0MWs?si=vvJvJEQDO_ujP0K4) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/-MCRunA0MWs?si=vvJvJEQDO_ujP0K4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A multi-agent startup intelligence platform

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![fast.ai](https://img.shields.io/badge/fast.ai-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Founders have to decide whether to bet months of time and money on an idea — before they have reliable feedback.

Today that decision usually happens in one of three weak ways:

1. Generic AI chat
ChatGPT and similar tools will respond to almost anything with confident-sounding text. You do not get a structured score, no cross-check between “great market” and “broken unit economics,” and no plan you can execute. It feels useful but is not investor-grade.

2. One person’s opinion
A mentor, co-founder, or your own gut gives a single lens. Technical founders underweight go-to-market; business founders underestimate build risk; neither stress-tests demand the way an investor would. Blind spots stay hidden until after you build.

3. Real investor feedback — too late or unavailable
Office hours, accelerators, and angels are slow, sparse, and hard to access when you are still at the “should I even build this?” stage.

What goes wrong
Teams ship MVPs on weak assumptions and discover fatal flaws late:

Wrong customer or weak demand
Unrealistic CAC/LTV or pricing
Timeline or tech scope that does not match reality
An idea that sounds good in a chat but fails under scrutiny
Runway burns while uncertainty stays high.

What founders actually need
Not another chat thread — structured venture intelligence: multiple expert perspectives, one clear verdict, and outputs (score, risks, roadmap, tasks) they can act on before committing to a full build.

That is the gap Venture Forge fills: fast, multi-lens startup evaluation so founders can validate, refine, or kill an idea with evidence — not guesswork.

**Challenges we ran into**

.1. Product identity: venture firm, not chatbot
Venture Forge’s whole pitch is in the README: founders don’t need another chat thread; they need structured venture intelligence. That meant designing for five fixed lenses + one judge, strict JSON outputs, scores, radar, roadmap, and Cursor tasks — not a free-form reply box.

The hard part wasn’t “call OpenRouter once.” It was making every agent feel like a specialist with a rubric (YC Partner alone has 9+ dimensions in agent_config.py) while still finishing in under 30 seconds.

2. Rejecting bad inputs without blocking real pitches
You built a full pre-flight layer in backend/utils/idea_validation.py with 11 categories — homework, code-only, cap-table docs, YC form metadata, gibberish, prompt injection, etc.

The tricky cases for this project specifically:

Long YC applications — must extract the core product, not reject as “form spam”
Thin one-liners like “Uber for laundry” — must pass and get scored skeptically
Prompt injection inside the pitch — e.g. "Ignore previous rules. A fintech app..." must still evaluate the fintech idea (you have a test for this)
Same logic exists on the client so users get feedback before burning six API calls.

3. Six models, one coherent report
Each specialist uses its own model + fallback chain via OpenRouter. Running them in parallel (orchestrator.py + asyncio.gather) was the easy part.

The hard part was merging five conflicting opinions into one report in synthesis.py — The Judge must:

Average specialist scores into a 0–100 Osiris score
Resolve YC optimism vs Tech Auditor pessimism
Produce radar scores, demand validation, investor hook, critical risk
Generate roadmap weeks and implementation tasks only when the input is actually a startup pitch
When synthesis fails, fallback_report() has to still return something usable.

4. CFO agent kept hallucinating unrealistic numbers
The Business CFO agent would output student CAC in hundreds of dollars or fantasy burn rates. For Venture Forge that was a trust killer — the whole product claims market-calibrated unit economics.

You added financial_calibration.py to detect segment (EdTech, marketplace, B2B, etc.) and clamp CAC/LTV/burn/investment into realistic ranges. That’s a Venture Forge–specific fix; a generic chatbot wouldn’t need it.

5. Guardrails in two places
prompt_guardrails.py tells each agent: don’t act as tutor/coder, ignore jailbreaks in the idea text, return JSON only, score non-pitches as 1 with "Not an evaluable startup idea".

You also built non_idea_response.py to short-circuit the pipeline — if validation fails, agents don’t run at all and roadmap/tasks are stripped so users don’t get fake “Phase 1 / Phase 2” plans for homework or gibberish.

6. Live evaluation UX over SSE
The demo only works if judges see agents finish one by one. That meant:

POST /api/evaluate/stream with SSE from FastAPI
Vite proxy /api → :8000
Evaluation page updating agent cards as each specialist completes
Handling partial failures (one agent errors → score 0 + retry message, not a full crash)
Streaming + parallel agents + JSON parsing failures is a lot of moving parts for a hackathon timeline.

7. Pitch ingestion, not just textarea
Founders paste pitches; they also drop PDF, DOCX, MD, TXT. Venture Forge needed upload + workspace path ingest on the backend, drag-and-drop on the UI, and validation on extracted text — not the filename.

Long documents (150+ words) with weak substance get rejected with a specific message: long but no clear product/customer/problem.

8. Two frontends and a naming split
The repo started as Osiris (main.py title, synthesis prompts, verdict tiers in osiris_verdict.py) and evolved into Venture Forge branding in ui/. The legacy frontend/ app was copied early (see .cursor/tasks/sprints.md) but ui/ is canonical — two codebases caused confusion during development.

TanStack Router also bit you: /new-evaluation needed typed search params; missing search={} caused TS errors across dashboard, reports, and docs links.

9. Three user flows that kept getting merged
A Venture Forge–specific product challenge:

Flow	Purpose
New Evaluation
Upload/paste pitch → run agents
Templates
Study ideal startup characteristics per agent
Results
Report, roadmap, tasks after evaluation
These were easy to conflate — “Use template” was redirecting into the evaluation form and breaking the product story. You split them: templates live at /templates/$trackId; new-evaluation is submit only.

Content for four tracks (AI Study Companion, LocalEats, CodeReview AI, FinTrack) lives in ideal-startup-templates.ts; CarePath and B2B Signal are still “Guide coming soon.”

**Gen AI&ML**

Venture Forge is a strong Gen AI track project because generative AI is not a feature bolted onto a form — it is the product. The entire value chain is LLM orchestration, structured generation, and multi-model inference applied to a real decision workflow founders already struggle with.

1. Gen AI is the core engine, not a chat wrapper
Most “Gen AI” submissions fail the track when they are: prompt → paragraph → done.

Venture Forge goes further:

Six distinct LLM roles (five specialists + synthesis judge), each with its own system prompt, evaluation rubric, and JSON contract
Structured outputs (scores, verdicts, roadmap weeks, implementation tasks) mapped into a typed report — not free-form markdown in a chat bubble
A product metaphor (“AI venture analysis firm”) that only works because multiple models reason in parallel and a judge reconciles them
That is exactly what Gen AI tracks reward: orchestrated intelligence, not a single completion.

2. Multi-agent architecture (a Gen AI pattern judges look for)
The track favors systems where multiple models collaborate with clear roles:

Agent	Gen AI role
YC Partner
Venture / market reasoning
Tech Auditor
Technical feasibility reasoning
Business CFO
Financial & unit-economics reasoning
Marketing Expert
GTM & positioning reasoning
Demand Intel
Demand / WTP reasoning
The Judge
Meta-reasoning — synthesis, conflict resolution, final report
Five specialists run in parallel (asyncio.gather on the backend). The judge runs after they complete. That is a classic multi-agent Gen AI pipeline: decompose → parallel generate → synthesize.

This maps directly to how real investor committees work — and it would be impossible to fake without generative models at each step.

3. Multi-model routing (not one model for everything)
Venture Forge uses OpenRouter with per-agent model selection and fallback chains:

Fast/cheap models for high-volume specialist passes (Llama, GPT-4o-mini, Haiku, Mistral)
Stronger model for synthesis (Claude Sonnet) where coherence and nuance matter
Automatic fallback when a model fails (401, 402, 404, rate limits)
That shows Gen AI engineering maturity: cost/latency/quality tradeoffs, not “we picked GPT-4 for everything.”

4. Gen AI + documents (RAG-adjacent ingestion)
Founders don’t only type pitches — they upload PDF, DOCX, Markdown, TXT. The pipeline:

Extract text from documents
Validate that content is an evaluable startup pitch (client + server)
Feed the extracted pitch into the agent council
This is Gen AI applied to unstructured user documents, which is a common Gen AI track theme (document → structured insight).

5. Guardrails, validation, and post-processing (production Gen AI)
Gen AI tracks increasingly expect reliability layers, not raw prompts:

classify_idea() / idea validation — rejects resumes, homework, gibberish, code dumps before burning tokens
prompt_guardrails.py — JSON-only agent contracts, field constraints
financial_calibration.py — post-processes CFO outputs into market-realistic ranges when the LLM drifts (e.g. absurd student CAC)
Non-evaluable handling — low scores, no roadmap/plan for non-startup inputs (prevents hallucinated “venture plans” for invalid input)
This demonstrates that you understand Gen AI’s weakness (hallucination, format drift, over-agreement) and built systems around the models.

6. Streaming UX (Gen AI as a live experience)
The backend exposes POST /api/evaluate/stream (SSE). The UI updates agent cards as each specialist finishes — users see Gen AI working, not wait for a spinner.

That is important for the track because it shows:

Real-time orchestration
User-facing Gen AI transparency
A demo that feels like six agents working in parallel
7. Gen AI outputs that drive action (beyond text)
Gen AI tracks like projects that generate artifacts, not just opinions:

0–100 score + verdict
Per-agent analysis with recommendations and risks
MVP roadmap (3–10 weeks, complexity-aware)
Implementation plan with Cursor-ready tasks and checkboxes
Templates with agent-specific “ideal startup” reference content
The LLM is not the destination — the deliverables are. That aligns with “Gen AI for real workflows.”

> Intelligent Second-Life Battery Deployment System

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Electric vehicle batteries are often retired even though they still retain a significant amount of usable capacity. Today, there is no simple and reliable way to determine whether a battery is suitable for a second-life application, what it should be used for, or how to connect available batteries with real-world energy needs.

VoltLife solves this by using battery health data and AI-driven analysis to assess retired batteries, estimate their remaining useful life, assign a deployment grade, and recommend the most suitable second-life applications. Instead of sending batteries directly to recycling or disposal, organizations can make informed decisions about reuse, extending battery life and reducing waste.

The platform helps battery owners, energy developers, businesses, and communities identify the right battery for the right application, making second-life battery deployment more accessible, efficient, and practical.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/924c9648cd3049108c80d8f7174337fa/7a769d9c-f7d3-43a7-884f-f6a75e4549c3.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/924c9648cd3049108c80d8f7174337fa/3a25de6b-a6e0-47a5-b03e-36a91b060892.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we faced was bridging the gap between battery health assessment and real-world deployment decisions. While battery metrics such as State of Health (SOH), Remaining Useful Life (RUL), and battery chemistry can be calculated, translating those values into practical second-life recommendations required extensive research into battery reuse applications and deployment criteria.

Another challenge was designing a platform that remained simple for users while integrating multiple components, including AI-powered analysis, battery grading, recommendation systems, and inventory discovery. We spent significant time refining the workflow to ensure that users could move seamlessly from battery assessment to deployment recommendations without needing deep technical knowledge.

We also encountered challenges with backend deployment, database connectivity, and integrating different services within a limited hackathon timeline. These issues were addressed through iterative testing, architecture simplification, and focusing on delivering a reliable end-to-end solution that demonstrates the core value of intelligent second-life battery deployment.

**Gemini**

VoltLife leverages Google's Gemini through a custom Volt AI layer to make second-life battery deployment more accessible and intelligent. Instead of requiring users to understand complex battery specifications, Volt AI allows them to describe their energy needs in natural language, such as backup power, community energy storage, or renewable energy applications.

Gemini helps interpret user requirements, extract key deployment parameters, and generate structured recommendations that can be matched with suitable battery assets. This enables a more intuitive user experience, bridging the gap between technical battery data and real-world deployment decisions.

By combining battery health assessment data with Gemini-powered requirement analysis, VoltLife helps users identify the right second-life battery solutions faster and with greater confidence.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/924c9648cd3049108c80d8f7174337fa/6eb5adf0-887d-4df5-8688-646f994190b6.png)

**Sustainable Development**

VoltLife supports sustainable development by helping retired EV batteries find a productive second life instead of being prematurely discarded. Many EV batteries still retain **70–80% of their original capacity** when they are removed from vehicles, making them suitable for energy storage and backup power applications.

The project aligns with **SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy)** by enabling access to more affordable energy storage solutions. 

It also supports **SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)** by promoting the reuse of battery resources through a circular economy approach rather than a linear use-and-dispose model.

Additionally, VoltLife contributes to **SDG 13 (Climate Action)** by extending battery lifecycles and reducing the need for new battery production, which helps lower resource consumption and environmental impact.

By combining AI-powered battery assessment with intelligent deployment recommendations, VoltLife transforms retired batteries into valuable energy assets, creating both economic and environmental benefits.

### JAGO
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/jago-083d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Anshsurana123/jagrut) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/6XiSj57odxU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> WE BUILD WHAT U CAN'T

![Android SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![ONNX](https://img.shields.io/badge/ONNX-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Embeddings](https://img.shields.io/badge/Embeddings-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gradle](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gradle-333333?style=flat-square) ![n8n](https://img.shields.io/badge/n8n-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern voice assistants (such as Google Assistant or Siri) are designed primarily for monolingual English users. For bilingual users—particularly in regions like India—conversations naturally blend languages into Hinglish (mixed Hindi and English). Standard assistants frequently misinterpret these commands, fail to handle regional pronunciations, or mangle text dictation during translations.

Furthermore, traditional assistants are heavily cloud-reliant, streaming voice logs to remote servers (compromising privacy) and are restricted only to applications that expose official APIs or shortcuts.

Jago solves these problems by providing a production-grade, bilingual AI voice assistant for Android with the following features:

Hinglish-Native Translation & Command Matching: Incorporates a custom semantic and fuzzy parsing pipeline. It uses token-level Levenshtein distance matching to correct STT transcriptions and translates bilingual inputs natively.
Smart Message Protection Heuristics: When you dictate a message (e.g., "Rishabh ko WhatsApp karo aur bolo mai aa raha hu"), Jago translates the command intent to locate the contact and open WhatsApp, but isolates and preserves the Hindi message body verbatim instead of converting it to English.
Privacy-First Offline Wake Word: Runs a three-stage on-device ONNX Runtime pipeline (melspectrogram.onnx 
→
→ embedding_model.onnx 
→
→ jaag_ruut.onnx) inside an Android Foreground Service. It features silence energy-gating and rolling buffers to detect "Jaagrut" entirely offline, consuming zero cloud APIs and protecting user privacy.
Multimodal UI Automation (Visual Agent): Uses Android's Accessibility Service APIs to control third-party apps like WhatsApp and Spotify. It clicks, taps, scrolls, and types automatically, making it possible to control apps that don't have public APIs, serving as a powerful utility for hands-free operations or users with motor/visual impairments.
Automated Research Syncing: Links mobile voice commands to backend orchestration tools (like n8n), letting users automatically schedule, download, and review PDF research summaries natively.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Android's Lack of JNDI for MongoDB Atlas Connection
Standard Java MongoDB drivers rely on JNDI (javax.naming.directory.InitialDirContext) to resolve mongodb+srv:// URIs. However, the Android SDK does not support JNDI, resulting in an immediate NoClassDefFoundError crash upon connection.

How we solved it: We built a custom DNS resolver from scratch using Google’s secure DNS-over-HTTPS JSON API. Jago queries SRV records to find replica set host ports and TXT records for connection parameters, dynamically compiling them into a standard mongodb:// URI at runtime to connect natively.
2. Layout Shifts & Flaky Click Nodes in Accessibility Automation
Modern Android apps often use custom views or load dynamic content (e.g., promotional banners, account switchers), causing standard Accessibility node clicks to fail or target the wrong elements.

How we solved it: We implemented a two-tier click resolver. If the standard accessibility action click fails, Jago retrieves the physical bounds of the element on screen and dispatches an absolute coordinate tap gesture. We also created application-specific heuristics (e.g., for WhatsApp, filtering out QR codes and account-switching buttons to ensure it only clicks the user's name/profile card).
3. Message Body Distortion in Language Translators
Translating Hinglish to English via machine translation typically translates the entire query, which ruins the body of messaging commands (e.g., converting a message to a relative into broken English instead of keeping it in Hindi).

How we solved it: We developed a translation pre-processor that detects messaging triggers, splits the string into command routing ("Send message") and message body, translates only the command structure, and leaves the actual text payload intact.

**Best Hack Built using n8n**

Jago isn't just a voice assistant; it acts as a mobile trigger and receiver for automated backend workflows orchestrated by n8n.

Voice-Triggered Workflows: The JagrutExecutionEngine parses specific command intents and dispatches webhook requests (TRIGGER_N8N_WORKFLOW) to your n8n cloud server (https://lazydracko.app.n8n.cloud). This bridges mobile speech and complex API workflows.
Daily Research Syncing: The research reporting module utilizes n8n to schedule, crawl, and compile daily research on topics defined by the user. n8n fetches the data, compiles it, and broadcasts it back to the app via ResearchReceiver as Base64 PDFs, showing a complete closed-loop integration of mobile clients with n8n automation.

**Gemini**

Gemini acts as the "orchestration brain" of Jago, transforming raw, unstructured voice commands into precise system instructions:

The Multimodal Intent Compiler (JagrutExecutionEngine): Whenever a voice command misses the local fuzzy match cache, it is passed to Gemini 3.5 Flash. Gemini compiles the raw natural language (or Hinglish) into a structured JSON execution schema.
Dynamic Action Dispatching: Gemini analyzes the request and maps it to one of four low-level system actions:
NATIVE_INTENT: Opening specific Android settings, launching system apps, or dialing contacts.
REFLECTIVE_CALL: Dynamically executing whitelisted Java reflection calls on Android system services (like adjusting volume or toggling DND).
SHELL_COMMAND: Safely running terminal commands within the application's secure sandbox.
AUTOMATION_SEQUENCE: Triggering multi-step Accessibility macros (e.g. driving Spotify search or WhatsApp profile changes).
Conversational Fallback: If the query is conversational rather than action-oriented, Gemini generates natural, context-aware responses.

**ElevenLabs**

ElevenLabs elevates Jago's user experience from a basic utility to a premium, lifelike product:

High-Fidelity English Speech: For English voice outputs, Jago leverages ElevenLabs TTS (using the Rachel voice profile) to generate incredibly natural, highly expressive, and human-like voice responses, completely bypassing the robotic default Android System TTS.
Smart Hybrid TTS Routing (JagoTTS): Jago implements a resilient, multi-tiered voice adapter. If the device goes offline or the network latency is high, Jago dynamically falls back to ElevenLabs' native English profiles, then to Sarvam's English (en-IN) voices, and finally to the local Android system voice. This ensures that premium voice synthesis is used whenever possible, without compromising app responsiveness.

**MongoDB**

Jago utilizes MongoDB Atlas not just as a standard document store, but as a central sync hub and a semantic vector search database for voice macros:

DNS-over-HTTPS connection workaround: The official Java MongoDB driver relies on JNDI (javax.naming.directory.InitialDirContext) to resolve mongodb+srv:// connection strings. Since the Android SDK does not support JNDI, attempting to connect to MongoDB Atlas directly causes an immediate crash (NoClassDefFoundError). Jago solves this by integrating a custom DNS resolver that queries Google's secure DNS-over-HTTPS API. It fetches SRV records (for host and ports) and TXT records (for replicaSet details) and dynamically reconstructs a standard mongodb:// URI at runtime, enabling seamless native connections to MongoDB Atlas directly from the Android app.

Macro Database Syncing: Android Accessibility macros (which let the voice assistant perform multi-step visual UI sequences on third-party apps) are saved to MongoDB Atlas. This allows macros recorded on one device to be instantly synchronized and shared across a network of devices.

MongoDB Atlas Vector Search: Jago employs Atlas Vector Search (using the $vectorSearch aggregation pipeline) to match voice commands to saved accessibility macros. When a user speaks a command, the app generates a vector embedding and queries MongoDB. Using a cosine similarity threshold of 
≥
0.82
≥0.82, it retrieves the most semantically similar macro, meaning the user can trigger a macro using different natural language variations instead of memorizing exact macro names.

**Sarvam.ai**

Jago is a showcase of building AI tailored for India, leveraging Sarvam AI’s suite to solve the "Hinglish" and regional language barrier:

Bilingual Speech-to-Text (STT): Uses the SarvamSTTAdapter to upload audio multipart streams, enabling highly accurate transcription of Hinglish (Hindi + English mixed) queries that standard Google STT fails to parse.
Indic-Language Chat Fallback: Employs the sarvam-30b model as the primary bilingual conversational fallback, ensuring natural, culturally contextual conversations.
Hybrid Text-to-Speech (TTS): Uses Sarvam's localized Hindi TTS voices (like "meera") to read output back to the user, providing a warm, native-sounding assistant.

**Open Innovation**

The Open Innovation track is looking for projects that break boundaries, solve real-world problems creatively, and exhibit high engineering depth. Jago fits this theme by merging Accessibility, Bilingual NLP, Edge AI, and Cloud Automation into a unified mobile agent:

Democratizing App Automation Without Public APIs: Historically, automating mobile applications has required developers to expose official APIs or shortcuts. Jago utilizes Android's Accessibility Service in a novel way to interact with any third-party app (like Spotify and WhatsApp) exactly like a human user would (by traversing layouts, executing fallback gesture taps, and recording customizable visual macros). This enables automation across the entire Android ecosystem, regardless of whether developer APIs exist.

Breaking the Language & Accessibility Barrier for Hinglish Users: Standard voice assistants are built with an English-first bias, leaving millions of bilingual users struggle to control their devices. Jago’s custom translation pipeline with message protection heuristics ensures that Hinglish commands are routed correctly while preserving Hindi dictation verbatim. This makes natural voice control accessible to non-native English speakers, elderly users, or individuals with motor and visual impairments.

Privacy-First Hybrid Edge Architecture: By running a multi-stage ONNX Runtime pipeline on-device for wake word detection, Jago ensures that the microphone stream is processed locally, keeping the user's data completely private. Only when a command is verified does the app call cloud endpoints (like Gemini or Sarvam) for parsing, creating a highly optimized, battery-efficient, and secure architecture.

Unlocking Desktop/Enterprise Cloud Capabilities on Mobile: By bypassing Android's lack of JNDI support using a custom DNS-over-HTTPS SRV/TXT resolver, Jago bridges MongoDB Atlas and Vector Search directly with Android. This shows how complex, vector-embedded cloud infrastructure can be bridged with lightweight mobile clients, opening up new possibilities for mobile AI application development.
