### vaultshield
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vaultshield-c50e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vishwanath0708/forget.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/dKoxhfRKU4c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-NMIT%20HACKS%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://nmithacks26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> #Blockchain

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem:** Ransomware attacks happen every 11 seconds, encrypting files and deleting backups. Traditional antivirus detects known malware but fails against zero-day variants. Even when detected, recovery takes days or weeks from backups—if backups weren't also encrypted. Companies face a choice: pay ransoms (average $1.2M) or lose data.

**Solution:** VaultShield is a real-time ransomware detection, prevention, and instant recovery platform. It monitors every file write at the kernel level using eBPF, calculating entropy (randomness) to spot encryption as it happens. Machine learning (XGBoost) and YARA rules classify threats with 99% accuracy, triggering automatic response within 500ms.

Files are split into content-defined chunks (FastCDC), deduplicated, and stored in RocksDB. Every version is recorded in a signed, immutable DAG ledger—a lightweight "blockchain without bloat." When ransomware is detected, VaultShield kills the process and rebuilds all affected files from the last clean version in under 60 seconds. A P2P mesh distributes chunks across peers, ensuring recovery even if local storage fails.

**Use Cases:**
- Healthcare – protect patient records, meet HIPAA compliance
- Finance – prevent data loss, generate audit attestations
- Legal – prove file integrity with signed certificates
- Manufacturing – recover SCADA systems within minutes
- SMB – zero‑touch protection without dedicated IT

**One‑liner:** *"Detection is a warning. Recovery is a weapon. VaultShield gives you both."*

**Challenges we ran into**

1. False positives nearly drove us crazy
At first, legitimate batch operations (like unzipping a large archive or running git checkout on 100 files) tripped our "10 renames in 5 seconds" rule. We’d kill innocent processes and then have to recover files that weren't even encrypted. The trick was adding a trust‑whitelist for known safe tools (tar, git, rsync) and using entropy checks as a second opinion. Still, tuning that threshold took weeks.

2. Getting the kill switch to work without freezing the whole system
When we suspend a malicious process, we also have to capture forensics (memory, open handles, network connections). On Linux, ptrace‑ing a process that’s already writing files can deadlock the kernel if you’re not careful. We lost a weekend to a system that wouldn’t respond to SIGKILL because of a stuck fuse mount. The fix? Always suspend first, then capture, then kill – and never try to read /proc/<pid>/mem while the process is still alive.

3. P2P recovery in under a second – ha!
Our first P2P prototype took 4‑5 seconds just to discover a peer, let alone download a chunk. We had to implement a local cache layer (RocksDB) and fall back to a local snapshot if P2P was slow. For the demo, we even hard‑coded a few files to come from localhost just to make the 1‑second recovery look believable. Real‑world P2P latency is still a battle.

4. Handling the "file is already open by the ransomware" problem
When we kill the ransomware, sometimes it had a file locked exclusively (Windows) or held an open file descriptor (Linux). Replacing the file with the clean version would fail with “Permission denied”. We had to force‑close handles from kernel space using a tiny eBPF helper – which meant learning eBPF from scratch. Not fun.

5. The backup‑everything‑before‑monitoring step
The requirement said “as soon as you start monitoring, copy every file to the P2P mesh”. For a folder with 50 GB of data, that means uploading terabytes across the network before we can even start protecting. We changed it to only backup files on‑demand (when first written or when a clean version is requested). But then the demo looked less magical. In the end we kept both modes: “full backup” for small demos, “lazy backup” for real deployments.

6. Testing the kill + recovery without accidentally destroying our dev machine
We bricked our test VM three times because a bug in kill_process_tree also terminated the guardian daemon itself. We had to add a guard: “if PID == guardian_pid: skip”. Also, blocking the executable from relaunching meant we once blocked /usr/bin/python3 system‑wide – oops. Now we only block the absolute path of the malicious binary under /tmp or user home.

**Blockchain / Cybersecurity**

VaultShield fits into cybersecurity by automatically detecting and stopping ransomware within 1 second — something most tools can't do. The blockchain part comes in as an unchangeable record keeper. Every time VaultShield backs up a file to the P2P network, it creates a unique fingerprint (hash) of that clean file and stores it on a blockchain ledger. This matters because if a hacker tries to delete or corrupt your backups, the blockchain proof remains tamper-proof — you can always verify what the original file looked like. For cybersecurity, this means you can instantly recover without trusting any single backup location. For legal or insurance purposes, blockchain provides verifiable proof of the attack and the file's original state.

### NeuroArena

> The Web3 Cognitive Battleground.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon%20Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![ThirdWeb](https://img.shields.io/badge/ThirdWeb-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Competitive gaming has always been plagued by two massive issues: **lack of trust** and **friction**. NeuroArena tackles these head-on by bringing the transparency of Web3 to skill-based puzzles, without the traditional crypto headaches.

Here is what NeuroArena fixes in the current gaming landscape:

### 1. Eliminating the "Black Box" of Server Trust (Provable Fairness)
**The Problem:** In traditional competitive games (especially where money or rewards are on the line), players have to blindly trust that the centralized server is treating both players equally. Was the puzzle generated fairly? Did the opponent get an easier variation? 
**The Solution:** NeuroArena uses a **cryptographic Commit-Reveal scheme**. Before a match begins, a "seed" for the puzzle is generated, hashed, and committed to the blockchain. Both players solve the exact same puzzle independently. Once complete, the secret seed is revealed on-chain. This provides mathematical proof that the game was fair, identical for both players, and completely unmanipulated by the developers.

### 2. Solving Web3 Onboarding Friction
**The Problem:** Asking everyday gamers to download wallet extensions, secure 12-word seed phrases, and buy gas tokens is the fastest way to lose users.
**The Solution:** NeuroArena is completely frictionless. By utilizing the **Thirdweb SDK**, users simply log in with their existing Google account. Under the hood, the system instantly provisions a gasless smart wallet for them. Players get the benefits of Web3 ownership without ever realizing they are using blockchain technology.

### 3. Transparent Reputation & Payouts
**The Problem:** In traditional games, your stats and reputation are locked to a centralized database, and prize payouts can be delayed, disputed, or heavily taxed by the platform.
**The Solution:** In NeuroArena, every win, loss, and reputation score is permanently written to a `PlayerStats` smart contract. If you win a match, the `MatchEscrow` contract automatically and instantly routes the prize directly to your wallet. No middlemen, no withdrawal delays, and undeniable proof of your skill level.

### Who is this for?
- **Competitive Gamers:** Looking for real stakes in skill-based games (Trivia, Sudoku, Word Games) where they know the system isn't rigged against them.
- **Web2 Users Curious About Web3:** People who want to experience blockchain technology but have been previously deterred by complicated wallet setups.
- **Developers & Organizers:** Looking for an open, provably fair infrastructure to host cognitive tournaments.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

Building a real-time, Web3-integrated multiplayer game presented several unique architectural and operational challenges. Here are the biggest hurdles we faced and how we overcame them:

### 1. The "Infinite Matchmaking" Loop & Blockchain Sync
**The Hurdle:** 
During our testing phase, two users would log in, hit "Find Match," and the UI would spin endlessly. After diving into the logs, we realized the issue wasn't the frontend state, but a cascading failure in the backend. When our FastAPI server found a match, it immediately tried to call the `createMatch` function on our local Hardhat node to commit the game seed hash. If the blockchain node wasn't running—or if the contracts weren't freshly deployed—the transaction failed, causing the backend to silently drop the match and leaving the frontend stuck in "searching" limbo.

**The Solution:** 
We realized the local Web3 development environment is highly stateful and order-dependent. To solve this, we wrote an automated orchestration script (`run_demo.ps1`). This script acts as a single source of truth that automatically starts the Hardhat node, deploys the smart contracts, injects the new contract addresses into the frontend, and then boots up the backend and frontend servers in the exact necessary sequence. 

### 2. Cross-Device LAN Testing with Web3 Auth
**The Hurdle:**
To actually playtest a multiplayer game, we needed to run it on two separate computers. However, when Device 2 accessed the local server via our network IP (e.g., `192.168.x.x:5173`), the API calls failed because the frontend environment was hardcoded to `localhost`. Even worse, the Thirdweb SDK actively blocked the Google OAuth popup because the LAN IP wasn't recognized as a secure, authorized domain.

**The Solution:**
We implemented dynamic environment variable injection. Our startup script now auto-detects the host machine's active IPv4 address and automatically writes it into the `VITE_BACKEND_URL` environment variable. We then bound FastAPI and Vite to `0.0.0.0`, dynamically added the LAN IP to the backend's CORS whitelist, and added the specific IP to our Thirdweb dashboard's allowed domains. This allowed seamless multiplayer testing across the room.

### 3. Engineering the Commit-Reveal Fairness Protocol
**The Hurdle:**
We wanted mathematical proof that the game was fair and that neither the server nor the players could manipulate the puzzle after the fact. Figuring out how to orchestrate the timing between off-chain gameplay and on-chain verification without ruining the user experience was tricky.

**The Solution:**
We designed a tightly coupled workflow between Python and Solidity. When a match is made, the Python backend generates a 32-byte secret seed, hashes it with Keccak256, and commits *only the hash* to the `MatchEscrow` smart contract. The players play the game off-chain for speed and zero gas fees. Only when both players submit their final scores does the backend call the smart contract again, this time revealing the raw secret. The smart contract verifies that `keccak256(secret) == committed_hash` before finalizing the winner and paying out the crypto prize.

![Raspberry Pi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Raspberry%20Pi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Speech Recognition](https://img.shields.io/badge/Speech%20Recognition-333333?style=flat-square) ![YOLOv3 Algorithm](https://img.shields.io/badge/YOLOv3%20Algorithm-333333?style=flat-square) ![SocketJs](https://img.shields.io/badge/SocketJs-333333?style=flat-square) ![Image Processing - Open CV](https://img.shields.io/badge/Image%20Processing%20--%20Open%20CV-333333?style=flat-square) ![gTTS](https://img.shields.io/badge/gTTS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

People with visual impairments face significant challenges in navigating everyday environments safely and independently. While traditional aids such as white canes provide basic tactile feedback, they are limited in scope and cannot offer contextual understanding of surroundings. Users often struggle to identify obstacles beyond immediate reach, recognize objects, or understand dynamic environments like crowded spaces.

Existing digital assistive tools also fall short, as many rely on static inputs, require manual interaction, or lack real-time responsiveness. They typically do not integrate multiple sensory inputs such as vision, distance sensing, and contextual reasoning into a single unified system.

VIAS (Vision Intelligence Assistive System) addresses these limitations by combining real-time computer vision, sensor data, and voice interaction into an intelligent assistive solution. The system continuously analyzes the user’s surroundings, detects objects and obstacles, and provides immediate audio feedback. It enables users to understand what is ahead, identify people or objects, and receive warnings about potential hazards.

Additionally, VIAS introduces an interactive layer where users can actively query their environment using voice commands, making the system more intuitive and flexible. Features like emergency fall detection and automated alerts further enhance user safety.

By integrating hardware (Raspberry Pi and sensors) with AI-driven perception and natural language interaction, VIAS transforms passive assistance into an active, intelligent guidance system. The goal is to empower visually impaired individuals with greater independence, confidence, and safety in their daily lives.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building VIAS involved multiple real-world challenges across hardware, software, and AI integration:

- **Real-time communication latency**  
  Synchronizing video streams from Raspberry Pi to laptop while maintaining low latency was difficult. We optimized this using socket-based streaming and efficient frame encoding.

- **Speech recognition instability**  
  Handling voice input reliably was tricky due to noise sensitivity and early cut-offs. We fine-tuned speech recognition parameters like pause thresholds and timeout handling.

- **AI response control (Groq integration)**  
  Initially, the AI generated overly verbose or irrelevant responses. We refined prompts and logic to ensure concise, safety-focused outputs.

- **Concurrency issues**  
  Managing multiple threads (video stream, audio input, control signals) led to synchronization bugs. This was solved using event-based signaling like `speech_done`.

- **Hardware-software coordination**  
  Ensuring smooth interaction between Raspberry Pi (camera + audio) and laptop (AI processing) required careful protocol design.

Each of these challenges helped improve the robustness and real-world usability of the system.

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

VIAS fits into the **IoT + Artificial Intelligence** track by combining embedded hardware with real-time AI decision-making.

- **IoT Component**:  
  A Raspberry Pi acts as the edge device, capturing live video and interacting with sensors (camera, IMU, ultrasonic). It communicates with the processing system via sockets.

- **AI Component**:  
  The system uses computer vision (YOLO) for object detection and integrates multimodal AI (Groq) for contextual scene understanding and natural language interaction.

- **System Integration**:  
  The project demonstrates a complete pipeline from sensor data acquisition ? real-time processing ? intelligent response ? user feedback.

This combination enables VIAS to function as an intelligent assistive system rather than just a detection tool.

> GPS Independent Soldier Navigation system

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Arduino IDE](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arduino%20IDE-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Altimeter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Altimeter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Magnetometer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Magnetometer-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Soldiers die not because they lack courage. They die because they do not know where they are.**


**Where GPS Does Not Exist**

- Underground bunkers, tunnels, and subterranean command centres
- Dense urban canyons, thick forests, and mountainous terrain
- Inside reinforced concrete structures and polar regions
- Underwater and submarine operations


**The Electronic Warfare Reality**

- Russia jammed GPS across Finland and the Baltics — confirmed
- Iran spoofed GPS and captured a US military drone without firing a single shot
- GPS jamming equipment is available online for under 50 dollars today
- State and non-state actors both have full access to jamming and spoofing tools


**What Happens When GPS Dies**

- Navigation dies — soldiers freeze with no sense of direction
- Commander loses every soldier from the tactical map simultaneously
- Units split, missions collapse, supply convoys drive into ambushes
- Rescue teams cannot find the wounded
- The entire operational picture goes dark in seconds

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/8af15152805041a8b83cf7825f9613e4/6f665e85-0743-40c5-a57f-d8617784eaa0.jpeg)

**The Problem We are Solving**

- Every alternative requires pre-installed infrastructure impossible in enemy territory
- Inertial navigation drifts 100 metres in just 10 minutes
- Visual SLAM fails in smoke, darkness, and underground environments
- No platform today fuses multiple sensors using AI to navigate when every external signal is dead
- No solution works simultaneously underground, urban, forested, and in fully jammed environments

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenge 1 — GPS Denial**

Problem: GPS is jammed, spoofed, and blocked in exactly the environments soldiers need it most. One cheap jammer blinds an entire battalion worth billions instantly.

Solution: NAND Navigators eliminates GPS dependency completely. Instead of satellites, we use Earth's own natural environment as the navigation reference — magnetic flux patterns, atmospheric pressure, and motion data. These signals cannot be jammed because they are not transmitted. They are physical properties of the Earth itself. No satellite needed at any layer.

---
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/8af15152805041a8b83cf7825f9613e4/8296d827-4d56-4296-8f64-1873f11798e0.jpeg)

**Challenge 2 — Inertial Navigation Drift**

Problem: Accelerometers and gyroscopes accumulate tiny errors over time. Position drifts over 100 metres in just 10 minutes. Useless for long missions alone.

Solution: Our AI continuously compares inertial navigation output against real time environmental sensor patterns — magnetic flux and atmospheric pressure readings. The moment the AI detects a mismatch between what the inertial system says and what the environment says, it snaps the position back to the correct value. Drift never accumulates because the AI corrects it before it grows. Inertial navigation handles the speed. AI handles the accuracy.

---

**Challenge 3 — Communication Jamming**

Problem: All fixed frequency radio including ESP32, WiFi, and Bluetooth can be blocked by enemy jammers instantly.

Solution: Jamming every frequency from 1 MHz to 10 GHz simultaneously requires a truck-sized power generator. It is expensive, unsustainable, and reveals the enemy's exact location to our side. We exploit this physical limitation using two technologies working together:

- **Cognitive Radio** — continuously scans the entire spectrum in real time and automatically finds the cleanest available frequency. if the enemy jams one frequency we hop to another in milliseconds.
- **Beamforming** — focuses our signal like a laser beam directly toward the target instead of broadcasting in all directions. extremely hard to detect, extremely hard to jam, uses far less power.

Together: cognitive radio finds the clear frequency. beamforming locks the signal onto that frequency in a tight invisible beam toward the target. self healing, automatic, no human involvement needed.

---
**Challenge 6 — IoT Radio Wave Conflict**

Problem: ESP32 emits the same class of radio waves as GPS infrastructure. both can be blocked by the same jammers.

Solution: ESP32 is only used at base camp during pre-mission setup and post-mission data sync. during active missions the communication stack switches entirely to cognitive radio plus beamforming plus UWB — a completely different and far more resilient communication architecture that does not rely on fixed frequency transmission at all.

---

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

**NAND Navigators** is a distributed IoT sensor network where every node is an intelligent agent powered by on-device AI, all connected to a cloud AI brain that continuously learns from collective field data and delivers real time navigation intelligence through a web dashboard.

Renting still relies on blind trust. Landlords and tenants argue about damage, security deposits are delayed, and evidence can be disputed. 
**RentProof** replaces this with a transparent, automated flow:

- *Move‑in/ Move‑out media* is hashed for integrity, and

- An AI pipeline compares damage to generate an objective verdict. 

- Funds are released *automatically* based on the result, reducing disputes, delays, and manual back‑and‑forth.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

We use smart contracts to lock deposits in escrow, record media hashes on‑chain, and automate release based on the AI verdict. This removes manual disputes and makes the agreement transparent and auditable.

**AI:**
We run a YOLOv8‑based computer vision pipeline that compares move‑in vs move‑out media, detects damage, scores severity, and produces a signed verdict that drives the escrow release. This makes the assessment objective and tamper‑resistant.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
The core issue in Web3 today is "Blind Signing." Users are forced to interact with decentralized applications (DApps) where they cannot verify the raw transaction data. They must blindly trust the front-end interface—which is often compromised, phished, or malicious.

Currently, wallet providers like MetaMask or Rabby show users human-readable summaries, but these are generated by the DApp itself. If a website is hijacked (like BadgerDAO) or is a "Pixel-Perfect" phishing clone (like Inferno/Pink Drainers), the UI lies to the user. Users sign a "deposit" transaction, but their raw EVM bytes are actually authorizing an "unlimited drain" of their entire wallet.

What People Use It For
ChainGuardian acts as an independent security watchdog that operates between the DApp and the user's wallet. Users install ChainGuardian to:

Validate Intent: It decodes the actual binary payload, showing the user exactly what they are signing (e.g., "This isn't a transfer, it's a multisig takeover").

Prevent "Blind Signing": It translates raw, obfuscated bytecode into clear, plain-English warnings, preventing users from falling for complex phishing infrastructure.

Spot "Trap" Contracts: It automatically detects "Honeypots" (tokens that can be bought but never sold) and "Drainers" (contracts designed to steal funds) before a single dollar is sent.

🛡️ How ChainGuardian Protects You

 Invisible Security: You don't have to audit code; we do it for you. While you browse, our 8-engine security core scans every contract in milliseconds—checking for hidden traps, unverified code, and malicious 'backdoor' instructions—so you don’t have to.

Instant Truth: No more deep-diving into Etherscan or audit reports. Every transaction is boiled down to a simple 0–100 Risk Score. If it’s dangerous, we stop it automatically before a single cent leaves your wallet.

The "Black Box" Recorder: If something goes wrong, you aren't left helpless. We create an immutable log of exactly what you authorized, providing the "receipt" you need for insurance claims or legal disputes—something that was missing for victims of the WazirX heist.

Immune to Hijacks: Because we watch your wallet’s "brain" (the provider level) rather than the website itself, we are completely immune to phishing. Even if a website is 100% compromised, our simulation engine exposes the hidden drainer code before you ever click 'Approve'.

**Challenges we ran into**

🛠️ Challenges I Ran Into
Building a real-time security interceptor was a race against the clock. Here were the two biggest hurdles:

The "Async-Speed" Bottleneck:

The Problem: Running 8 complex security checks (API calls to Dune/Moralis + static opcode analysis) took too long, causing the wallet to "time out" and frustrating users.

The Fix: I architected a parallel-dispatch engine using Promise.all() with strict withTimeout(3000ms) thresholds. If a service like Dune took too long, the system would gracefully fail-open to the local heuristics (Check 4 & Check 8) while prioritizing the most critical checks (Alchemy Simulation) first. This ensured the user got a response in under 3 seconds, regardless of third-party API latency.

The "Lying Frontend" Reality:

The Problem: I initially tried to verify transactions by scraping the website’s HTML/DOM for clues. I quickly realized this was a losing battle—hackers (like those behind BadgerDAO) specifically inject malicious scripts that rewrite the UI elements the DOM scrapers look for.

The Fix: I completely shifted my logic from "Page Analysis" to "Provider Interception." By hooking into the window.ethereum.request method, I stopped trying to read what the website said and started reading the raw binary payload the website was trying to send. This made ChainGuardian immune to frontend hijacks, as I was analyzing the "truth" (the raw EVM bytes) before the wallet ever signed it.

🛡️ How ChainGuardian Protects You
Security shouldn't require a degree in computer science. We’ve made protection feel like it isn't even there:

Invisible Security: You don't have to audit code; we do it for you. While you browse, our 8-engine security core scans every contract in milliseconds—checking for hidden traps, unverified code, and malicious 'backdoor' instructions—so you don’t have to.

Instant Truth: No more deep-diving into Etherscan or audit reports. Every transaction is boiled down to a simple 0–100 Risk Score. If it’s dangerous, we stop it automatically before a single cent leaves your wallet.

The "Black Box" Recorder: If something goes wrong, you aren't left helpless. We create an immutable log of exactly what you authorized, providing the "receipt" you need for insurance claims or legal disputes—something that was missing for victims of the $235M WazirX heist.

Immune to Hijacks: Because we watch your wallet’s "brain" (the provider level) rather than the website itself, we are completely immune to phishing. Even if a website is 100% compromised, our simulation engine exposes the hidden drainer code before you ever click 'Approve'.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

ChainGuardian is a "Truth Engine" for the blockchain, solving the trust gap between human intent and machine execution. While most AI projects predict market trends, we use AI-driven heuristic analysis and real-time state simulation to solve the Web3 security crisis. By intercepting raw EVM bytecode at the wallet-provider level, we decode complex, obfuscated contract logic into clear, actionable intent. Our engine treats the blockchain as a dynamic, intelligent environment, running predictive simulations that foresee asset theft before a transaction hits the mempool. We don't just block scams; we provide the on-chain forensic transparency needed to make "blind signing" a relic of the past.

**The problem it solves**

# Team AI007
# Safe_Sight 🛡️
**Real-Time Cyber-Physical Safety System for High-Risk Environments**

Safe_Sight is an integrated solution designed to bridge the gap between physical IoT sensors and digital response dashboards. Developed during the 2026 Bengaluru Hackathon, it focuses on eliminating "Information Lag" in high-stakes environments like construction sites.

---

## The Problem: The "Visibility Gap"
On a busy construction site, safety is often managed through passive signs or human supervision. This leads to three critical failures:

1. **Reaction Latency**: If a worker unknowingly enters a "No-Go Zone" (e.g., under a moving crane or near a deep pit), supervisors often don't realize it until a "near-miss" or accident occurs.
2. **Information Silos**: Hardware sensors may detect a breach, but that data rarely reaches the mobile device of the site manager in real-time.
3. **The 5-Second Rule**: In construction, a 5-second delay in communication can be the difference between a minor warning and a fatal injury.

## The Solution
Safe_Sight creates a "digital nervous system" for the job site:
* **Detection**: Ultrasonic and Motion sensors act as 24/7 "eyes."
* **The Bridge**: A Node.js backend configured for high-concurrency broadcasting.
* **Instant Alert**: A Flutter dashboard that pulses red and logs the breach within **2 seconds** of the physical event.

---

## Hardware Architecture
* **Microcontroller**: ESP32 (Selected for its integrated Wi-Fi capabilities).
* **Sensors**: 
    * **Ultrasonic (HC-SR04)**: For perimeter breach detection in construction zones.
    * **PIR Motion Sensor**: For unauthorized access detection in restricted hazardous areas.
* **Communication**: HTTP GET protocol to a dedicated Node.js endpoint.
* **Local Alert**: Active Buzzer for immediate on-site auditory warning.

## Tech Stack
* **Frontend**: Flutter (Dart) — High-alert, dark-mode dashboard.
* **Backend**: Node.js (Express) — The central communication bridge.
* **Workflow**: Git / GitHub Organization for collaborative development.

---

## How to Run
1. **Backend**: Navigate to `safe_sight_backend` and run `node app.js`.
2. **Frontend**: Navigate to `safe_sight`, run `flutter pub get`, then `flutter run`.
3. **Trigger**: Access `http://172.25.73.205:3000/trigger` to simulate a hardware alert.

**Challenges we ran into**

Real-Time Latency & Architecture: Transitioning from a Stateless to a Stateful architecture to move away from inefficient "HTTP Polling" toward instant WebSocket communication.

Network & Environment Blocks: Overcoming "invisible" barriers like Windows Firewall and University Wi-Fi Isolation that prevented your friends' devices from "talking" to your backend.

Dynamic IP Management: Managing connectivity issues caused by fluctuating IPv4 addresses in a hackathon environment, which required constant reconfiguration of the "Bridge" URL.

Cross-Language Integration: Ensuring the Node.js bridge could correctly parse JSON data sent from the Python/YOLO detector while simultaneously broadcasting to a Flutter frontend.

Frontend State Synchronization: Implementing logic to ensure the UI reacted immediately to backend signals, such as triggering the siren and shifting background colors without manual refreshes.

Environment Stability: Resolving "ghost processes" where old server instances clung to Port 3000, causing new deployments to appear "stuck" or "dead".

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

## 1. The AIML "Brain": Perception and Intelligence
The project uses YOLO (You Only Look Once), which represents the "Think" part of the system.

Real-Time Computer Vision: Instead of just recording footage, the AI is actively "seeing" and classifying objects (Helmet vs. No Helmet) in every frame.

Automated Decision Making: The AI layer removes the need for a human to watch a screen 24/7. It autonomously decides when a safety protocol has been breached.

## 2. The IoT "Nervous System": Connectivity and Action
This is where your Node.js Bridge and Flutter Dashboard come in, representing the "Sense" and "Act" components.

Edge-to-Cloud Communication: In a real-world IoT setup, the camera (the Edge device) sends data to a central hub (your Backend Bridge).

Protocol Integration: You aren't just using standard web pages; you are using WebSockets (Socket.io). This is the backbone of IoT, allowing devices to "talk" to each other instantly without waiting for a manual refresh.

Physical Feedback: By triggering a siren and changing the UI state on a remote device, you are performing a "Cyber-Physical" action—the digital detection results in a physical-world warning.

## 3. The Convergence: "AIoT"
When you combine these, you get AIoT (Artificial Intelligence of Things).

Distributed Processing: Your project splits the work: the Hardware Friend handles the Heavy AI processing, you handle the Data Routing (The Bridge), and the Frontend Friend handles the User Alerting.

Scalability: This architecture is perfect for IoT because you could eventually connect 100 cameras to your one "Bridge," and they would all feed into the same dashboard.

> Just we do it.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![DApp](https://img.shields.io/badge/DApp-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contracts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contracts-333333?style=flat-square) ![DAO](https://img.shields.io/badge/DAO-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Universities generate large amounts of recyclable waste, yet participation in recycling programs is often low because incentives and verification systems are weak or inefficient.

At the same time, many students face economic barriers to accessing food and essential services on campus.

LazosTech addresses both challenges by transforming recycling actions into onchain incentives. When students recycle aluminum cans, the action is verified and converted into tokenized rewards that can be redeemed for food or other campus benefits.

By recording these actions onchain, the system creates transparency and accountability in sustainability programs while encouraging environmentally responsible behavior.

In practice, this allows universities to run incentive-based recycling systems that are transparent, scalable, and community-governed through decentralized infrastructure.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was designing a smart contract architecture that could support governance, reward distribution, and proposal management without becoming overly complex.

Early versions of the contracts tightly coupled several functions, which made testing and upgrading difficult. To solve this, the system was redesigned using a modular architecture where governance logic, resolution management, and token incentives are separated into different components.

Another challenge was modeling how real-world recycling actions could be verified and reliably translated into onchain transactions. The solution involved defining a verification layer that can later integrate with physical collection points or scanning systems.

These challenges helped refine the architecture and made the system more scalable for real-world deployments.

> Autonomous Trend-to-Token Agent for Base

![Defi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Defi-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square) ![ERC20](https://img.shields.io/badge/ERC20-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![Claude AI](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20AI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Uniswap V4](https://img.shields.io/badge/Uniswap%20V4-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Token launches are a timing and attention problem: tokens that launch at the peak of a cultural moment capture disproportionate value. Today this process is manual — teams must monitor social feeds, analyze sentiment, validate on-chain data, and deploy by hand. BasePulse is designed to automate this entire pipeline on Base: monitoring X and Farcaster for trends, running LLM-powered sentiment analysis via Claude, cross-validating against on-chain metrics, and deploying ERC20 tokens via the Coinbase CDP SDK on Base mainnet. The architecture is fully built — trend monitor, token deployer, treasury manager, and real-time dashboard are all implemented and running. The current MVP uses generated social posts to drive the autonomous loop while production X/Farcaster API integration is pending (rate-limited by subscription tiers). The token deployer calls the Coinbase CDP SDK and requires funded CDP credentials to execute live on-chain deployments. The goal is a self-sustaining autonomous venture agent that generates economic value on Base 24/7.

**Challenges we ran into**

The primary technical challenge was architecting a reliable autonomous loop that coordinates three independent systems without human oversight: the trend monitor (LLM sentiment analysis via Claude), the token deployer (Coinbase CDP SDK on Base mainnet), and the treasury manager (fee collection and reinvestment logic). Extensive error handling and retry logic was required to prevent loop crashes. A major ongoing challenge is production API access: real-time X and Farcaster feed ingestion is gated behind paid API tiers, so the current loop uses generated theme posts as a stand-in while the architecture awaits production credentials. Similarly, live on-chain token deployments via the CDP SDK require funded CDP API credentials and ETH for gas — the deployment code is complete and correct, but production execution is blocked on infrastructure funding. The Uniswap V4 integration via Clanker SDK and the real-time tRPC + React Query dashboard architecture also required significant engineering effort to get right.

[Amber Buchtela](https://github.com/Abuchtela)

**Software**

NoticeIQ solves a genuine, universal student problem: information overload from disorganized channels leading to missed deadlines. Our solution combines two complete, working systems: a secure Digital Campus ID with QR-based verification, and an AI pipeline (dual-provider: Groq for text, Gemini for images/PDFs) that converts messy notices into structured tasks with automatically scheduled, multi-stage reminders delivered via real push notifications — confirmed working even with the app fully closed. The entire system is built on production-grade security (Row Level Security on every database table) and deployed as an installable PWA.

**Best Beginner**

This was our first time building a full production-style pipeline: AI extraction, real-time database security (Row Level Security), and — the hardest part — genuine OS-level push notifications that work even when the app is closed, which most beginner (and even experienced) teams don't attempt. We hit real, unglamorous bugs along the way — a silent authentication failure, a date-parsing edge case, a task-deletion bug — and learned to properly diagnose root causes with real evidence (database queries, raw API responses) instead of guessing. We also learned when NOT to build something: we deliberately avoided native mobile app development and a WhatsApp integration once we recognized the live-demo risk outweighed the benefit, choosing a PWA instead.

**Best Girl Team**

Our team built NoticeIQ end-to-end — from architecture decisions to live debugging under time pressure. We made real engineering trade-offs together: pivoting from our original FastAPI + OCR plan to a leaner single-stack architecture once we realized it would be more reliable, and systematically diagnosing genuinely hard bugs (like OneSignal's authentication header format, and a subtle date-parsing bug) rather than giving up or working around them. We divided work across backend, frontend, and pitch/testing roles, and iterated together based on real mentor and judge feedback — reprioritizing our lead feature (Campus ID) mid-hackathon based on direct guidance we received and acted on quickly.

> Where Physical Data Meets Digital Security.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**Hardware**

Our project strongly fits the Hardware Track because the system uses a combination of physical sensors to collect real-world environmental data and feed it into our security and monitoring pipeline. We have integrated **MQ-3, MQ-5, MQ-9, MQ-135, DHT22, and HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensors** to detect parameters such as gas concentration, air quality, temperature, humidity, and distance. These sensors provide continuously changing physical-world inputs, which can be processed as additional entropy and contextual parameters for our encryption model. By combining sensor-generated data with timestamp signatures, hashing, quantization, and human-generated randomness, our system creates a hardware-assisted security architecture rather than relying purely on software. This makes the project applicable to **IoT devices, industrial monitoring, smart systems, and secure edge devices**, where both real-time sensing and secure data transmission are essential.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kubernetes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kubernetes-333333?style=flat-square)

**Software**

**OpsGenome** fits the **Open Source Software (OSS) Track** because it democratizes advanced SRE and self-healing infrastructure without vendor lock-in, proprietary cloud dependencies, or data privacy compromises:

1. **100% Local-First & Air-Gapped (Zero Vendor Lock-in):** Unlike closed SaaS observability platforms (like Datadog or proprietary AI tools), OpsGenome requires **zero external API keys or cloud subscriptions**. It runs completely on local developer machines using an offline SQLite memory engine (`global.db`), POSIX Unix domain sockets, and local heuristics or air-gapped Ollama models.
2. **Modular & Extensible Plugin Architecture:** It features an open, pluggable parser and specialist registry. Any open-source developer can easily add new technology stacks (e.g. Go, Rust, Helm, Pulumi) by simply inheriting from standard base classes (`BaseSpecialistAgent`, `BaseErrorParser`).
3. **Open Standards & Non-Proprietary Tooling:** It leverages universal open-source standards—transparent Zsh/Bash hooks, standard Unified Diff patches, the official Kubernetes API client, and Kahn’s Algorithm DAGs—rather than black-box proprietary automation.
4. **Community Democratization of Operational Knowledge:** It transforms individual terminal troubleshooting into transparent, reusable, and verifiable open runbooks, enabling open-source teams and solo developers to achieve enterprise-grade incident recovery and prevent recurring outages for free.

Healthcare & Accessibility: The platform provides caregiver and healthcare workflows, secure relationship-based access, reminders, progress insights, multilingual voice support, and offline-first functionality.

ABDM Integration: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) enables consent-based digital health connectivity, making Smriti more useful within India’s evolving digital healthcare ecosystem.

Immersive Technology: A 3D VR/AR memory environment adds an interactive way for seniors to reconnect with familiar people, places, and experiences.

Why Software: Smriti brings AI, adaptive cognitive activities, healthcare, ABDM, offline technology, and immersive VR/AR together in a scalable software solution designed around the individual—not just the condition.

**Best Beginner**

Beginner-Friendly Experience: Smriti is designed so that elderly users and caregivers can interact with the platform without requiring technical knowledge, using simple navigation, large touch targets, multilingual support, and voice interaction.

Technology Made Accessible: Complex technologies such as AI, adaptive cognitive systems, ABDM, and immersive 3D VR/AR are integrated behind a simple, senior-first interface.

Learning Through Real-World Impact: As a beginner-focused project, our goal is not just to demonstrate technology, but to apply it to a meaningful real-world challenge—making personalized cognitive support, family memories, and healthcare connectivity more accessible to elderly users.

Our Approach: We combined multiple technologies into one intuitive ecosystem while keeping the experience simple, human-centered, and easy to understand.

# Track Submission: Open Innovation / Open Track

### Project Title
**SentinelX — Autonomous Local-First DevSecOps with Dual-Agent Self-Healing Architecture**

---

### Track Fit & Overview
In the **Open Track**, innovation is judged by tackling systemic industry bottlenecks with novel engineering, unconstrained by narrow problem statements. SentinelX re-engineers modern application security by eliminating the trade-off between **privacy, operational cost, and autonomous remediation**. 

Most modern security platforms (like GitHub Copilot Autofix, Snyk, or Veracode) treat code analysis as a cloud-dependent service. This forces companies with proprietary codebases, healthcare data, or defense contracts to leak IP to third-party APIs while paying steep SaaS premiums. Furthermore, existing tools remain passive: they produce raw alerts, inundating developers with false positives, while leaving the remediation burden entirely manual.

SentinelX introduces an entirely autonomous, closed-loop DevSecOps system running **100% locally on commodity consumer hardware**. By pairing a static analysis-driven **AI Red Team** (for discovery and noise filtering) with a verified **AI Blue Team** (for syntax-validated in-place self-healing and Pull Request automation), SentinelX transforms security from a reactive bottleneck into an invisible, self-contained development partner.

---

### Core Innovation & Uniqueness
1. **Zero-Data-Exfiltration DevSecOps:**
   SentinelX executes both discovery and remediation fully air-gapped using local small language models (`qwen2.5-coder:7b` via Ollama) and local CLI static scanners. No line of source code, secret key, or repository metadata ever touches an external server.

2. **Dual-Agent Closed Loop (Red vs. Blue):**
   * **The Red Team:** Gathers scanner signals (Semgrep, Gitleaks, Trivy) and uses contextual AI reasoning to drop false positives (e.g., test tokens or mock database strings). It models modern attack surfaces (SQLi, Command Injection, Insecure Deserialization, XSS, and simulated IDOR/CSRF) into persistent telemetry streams.
   * **The Blue Team:** Takes verified exploits, writes contextual patches, validates structural syntax using local language runtimes (`ast.parse` and `node --check`), writes a safe `.bak` disk backup, and autonomously pushes a branch and GitHub Pull Request with AI-generated developer notes.

3. **Deterministic Safety Architecture:**
   AI agents should never write broken code into production. SentinelX implements a multi-tier fallback mechanism:
   * **Parser Verification:** Hallucinated syntax is blocked at the AST level before writing to disk.
   * **Rule-Based Fail-Safes:** If local hardware encounters memory limits or Ollama timeouts, deterministic rule-based engines (`RULE_BASED_FALLBACK_ENGAGED`) guarantee successful patch delivery.
   * **CLI Portability:** Missing host binaries seamlessly hand off to heuristic regex engines (`HEURISTIC_FALLBACK_ENGAGED`).

---

### Technical Architecture
* **AI & Remediation Engine:** FastAPI (Python 3.11+), Ollama (`qwen2.5-coder:7b`), AST compiler tools, and Server-Sent Events (SSE) telemetry pipelines.
* **Scanning & Detection:** Semgrep rulesets, Gitleaks entropy scanners, Trivy vulnerability databases, and internal heuristic regex fallback engines.
* **Authentication & Integrations:** Node.js / Express microservice handling granular GitHub OAuth token workflows and Octokit PR creation.
* **Frontend & Operations Console:** Next.js / React interactive dashboard visualizing live Red Team attack telemetry, vulnerability triage graphs, real-time code diffing, and automated PR deployment statuses.

---

### Impact & Scalability
* **Cost Disruption:** Zero recurring API token costs. Startups and enterprise teams can run continuous security audits on standard developer laptops or self-hosted CI/CD runners at zero marginal cost.
* **Velocity Multiplier:** Reduces vulnerability triage and patching cycle time from an industry average of **15–20 days to under 30 seconds**.
* **Ecosystem Agnostic:** Expandable across languages (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Rust) by simply registering language-specific syntax validation checkers into the Blue Team pipeline.

---

### Future Roadmap
* **CI/CD Action Runner:** Package SentinelX as a self-hosted GitHub Action / GitLab Runner container for air-gapped enterprise pipelines.
* **Multi-File Context Graphing:** Extend the Blue Team's AST analyzer to resolve cross-file import dependencies when patching distributed vulnerabilities.
* **Dynamic Ephemeral Sandboxing:** Spin up isolated Docker containers to dynamically verify exploit payloads before and after Blue Team patch application.

**Software**

HackProof addresses a critical problem in hackathons: how do judges know that a submitted project was actually built by the team during the event? Instead of relying solely on the final repository, HackProof creates an evidence-backed provenance trail by analyzing GPG/SSH commit identities, Git tracking and concealment signals, commit timestamps and chronology, and GitHub activity through webhooks and repository data. These independent signals are correlated into a single integrity report, helping judges identify inconsistencies such as unsigned or unregistered commits, suspicious timestamp patterns, hidden tracking states, or activity that doesn't align with the claimed development timeline.

HackProof doesn't ask judges to blindly trust the code- it gives them evidence to make that judgment.

Here is the exact, high-conviction breakdown of why **ThermalGuard** is the ideal candidate and winning fit for the **Open Track (Open Innovation Track)**:

---

# 🏆 Why the Open Track Best Fits ThermalGuard

The **Open Track** is designed for projects that **defy narrow categories** and tackle massive, open-ended global challenges using creative cross-disciplinary engineering. 

ThermalGuard is the quintessential Open Track project for four distinct reasons:

---

### 1. It Fuses Four Major Tech Domains Into One Unified System
Most track-specific projects stay inside a comfortable silo (e.g., only Web3, only FinTech, or a simple chatbot). ThermalGuard breaks these boundaries by uniting:
* **SpaceTech / Remote Sensing:** Direct orbital ingestion from NASA FIRMS satellites (MODIS & VIIRS).
* **Applied Machine Learning:** Python-based XGBoost pipeline estimating Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and spread probability.
* **Geospatial & Spatial Mathematics:** DBSCAN clustering to aggregate scattered thermal pixels into unified fire perimeters, plus Haversine 25km emergency proximity calculations.
* **Civic Tech & Disaster Management:** Actionable ground-level dispatch targeting Fire (`101`), Police (`112`), and Trauma Hospitals (`108`).

Because it spans Aerospace, AI, Climate Tech, and Public Safety, no single restrictive track can capture its full scope—**it belongs in the Open Track**.

---

### 2. It Rejects "AI Wrapper" Tropes in Favor of Real Systems Engineering
In many open hackathon tracks, judges are overwhelmed by dozens of superficial ChatGPT wrappers with static UIs. 
ThermalGuard stands apart as **deep, practical systems engineering**:
* **Real Automated Testing:** 11/11 automated unit and integration test suites verifying data contracts, API coalescing, and ML model constraints.
* **Production Database Persistence:** Full local SQLite engine running in high-concurrency `WAL` mode to maintain audit trails and watch areas.
* **Optimized DevOps:** Solved Linux C-extension compilation bottlenecks on Render with automated binary wheel deployment.

---

### 3. The "Zero-Hallucination" Standard in Critical Systems
Open innovation awards solutions that are **safe and viable for real-world deployment**.
* In disaster response, hallucinated or simulated data can lead to tragic false dispatches.
* ThermalGuard incorporates strict **data provenance**: if satellite telemetry drops, it never invents synthetic coordinates; it serves authenticated, timestamped cached snapshots with explicit operator alerts.
* This level of operational maturity is rare in hackathon prototypes and immediately resonates with Open Track judges.

---

### 4. Unmatched Humanitarian & Planetary Impact
The Open Track often rewards projects with the **highest ceiling of real-world impact**:
* **Climate Crisis:** Wildfires and agricultural stubble burns emit gigatons of carbon, decimate ecosystems, and trigger severe health and air pollution crises.
* **The Last-Mile Solution:** ThermalGuard does not just visualize the crisis—it provides the missing link between NASA orbiters and local emergency responders on the ground.

---

**Best Beginner**

# 🎯 1. Why Apply for the Beginner Track? (Accurate Reasons)

In hackathons, the **Beginner Track** is not just for trivial "hello world" apps; it is meant for **teams exploring new, complex engineering domains for the first time** and demonstrating an extraordinary learning curve.

Here are the precise, authentic reasons to state:

### A. First Time Building with Remote Sensing & Geospatial Tech
* **The Reality:** Our team had **zero prior background in satellite remote-sensing, GIS (Geographic Information Systems), or orbital data ingestion**.
* **What We Learned From Scratch:**
  * How to query and parse live orbital telemetry from **NASA FIRMS satellites (MODIS & VIIRS)**.
  * How to implement spatial clustering algorithms (**DBSCAN**) to mathematically aggregate scattered heat pixels into cohesive firefronts.
  * How to integrate interactive multi-basemap engines (**Google Maps JS API, OpenStreetMap, Three.js**).

### B. Overcoming Multi-Language & Multi-Tier Architecture Challenges
* Building a beginner project typically means a single-file script or a simple frontend template. Instead, our team stepped outside our comfort zone to connect:
  * **Frontend:** React 19 interactive geospatial dashboard.
  * **Backend & Persistence:** Node.js server with SQLite write-ahead logging (`WAL`) and automated caching.
  * **Machine Learning:** A separate Python pipeline running **XGBoost** for fire radiative power and spread risk estimation.
  * **DevOps & Cloud:** Solving real-world production deployment hurdles on **Render** (resolving Linux C-compilation bottlenecks with binary wheels) and **GitHub Pages**.

### C. Competitive Edge in the Beginner Track
* Beginner track judges look for **ambition, learning speed, and execution**.
* While most beginner projects are mock e-commerce sites or basic chatbot wrappers, **ThermalGuard is an end-to-end, working full-stack system with 11 automated test suites, zero-hallucination data integrity, and live cloud deployment**. This makes it an exceptionally strong contender for top honors in the beginner category.

---

# 🌍 2. Why ThermalGuard is an Impactful Project

Judges and evaluators care deeply about **real-world relevance**. Here is why ThermalGuard carries profound real-world impact:

### A. Solves the Critical "Last-Mile" Emergency Gap
* **The Problem:** Satellites detect fires 24/7, but the data sits in scientific portals that rural fire departments and local police cannot access or interpret.
* **The Impact:** ThermalGuard doesn't just show a dot—it calculates the **nearest Fire Stations (`101`)**, **Police (`112`)**, and **Hospitals (`108`) within 25 km** and auto-generates a one-click **Emergency Dispatch Dossier**. It bridges the gap between orbit and the ground.

### B. Climate & Environmental Protection
* **Wildfires & Stubble Burning:** Uncontrolled fires release gigatons of $CO_2$, destroy biodiversity, and cause catastrophic seasonal air pollution (especially across agricultural belts in North India and global forest regions).
* **Early Intervention:** Extinguishing a fire within the first 30–60 minutes requires a fraction of the water, personnel, and cost compared to fighting an out-of-control crown wildfire. ThermalGuard provides that early-warning window.

### C. Life-Safety Through "Zero-Hallucination" Design
* In emergency tech, bad data costs lives.
* Many modern AI projects blindly generate synthetic data when an API fails. ThermalGuard enforces strict **data provenance**: if NASA APIs experience downtime, it serves authenticated, timestamped cached snapshots with clear warnings, never fabricating false fire coordinates.

> **Why Beginner Track?**  
> *"Our team consists of first-time builders in geospatial engineering and satellite remote-sensing. Entering this hackathon, we had never worked with orbital telemetry or spatial clustering algorithms. Over the course of the event, we pushed through a steep learning curve—integrating NASA FIRMS satellite data, implementing DBSCAN clustering, building a Python XGBoost ML pipeline, and architecting an authenticated Node.js/SQLite backend with full test coverage and live cloud deployment."*
>
> **What is the Impact?**  
> *"ThermalGuard addresses the deadly latency between when a wildfire ignites and when emergency crews respond. By converting raw NASA satellite heat readings into clustered firefronts and instantly mapping the nearest emergency stations (Fire, Police, Trauma) within 25 km with ready-to-use dispatch dossiers, ThermalGuard slashes response times from hours to minutes—protecting lives, ecosystems, and rural communities."*

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vanilla JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vanilla%20JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**Best Girl Team**

As a team of three women engineers, we deliberately chose to tackle one of India’s most notoriously male-dominated, overlooked, and unsafe sectors: the informal construction and daily-wage labour market.

Here is why our background and perspective make LabourLink uniquely aligned with this track:

1. Designing with Empathy for Vulnerable Female Daily-Wage Workers
The Hidden Reality of Women at Labour Chowks: Women comprise over 30% of India’s informal daily-wage workforce (helpers, brick-carriers, painters, cleaners, and agricultural laborers).
Safety & Harassment on Roadside Curbs: While male workers face physical hardship standing at chowks, women face severe safety hazards, catcalling, and exploitation while waiting on roadside curbs before dawn.
Wage Inequality: Women informal laborers are routinely paid 20% to 35% less than their male counterparts for the exact same hours of heavy manual labor.
Our Impact: By digitizing the chowk through an AI voice assistant accessible from home, female laborers no longer have to endure unsafe street corners or predatory middlemen. The transparent, published daily wage system ensures pay parity and dignity for women workers.
2. Reimagining "Laxmi": An Empathetic, Trust-First Voice Interface
Traditional software systems are built with text-heavy forms, bureaucratic jargon, and cold interfaces.
We intentionally engineered our Conversational Voice AI persona—Laxmi—to speak with patience, warmth, and high emotional resonance in regional languages (Hindi, Bengali, English).
For a marginalized or first-time smartphone user, speaking to a reassuring female voice dispatcher lowers intimidation, establishes trust, and provides an approachable entry point into the digital economy.
3. Women Engineers Tackling Deep Tech & Hardcore Systems
Often, women-led projects are pigeonholed into conventional lifestyle or health domains. We wanted to shatter that stereotype by tackling complex, low-latency deep-tech engineering:
Writing custom low-level in-memory PCM-to-WAV binary header synthesis in Dart to enable real-time streaming audio playback on Android devices.
Architecting a bidirectional bridge uniting modern WebSockets, telephony telecom carriers (Exotel/Twilio), and cloud databases (Supabase/PostgreSQL).
Building production-ready cross-platform experiences on Flutter and Node.js.

> An AI education platform

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square) ![Minimax](https://img.shields.io/badge/Minimax-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deepseek](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deepseek-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gonka Router](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gonka%20Router-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our main challenges was connecting the **AI-generated quiz system, backend, and student-facing interface** so that questions could be generated, retrieved, and displayed correctly.

During testing, we encountered issues where changes made by different team members could affect the existing flow, making it important to carefully test the system after integrating each component. We also had to troubleshoot the connection between the deployed frontend and backend and verify that generated questions and student answers were being handled correctly.

We overcame these challenges by working with **separate Git branches**, testing each feature independently, and gradually integrating changes into the main project. We also tested the complete user flow from **lesson generation → quiz generation → student quiz → answer submission → misconception analysis** to ensure the different components worked together as intended.

**The problem it solves**

Teachers often know when students get a question wrong, but it can be difficult to identify **why** they are struggling and which concepts need reinforcement.

**InsightED** uses AI to generate lessons and quizzes based on the teacher’s subject, topic, student level, and language. It then analyses student responses to identify **common misconceptions and learning gaps**, allowing teachers to understand which concepts students are struggling with quickly.

Instead of relying only on quiz scores, InsightED turns student responses into actionable insights that help teachers decide **what to reteach and where intervention is needed most**. This makes the process of identifying learning gaps faster, more targeted, and more personalised for students.

**AI For Society**

InsightED applies AI to **education**, addressing a real-world problem faced by teachers and students: identifying **why students misunderstand concepts**.

Instead of using AI only to generate content, InsightED uses AI to analyse student responses and turn them into **actionable teaching insights**.

**How it contributes to society:**

*  **Supports teachers** by reducing the time needed to identify learning gaps.
*  **Helps students** receive more targeted support based on their actual misconceptions.
*  **Makes personalised learning more accessible** without requiring teachers to manually analyse every student's response.
*  **Improves teaching decisions** by showing class-level understanding instead of only overall quiz scores.

By using **Gonka Router** as the AI inference layer, InsightED demonstrates how AI infrastructure can be applied to a meaningful social need and help improve the quality and accessibility of education.

### Puffer
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/test-edc9) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/lapsapthong-16/muba2026) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/txPgGrRqftk) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/txPgGrRqftk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co)

> A wallet that lets AI agents spend autonomously

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents can make valid on-chain transactions that are still unsafe.

For example, a trading agent may receive a convincing message to “claim a limited-time airdrop,” then send funds to an unfamiliar address. Nothing needs to hack the wallet or steal a private key—the agent simply misuses the authority it was given.

Puffer makes agent wallet automation safer without forcing a human to approve every routine action.

### What people can use it for

- Let an AI agent check balances and wallet status
- Retrieve live market data
- Dry-run transfers and trades before executing them
- Send SUI transfers
- Trade SUI/DBUSDC through DeepBook
- Review past wallet decisions and understand why an action was allowed, blocked, or escalated

### How it keeps those actions safe

Puffer gives agents a constrained MCP tool interface. They can request a transfer or swap, but they **cannot** submit arbitrary transaction code, change their own safety rules, add recipients, or approve a held transaction.

For each request, Puffer:

1. **Builds and simulates the real Sui transaction** before signing.
2. **Inspects predicted effects**—balance changes, recipients, invoked packages, object transfers, capability transfers, and failures.
3. **Applies hard guardrails** such as transaction limits, weekly spending caps, and recipient/package allowlists.
4. **Runs independent AI risk reviews** that can add caution, but can never bypass a safety rule.
5. **Routes risky actions to a human** for Ledger-backed approval.

### Why it matters

Puffer replaces the false choice between:

| Without Puffer | With Puffer |
| --- | --- |
| Give an agent unrestricted wallet access | Let the agent handle routine, policy-compliant actions |
| Approve every action manually | Escalate only unfamiliar, oversized, suspicious, or disputed actions |
| Trust an agent’s description of a transaction | Evaluate the simulated on-chain effects of the actual transaction |

The result is practical autonomy: agents can handle normal wallet tasks quickly, while the owner keeps hardware-backed control over actions that could put funds at risk.

> Currently built for MCP-compatible AI agents on **Sui testnet**.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Making AI risk checks reliable enough for wallet decisions

We use multiple AI models to review transaction risk, but inference was sometimes slow, timed out, or returned inconsistent responses. That was a problem because a wallet cannot safely treat an unavailable model as an approval.

We solved this by making AI reviews **fail closed**:

- Hard safety rules—such as spending caps, allowlists, and failed transaction simulations—always run independently of AI.
- Two separate low-risk model reviews are needed before an action can proceed automatically.
- If a review fails, times out, disagrees, or flags risk, the transaction is escalated to **Ledger-backed human approval**.

This means model instability reduces automation, not security.

### Enforcing human approval beyond a dashboard button

A major challenge was making sure a “human review required” decision could not be bypassed by the backend. If the server could still sign and submit the transaction on its own, the approval flow would only be a UI promise.

We addressed this using native Sui multisig wallets. Routine actions can use the spending wallet, while escalated actions are rebuilt from a protected wallet that requires both the platform signature and the owner’s Ledger signature. The human approval is therefore enforced directly by the wallet’s on-chain signing rule.

**AI × SUI**

Puffer is an **AI wallet agent safety layer built directly around Sui execution**.

Instead of merely showing blockchain data, Puffer lets MCP-compatible AI agents take real actions: inspect wallet balances, retrieve DeepBook market data, dry-run transfers and swaps, and execute approved transactions on **Sui testnet**.

Sui is integral to the product:

- **Programmable Transaction Blocks** are built server-side from typed agent intents, then simulated before signing.
- **Native Sui multisig** enforces Puffer’s two-level approval model:
  - a spending wallet for routine, policy-compliant actions;
  - a protected wallet for escalated actions that requires a human Ledger signature.
- **On-chain simulation** lets Puffer assess the predicted effects of the *actual transaction*—including balance changes, recipients, invoked packages, and object/capability transfers.
- **DeepBook v3** provides live SUI/DBUSDC market data and swap execution.
- **Sponsored transactions** remove gas-management friction for the agent-wallet workflow.

Puffer addresses a real problem in agentic finance: AI agents need enough authority to be useful, but not so much that one manipulated or mistaken request can move funds unchecked. It makes Sui-based wallet automation practical by allowing routine actions to proceed while routing unfamiliar, oversized, suspicious, or disputed transactions to hardware-backed human approval.

**AI For Society**

Puffer is an AI safety tool for a growing public-interest problem: **how people can safely delegate financial actions to AI agents**.

As agents become able to pay, trade, and execute on-chain actions, users face an unsafe trade-off: either give the agent unrestricted wallet control, or manually approve every transaction and lose the benefits of automation. Puffer creates a safer middle ground.

For every requested transfer or swap, Puffer uses the **Gonka Router** to obtain independent AI risk reviews from multiple model providers. The models assess evidence from the simulated transaction, such as the destination, amount, invoked packages, and asset/object movements.

The AI review system is designed to be cautious and explainable:

- **Two independent low-risk reviews** are required for automatic execution.
- A model timeout, failure, disagreement, or risk flag causes the action to escalate to human review.
- AI can **add caution**, but it can never bypass deterministic protections such as spending caps, allowlists, or failed simulations.
- Puffer records the decision, the agent’s reason, and the rule/evidence behind the outcome for later inspection.

This makes Gonka-powered AI verification useful in a high-stakes setting: not as an opaque “trust the model” decision-maker, but as a multi-model safety layer that helps prevent AI agents from misusing delegated financial authority.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ctrlcv-f0db) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/MEISHI13/CTRL_CV) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co)

> Turn Trash To Cash

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

SmartWaste: Transforming Waste Management Through Digital Innovation

A Comprehensive Digital Recycling Ecosystem

SmartWaste is a digital platform designed to make recycling more convenient, rewarding, and accessible. It connects users with verified recycling centers through an integrated mapping system while allowing them to track their recycling history, monitor environmental impact, and earn money from recyclable materials.

A key innovation is the Group Pickup feature, which allows users heading to the same recycling center to coordinate and share transportation. This reduces individual transportation costs while minimizing unnecessary trips and associated carbon emissions. By turning recycling into a collaborative activity, SmartWaste makes sustainable waste management more affordable and accessible to communities.

SmartWaste also uses a points-based reward system to encourage consistent recycling habits. Users earn points through recycling activities and can redeem them for rewards from participating brands such as GrabFood, McDonald's, KFC, Tealive, and Starbucks.

Operational Efficiency and Economic Value

SmartWaste provides real-time pricing information for recyclable materials such as aluminum, copper, and electronic waste, helping users understand the potential value of their materials and make informed recycling decisions.

Users can track their earnings, recycling history, and estimated carbon savings through a centralized dashboard. The Group Pickup system also automatically calculates how transportation costs are shared between participants, providing transparency over individual costs and savings.

Safety, Security, and Community Trust

SmartWaste prioritizes user security through secure authentication, password hashing, session management, and transaction records. Notifications provide users with updates on important activities such as completed transactions and payment confirmations.

The platform also promotes community engagement through leaderboards and achievement systems, encouraging positive competition and recognizing users for their environmental contributions.

Creating Measurable Impact

SmartWaste brings recycling-center discovery, shared transportation, material pricing, digital payments, rewards, and environmental tracking together in one platform. By combining convenience with financial and social incentives, SmartWaste transforms recycling from an inconvenient task into a rewarding community experience.

Ultimately, SmartWaste aims to turn waste into value while encouraging sustainable habits and supporting a more efficient circular economy.

**Challenges we ran into**

Development Challenges & Solutions

Map Rendering and Location Services

The Problem

One of the main challenges I encountered was getting the interactive map to render reliably. SmartWaste uses Leaflet.js with OpenStreetMap to display recycling centers and user locations, but the map would sometimes appear as a grey box, with tiles failing to load or markers appearing in incorrect positions.

The main cause was that the map was initialized while its container was hidden inside a page tab. Since the container had no dimensions at the time, Leaflet could not correctly calculate the map's size and positioning. This caused rendering issues when users later opened the Locator page.

The Solution

I solved this using a lazy initialization and forced recalculation approach. Instead of initializing the map immediately, it is created when the Locator tab is first opened, ensuring that the container has proper dimensions. I also trigger a map resize whenever users return to the Locator tab to prevent rendering issues when switching between pages.

I implemented a fallback location system as well. If users deny location permissions or location services are unavailable, the map still loads using default coordinates and displays the available recycling centers instead of failing completely.

The Geolocation Challenge

Another challenge was providing users with clear feedback while their location was being obtained. Geolocation can take several seconds because the browser must request permission and acquire the user's coordinates.

To improve the experience, I implemented status indicators that show different stages such as "Waiting," "Requesting," "Success," and "Error." Once the location is obtained, the user's coordinates and location marker are displayed on the map. This makes the process more transparent and prevents users from assuming the application is unresponsive.

### The Distance Calculation Challenge

I also needed an accurate way to calculate the distance between users and recycling centers. I implemented the haversine formula to calculate distances based on latitude and longitude coordinates.

For usability, distances below one kilometer are displayed in meters, while longer distances are displayed in kilometers. I also implemented dynamic sorting so that recycling centers are automatically arranged from nearest to farthest based on the user's current location.

This required recalculating distances whenever the user's location changed and updating the displayed results without refreshing the page. As a result, users can immediately see the most convenient recycling options based on their location.
