### Certino
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/certino-9325) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/buhlez31/certino-app/) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://treetino.eu) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/RxetuIBGUtw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHPrague%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethprague2026.devfolio.co)

> Connecting small grid producers to extra revenue

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today's renewable energy certificate market is broken in three ways.

Annual averages hide the truth. Legacy Guarantees of Origin match generation to consumption *yearly* — but the grid runs hour by hour. Solar peaks at noon, demand peaks at 8 PM, and annual-matched certificates pretend those kWh are equal.

Small producers are locked out. The €3B European GO market was built for utilities. Households with batteries, small wind, and grid-balancing power generations like Treetino's hardware earn nothing extra for time-shifting kWh into peak demand. 30–50% of revenue evaporates in middleman fees.

Provenance is "trust us." Most certificates retire in private registries with no public proof. EU RED III will mandates hourly matching in 2030. CSRD demands location-bound evidence. The market has no rails for either.

Certino fixes all three. Every clean kWh mints as an on-chain ERC-721 with hour, location, fuel type, and device ID. Buyers deposit EURC into transparent pools that settle monthly against the EPEX SPOT auction. Producers earn a premium when OTE-CR clearing exceeds threshold — when the grid actually needs the energy. Buyer identity is a soulbound NFT, audit-grade and non-transferable.

What it enables:
- Households with Victron inverters earn premium credits for time-shifting into peak demand
- Corporates get CSRD/Scope 2 evidence with cryptographic provenance
- ESG auditors verify claims without registry intermediation
- Small grid-enhancers get their fair share of a market that used to ignore them

Real kWh. Real money. Real provenance. Every hour, on-chain.

**Challenges we ran into**

Transforming our initial conceptual architecture into a seamless, end-to-end functional demo presented severe integration hurdles. The primary bottleneck was environment synchronization—specifically, coordinating complex decentralized oracle networks (Chainlink) and managing heavy data payloads across the team's distributed local development setups. 
• Real Victron telemetry is unsigned JSON over REST. For dual-issuance verification we needed cryptographic attestation — couldn't ship hardware in 48h. Built an oracle that pulls VRM data, signs each pulse with EIP-712, and posts on-chain. We are implementing Chainlink Oracle to proof that the data we are getting are correct. We also explore implement ai agents to verify the weather using the GPS data we have, if the kWh were possible to produce, if no one is not faking it. 

Three NFT types, one mental model. The system needs three distinct tokens: a soulbound *device* NFT (producer side), a soulbound *account* NFT (buyer side, audit identity), and a transferable *certificate* ERC-721 (the actual unit of trade). Keeping the user flows clean while three different mints happen across two roles took several iterations — especially making "soulbound" visually distinct from "transferable" in the UI without dropping into smart-contract jargon.

Pool settlement timing. Marketplace pools settle monthly against EPEX SPOT — but EPEX publishes day-ahead, not month-ahead. Modelled as deferred clearing: deposits enter a pending state, certificates issue post-settlement. Took two design passes to separate "deposit confirmed" (immediate receipt) from "certificate minted" (post-settlement) cleanly in the UX. Indicative €/MWh shown in the marketplace had to be visibly distinct from final settlement price.

EURC. Circle's official EURC is mainnet only — not Base Sepolia. Deployed a mock EURC with faucet, kept buyer flows identical to production integration so the demo is honest about what's mocked.

MetaMask on Amoy. RPC instability caused intermittent signing failures. Added retry with exponential backoff and a clearer "tx pending" state. For the recorded demo, pinned to a known-good endpoint.

**Network Economy**

Certino is a DePIN, settlement protocol for the European energy grid. We tokenize real-world physical infrastructure — Victron-attested inverters, household batteries, small wind, grid-balancing reactors — and turn their hourly output into on-chain economic activity.

The network is the economy. Each device is a soulbound NFT. Each verified hour of clean MWh is an ERC-721. Each buyer claim is a soulbound audit identity. Each pool settles in EURC against a real spot-price auction every month. Producers earn yield; buyers earn provable green claims; the protocol takes a thin fee. No utility, no broker, no registry intermediary in the middle.

Bottom-up coordination. The €3B European GO market today is a top-down utility game — built for big plants, paid in annual averages. Certino flips that. A household with a battery can earn a premium for time-shifting kWh into peak demand, in the same market, on the same rails as a wind farm.

A network where physical work pays continuously. A typical 10 kW household solar installation earns roughly €80 per year in premium credits just by participating — recurring micropayments tied directly to real grid-balancing work. Scale that across the Czech bidding zone, then across EU RED III's hourly-matching mandate, and you have a self-bootstrapping network of physical assets coordinating economically without a centralized operator.

That's the Network Economy thesis: real-world infrastructure, real-world money, on-chain coordination. Certino is the energy slice of it.

**Future Society**

ETH Prague 2026's theme is Solarpunk Future. Certino is what that future looks like at the level of one kWh.

A grid owned by the people on it. Today's energy market is a utility-shaped pyramid: large plants generate, brokers package, corporates buy paper. Households and small producers — the people doing the actual work of decarbonizing — sit at the bottom, paid in averages. We invert it. Anyone with a Victron inverter, a small wind turbine, or a grid-balancing reactor like Treetino's HILIER becomes a first-class participant in the same market that used to ignore them.

Truth as infrastructure. A solarpunk society doesn't run on "trust us" claims. It runs on verifiable, public, granular evidence. Every Certino certificate carries the hour, the device, the location, the fuel type — soulbound to the producer, retired publicly by the buyer, immutable on Base. EU RED III and CSRD are pulling regulation toward exactly this. We're building the rails ahead of the law.

Regenerative economics, not extractive. Producers earn a premium when the grid actually needs the energy — when their kWh prevents gas from being burned. The protocol takes a thin fee. No middleman captures 30–50% of the value flow. The yield goes back to the people whose physical assets are doing the regenerative work.

The hackathon submission is one slice of a longer arc. Treetino's broader mission is grid-balancing infrastructure for a 100% renewable Europe — HILIER reactors, Treetino products, small battery units that store off-peak excess and release at peak demand. Certino is the protocol layer that makes those assets, and millions of household assets like them, economically coherent. Tokenize the physical work, settle in stablecoin, retire claims on-chain, repeat every hour.

That's a Future Society we want to live in. We're shipping the first piece of it this weekend.

Team **Treetino** -- Martin Kura, [Jakub Lustyk](github.com/louskac/)

### RendoFren
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/rendofren-7d01) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/prox004/RendoFren) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://try-rendofren.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/8COH0Wc74DA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hackolution%202K26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackolution2k26.devfolio.co)

> RendoFren is a decentralized GPU rendering network

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional GPU rendering systems are expensive, time-consuming, and heavily dependent on centralized cloud infrastructure. Independent creators, freelancers, animation studios, and students often struggle to access high-performance rendering resources because of the high cost of GPUs and cloud rendering services. Large-scale projects created in software like Blender or Adobe After Effects can take hours or even days to render on a single machine, slowing down production workflows and limiting creativity.

At the same time, millions of GPUs around the world remain underutilized or completely idle for long periods. Gaming PCs, mining rigs, and personal workstations often possess significant unused computational power that is not efficiently utilized.

Another critical problem in the rendering and entertainment industry is content security and data leakage. In real-world production environments, unreleased movie scenes, VFX assets, animations, and confidential media files are sometimes leaked during rendering or file-sharing processes due to weak centralized security systems. When rendering tasks are outsourced or distributed, creators often lose full control over who can access their files.

Our project solves these problems by building a decentralized GPU rendering network that utilizes unused GPU power from systems around the world to process rendering tasks faster and more efficiently. The rendering workload is divided into smaller encrypted segments and distributed securely across multiple GPU nodes, significantly reducing rendering time and operational cost.

To ensure a much higher level of security, our project integrates blockchain-based encryption and verification mechanisms. Before any 3D scene, animation, or video asset is distributed across the network, the files are encrypted and securely fragmented. This ensures that GPU providers contributing computational power cannot access, view, or copy the original content while processing rendering tasks. Blockchain technology further guarantees transparency, tamper resistance, secure transaction records, and trustless validation across the network.

By combining decentralized computing with blockchain-powered security, our project creates a highly secure rendering network/ecosystem that prevents unauthorized access, minimizes the risk of media leaks, protects confidential creative assets, and delivers fast, scalable, and cost-effective rendering for creators worldwide.

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of the Decentralized GPU Rendering Network, several technical and architectural challenges were encountered. One of the primary issues was ensuring that rendering tasks utilized the GPU instead of defaulting to CPU rendering. Due to driver incompatibilities, incorrect CUDA/OpenCL configurations, and environment-related issues, some rendering engines automatically switched to CPU mode, resulting in significantly slower rendering performance and increased processing time.

Another major challenge was managing distributed rendering tasks across multiple decentralized nodes. The system needed to efficiently divide rendering jobs into smaller segments, assign them to available GPU providers, monitor task progress, and finally merge the rendered outputs accurately. Maintaining synchronization between nodes while preventing data loss or duplication required careful coordination.

Cross-platform compatibility also became a significant obstacle, as different contributors used varying operating systems, GPU architectures, and driver versions. Ensuring consistent rendering outputs across diverse hardware environments required additional optimization and testing. Furthermore, transferring large project assets such as textures, animations, and scene files across the network introduced bandwidth and latency challenges, especially when dealing with high-resolution rendering workloads.

Security and trust management were equally important concerns. Since rendering tasks were distributed among independent nodes, mechanisms had to be implemented to verify rendered outputs and prevent corrupted or incomplete results. Protecting sensitive project files while maintaining decentralization required secure data handling and encryption strategies.

Finally, balancing workloads among nodes with different GPU capabilities and integrating transparent reward mechanisms for contributors added further complexity to the system architecture. Despite these challenges, overcoming them helped create a more efficient, scalable, and reliable decentralized rendering solution.

Unlike traditional security tools that focus on input filtering, CipherWatch introduces a novel approach by verifying the integrity of AI decisions themselves. It leverages AI/ML techniques to detect semantic deviations and unsafe actions, ensuring that AI-driven workflows remain secure. This makes it highly relevant for modern applications where AI agents are trusted with sensitive operations in cloud, finance, and data systems.

> Credit History for Everyone!

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

**150 million gig workers in India are financially invisible.**

Swiggy delivery partners. Zomato riders. Ola drivers. These are people who show up every day, complete thousands of orders, and generate real, verifiable income — yet they own zero formal financial identity. No payslips. No CIBIL score. No credit history. Banks reject **90% of their loan applications on sight.**

The result: they borrow from moneylenders at **36–60% annual interest**, trapped in a cycle of debt that no amount of hard work can break.

---

**The core failure is not a lack of income — it is a lack of proof.**

Existing credit infrastructure was built for salaried employees with formal payslips and employer records. It was never designed for the platform economy. There is no mechanism for a gig worker to walk into a bank and say: *"I have earned consistently for 3 years. Here is the cryptographic proof."*

---

**ZeroTrace fixes this at the infrastructure level.**

- It ingests raw platform activity — earnings history, order frequency, tenure, consistency — and runs it through an **AI scoring engine** that computes a GigScore: a standardized, interpretable measure of creditworthiness.
- That score, along with the computation proof, is passed through a **Zero-Knowledge proof layer**, generating a cryptographic attestation that the calculation was performed correctly — without ever exposing the worker's raw income data to any third party.
- The attestation is written to a **Polygon blockchain smart contract**, making it permanently immutable, instantly verifiable, and worker-owned.

A bank or NBFC can verify the on-chain proof in seconds. They do not need to trust the platform. They do not need to trust us. **The mathematics is the guarantee.**

---

**The outcome is concrete.**

A gig worker currently paying 48% interest on an informal loan, armed with a verified GigScore, qualifies for a formal bank loan at **14% interest**. That difference, compounded over years, is the difference between debt and wealth.

Reaching just **1% of the Indian gig workforce** means **1.5 million people** receive their first formal financial identity — unlocking housing loans, business credit, insurance, and generational financial stability.

ZeroTrace does not build a better credit score. **It builds the right to have one.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. The Blockchain Would Not Cooperate — And We Shipped Anyway

The single hardest challenge was getting live on-chain transactions to work reliably on the Polygon Amoy testnet under hackathon time pressure.

Every call to push a GigScore proof hit a `UNPREDICTABLE_GAS_LIMIT` error — specifically a **"missing revert data"** failure during gas estimation. The contract was rejecting transactions before they even reached the chain. Debugging this meant tracing the failure across three layers simultaneously: the Solidity contract logic, the ethers.js service layer, and the frontend modal triggering the call.

The root cause turned out to be an `onlyAuthorized` modifier on the `updateProof` function that silently blocked worker-initiated writes. The contract was reverting with no data, causing ethers.js to fail at estimation with a completely opaque error. The fix required redeploying the contract, updating the ABI across the backend and frontend, and re-syncing all contract addresses — multiple times as each fix exposed the next layer of breakage.

---

### 2. ZK Proof Architecture vs. Hackathon Reality

The architecture we designed — AI scoring feeding into a Zero-Knowledge proof layer feeding into an on-chain attestation — is the right architecture. It is also not a 24-hour build.

Production zkML requires compiled arithmetic circuits, a trusted setup ceremony, and a verifier contract. None of that exists in a ready-to-drop library. We had to make a deliberate decision: implement a **cryptographic commitment scheme** that preserves the privacy guarantees and proof structure of zkML, while being demonstrable within the time constraint. The hash-based proof anchored on-chain is not a compromise of the concept — it is the first working layer of the full ZK stack.

---

### 3. Testnet Congestion Killed the Live Demo Path

Even after the contract logic was fixed, Polygon Amoy testnet congestion made gas estimation unpredictable at demo time. Transactions would hang, timeout, or fail with insufficient gas errors despite correct parameters.

Rather than risk a broken live demo, we built a **deterministic simulation layer** that executes the full proof generation and contract interaction flow client-side, with real transaction hash formatting and on-chain verification UI — so the end-to-end user journey is demonstrable without being blocked by testnet instability.

---

### 4. Three Runtimes, One Coherent System

The stack spans a React frontend, a Node.js/Express backend, a Python Flask ML engine, and a Hardhat blockchain environment. Making these four runtimes communicate reliably — correct ports, correct CORS headers, correct data serialization between Python and JavaScript — required careful integration work that is invisible in the final product but consumed a significant portion of build time.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

## Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence

ZeroTrace is not a project that uses blockchain as a badge or AI as a buzzword. Both are load-bearing components of the architecture — remove either one and the system fails its core promise.

**The AI layer** is a trained scoring engine that analyzes gig worker behavioral data — earnings consistency, order volume, tenure, activity frequency — and produces a GigScore. This is not rule-based logic. It is a model that learns creditworthiness signals from patterns that traditional banking infrastructure is completely blind to.

**The Blockchain layer** is what makes the AI's output trustworthy to a third party. Any bank can run its own model and produce its own score. What they cannot do is prove to a borrower — or to a regulator — that the score was computed correctly, on unaltered data, without exposing private income records. ZeroTrace anchors a cryptographic proof of the AI computation onto a Polygon smart contract. The proof is immutable, timestamped, and publicly verifiable. The bank does not trust us. They verify the chain.

**The ZK layer** bridges the two: Zero-Knowledge proof architecture ensures that the attestation proves computation integrity without leaking the underlying data. A worker's raw earnings never leave their control. What goes on-chain is the proof, not the payload.

This is the precise intersection the Web3 + AI track is designed for — not AI alongside blockchain, but AI whose outputs are made credible *because of* blockchain, and blockchain whose data is made meaningful *because of* AI.

**The problem it solves**

PharmaTrace: Predictive Pharmaceutical Tracking & Provenance

PharmaTrace is a next-generation supply chain solution that combines Blockchain Immutability and AI-Driven Analytics to secure the pharmaceutical lifecycle. It ensures that every medicine batch is authentic, optimized for delivery, and transparently tracked from manufacturer to patient.
Key Features

Immutable Blockchain Ledger: Every handoff is cryptographically signed and recorded on an Ethereum-compatible ledger, preventing counterfeiting and data tampering.

AI Route Optimization: A Python-based AI engine calculates demand scores and suggests optimal delivery routes based on regional health crises and flu outbreaks.

Real-Time Supply Chain Visibility: A high-performance, glassmorphic dashboard for Manufacturers, Distributors, and Local Shops to manage inventory in real-time.

Smart QR Verification: Patients and regulators can instantly verify the entire provenance of a medicine batch by scanning a QR code.

Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Secure identity management using MetaMask and WTech Stack

Frontend
Framework: React + Vite
Styling: Tailwind CSS + Framer Motion (Animations)
Icons: Lucide React
Web3: Ethers.js + MetaMask

Blockchain
Language: Solidity
Framework: Hardhat
Network: Localhost (Hardhat Node)

AI Backend
Framework: FastAPI (Python)
Core Logic: Predictive analysis for regional health demand and routingeb3 authentication.
Security and Provenance

PharmaTrace uses a "Proof of Custody" model. When a package moves from a Manufacturer to a Distributor, a Web3 transaction is triggered. This creates a permanent, undeniable record of who had the package and when, making it impossible to slip counterfeit drugs into the system without detection.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges while building PharmaTrace was integrating blockchain with a real-time system. Blockchain technology is inherently slow and immutable, whereas a supply chain platform requires fast updates and flexible data handling. Deciding what data to store on-chain versus off-chain was difficult, as storing everything on the blockchain would increase costs and latency, while storing too little would weaken transparency and trust. Ensuring smooth synchronization between the blockchain transactions and the frontend dashboard without affecting performance required careful architectural planning.
Another major challenge was developing secure and efficient smart contracts along with seamless Web3 authentication. Writing Solidity contracts demanded precision, as even small bugs could lead to permanent issues once deployed. Additionally, optimizing gas usage while maintaining functionality was complex. Integrating MetaMask for role-based access control added another layer of difficulty, as handling wallet connections, transaction approvals, and user roles in a decentralized environment is not as straightforward as traditional login systems.
The integration of the AI backend with the overall system also posed significant challenges. The AI model required structured and meaningful data, but blockchain data is not directly suitable for predictive analysis, making data transformation necessary. Designing a model that provides realistic demand predictions and route optimization without access to large-scale real-world datasets was difficult. Moreover, ensuring that the AI outputs aligned with real-time supply chain updates and reflected accurately on the dashboard required continuous synchronization across the backend, blockchain, and frontend components.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

Our project, PharmaTrace, represents the perfect synergy between Decentralized Trust and Predictive Intelligence to solve the $400B global counterfeit medicine crisis.

1. How it uses Web3 / Blockchain: We utilize an Ethereum-based smart contract to create an immutable "Proof of Custody" chain. Unlike traditional databases that can be edited or hacked, our system requires every manufacturer and distributor to cryptographically sign every handoff using MetaMask. This ensures 100% tamper-proof provenance—once a batch is registered on the ledger, its origin and journey cannot be faked or altered.

2. How it uses Artificial Intelligence: Tracking is only half the battle; knowing where to send medicine is the other. We integrated a Predictive AI engine (FastAPI/Python) that analyzes regional health data, such as flu outbreak trends and antibiotic resistance levels. The AI calculates a "Demand Score" and generates an optimized delivery route, which is then stored on the blockchain alongside the batch data.

The Synergy: AI provides the intelligence to optimize the supply chain and save lives during health crises, while Blockchain provides the trust layer that guarantees the medicines delivered are 100% authentic. This dual-layer approach creates a "Smart Supply Chain" that is both optimized and unhackable.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/violens-06d5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Altaria-hackathon-teams/iot-code-crafters) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1188320583?share=copy) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co)

> Detect. React. Save Lives.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

VioLens is an AI-powered smart traffic management system designed to improve road safety, automate violation detection, and enable rapid emergency response. It uses computer vision models to detect common traffic violations such as riding without a helmet, overspeeding, and triple riding in real time. The system processes live video feeds and identifies these violations accurately, helping authorities monitor traffic more efficiently without manual intervention. What makes VioLens stand out is its integrated approach that combines AI detection with real-world actions.

The most important feature of VioLens is its accident detection system. When an accident is detected using the AI model, the system immediately triggers alerts by sending notifications or SMS messages to emergency contacts and ambulance services, ensuring quick response and assistance. At the same time, it activates a connected hardware module using an ESP32, which changes the traffic signal to red and turns on a buzzer to alert nearby people. This is especially useful in low-visibility conditions like fog or nighttime, as well as in areas with low population density where accidents might otherwise go unnoticed. By combining intelligent detection with instant alerts and physical response, VioLens acts not just as a monitoring system but as a proactive safety solution aimed at saving lives and making roads smarter.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges I faced was integrating the AI detection system with the hardware (ESP32) in real time. Initially, my ESP32 code was working with a manually defined variable (`accidentDetected = true/false`), but when I tried to make it dynamic using data from my Flask backend, nothing worked. The LEDs and buzzer stopped responding because the ESP32 was not receiving any data. It turned out that the issue was not with the hardware, but with how serial communication was handled. I had not implemented proper reading from the USB serial input, and also forgot to send data with a newline character (`\n`), which caused the ESP32 to never recognize incoming commands.

Another hurdle was debugging the serial communication between Python and ESP32, especially when switching between Windows and macOS. On Windows, I used COM ports, but on macOS the device paths were different (like `/dev/cu.usbserial-0001`). I also ran into issues where the port was busy because the Arduino Serial Monitor was still open, which prevented Python from accessing it. I resolved this by ensuring only one connection was active at a time and by adding proper error handling and reconnection logic in my Python code.

I also struggled with the buzzer sound being very low. Even though the code was correct, the output was weak due to the ESP32’s 3.3V limitation and the type of buzzer I was using. I experimented with different approaches like PWM signals and rapid pulsing to make the sound more noticeable. While it didn’t become extremely loud, I improved it enough for a clear demo by adjusting frequency and using repeated beep patterns.

Overall, these challenges taught me a lot about hardware-software integration, debugging real-time systems, and handling edge cases like device connectivity and communication protocols. Once I fixed these issues, the system worked smoothly, and I was able to achieve real-time AI-driven hardware response.

Status Version License Stack

Sakhi-Agri is a state-of-the-art, multi-service agricultural platform designed to empower farmers with real-time data, AI-driven insights, and a direct-to-consumer marketplace. By bridging the gap between physical IoT sensors and intelligent cloud analysis, Sakhi-Agri transforms traditional farming into data-driven precision agriculture.

🌟 Core Features
📡 Real-Time Telemetry Dashboard
Live Sensor Feed: Instant visualization of Soil Moisture, Water Levels (Ultrasonic), pH, NPK, and Humidity.

🏗️ System Architecture
Sakhi-Agri follows a Microservices-inspired Gateway Architecture to ensure scalability and reliability:

Hardware Layer (Arduino Mega): Captures raw sensor data and streams it via Serial (USB).
IoT Bridge (Node.js): Reads Serial streams, parses JSON, and pushes data to the Gateway.
Gateway Server (Express.js): The central hub for Authentication (JWT/Bcrypt), WebSockets, and proxying AI requests.
AI Services (Flask): Dedicated Python services for ML inference, Computer Vision, and Generative AI (Gemini).
Frontend (Next.js 14): High-performance, responsive UI with modern glassmorphic design and real-time React state management.

**The problem it solves**

## 🎯 The Problem It Solves

Digital content today is extremely easy to copy, modify, and redistribute without permission. Creators, companies, and platforms face major challenges:

* ❌ No reliable way to **prove ownership** of original content
* ❌ Difficult to **detect leaks**, especially after modifications
* ❌ Impossible to **trace who leaked** the content
* ❌ Centralized systems can be **tampered with or manipulated**

---

## 💡 Our Solution: LeakGuard AI

LeakGuard AI solves these problems by combining **AI + Blockchain-inspired security** into one system.

---

### 🔍 1. Detects Content Leaks (Even After Modification)

Using AI-based similarity detection and perceptual hashing, the system can:

* Identify leaked images/videos even if they are:

  * resized
  * compressed
  * slightly edited

👉 This makes leak detection far more reliable than traditional methods.

---

### 🔐 2. Invisible Watermarking for Ownership Tracking

Each uploaded asset is embedded with a hidden watermark containing the owner's identity.

* Cannot be easily removed or seen
* Survives common edits
* Acts as a **forensic fingerprint**

👉 This allows the system to **trace leaks back to the source**.

---

### 🔗 3. Tamper-Proof Integrity with Hash Chain

Every upload is linked using a blockchain-inspired hash chain:

* Each asset stores:

  * its own hash
  * the previous asset’s hash

👉 If someone tries to:

* delete records
* modify data

➡️ The system immediately detects inconsistencies.

---

### 🌐 4. Trust Layer with Blockchain

A cryptographic hash of each asset is stored on blockchain:

* Provides **immutable proof of ownership**
* Ensures data cannot be forged
* Enables independent verification

👉 This builds trust without relying on centralized systems.

---

### 🧠 5. Identifies the Exact Leaker

With per-user watermarking:

* Same content → different watermark per user
* If leaked → system identifies:

  * who leaked
  * when
  * from which session

👉 This is similar to **forensic watermarking used in OTT platforms**.

---

## 🚀 Real-World Use Cases

* 🎬 Protecting movies and OTT content from piracy
* 🎨 Safeguarding digital art and NFTs
* 📸 Preventing unauthorized reuse of images
* 📊 Securing confidential media in organizations
* 🎓 Protecting educational or premium content

---

## 🔥 Why It Matters

LeakGuard AI makes digital content:

✔ More secure
✔ Traceable
✔ Tamper-proof
✔ Trustworthy

---

## 🧠 Summary

> LeakGuard AI transforms how digital ownership and piracy are handled by combining AI-powered detection with blockchain-backed trust, making content protection smarter, safer, and verifiable.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges We Ran Into

### 1. 🔗 Integrating Multiple Tech Stacks (Spring Boot + Python + Frontend)

One of the biggest challenges was connecting three different layers:

* Spring Boot (Java backend)
* Python AI service (watermarking + detection)
* Vite frontend

Initially, the communication between Spring and Python APIs failed due to incorrect request formats and file handling (multipart issues).

**How we solved it:**

* Standardized API contracts (JSON + multipart)
* Used consistent endpoints (`/watermark`, `/detect`)
* Debugged using Postman before integrating with frontend

 2. 🧠 Handling File Upload + Watermark Processing

Passing video/image files from frontend → Spring → Python was tricky.

Issues:

* File not reaching Python correctly
* Corrupted file during transfer
* Incorrect response handling

**Solution:**

* Used `MultipartFile` in Spring Boot
* Sent files using `RestTemplate` properly
* Validated responses step-by-step before saving in MongoDB

 3. 🔐 Implementing Hash Chain (Blockchain-like Structure)

Creating a chain of hashes (previousHash + currentHash) required careful handling.

Issues:

* Chain breaking due to wrong order
* Incorrect hash generation
* Difficulty validating chain integrity

**Solution:**

* Introduced a consistent hashing utility (SHA-256)
* Stored index + previousHash properly
* Built a validation API to detect tampering

4. 🤖 AI Detection Accuracy (Modified Files)

Simple file comparison failed when files were:

* resized
* compressed
* renamed

**Solution:**

* Used perceptual hashing (pHash)
* Added similarity scoring instead of exact matching
* Combined with watermark extraction for reliability

 5. 🔌 Git & Repository Issues

We faced multiple Git problems:

* Permission denied (403 errors)
* Wrong remote repository
* Nested Git repositories (embedded repo issue)

**Solution:**

* Fixed remote using `git remote set-url`
* Removed embedded `.git` folders
* Used `--force` push for clean setup

6. ⚙️ Vite + Node Polyfill Errors

While integrating wallet libraries and external packages, we faced:

* `buffer` and `global` not defined errors

**Solution:**

* Added polyfills using Vite config
* Used compatible package versions
* Cleaned dependency cache

 7. 🔄 Keeping Data Consistent Across UI

Initially, data was stored in `localStorage`, causing mismatch between screens.

**Solution:**

* Removed localStorage dependency
* Fetched all data from MongoDB APIs
* Added refresh functions after each action

 💡 Key Learning

> Building a full-stack Web3 + AI system requires careful coordination between multiple services. Debugging step-by-step and isolating each layer helped us successfully integrate everything into a working system.
🚀 Outcome

Despite these challenges, we successfully built:

* AI-based leak detection system
* Blockchain-inspired tamper-proof storage
* Real-time leak tracing with user identification

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

Where Web3 / Blockchain fits
1) Decentralized identity (wallet-based)
Users can log in via wallet (e.g., Algorand).
The wallet address becomes a verifiable, user-controlled identity (no fake accounts).
Ownership is tied to a cryptographic address, not just email.
2) Immutable ownership proof (on-chain hash)
On upload, you generate a file hash (SHA-256).
You anchor this hash on-chain (e.g., Algorand).
This creates a timestamped, tamper-proof record of ownership.
Upload → Hash → Store on-chain → Permanent proof
3) Trust layer (independent verification)
Even if your server is compromised, anyone can:
Recompute the file hash
Compare with on-chain record
That’s trust without relying on your backend (core Web3 idea).
4) Optional: smart contracts (next step)
Licensing / access rules
Ownership transfer
Revenue sharing for creators
🤖 Where AI fits
1) Content fingerprinting (robust identity)
Convert images/videos into feature embeddings or use pHash.
Works even if content is:
compressed
resized
slightly edited
2) Invisible watermarking (forensic ID)
Embed user/owner ID inside media (not visible).
Survives typical transformations.
3) Leak detection
On suspected upload:
Extract watermark → identify user
Run similarity → confirm it’s the same content

**The problem it solves**

# 🚀 Cognitive UAV Ground Control System (C-GCS)

> **A real-time, model-driven, AI-augmented Ground Control System enabling predictive autonomy, system introspection, and intelligent decision orchestration for unmanned aerial platforms.**

---

## 🧠 Executive Summary

Traditional Ground Control Systems (GCS) are fundamentally **observational interfaces**—they visualize telemetry but lack semantic understanding.

This system introduces a **Cognitive GCS**, integrating:

* **State-space estimation**
* **Digital twin simulation**
* **Probabilistic anomaly detection**
* **Predictive failure modeling**
* **Risk-aware decision synthesis**

The result is a system that **perceives, reasons, forecasts, and recommends actions in real time**.

---

## 🧩 Core System Components

### 📡 1. Telemetry Ingestion & Normalization

* MAVLink protocol decoding with asynchronous streaming
* Time-synchronized state reconstruction
* Noise-aware preprocessing pipelines

---

### 🧠 2. State Estimation (Extended Kalman Filter)

Implements nonlinear state-space estimation:

* Multi-sensor fusion (IMU, GPS, barometer)
* Bias correction and drift mitigation
* Continuous-time → discrete-time transformation

Outputs:

* Position, velocity, orientation
* Covariance matrices representing uncertainty

---

### 🔮 3. Digital Twin (Model-Based Simulation)

A **physics-informed virtual replica** of the UAV:

* Flight dynamics approximation
* Battery discharge modeling
* Motor thrust degradation simulation

Supports:

* Forward simulation
* Counterfactual analysis (*“what if motor 2 fails?”*)

---

### 📉 4. Predictive Intelligence Engine

Time-series forecasting using:

* Sliding window temporal features
* Regression-based or sequence models

Predicts:

* Battery depletion trajectory
* Motor efficiency decay
* Signal integrity degradation

---

### 🚨 5. Anomaly Detection Engine

Hybrid detection framework:

* Statistical residual analysis (baseline deviation)
* Temporal inconsistency detection
* Threshold-adaptive alerting

Detects:

* Sensor drift
* Sudden voltage collapse
* Mechanical inconsistencies

---

### ⚠️ 6. Probabilistic Risk Engine

Computes a **dynamic risk score**:

* Integrates:

  * Current state estimate
  * Predicted trajectories
  * Detected anomalies
* Uses weighted risk aggregation

Outputs:

* Continuous risk metric ∈ [0,1]
* Categorized severity levels

---

### 🤖 7. Decision Synthesis Engine

Transforms system intelligence into **actionable advisories**:

* Rule-based + heuristic reasoning
* Context-aware recommendations

Examples:

* *Initiate Return-to-Home*
* *Throttle reduction advised*
* *Immediate landing required*

---

### 🖥️ 8. Immersive 3D Digital Twin Interface

* Real-time WebGL rendering (Three.js / R3F)
* Component-level semantic highlighting
* Event-driven alert overlays
* Smooth state interpolation animations

**Challenges we ran into**

⚙️ Challenges I Ran Into
Building a real-time AI-augmented UAV Ground Control System on top of ArduPilot and interfacing with tools like Mission Planner introduced multiple non-trivial engineering challenges across telemetry handling, ML integration, and system architecture.
🧩 1. MAVLink Telemetry Synchronization & Data Integrity
Problem:
MAVLink streams from ArduPilot are asynchronous and high-frequency, leading to:
Packet drops under unstable connections
Out-of-order message arrival
Inconsistent timestamps across telemetry fields
This made it difficult to construct a coherent system state vector required for ML inference and digital twin updates.
Solution:
Implemented a buffered ingestion pipeline with timestamp alignment
Designed a lightweight state reconciliation layer to normalize telemetry frames
Used interpolation for missing values and prioritized critical message IDs (e.g., ATTITUDE, SYS_STATUS)
🧠 2. Bridging Real-Time Systems with ML Inference
Problem:
Machine learning models trained on NASA and Kaggle datasets were:
Offline-trained and batch-oriented
Not directly compatible with real-time streaming inputs
Sensitive to noise and distribution shift from live UAV telemetry
Solution:
Built a feature extraction pipeline to match training distribution with live MAVLink data
Applied online normalization and smoothing filters (moving averages, noise suppression)
Optimized inference latency to avoid blocking the control loop
⚡ 3. Real-Time Performance Bottlenecks (WebSockets + Backend)
Problem:
The system required:
Continuous telemetry streaming
Real-time ML predictions
Live frontend updates (digital twin visualization)
This caused:
WebSocket congestion
Backend event loop blocking
Increased latency in UI updates
Solution:
Adopted an asynchronous architecture (FastAPI + async WebSockets)
Decoupled pipelines:
Telemetry ingestion
ML inference
Visualization updates
Implemented rate limiting + batching for frontend updates
🌐 4. Digital Twin State Consistency
Problem:
Maintaining a synchronized digital twin required:
Accurate mapping of UAV kinematics
Continuous updates without jitter or drift
Consistency between real UAV and virtual model
Even small delays caused:
Visual desynchronization
Incorrect system interpretation
Solution:
Introduced a state prediction layer to compensate for latency
Used interpolation between telemetry frames for smooth rendering
Ensured deterministic update cycles for the twin
⚠️ 5. Designing a Reliable Risk Scoring System
Problem:
Combining multiple inputs:
Telemetry anomalies
ML predictions
System thresholds
into a single risk score was non-trivial due to:
Conflicting signals
Noise in sensor data
Lack of standardized weighting
Solution:
Designed a weighted probabilistic risk model
Tuned weights empirically based on simulated failure scenarios
Added threshold-based overrides for critical safety conditions
🔌 6. Integration with Existing GCS Ecosystem
Problem:
Ensuring compatibility with:
ArduPilot firmware
Mission Planner workflows
without breaking existing pipelines was challenging.
Solution:
Built the system as a non-intrusive overlay layer
Used MAVLink as the single source of truth
Avoided modifying flight controller firmware
🧪 7. Dataset Generalization & Domain Gap
Problem:
Models trained on:
NASA prognostics datasets
Kaggle UAV datasets
did not perfectly generalize to:
Real UAV flight conditions
Noise characteristics of actual sensors
Solution:
Applied domain adaptation techniques
Used synthetic noise injection during testing
Focused on relative anomaly detection rather than absolute predictions
🧠 Key Takeaway
The biggest challenge was not any single bug, but integrating heterogeneous systems:
Real-time embedded telemetry (ArduPilot)
Streaming backend architecture
Machine learning inference
Digital twin visualization
into a low-latency, reliable, and scalable system.
Overcoming this required a shift from:
“building components individually”
to:
“engineering a tightly coupled, real-time intelligent system.”

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

🌐 How the Project Fits into IoT and AI
This project operates at the intersection of Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), forming a tightly integrated cyber-physical system where real-world UAV hardware is continuously monitored, analyzed, and optimized through intelligent algorithms.

📡 IoT Integration (Internet of Things)
The UAV system functions as a distributed IoT node within a larger connected ecosystem.
🔗 Device Connectivity & Data Acquisition
* The drone, powered by ArduPilot, acts as a sensor-rich edge device
* Continuously streams telemetry via MAVLink protocol
* Data includes:
    * IMU (acceleration, gyroscope)
    * GPS coordinates
    * Battery voltage/current
    * ESC and motor metrics

☁️ Real-Time Data Transmission
* Telemetry is transmitted to the Ground Control System using wireless communication links
* Backend (FastAPI + WebSockets) acts as an IoT gateway
* Enables:
    * Low-latency data streaming
    * Continuous device monitoring
    * Remote system control

🧩 Data Aggregation & System Integration
* Multiple subsystems (flight controller, sensors, communication modules) are integrated into a unified IoT architecture
* Works alongside tools like Mission Planner but extends them with deeper data processing layers

🌍 Digital Twin as an IoT Abstraction
* The Digital Twin represents a virtual IoT entity
* Maintains real-time synchronization with physical UAV state
* Enables remote diagnostics without direct hardware interaction

🧠 AI Integration (Artificial Intelligence)
The system leverages AI to convert raw IoT data into actionable intelligence and predictive insights.

🔮 Predictive Analytics & Prognostics
* Machine learning models trained on:
    * NASA prognostics datasets
    * Kaggle UAV/sensor datasets
* Capabilities:
    * Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation
    * Battery degradation prediction
    * Early anomaly detection

⚙️ Real-Time Inference Pipeline
* Processes streaming telemetry in real time
* Applies:
    * Feature extraction
    * Noise filtering
    * Model inference
* Produces:
    * Anomaly flags
    * Health indicators
    * Failure probabilities

⚠️ Intelligent Decision-Making
* AI outputs are fed into a decision engine
* Generates:
    * Risk scores
    * Safety recommendations (RTH, emergency landing)
* Transitions system behavior from:
    * Rule-based → Data-driven intelligence

🧩 Adaptive Learning Potential
* System can be extended to:
    * Continuously retrain models using flight logs
    * Improve accuracy over time
    * Adapt to different UAV configurations

🔄 IoT + AI = Intelligent Cyber-Physical System
The true innovation lies in the fusion of IoT and AI:
IoT Layer	AI Layer
Collects real-world UAV data	Interprets and predicts from data
Enables connectivity and streaming	Enables intelligence and autonomy
Represents physical system	Enhances decision-making capability
🚀 Final Insight
This project is not just an IoT system or an AI model—it is an end-to-end intelligent UAV ecosystem where:
* IoT provides continuous situational awareness
* AI provides predictive intelligence and autonomy
Together, they enable a shift from:
Connected Devices → Intelligent Autonomous Systems

**The problem it solves**

The Core Problem: Everyday users on the Stellar network lack transparent, manipulation-resistant tools to evaluate the safety of tokens, leaving them vulnerable to rug pulls, honeypots, and scams.

Specific Problems Solved:

Hidden Traps (Clawbacks): Scammers hide settings that let them freeze or steal back your tokens. Solution: TrustProof automatically scans and flags dangerous ledger settings.
Honeypot Scams: Tokens that you can buy, but can't sell. Solution: The ML engine mathematically verifies if a safe "sell path" actually exists.
Fake Reviews: Scammers use bots to flood forums with fake 5-star reviews. Solution: TrustProof stores reviews on a Soroban smart contract and mathematically proves a user's wallet history before letting them post, killing review-bots instantly.
"Perfect Code" Rug Pulls: Scammers launch tokens with safe code, but act maliciously in secret. Solution: TrustProof extracts the creator's "Behavioral DNA" from past transactions to spot scammer habits, regardless of how safe the code looks.

**Challenges we ran into**

TrustProof fits perfectly into a Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence track because it uses the strengths of both technologies to compensate for each other's weaknesses. In DeFi security, neither blockchain data nor AI alone is enough to protect users; TrustProof merges them into a cohesive safety layer.

Here is exactly how the project bridges the two fields:

1. The Blockchain Layer (The Source of Truth)
Blockchain provides immutable, verifiable data, but raw ledger data is incredibly difficult for an average user to understand.

On-Chain Sybil Resistance: Web2 review platforms rely on algorithms to stop bots, which often fail. TrustProof uses the Stellar blockchain and Soroban Smart Contracts to solve this. Because the backend verifies a user's on-chain transaction history before allowing them to post a review to the smart contract, it mathematically guarantees that the reviewer is a real participant, completely preventing bot manipulation.
The Ground Truth Data: The Stellar ledger (via the Horizon API) acts as the un-fakable foundation. It provides the raw, unalterable data regarding liquidity, holder distribution, and issuer authority flags that the ML models rely on.
2. The Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Layer (The Context & Pattern Recognition)
While blockchain provides the data, AI and ML provide the pattern recognition and human context needed to make that data actionable.

Machine Learning (Behavioral DNA): Scammers frequently change their token's code to evade standard security scanners. TrustProof's runDNA engine uses ML concepts (specifically, extracting a 40-feature vector array and computing Cosine Similarity against known threats) to fingerprint how an issuer behaves. It analyzes transaction velocity, airdrop patterns, and funding sources to detect rug-pull behavior, even if the token's code is technically flawless.
Generative AI (OSINT via Gemini): A token might look safe mathematically on the blockchain, but off-chain, users on Reddit and Twitter might be warning others that the team disappeared. TrustProof uses Google's Gemini LLM equipped with Google Search Grounding to perform Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT). The AI actively searches the public web for mentions of the token or issuer, reads the sentiment, and summarizes off-chain scam reports into a single verdict.
The Synergy: Why They Must Be Combined
If you only have Blockchain, you have unreadable hex codes and raw numbers that the average user can't use to protect themselves. If you only have AI, you run the risk of hallucinations and the AI giving bad financial advice based on manipulated data.

How TrustProof Combines Them: TrustProof uses Blockchain to ensure the core safety data (reviews, liquidity, code flags) cannot be faked or manipulated. It then uses Machine Learning to find hidden malicious behavioral patterns within that massive dataset. Finally, it uses Generative AI to investigate the human context across the web and translate the complex on-chain math into a simple, human-readable risk summary.

By marrying the un-fakable math of Blockchain with the pattern-recognition and context-awareness of AI, TrustProof provides a complete, 360-degree security shield.

AI Formatting Conflicts: Getting the Gemini AI to reliably return clean JSON data while actively using its Google Search Grounding tool was difficult, requiring us to build custom text-extraction and fallback algorithms.
Stellar's Unique Architecture: Standard security scanners are built for Ethereum smart contracts. We had to build our Python ML Engine from scratch to specifically read Stellar's unique ledger-level flags (like auth_clawback).
Preventing Bot Reviews: To stop scammers from faking 5-star reviews on our Soroban smart contract, we had to engineer a backend gatekeeper that queries the blockchain to mathematically prove a user's transaction history before letting them post.
Extracting "Behavioral DNA": Fetching and compressing up to 1,000 ledger transactions per issuer into a 40-feature mathematical vector for pattern recognition was highly resource-intensive and required heavy optimization.
Complex Orchestration: Coordinating the data flow between a React frontend, a Node.js backend, a Python Flask ML-engine, local SQLite caches, and the Soroban testnet required careful architectural planning.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

TrustProof fits perfectly into a Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence track because it uses the strengths of both technologies to compensate for each other's weaknesses. In DeFi security, neither blockchain data nor AI alone is enough to protect users; TrustProof merges them into a cohesive safety layer.

Here is exactly how the project bridges the two fields:

1. The Blockchain Layer (The Source of Truth)
Blockchain provides immutable, verifiable data, but raw ledger data is incredibly difficult for an average user to understand.

On-Chain Sybil Resistance: Web2 review platforms rely on algorithms to stop bots, which often fail. TrustProof uses the Stellar blockchain and Soroban Smart Contracts to solve this. Because the backend verifies a user's on-chain transaction history before allowing them to post a review to the smart contract, it mathematically guarantees that the reviewer is a real participant, completely preventing bot manipulation.
The Ground Truth Data: The Stellar ledger (via the Horizon API) acts as the un-fakable foundation. It provides the raw, unalterable data regarding liquidity, holder distribution, and issuer authority flags that the ML models rely on.

2. The Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Layer
 (The Context & Pattern Recognition)
While blockchain provides the data, AI and ML provide the pattern recognition and human context needed to make that data actionable.

Machine Learning (Behavioral DNA): Scammers frequently change their token's code to evade standard security scanners. TrustProof's runDNA engine uses ML concepts (specifically, extracting a 40-feature vector array and computing Cosine Similarity against known threats) to fingerprint how an issuer behaves. It analyzes transaction velocity, airdrop patterns, and funding sources to detect rug-pull behavior, even if the token's code is technically flawless.
Generative AI (OSINT via Gemini): A token might look safe mathematically on the blockchain, but off-chain, users on Reddit and Twitter might be warning others that the team disappeared. TrustProof uses Google's Gemini LLM equipped with Google Search Grounding to perform Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT). The AI actively searches the public web for mentions of the token or issuer, reads the sentiment, and summarizes off-chain scam reports into a single verdict.
The Synergy: Why They Must Be Combined
If you only have Blockchain, you have unreadable hex codes and raw numbers that the average user can't use to protect themselves. If you only have AI, you run the risk of hallucinations and the AI giving bad financial advice based on manipulated data.

How TrustProof Combines Them: TrustProof uses Blockchain to ensure the core safety data (reviews, liquidity, code flags) cannot be faked or manipulated. It then uses Machine Learning to find hidden malicious behavioral patterns within that massive dataset. Finally, it uses Generative AI to investigate the human context across the web and translate the complex on-chain math into a simple, human-readable risk summary.

By marrying the un-fakable math of Blockchain with the pattern-recognition and context-awareness of AI, TrustProof provides a complete, 360-degree security shield.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vanilla JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vanilla%20JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![RTDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/RTDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3​](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3​-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Primary Problem**: The Lost "Golden Hour"
In major metropolitan cities, the difference between life and death is often decided by a single red light. Ambulances regularly lose their critical "golden hour" trapped in urban gridlock. Current solutions are insufficient.
Sirens rely on human reaction times in densely packed spaces where cars physically have nowhere to move.
Hardware pre-emption systems (like RFID sensors) require ripping up roads and executing expensive, city-wide hardware overhauls.

**How Namma Marga Solves It**
Namma Marga acts as an invisible, digital traffic cop that parts the sea of traffic before the ambulance even arrives—using zero new road hardware.
We solve this by turning the ambulance driver's smartphone into a high-frequency IoT beacon. Our cloud-based Logic Engine constantly calculates the Haversine distance between the moving ambulance and registered "smart intersections." When the ambulance breaches a 500-meter radius, the system autonomously secures the intersection, giving the emergency vehicle a clear green light without requiring the driver to interact with the system.

**The Secondary Problem: Post-Emergency Gridlock**
Traditional pre-emption systems solve the emergency problem but create a massive secondary problem: horrific traffic jams for civilian commuters who were forced to wait.
Namma Marga solves this through a closed-loop Computer Vision pipeline. The moment the ambulance clears the intersection, our AI cameras calculate a live "congestion index" based on the backlog of waiting cars. The system then autonomously holds the green light for those specific civilian lanes just long enough to flush the displaced traffic, instantly restoring normal urban mobility.

**Challenges we ran into**

Android Background Kills: Android 14's strict battery limits kept killing our live GPS tracking when the phone screen turned off.

Solution: We built a robust LocationForegroundService with explicit OS-level permissions to keep the app alive and safely pinging coordinates every second.

Map Routing Crashes: Fetching complex route data from our routing API caused the Android app to freeze and silently fail.

Solution: We moved all heavy network calls to background threads, cleanly bridging the data back to the main screen only when it was ready to draw.

Cloud Data Desync: Getting the Android app, web simulator, and Node.js engine to speak the exact same language in Firebase was a nightmare. A single missing variable broke the system.

Solution: We created and enforced a strict, universal 9-field JSON "data contract" across the entire stack to guarantee flawless synchronization.

Database Overload: Scaling our math to track multiple intersections at once threatened to exhaust our Firebase database write limits.

Solution: We optimized our Logic Engine so it only writes to the database at the exact moment the ambulance crosses the 500-meter trigger boundary, drastically reducing server load.

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

**The IoT Component**: The emergency vehicle acts as a high-frequency IoT beacon. Using a native Android app, it streams live GPS telemetry (latitude, longitude, speed) to our Firebase cloud infrastructure every second. Our Node.js Logic Engine continuously calculates the Haversine distance between this moving IoT node and registered "smart intersections" to autonomously trigger traffic light pre-emption.

**The AI Component**: To prevent the pre-emption from causing civilian gridlock, we deployed a Computer Vision pipeline. Using OpenCV and a custom Roboflow model, our system analyzes live camera feeds at the intersection to calculate a real-time "congestion index." The AI dynamically adjusts the subsequent green-light duration to flush the displaced traffic, creating a closed-loop, intelligent traffic management system.

**The problem it solves**

Commercial buildings waste up to 30% of their energy because equipment faults and gradual degradation often go unnoticed until a breakdown occurs. NeuralGrid addresses this by detecting issues in HVAC systems, compressors, and pumps early, giving teams time to act before failures happen. It helps reduce energy waste by identifying equipment that is consuming more power than normal in real time. The system replaces manual inspections by operating 24/7 and monitoring all equipment simultaneously. It also makes maintenance more actionable by providing a complete AI-based diagnosis, including the root cause, confidence level, recommended fix, urgency, and estimated cost impact in rupees per day. **Challenges we ran into**

1) False positive storm
Isolation Forest flagged too many anomalies during small occupancy spikes
Solution: Added ARIMA as a second check
Alert triggers only when both models agree
Result: False positives almost eliminated

2) ARIMA crashing on short data
Errors occurred for short, constant, or invalid time series
Solution:
Wrapped code in try/except
Added minimum 30 readings requirement

3)Telegram asyncio conflict
python-telegram-bot v21 is async but monitoring loop is sync
Using asyncio.run() caused RuntimeError
Solution: Created a new event loop for each alert

4) Cross-process buffer sharing issue
Streamlit and FastAPI run as separate processes
Cannot share in-memory data
Solution:
Dashboard runs its own MQTT subscriber
Used alerts_log.json and reports folder for shared data

5) Groq returning malformed JSON
LLaMA3 sometimes returned responses with markdown formatting
Caused parsing issues
Solution:
Removed backticks and json labels before parsing
Added fallback error logging to prevent crashes

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

Here it is rewritten in **simple points (no bullets, only numbers and clean text):**

---

1 NeuralGrid combines AI/ML and IoT tightly
NeuralGrid is not just AI using sensor data and not just IoT running a model
Both parts depend on each other and cannot work separately

2 IoT layer provides real-time data
Six sensors send data every 2 seconds using MQTT
Sensors include power meter, HVAC, lighting, compressor, and two pumps
Each reading has value, baseline, unit, and timestamp
This continuous data is the only input for the ML system

3 AI layer makes data useful
Raw sensor values alone are not meaningful
Example: compressor using 29 kW means nothing without context

4 Isolation Forest detects anomalies
Compares current data with normal behavior
Gives an anomaly score to identify unusual patterns

5 ARIMA predicts future trends
Uses last 60 readings to forecast future behavior
Helps identify if the issue is growing or just normal variation

6 Dual-gate system improves accuracy
ThreatConfirmer triggers alerts only if both models agree
Reduces false alerts and makes system reliable

7 AI + IoT work together for deep analysis
When alert triggers, LLaMA3 receives data from all sensors
Does not analyze one sensor alone
Compares multiple sensor readings together

8 Context-based fault detection
Example:
Compressor high + power meter high + HVAC rising → likely motor issue
Compressor high alone → different problem
This level of reasoning is not possible with basic IoT rules

9 Final outcome
IoT acts as the data source (eyes)
AI acts as the decision maker (brain)
System converts raw sensor data into clear maintenance actions quickly

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
In modern enterprise cybersecurity environments, critical assets (Crown Jewels) such as databases and sensitive servers are the primary targets for attackers. However, security analysts often struggle to clearly understand how an attacker can move through the network from an initial entry point to these high-value systems.

Today’s enterprise networks are:
Large and highly distributed
Complex and deeply interconnected
Segmented but misconfigured
Filled with hidden privilege relationships
Because of this, organisations fail to fully identify:
Complete attack paths
Lateral movement routes
Privilege escalation chains
Real risk to Crown Jewel assets
This lack of visibility leads to reactive security, where threats are addressed only after damage is done—resulting in financial loss, data breaches, and regulatory impact.

💡 What This System Enables
Our platform transforms this process into a proactive, intelligent, and automated defence system.
1. End-to-End Attack Discovery
Instead of isolated alerts, the system models the entire enterprise as a graph-based network, capturing:
Assets (servers, applications, databases)
Identities and privileges
Vulnerabilities (CVEs, misconfigurations)
Relationships between all components
This allows analysts to see complete multi-hop attack paths, not just individual weaknesses.

2. Realistic Attack Simulation (Red Team Automation)
The system integrates real-world attack simulation using multiple payloads such as:
SQL Injection
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
Brute Force attacks
Directory fuzzing
Parser-based attacks (DSL / HTTP parsing)
It actively identifies exposed servers linked to the system and attempts exploitation, mimicking real attacker behaviour.

3. Intelligent Path Analysis
Using graph algorithms like:
K Shortest Paths → finds realistic attack routes
Min S-T Cut → identifies critical choke points
The system highlights:
The easiest paths attackers will take
The minimum set of defenses needed to block all attacks

4. Risk-Based Prioritisation
Each attack path is ranked using:
Exploitability
Asset criticality
Path complexity
This ensures teams focus only on high-impact vulnerabilities, reducing noise and effort.

5. AI-Driven Reasoning & Mitigation
The platform uses an LLM-based reasoning engine to:
Understand relationships between vulnerabilities and assets
Generate realistic attack chains
Recommend targeted, cost-effective mitigations
Instead of generic fixes, it suggests:
Which CVEs to patch first
Which privileges to revoke
Which nodes to secure for maximum impact

6. What-If Simulation (Decision Support)
A built-in simulation engine allows teams to:
Patch vulnerabilities virtually
Modify configurations
Instantly see how attack paths change
This enables safe testing of security decisions before deployment.

🎯Real-World Impact
This system helps:
SOC Teams detect attack paths faster
Red/Blue Teams simulate real attack scenarios
Security Architects design stronger networks

It:
Reduces time to detect threats
Cuts remediation costs
Improves compliance and audit readiness

Getting a real dataset that is as close to a enterprise network was the biggest hurdle we faced when we were starting this project.

Another hurdle was finding websites were we can test our attack detection model since most of the websites would directly flag our model we then figured we will have to test it for a protected environment like a docker or juice shop.

README.md:# FairChain — AI Governance Platform

![FairChain Dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stellar/stellar-logo/master/stellar-logo.png) <!-- Replace with actual banner if available -->

**FairChain** is a production-ready, blockchain-anchored AI Governance Platform built to ensure fairness, transparency, and accountability in automated hiring and decision-making systems.

By combining **Multi-Agent AI Debate**, **Deterministic Rule Engines**, and **Stellar Blockchain Cryptographic Audits**, FairChain transforms the "black box" of AI into a transparent, legally defensible, and auditable process.

---

## 🌟 Key Features

### 1. Multi-Agent Courtroom Debate
Instead of relying on a single, potentially biased LLM, FairChain uses an adversarial multi-agent system:
*   **The Advocate (Pro Agent):** Evaluates candidates purely on merit (skills, experience, certifications).
*   **The Inquisitor:** Actively searches for bias signals, proxy variables, and fairness violations.
*   **The Judge:** Weighs both arguments and delivers a final, balanced verdict.

### 2. Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR) Monitoring
FairChain actively calculates the **Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR)** for protected classes (gender, race, age) in real-time. If the DIR falls below the EEOC-standard **0.80 threshold**, the system detects a fairness violation and triggers visual alerts (glitch effects) and potential rule overrides.

### 3. Cryptographic Blockchain Audit (Stellar Testnet)
To ensure legally defensible decisions:
*   Every decision generates a cryptographic receipt using a **Merkle Tree**.
*   The **Merkle Root** is anchored to the **Stellar Testnet**.
*   **Soroban Smart Contracts** validate the DIR score on-chain.
*   Fairness **Soulbound Tokens (SBTs)** can be minted to prove a candidate was treated fairly.

### 4. Interactive 3D Command Center
The frontend is a "Command Center" built with **Next.js** and **Tailwind CSS**, featuring a pitch-black, dark-glass aesthetic.
*   **React Three Fiber (R3F):** Powers a live 3D courtroom where holographic agents debate decisions in real-time.
*   **MerkleChain3D:** An interactive 3D visualization of the cryptographic audit ledger.

### 5. Automated Telegram Bot & Email Receipts
*   **Telegram Integration:** Recruiters can upload resumes (PDF/TXT) directly via Telegram for instant processing.
*   **Automated Email Receipts:** Candidates receive a personalized cryptographic audit receipt detailing their evaluation, fairness score, and a link to the Stellar Testnet transaction proving the integrity of their assessment.

### 6. Red-Teaming "Saboteur" Agent
An integrated adversarial testing feature that generates highly qualified but structurally biased candidate profiles to stress-test the platform's bias detectors and Inquisitor agent.

---

## 🏗️ Architecture Stack

### Backend (FastAPI / Python)
*   **Framework:** FastAPI for high-performance





The "Black Box" of AI Hiring
As companies rush to adopt AI for screening resumes, they face a critical problem: AI models act as opaque black boxes. Single-model LLMs silently reject candidates based on hidden biases (proxy variables like zip codes or employment gaps), leaving companies vulnerable to massive legal risks under frameworks like the EU AI Act. Meanwhile, candidates are frustrated by unexplained ghosting. Furthermore, centralized HR databases can be easily manipulated by corrupt managers to cover up discriminatory practices.

The FairChain Solution
FairChain transforms AI recruitment from a legal liability into a transparent, mathematically verified, and fully auditable process.

For HR Teams (Risk Mitigation): Instead of blindly trusting a single AI, FairChain acts as a "Digital Courtroom." Three distinct AI agents (Advocate, Inquisitor, and Judge) actively debate the candidate to hunt for bias. It calculates a strict Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR), automatically blocking decisions that violate fairness thresholds.

For Legal Auditors (Tamper-Proof Proof): We use the Stellar Blockchain to ensure records can never be secretly edited. The system hashes the AI debate into a Merkle Root and anchors it to the Stellar Testnet, providing cryptographic proof of a fair audit.

For Candidates (Total Transparency): Candidates automatically receive a Cryptographic Audit Receipt via Email. If approved, the system mints a Soulbound Token (SBT) to their Freighter wallet, giving them a permanent, verifiable "Proof of Fairness" badge.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/702866d3118948a086c708287d7bd1dc/a42d18b4-f197-4397-a2d6-5b99ca67290d.png)                                                                                                       

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/702866d3118948a086c708287d7bd1dc/e6a99171-d085-4df5-a52c-7eb91e1cd601.png)                                                          

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/702866d3118948a086c708287d7bd1dc/cda3def2-58a9-4dba-8131-db4d16ea5aaa.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a platform that bridges advanced multi-agent AI with Web3 cryptographic verification presented several intense engineering hurdles:

1. Multi-Agent Orchestration (LangGraph)
Getting three distinct AI agents (Advocate, Inquisitor, Judge) to debate dynamically without hallucinating or falling into infinite loops was difficult.

How we got over it: We utilized LangGraph to enforce a strict state-machine architecture. We isolated the agents' system prompts and forced the Judge agent to act as a strict deterministic router, cutting off the debate once sufficient bias-checking conditions were met.

2. Deterministic Cryptography for AI Transcripts
To anchor the decision to the Stellar blockchain, we needed to generate a Merkle Root from the AI debate. However, AI outputs can contain slight whitespace or formatting variations, which completely breaks cryptographic hashing.

How we got over it: We built a normalization pipeline in FastAPI that strips and sanitizes the JSON payload of the debate transcript before passing it to our SHA-256 hashing functions. This ensured 100% deterministic Merkle Roots every time.

3. Seamless Web3 UI Integration
We wanted a dominating, immersive 3D Web2 aesthetic (using React Three Fiber and Glassmorphism) while running heavy Web3 wallet interactions in the background. Initially, triggering the Freighter Wallet API caused frame drops in our 3D particle background.

How we got over it: We decoupled the wallet authentication state from the 3D rendering canvas using custom asynchronous React hooks, allowing the 3D nodes to continue pulsing smoothly while awaiting Stellar network consensus.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

FairChain sits perfectly at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Web3 by using blockchain to solve AI's biggest flaw: the "black box" trust problem.

Here is exactly how the two technologies work together in our platform:

The Artificial Intelligence Layer: We built a complex multi-agent system (using LangGraph and Python) acting as a digital courtroom. Instead of one opaque algorithm, three distinct AI agents—an Advocate, an Inquisitor, and a Judge—actively debate candidate resumes to hunt for hidden biases and calculate strict Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR) scores.

The Web3 / Blockchain Layer: Because AI logs can be secretly altered by humans on private servers, we use the Stellar Blockchain as an immutable vault for AI governance.

The Synergy: We mathematically hash the AI's final debate transcript into a Merkle Root and anchor it directly to the Stellar Testnet. Furthermore, we wrote Soroban Smart Contracts to act as automated referees that physically block biased AI decisions on-chain, and we use the network to mint Soulbound Tokens (SBTs) to candidates as a cryptographic "Proof of Fairness."

FairChain uses AI to do the heavy lifting of evaluation, and Web3 to provide the mathematical, untamperable trust that AI inherently lacks.
